PASTORIBVS, DIACONIS ET SENIORIBVS reformatarum Gallici Regni Ecclesiarum, honorandis Dominis & fratribus, Theodorus Beza gratiam & pacem à Deo Patre & Domino nostro Iesu Christo.
units.tr: To the pastors, deacons and elders of the reformed Churches of the kingdom of France, to be honoured lords and brothers: Theodore Beza, grace and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: HONORANDI fratres in Domino, praeterquā quòd ipsa Christiana religio in genere, & nominatim ea vocatio, qua nos Deus domi suæ dignatur, nos ad sacrosanctā mortis Domini historiam summa cura & studio cognoscendam, vsuíque suo applicandam adstringit: luctuosissimæ illæ tragoediæ, quibus Gallia totos iam annos triginta sensim absumitur, ab iis nefariis hominibus excitatæ, qui tuendæ veræ, quam vocant, religionis studium ambitiosissimis conatibus suis praetexunt, & cuius incendij flamma ad has quoque regiones peruasit, desiderium illius maiore quàm vnquam cura cognoscendæ in me accenderunt, consolandæ illius Ecclesiæ causa, quam mihi Deus excolendam commisit. In hoc igitur opere, quanta maxima cura potui versatus, istud quidquid est nunc vobis offero, minimè id quidem vt eos erudiam, quorum malim esse discipulus, sed partim vt de summo nostro in vera & sana doctrina consensu magis ac magis in vniuerso terrarum orbe ad mutuam nostram in istis æuissimis tempestatibus consolationem constet: partim vt, occasione hinc arrepta, de nonnullis aduersus Satanæ in his turbulentis temporibus insidias, non tantum, vt ego quidem opinor, utilibus, sed etiam penitus necessariis vobiscum agam. Nullus est igitur, nisi omnis diuini & humani iuris hostis, qui miserrimum hunc statum Galliæ tanta phrenitide laborantis non agnoscat, ac etiam deploret, sed vtinam eius mali causæ meliùs essent perspectæ, & vera illi curando remedia adhiberentur. Quum enim vtrinque & hos & illos oportuerit tucrit sese apud Domini tribunal, iustissimam & asperrimam iram suam aduersus manifestissima nostra scelera testantis, reos & poenitentes sistere: ecce e contrario vni quidem calamitates istas omnes iis imputant, quos ipsi haereticos appellant: alteris vero, per Dei gratiam, non desunt quidem peremptoriae, quas vocant, exceptiones: sed (quod bona cum eorum venia dictum esto) per quos non stat quominus ista corrigatur, mores doctrinae quam profitemur, ex diametro repugnantes, & cum iis prorsus consentientes, quae in aliis reprehendimus, non modo exceptiones illas elidunt, verum etiam aduersariis praebent pretiosi illius nominis Ecclesiarum reformatarum, quales cognominamur, occasione blasphemandi: vsq; adeo vt, quod olim Prophetae vociferabatur, Iuda Dei nomine abutes, Israelem Apostatam iustificet. Eamus igitur nunc & Dominum miremur plagas plagis cumulare, clementissime tamen in eo nobiscum agentem, quod poenas iustissime pecc-tis nostris inflictas sanctissimo suo no-
units.tr: Honoured brothers in the Lord, apart from the fact that the Christian religion in general, and especially that calling by which God deigns to call us into his house, binds us to learn the history of our Lord's death with the greatest care and zeal and to apply it to our use, those most lamentable tragedies by which France has been gradually consumed for thirty years now have kindled in me a desire to know it more carefully than ever, for the sake of comforting that Church which God has entrusted to me to cultivate. Those tragedies were stirred up by wicked men who cover their most ambitious schemes with the pretext of defending what they call the true religion, and their flames have spread even to these regions. In this work I have laboured with the greatest care I could, and I offer you now whatever it is. Certainly I do not offer it to teach those whose disciple I would rather be, but partly so that our common agreement in true and sound doctrine may become more and more evident throughout the whole world, for our mutual consolation in these most troubled times; and partly so that, having seized the occasion, I may deal with you about some matters concerning Satan's snares in these turbulent times, matters that are not only useful, as I at least think, but absolutely necessary. There is therefore no enemy of all divine and human law who does not recognise, and also deplore, the most wretched state of France, labouring under such frenzy. But I wish the causes of that evil had been better perceived and true remedies applied to heal it. For since both these and those must present themselves at the Lord's tribunal, as guilty parties and penitents, bearing witness to his most just and bitter anger against our most manifest crimes, behold, on the other hand, some impute all those calamities to those whom they themselves call heretics. To the others, by God's grace, there are not lacking those peremptory objections, as they are called. But (let it be said with their good pardon) those through whom it is not that this is corrected, namely the morals of the doctrine we profess, which are in direct conflict with it and wholly in agreement with those very things we condemn in others, not only overturn those objections but also give our adversaries an occasion to blaspheme the precious name of the reformed Churches, by which we are called. So much so that what the prophets once cried out has come true: "Judah, abusing the name of God, justifies Israel the apostate." Let us go then and marvel that the Lord heaps blow upon blow, yet deals most mercifully with us in that he

units.la: ¶. iij. mine exornat? Quænam autem hîc sint adhibenda remedia noftis quàmopti-mè, neque dubito quin illa sedulò publicè ac priuatim ægris conscientiis applicetis: sed nullo, vel perexiguo cū fructu. Hîc verò meminisse vos oportet idem eximiis quibusque Prophetis, immo ipsi Iesu Christo Domino nostro apud populum illum suum vsque-niste. Ipsius ergo vnius Domini messis in hoc agro, de quo nunc agimus, partes sunt, seruis suis feretibus, plantantibus, & rigantibus, prout ipsi visum fuerit, benedicere. Fidum autem seruum vnum quemque decet nihil de labore suo remittere, atque adeò quò contumacius est solum ipsius culturæ commissum, tanto maiore contentione in illud excolendum incumbere, etiamsi per ipsas rupes trahendum ipsi fuerit aratrum. Hanc autè peritorum & summa cum solicitudine laborantium colonorum operam impedire quamplurima consueuerunt. Non desunt enim nonnulli turbis istis tam assueti, ut si forte procurandi aliorum exitii via ipsis præcludatur, sese perditos exististimet. Sunt & alii,quos vana quœdã sese esse-rendi spes animis præcepta à nefariis consiliis abduci nunquam sinat:vsque adeò vt quibusuis vltrò periculis caput exponant, potiùs quàm expestatione sua frustrari sese patiantur. Denique non desunt, & ij multò quidé plures quàm oportuerit, turbarū istarū auidissimi fautores,partim vt priuatas inimicitias vlcilcantur,partim vt illata sibi damna resarciant.Sed in hoc argumento longius non progrediar, quoniam remediū istis malis accommodatum ab iis expestandum est,quibus Deus publicam auctoritatem attribuit : quod muneris huius nostri proprium nō est. Satis igitur esto mihi, fratres honorandi,audacia sanéta quadam freto,vos quantumuis vigiles, ad perpetuas excubias, & assiduam huic sanando malo necessariam diligentiā, hortari, vt Prophetarum & Apostolorum exemplum sequuti, gladium illū verbi diuini spiritualem vobis commissum distringere & versare magis ac magis pergatis, prout temporum, locorum & personarum ferent cir-
units.tr: adorns with his most holy name the punishments most justly inflicted on our sins? What remedies ought to be applied here, you know best, and I do not doubt that you apply them diligently, publicly and privately, to troubled consciences, but with little or no fruit. Here, however, you must remember what the outstanding prophets, and indeed Jesus Christ our Lord himself, did among that people of his even until now. It is therefore the part of the Lord alone, in this field of which we now speak, to bless his servants, who sow, plant and water as it seems good to him. A faithful servant ought to remit nothing of his labour, and indeed the more stubborn the soil committed to his cultivation, the greater the effort he should put into tilling it, even if the plough must be dragged over the very rocks. Yet very many things are accustomed to hinder the work of skilled and most anxious farmers. For there are some so accustomed to these disturbances that, if perchance the way to bringing about the destruction of others is closed to them, they think themselves ruined. There are others whom some vain hope of making themselves known never allows to be drawn away from wicked plans, so much so that they willingly expose their heads to any dangers rather than suffer their expectations to be frustrated. Finally, there are not lacking, and indeed far more than there should be, most eager supporters of these disturbances, partly so that they may avenge private enmities, partly so that they may repair damage inflicted on them. But I will not go further on this subject, since the remedy suited to these evils must be looked for from those to whom God has given public authority, which is not the proper task of our office. It is enough for me, honoured brothers, relying on a certain holy boldness, to exhort you, however watchful you already are, to perpetual vigilance and the constant diligence necessary for healing this evil; that, following the example of the prophets and apostles, you may keep on drawing and turning ever more the spiritual sword of the divine word committed to you, as the circumstances of times, places and persons may require, and

units.la: ¶. iiij. cunstatiæ & sanctus ille Dominus Dei nostri Spiritus vobis præibit. Vt ergo ad ea quæ sunt muneris nostri propria, mea nunc redeat oratio, quum plane sit necesse præcipuo & summè cauendo Satanæ conatui occurrere, in hoc vnum intenti vt ipsius Regni Gallici ruina, Gallicas Ecclesias semel radicitus subuertat: hunc autem ipsius conatum Deus, pro summa & verè admirabili benignitate sua infregerit, quo tempore coniurati sese nefariis votis suis potitos arbitrabantur: exhortari vos non desinam, vt nullam instaurandarum sacræ domus Domini ruinarum occasionem prætermittatis: sic nimirum conseruandis illis sacri huius ædificij partibus & regionibus quæ præ aliis adhuc ab istis tëpestatibus illesæ perstant, incumbè tes, vt miserorum vestrorum fratrum solicitè memores sitis, in quos totum hoc onus sic recumbit, vt adhuc sub eius pondere gementes vix caput attollant. Quoniam autem hac in reprocuranda plurimum in eo positum est vt neque, præbentibus sese speciosis occa-
units.tr: and that holy Spirit of our God will go before you. So, to return my discourse to what is proper to our office: since it is entirely necessary to meet Satan's chief and most carefully guarded attempt, which is intent on this one thing, that by the ruin of the kingdom of France he may once for all utterly overthrow the Churches of France; and since God, by his supreme and truly admirable kindness, has broken this attempt of his at the very time when the conspirators thought they had obtained their wicked desires, I will not cease to exhort you not to let slip any opportunity of restoring the ruins of the Lord's holy house. Thus, indeed, you labour to preserve those parts and regions of this sacred building which, unlike the others, still stand unharmed by these storms, while being mindful of your wretched brothers, on whom this whole burden so weighs that, groaning under its weight, they can scarcely lift their heads. Since, however, in this restoration much depends on this: that neither, when specious opportunities present themselves,

units.la: occasionibus, quæ prætermittendæ nō videantur, præpropera festinatione peccetur: neque, dum ordinaria & humana remedia expectantur, cunctando præclaræ bene gerendæ rei & promouendi operis Domini rationes amittantur, Deum & Patrem illum nostrum Opt. Max. precor, vt præeunte vobis vbique Sancto illo suo Spiritu, neque temerarii, neque negligentes comperiamini. Interea tamen prætermittere nec volo, nec debeo quod ipsa nos experientia hisce nostris temporibus docuit: nempe si ab humanæ prudentiæ consiliis pependissent qui primi Gallicarum Ecclesiarum fundamenta iecerunt; futurum omnino fuisse vt ne nunc quidem vlla cœptæ structuræ indicia appareret. Quòd si aduersariorum minæ & immanitas, vel Regiorum edictorū subdolæ, quas vocant, modificationes, ipsis apertis persequutionibus periculosiores, fidos illos Domini operarios essent remoratæ: haud satis scio an vlla nunc vel vnica Ecclesia staret. Altera verò ex parte dum mecum expendo mirabilia illa Domini Dei nostri gesta lucem ex profundissimis illis tenebris eruentis.Is enim est qui ex horrenda & summe abominanda,& vt paucis omnia comp lectar, monachali spiritu perpetrata defuncti Regis cæde, statim prodire nauis,iam iam naufragium faturæ, vel in horum piratarum & Gallici maris prædonum manus casuræ,tantum gubernatorem iussit, vel cœlitus potius in terras demisit:& dum mecum præterea considero, diuinitus factum vt Gallicæ veræ Nobilitatis animi subito in publicæ Regni quietis instaurationem vltro inclinarint (quod sperare nos iubet futurum vt idem Deus huic sanctæ & ab ipso perfectæ consensioni successu temporis benedicat) Deum ipsum supplex inuoco, vt eam, qua hic opus est prudentia & circunspectione vobis ipse suggerere dignetur. Cæterum fratres honorandi, satis esse vobis perspectas arbitror alteras vobis à Satana intrinsecus in hac tanta rerum omniū perturbatione adoriedi insidias comparatas: docete nos historia Ecclesiastica tunc demū ingentes illas
units.tr: which must not be let pass, is there error through excessive haste, nor, while ordinary and human remedies are awaited, are the chances of carrying through this splendid work and advancing the Lord's work lost by delay. I pray God our Father, our Best and Greatest, that, with his Holy Spirit going before you everywhere, you may be found neither rash nor negligent. Meanwhile, however, I neither wish nor ought to omit what experience itself has taught us in these times: namely, had the founders of the French Churches depended on the counsels of human prudence, there would certainly be no sign even now of the structure they began. But if the threats and savagery of the adversaries, or the deceitful so-called modifications of the royal edicts, more dangerous than open persecutions, had delayed those faithful workers of the Lord, I scarcely know whether a single Church would still stand. On the other hand, when I weigh within myself those wonderful deeds of the Lord our God, who brings light out of those deepest darknesses (for he it is who, after the horrible and most abominable murder of the late king, committed in a monkish spirit, to sum it up briefly, ordered a pilot, or rather sent one down from heaven, for the ship which was about to be wrecked at once or fall into the hands of these pirates and robbers of the French sea), and when I further consider that it was divinely brought about that the minds of the true French nobility spontaneously inclined to the restoration of public peace in the kingdom (which bids us hope that in time the same God will bless this holy agreement, which he himself has brought to completion), I beseech God as a suppliant that he may deign himself to suggest that prudence and circumspection which is needed here. But, honoured brothers, I think you have seen well enough that other snares have been laid for you by Satan from within, in this great upheaval of all things. Church history teaches us that those great disturbances

units.la: in Ecclesia Christiana exortas consu-fiones,quum,Constantino magno im-perante, veteres illæ persecutiones de-siissent.Moneo vos igitur etiam atque etiam vt vigilare magis ac magis per-gatis.Nã certè, fi Dominus, quod spe-randum nobis est, quietem aliquam Ecclesiis in Gallia concesserit, non est quod dubitetis fore vt leuis & ambi-tiofi ingenij homines mox passim ca-put attollant. Et simulatque optatiffi-mum illud pacis & quietis nomen au-ribus insonabit, tum demũ,nisi,(quod Deus auertat) vltrò decipi vultis,scito-te exorituros non paucos, vnos quidë oneri crucis Domini diutius ferendo impares: alios verò, vt adhuc doctrinæ sanæ rudes discipulos: alios præ infir-mitate metuentes mox fequuturã ali-quam istarum turbarum renouationë: non paucos denique leuis & arrogan-tis ingenii homines, prius magistros quàm bonos discipulos, qui quibusuis conditionibus speciosissimo pacis hu-ius nomine sese extra viam ferri pa-tiantur.Istis autem succenturiati faue-bunt, vel nutantes etiam illos impellent boni illi.& publicæ scilicet tran-quillitatis studiosi sequestres medium quiddam ibi quærentes, vbi nusquam est,nec vnquam erit,sibi & aliis persua-dentes mediis quibusdam consiliis lu-cem & tenebras conciliari, At vos fra-tres,& verbis,& reipsa veris & legiti-mis modis sedulò testati, nihil esse vo-bis optatius quàm vt omnes in pace & quiete ex mandatorum Dei præscri-pto sanctè & honestè viuat, cauete in-terea vobis summa solicitudine,&, quantū vobis chara est vestra & com-missarum vobis omium salus,istos do-ctrinę mediatores fugite:& sanctam il-lam & rectam Fidei confessionem ex Dei verbo purè descriptam,tot legiti-mis & verè Christianis synodis confir-matam, tot denique fidelium fratrum martyrum Domini sanguine sancitam prorsus integram & illibatam constan-ter retinete: quam etiam quoties opus erit ex puro Dei verbo facile vobis e-rit in omnibus liberis sanctis & legiti-mis conuentibus,ad quos vocati sueri-t s, tueri. Eandé in vobis constantiam opto in Ecclesiastica disciplina,tam fe-liciliciter haƈtenus in prouincialibus & generalibus synodis constituta & vsur-pata: quam etiam instar nerui & sancti vinculi fuisse non ignoratis, quo vos benignissimus ille Deus noster & Pa-ter per suum Spiritum sibi in Iesu Chri-sto adiunƈtos, in mediis persequutio-nibus exteris,& intus motis insultibus in cósenlione mutua quietos cóserua-u it.Hoc igitur indissolubili retéto vin-culo, & constanter obseruato illius v-su, sperãdus est vobis diuinæ illius be-nediƈtionis perpetuus tenor: & contrà si forte, quod Deus auertat, vel tan-tillum illud vinculum relaxari,persua-sionibus & commentis istorum inno-uatorum decepti, patiamini, aut ego prorsus vehementer fallor aut, isto vinculo primùm quidé inflexo, & sic tandem paulatim dissoluto, horrendæ mox confusiones in vestrarum Eccle-siarum sinu exorientur. At è contra rio maxima spes est, fore, si Deo vi-sum erit coniunƈtionem inter ortho-doxos Principes Germanos, & Chri-stianissimum Regem diuinitus nobis datum cœptam promouere,vt integra pax inter omnes reformatas Ecclelias effloresçat. Tanto igitur procurando bono, & tanto impediendo malo, ego eorum minimus quos Deo visum est sancto Euangelij sui ministerio dignari, & licet in mea statione extra regnū Galliæ collocatus: tamen vt Dei servus per ipsius gratiam, & genere Gallus, & vos de mea fide minime dubitare persuasus, omnes honorandos meos fratres, & veteranos illos meos in opere Domini collegas, quos aurei seculi reliquias appellare consueui, obtestari non dubito, per sacrosanctum Christi nomen, vt his rebus magis ac magis inuigilent, & (quam sunt auctoritatem longa experientia in Ecclesia consequuti) cæteros sanctis consiliis in officio retineant. Eos autem qui postea superuenerunt eodem affectu precor, vt graue illud Pauli Timotheū suum compellantis dictum memoria tenentes, Maneto in iis quæ didicisti, & quæ tibi concredita sunt: & à quo didiceris, tum defunctorum fratrum memoriæ, tum adhuc superstitum senectuti & prudentiæ tantum tribuere meminerint, quantū res ipsa poscit. Denique à vobis omnibus peto vt hanc oppellā meam à me oblatam perinde ac quandam Testamenti specie accipiatis, vt pote, qua cōtineatur doctrina quadraginta hisce annis à me tradita: in qua etiam (licèt censuris iudicióque vestro summissa) perseueraturum esse me confido ad beatum vsque illum finem, qui veram nostram vitam auspicatur. Cæterùm, venerandi fratres, vestris assiduis precibus & hanc ciuitatem totam grauissimo bello implicitam, & hunc nostrum cœtum nominatim velim vt Opt. Max. Deo pergatis magis ac magis commendare: eundem illum precatus vt vos pro clementia singulari sua eximiis omnibus suis donis augeat: vt sanctam firmamque tam in doctrina sana, quàm iisdem voluntatibus consensionem nostram confirmet: vestris laboribus, & quibus fidei vestræ commissis quàm cumulatissimè benedicat. Geneuæ die Iunii 24. Ioannis Baptistæ natalibus sacro, anni huius vitæ meæ 72. termino, & subsequentis 73. initio.
units.tr: ...in the Christian Church, when the great Constantine was emperor and those old persecutions had ceased. I therefore urge you to keep watch more and more. For certainly, if the Lord (which we must hope for) grants some quiet to the Churches in France, you should have no doubt that men of light and ambitious character will soon raise their heads everywhere. And as soon as that most welcome name of peace and quiet sounds in your ears, then, unless (which God forbid) you wish to be deceived of your own accord, know that not a few will arise: some, indeed, unequal to bearing the cross of the Lord for long; others, still raw disciples of sound doctrine; others, fearful through weakness, who will soon follow some renewal of those disturbances; and finally not a few men of light and arrogant character, who would sooner be teachers than good disciples, and who will allow themselves to be carried off course under any terms, in the most specious name of this peace. These men will be backed by reinforcements, or those good men will push even the wavering, and clearly those who are keen on public tranquillity, acting as go-betweens, seeking some middle ground where there is none and never will be, persuading themselves and others that light and darkness can be reconciled by certain middle counsels. But you, brothers, who have diligently borne witness, both in words and in deeds, by true and lawful means, that nothing is more desirable to you than that all should live holily and honourably in peace and quiet according to the prescription of God's commandments, take care in the meantime with the utmost solicitude, and, as dear to you as your own salvation and that of all committed to you, flee those mediators of doctrine. Hold firmly and entirely unimpaired that holy and right confession of faith, purely drawn up from the Word of God, confirmed by so many lawful and truly Christian synods, and finally sealed by the blood of so many faithful brothers and martyrs of the Lord. Whenever need arises, you will easily be able to defend it from the pure Word of God in all free, holy and lawful assemblies to which you are called. I wish the same steadfastness in you in Church discipline, so happily established and practised hitherto in provincial and general synods, which, as you know, has been like a sinew and a holy bond, by which that most kind God and Father of ours, joining you to himself in Jesus Christ through his Spirit, has kept you at peace in mutual agreement amid external persecutions and inward assaults. Therefore, if this indissoluble bond is kept and its use constantly observed, the perpetual course of that divine blessing is to be hoped for you. But on the contrary, if perhaps, which God forbid, you allow even that small bond to be loosened, deceived by the persuasions and devices of these innovators, then either I am greatly mistaken, or, once that bond has first been bent and so at last gradually dissolved, dreadful confusions will soon arise in the bosom of your Churches. On the other hand, there is the greatest hope that, if it seems good to God, the union begun between the orthodox German princes and the most Christian King, given to us by God, will be advanced, so that complete peace may flourish among all the reformed Churches. Therefore, in pursuing so great a good and in hindering so great an evil, I, the least of those whom God has been pleased to count worthy of the holy ministry of his Gospel, though placed outside the kingdom of France in my station, yet, as a servant of God by his grace and a Frenchman by birth, and persuaded that you have no doubt of my faith, I do not hesitate to beseech all my honoured brothers, and those veterans, my colleagues in the work of the Lord, whom I am accustomed to call the remnants of the golden age, by the holy name of Christ, that they keep more and more vigilant watch over these matters and (with the authority they have gained through long experience in the Church) keep the others in their duty by holy counsels. As for those who came afterwards, I pray with the same feeling that, keeping in mind that weighty saying of Paul addressing his Timothy, "Continue in the things you have learned and which have been entrusted to you, and from whom you learned them," they remember to give as much weight to the memory of departed brothers as to the old age and prudence of those still living, as the matter itself requires. Finally, I ask all of you to accept this little work offered by me as a kind of testament, since it contains the doctrine I have taught these forty years; in it, too (though submitted to your censures and judgement), I trust I shall persevere until that blessed end which begins our true life. Furthermore, venerable brothers, I would have you commend more and more, by your constant prayers to God Best and Greatest, this whole city, entangled in a most grievous war, and this our assembly by name; praying that he, in his singular clemency, may enrich you with all his excellent gifts, confirm our agreement, holy and firm both in sound doctrine and in the same wills, and bless most abundantly your labours and the charges committed to your faith. Geneva, 24 June, on the holy feast of the birth of John the Baptist, the close of the seventy-second year of my life and the beginning of the seventy-third.

units.la: TH. BEZÆ HOMILIÆ IN HISTORIAM PASSIONIS ET sepulturæ Domini nostri Iesu Christi, à quatuor Euangelistis descriptam.
units.tr: Th. Bezae Homiliae in historiam passionis et sepulturae Domini nostri Iesu Christi, a quatuor Evangelistis descriptam.

units.la: ETsi totius Domini nostri Iesu Christi vitæ curriculum id est, vt loquitur Lucas Act. 1.1. quicquid, iam inde à Mariæ Virginis matris vtero, fecit ac docuit, nihil nisi perpetua pro peccatis nostris perpessio fuit atque satisfactio: nihilominus tamen quum mortem eius omnium certaminum acerbissimum & grauissimum, & obedientiæ ipsius erga patrem clausulam fuisse constet, vel ipso teste Apostolo Philipp. 2. 8. & Coloss. 2. 14. & 15. & aliis a. j. multis locis similibus, quibus ad sanguinem eius pro nobis fusum remittimur, hinc efficitur hac mortis ipsius historia prae reliquis quam memoriae infigamus & sedulo perpendamus esse dignissimam. Hac sane ob causam Sp. S. a quatuor Euangelistis illam summo consensu amplissime describi, & literis mandari voluit, omnibus Christianis sedulo noctes diesque, imo singulis momentis meditandam & penitandam.
units.tr: Although the whole course of our Lord Jesus Christ's life, which, as Luke says (Act. 1.1.), consisted of everything he did and taught from the very womb of the Virgin Mary his mother, was nothing but a continual suffering and satisfaction for our sins, nevertheless his death is agreed to have been the most bitter and grievous conclusion of all his struggles and of his obedience toward the Father. The Apostle himself bears witness to this (Phil. 2.8; Col. 2.14–15), and so do many other similar passages, by which we are referred to the blood shed for us. It follows that this history of his death is, above all others, most worthy to be fixed in our memory and carefully weighed. For this reason the Holy Spirit willed that it be described most fully, with the greatest agreement, by the four Evangelists, and committed to writing, so that all Christians should meditate on it diligently night and day, indeed at every moment.

units.la: Idcirco etiam iam inde ab ipsius Ecclesiae incunabilis, tempus hoc anni Christiani veteres illius enarrationi dicarunt, ad quam sece ieiuniis & piis aliis exercitiis comparabant: unde illae natae voces, Septuagesimae, Sexagesimae, Quinquagesimae & Quadragesimae, prout alij aliis ad huius mysterij meditationem & praeparationem sese & maturius accingebant & diutius exercebant, ut vetus historia Ecclesiastica testatur. Sed erat in iis libera cuique voluntas & arbitrium, praeeunte fana & pura doctrina sine superstitione, donec tandem Satan, frustra de hac re Paulo Ecclesiam praemonente Col. 2. 18. & 23. partim ambitione, partim ignorantia quorundam Episcoporum abusus, qui statim in Ecclesiam post Apostolorum tempora irrepserunt, quod diserte ac vere praedixerat Act. 20. 29. & 30. & plebeculae pabulo privatae simplicitate & ignorantia sunt abusi, quicquid in illis piis ac religiosis exercitiis inerat boni, primum in quoldam abusus, deinde in superstitionem. tionem, tandémque in manifestam impiera-tem transformauit: deprauata nimirum penitus tota veræ Pœnitentiæ doctrina: fructúque mortis ac passionis Dominicæ sublato, tandémque plus quàm Pharisaicis inuectis superstitionibus.Noh igitur immerito nostro secu-lo præstantissimi illi viri & à Deo nouissimis hisce temporibus terris immissa lumina, magnum illum & pium regem Ezechiam imitati serpentem illum æneum, licet Dei ipsius mandato constructum, & longo tempore non sine ædificatione conseruatum, contringentem & destruentem, 2. Reg.18.4. superstitiosa illa omnia semel sustulerit, & pro nefaria illa conscientiarum carnificina in dierum festorum numero scrupulosè obseruando, & in cibotum delectu, sinceram de Christiana Pœnitentia doctrinam, de sobrietate, de veris ieiuniis, & in primis de fructibus & effectis mortis & passionis Domini restituerunt, atque redintegrarunt. Libeter igitur ex huius Ecclesiæ nunquam satis laudato more & instituto explicandam hoc tempore hanc historiam suscepi; sed paulò maturius solito, vt maiore cum otio diligenter illam considerare & sigillatim explicare nobis liceat. Ea sunt enim tempora, vt maximè nobis, si alias vnquam, sit istius doctrinæ meditatio necessaria, vt aduersus belli huius tam cruenti, quo nos Deus probat & exercet, calamitates & infinitas omnis generis miserias, erigamur & confirmemur: paternis nimirum istis iudiciis, quibus nos benignus pater explorat, in nostrum maximum commodum cessuris, ea, si modò ad eum scopum & finem referamus in quem à Domino nobis immittuntur: sin minus, in extremam perniciem ac ruinam, futuris nisi mature sub potente manu Dei nos summittetes agnoscamus nos nimium diu plus quàm patientissima ipsius abusos esse patientia, qua nos etiam num hodie ad omnium suorum ac nostrorum hostium vesque stuporem iam annu integrum omni beneficiorum suorum genere cumulatos benignissime tolerat.
units.tr: For this reason, from the very cradle of the Church, the ancient Christians dedicated this season of the Christian year to the narration of it, and prepared themselves for it with fasts and other pious exercises. Hence the names Septuagesima, Sexagesima, Quinquagesima and Quadragesima arose, as some began earlier and practised longer in preparing for and meditating on this mystery, as ancient ecclesiastical history attests. But in these matters each person had free will and judgment, provided that sound and pure doctrine went before, without superstition. Then at last Satan, though Paul had warned the Church about this in vain (Col. 2.18 and 23), and though Acts 20.29–30 had clearly and truly foretold it, abused these things. Partly through the ambition and partly through the ignorance of some bishops, who crept into the Church right after the times of the Apostles, and through the simplicity and ignorance of the common people, who were deprived of proper food, he turned whatever good there was in those pious and religious exercises first into certain abuses, then into superstition, and at last into manifest impiety. The whole doctrine of true repentance was utterly corrupted, the fruit of the Lord's death and passion was taken away, and superstitions were heaped up more than Pharisaical ones. Not undeservedly, therefore, in our age those most eminent men, lights sent by God into the earth in these last times, imitating the great and pious King Hezekiah, who crushed and destroyed the bronze serpent, though it had been made by God's own command and had for a long time been preserved, not without edification (2 Kings 18.4), at once removed all those superstitions. In place of that nefarious butchery of consciences, by scrupulous observance of the number of feast days and by the choice of foods, they restored and renewed the sound doctrine of Christian repentance, of sobriety, of true fasting, and above all of the fruits and effects of the Lord's death and passion. I have therefore gladly undertaken to explain this history at this time, following the never sufficiently praised custom and institution of this Church, though a little earlier than usual, so that we may have more leisure to consider it diligently and explain it point by point. For these are times when, more than ever, meditation on this doctrine is necessary for us, so that we may be raised up and strengthened against the calamities of this so bloody war, by which God tests and exercises us, and against endless miseries of every kind. These fatherly judgments, by which our kind Father tries us, will turn to our greatest benefit if we refer them to the goal and end for which the Lord sends them to us. Otherwise, unless we humble ourselves in time under God's mighty hand, they will bring us to extreme ruin and destruction. Let us acknowledge that we have abused his most patient forbearance for far too long, the forbearance by which, even today, after a whole year, he kindly bears with us, heaping us with every kind of benefit, while we remain stupefied toward all his and our enemies.

units.la: Absit verò cogitemus in hoc tractationis huius cardinem vti, vt Mortis ac Passionis Domini mentionem tàtum crebrò faciamus, aut eum Seruatorem appellemus: sed penitius ad tanti mysterij cognitionem cum timore & reuerentia nobis est penetrandum, quantum quidem Deus id patefacere dignabitur, vt hinc quidem quanta fuerit eius qui passus est respectu dolorum immensorum acerbitas inspiciamus: inde verò ingentem suauitatem in nos ex tantis iámque immensis eius doloribus redundantem hauriamus. Et quidé ego vos istud prætmonitos velim, vt intelligamus in huius historiæ lectione & interpretatione sic nobis versandum, non vt nuda demum commiseratione vel humanitatis quodam sensu tangamur, quum eum qui omnium iustissimus est, tam indignis & atrocibus pœnis affectum intelligimus, aut facinorosos detestati vel Iudeis succenseamus, vel Iudam execremur, vel Caiapham pham Pilatúmque abominemur (quanquam quis hanc historiam fine indignatione legat?) fedvt ferio sensu peccatorum nostrorum assi-ciamur, quibus expiandis Scruatoré nostrum in tantas támque acerbas angustias immer-sum & in crucem actum cIfe videmus: vera pœ nitentia viram anteactam deteltemur, resipi-fcentiam ex animo amplectamur: ardenti de-fiderio contemplemur altitudinem latitudi-nem & profunditatem, hinc quidem immensę dilectionis Dei, qui filio suo vnigenito non pepercit, sed dedit ipsum in pretium tam pre-tiofæ redemptionis pro peccatis nostris: inde vero incomprehenfæ bonitatis filij Dei, ini-micos suos plus quàm fe ipsum amantis, ad mortem vsque, mortem inquam Crucis: deni-que vera conscientiæ pace & tranquillitate fruamur, quum paradisum nostrum inuenia-mus vel in ipsis inferis, ad quos fummus ille & vnicus hominum seruator & redemptor no-bis ex iis extrahendis secúmque supra cœlos omnes euehendis descendere non horruit.
units.tr: Far be it from us to think that the hinge of this treatment is merely to mention the death and passion of the Lord often, or to call him Saviour. Rather we must penetrate more deeply, with fear and reverence, into the knowledge of so great a mystery, as far as God will deign to reveal it. From this we should see how great was the bitterness, in relation to his immense sufferings, of him who suffered, and from it we should draw in the great sweetness that flows over us from such great and already immense sorrows of his. Indeed I would have you forewarned of this, so that we understand that in reading and interpreting this history we must not be moved merely by bare pity or some feeling of humanity, when we understand that he who is most just of all was afflicted with such unworthy and atrocious punishments; nor should we merely detest the wicked, be angry at the Jews, curse Judas, or abhor Caiaphas and Pilate (though who could read this history without indignation?). Rather, we must be affected by a true sense of our sins, for whose expiation we see our Saviour plunged into such great and bitter anguish and nailed to the cross. We must truly repent, detest our past life, and embrace repentance from the heart. With ardent desire we must contemplate the height, breadth and depth: on the one hand, of the immense love of God, who did not spare his only-begotten Son but gave him up as the price of so precious a redemption for our sins; on the other hand, of the incomprehensible goodness of the Son of God, who loved his enemies more than himself, even unto death, yes, the death of the Cross. Finally, we should enjoy the true peace and tranquillity of conscience, since we find our paradise even in hell itself, to which that highest and only Saviour and Redeemer of men did not shrink from descending, in order to draw us out of it and carry us with him above all the heavens.

units.la: Porrò vt scopum istum ad quem colliman-dum esse diximus tanto facilius attingamus quædam prius nobis ordine capita sunt per-tractanda, ad quæ totam istam explicationem referamus. Ac primùm quidem, Quis ille fit qui passus elt. Deinde quibus causis adductus fuerit Dominus vt hanc rationem in nobis redimendis sequeretur: tum, quo respectu paf-sus dicatur, quarto, quid pro nobis passus fit: denique, quis fructus ex his omnibus perci-
units.tr: Moreover, so that we may more easily attain the goal toward which we have said we must aim, some heads must first be treated in order, to which we refer this whole explanation. First, who he is who suffered. Then, by what causes the Lord was moved to follow this plan in redeeming us. Third, in what respect he is said to have suffered. Fourth, what he suffered for us. Finally, what fruit is to be gathered from all these things.

units.tr: a. iij.

units.la: Quòd ad primum igitur attinet, quo veluti fundamento & basi reliqua niti & superstrui oporteret, vt docet Dominus, Ioh.17. hac nimirum esse vitam æternam, vt Patrem cognoscamus solum verum Deum, & eum quem misit Iesum Christum: & vt loquitur Apostolus, omnes promissiones Dei in Iesu Christo esse Etiam, & in eodem esse Amen, hoc habete: cum cuius in hac tota historia passionem memorarur, esse vnicum Dei filium, Iesum Christum, quemadmodum ex Apostolorum Symbolo, quod fidei nostræ summam complectitur, profitemur.
units.tr: As to the first point, which ought to serve as the foundation and basis on which the rest must rest and be built: the Lord teaches (John 17.3) that this is eternal life, that we know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent. And as the Apostle says, all the promises of God are in Jesus Christ, Yea, and in him Amen (2 Cor. 1.20). Hold to this: that the one whose passion is recounted in this whole history is the only Son of God, Jesus Christ, as we profess in the Apostles' Creed, which embraces the sum of our faith.

units.la: Verùm quum hic articulus maximi momenti, iam Apostolorum temporibus à Satana & variis hæreticis sit oppugnatus, tanto accuratiorem & dilucidiore à nobis etiam polulat explicationem. Quòd igitur Deitas essentia vnica est prorsus spiritualis, inuisibilis, infinita denique, alij quidem mente sua tantum mysterium non assequentes, sed illud suo sensu metientes, quum animaduerterent non nunquam Angelos, nonnunquam Magistratus, immo ipsos etiam fideles sæpe filios Dei vocari, atque adeò ipsum Israelem primogenitum Dei Filium dici, Exod.4. 22. docuerunt Iesum Christum vocari Deum, nó quòd Deus esset illa essentiali Deitate, sed propter excellentiam qua longè res creatas omnes antecellit. Alij non minori errore implicati, sed alio diuerticulo à vero aberrantes, agnouerunt quiquidem & fafli sunt essentialem Iesu Chri- sti Deitatem , humanitatem vero sic op- pugnarunt,vt alferetent, sic Dei filium forma humana fe hominibus conspicuum praebuif- fe,vt fe illis familiarius communicaret, vt vi- demus saepe Deum & Angelos variis formis apparuifle, reuera autem naturam humanam & essentialem non habuisse. Vtraque autem haec haeresis quum infinitis pene expressis tum Veteris tum Noui Testamenti locis refellatur, iam pridem est explosa, & anathemate dam- nata,non vt simplex aliqu is error, sed tanquam erronea doctrina qua fidei & spei salutis no- ftrae fundamenta penitus conuellantur , vti paulo post dicturi fumus. Ab hac autem vtra- que velut arce depulsus Satan , duplici tamen alia diuersa via huius articuli veritatem ag- gressus est, excitatis hominibus qui Deitatem & Humanitatem essentialem Christi fatceren- tur quidem , sed mixtionem & confusionem tum essentiarum tum naturalium proprieta- tum vtriusque naturae inducerent:Contra etiam aliis qui pro illa mixtione & confusione tum essentiarum,tum proprietatum,fepatationem earundem imaginarentur, docerentque Dei- tatem, praesertim a Christi baptismo,sic Chri- sto homini vt Prophetis, aut aliis viris prae- stantibus adfuisse, quanuis peculiari quadam & excellentiori virtute, cuius ratione Dei no- men illi datum fit:quas abominandas haereses Oecumenica & orthodoxa concilia iampri- dem ex puro Dei verbo redarguerunt & anathemate ferierunt.
units.tr: But since this article of the highest importance was already assailed by Satan and various heretics in the times of the Apostles, it requires a more accurate and clearer explanation. Some, because the divine essence is one, altogether spiritual, invisible and infinite, and because they did not grasp this mystery with their mind but measured it by their own sense, noticed that angels, sometimes magistrates, and even the faithful themselves are often called sons of God, and that Israel himself is called God's firstborn son (Exod. 4.22). They therefore taught that Jesus Christ is called God not because he was God in essential Deity, but on account of the excellence by which he far surpasses all created things. Others, entangled in an error no smaller, but straying from the truth by another byway, acknowledged and confessed the essential Deity of Jesus Christ, yet so attacked his humanity that they asserted that the Son of God showed himself to men in human form, so that he might communicate with them more familiarly. We often see God and angels appear in various forms, while in truth he had no real and essential human nature. Both of these heresies, though refuted by almost endless express passages of both Old and New Testaments, were long ago exploded and condemned with anathema. They were condemned not as a simple error but as a false doctrine by which the foundations of our faith, hope and salvation are utterly overthrown, as we shall say shortly. Satan, driven from this stronghold on both sides, nevertheless attacked the truth of this article by another, double, and different way. He stirred up men who confessed indeed the Deity and essential humanity of Christ, but introduced a mixture and confusion both of the essences and of the natural properties of each nature. On the other hand, he stirred up others who, in place of that mixture and confusion of essences and properties, imagined a separation of them, and taught that the Deity was present to Christ the man, especially from his baptism, just as it was present to the Prophets or other excellent men, though with a peculiar and more excellent virtue, by reason of which the name of God was given to him. These abominable heresies the ecumenical and orthodox councils long ago refuted from the pure Word of God and struck with anathema.

units.la: Ecquis vero non videt, si qua ex istis haeresibus admittatur, salutis nostrae fundamenta radicitus convelli? Nam, ut de harum blasphemarum & portentosarum haereseon priore dicam, si Christus est φιλὸς ἀνθρωπος, & creatura tantum, quantumuis excellentem & eximiis ornatam dotibus dicas, idololatrae tamen necessario dicendi quotquot in illo spem suam collocant, & cum invocant. Nec vero potest ille nobis peccata condonare, nec mortua corpora suscitare, nec vitam aeternam dare, quum haec sint essentiae uni divinae sic propria, ut ea sei vlli creatae communicari sit nefas. Age vero, nisi Deus esset Christus, quomodo in eius nomen non secus quam in Patris & Sp. S. baptizaremur? quomodo filius unicus Dei appellaretur? quomodo ante res omnes creatas fuisse, & ante omnia saecula extitisse diceretur? Ioh. 1.3. qua ratione si nihil nisi mera creatura fuisset, potuisset iram Dei Creatoris sui sustinere quin ab ea prorsus absorberetur? quomodo seipsum a mortuis excitasset? quo denique pacto noster Iesus, id est Seruator esset?
units.tr: Who does not see that, if any of these heresies is admitted, the foundations of our salvation are torn up by the roots? For, to speak first of the former of these blasphemous and monstrous heresies: if Christ is a mere man [ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος] and only a creature, however excellent and endowed with outstanding gifts you call him, then all who place their hope in him and call upon him must necessarily be called idolaters. Nor can he forgive us our sins, raise the dead, or give eternal life, since these belong so properly to the one divine essence that to communicate them to any created being is wicked. Come now: unless Christ were God, how should we be baptized into his name no less than into that of the Father and the Holy Spirit? How should he be called the only Son of God? How could it be said that he existed before all created things and before all ages? (John 1:3) On the other hand, if he had been nothing but a creature, could he have borne the wrath of God his Creator without being utterly swallowed up by it? How could he have raised himself from the dead? In short, how could our Jesus, that is, our Saviour, be who he is?

units.la: Ad secundam haeresin accedo, aióq; si Christus, nostra natura in specie tantum induit, non autem revera humanitatem assumpsit, nos adhuc Dei maledictioni obnoxios esse: & eius perpessiones fictas & ludicras fuisse, ac proinde totu nostrae redemptionis opus imaginarium & inane. Idem etiam de tertia illa haeresi iudicium esto, qua Deitas varia & mutabilis & in seipsa immuniimminuta redditur: humana vero natura in tanta effertur dignitate vt in Deitate transmutetur: vnde sequitur Christum nec esse verum Deum, nec verum hominem, sed tertia quandam essentiam ex duarum illarum coniunctione & mixtione conflatam. Apagesis igitur blasphemium & portentosum dogma, quo nobis prorsus inutilis Christus proponitur, indigno longiore refutatione, licet eius veneno multos homines imbutos infelix Monachus deceperit.
units.tr: I come to the second heresy. If Christ took on our nature only in appearance, and did not in truth assume humanity, then we would still be liable to God's curse; his sufferings would have been feigned and mocking, and therefore the whole work of our redemption would be imaginary and empty. The same judgement is to be passed on that third heresy, in which the Deity is made varied and changeable and diminished in itself, while human nature is so exalted in dignity that it is transformed into the Deity. From this it follows that Christ is neither true God nor true man, but a third kind of essence compounded from the joining and mixing of those two. Away, then, with this blasphemous and monstrous dogma, by which Christ is presented to us as wholly useless. It does not deserve a lengthy refutation, although the unhappy monk has deceived many people imbued with its poison.

units.la: Superest quarta blasphemia, qua posita duos Filios poni esset necesse, alterum nimirum separatim Dei filium: alterum vero Mariae Virginis etiam separatim filium: quorum neuter esset separatim Seruator noster: quum tamen Deitas non seruet nos aliter quam per satisfactionem Humanitatis: & viciflim Humanae naturae perpessiones non aliunde nos viuificandi vim accipiant quam a Deitate, cum qua inseparabiliter est coniuncta & vnita, vt copiosius paulo post dicturi sumus.
units.tr: There remains a fourth blasphemy. If it were posited, it would be necessary to posit two Sons: one, of course, the Son of God separately, and the other the Son of the Virgin Mary, also separately. Neither of them would separately be our Saviour, since the Deity does not save us except through the satisfaction of the humanity, and conversely the sufferings of human nature do not receive their power to make us alive from anywhere but the Deity, with which it is inseparably joined and united, as we shall say more fully a little later.

units.la: Omnibus illis igitur impuris & abominadis blasphemiis hac vnica pura & simplice veritate opponetes, ingenue profitearmur, Solum & vnicum Dei Filium cum Patre & Sp.S. coaeternum & coessentiale, secunda Trinitatis persona (sunt enim in vna Trinitate personae tres vnusidemque Deus, minime illae quidem diuisae sua essentia, sed distinctae tamen suis proprietatibus hypostaticis) hanc, inquam, secundam personam ex Dei patris voluntate, per operationem Sancti Spiritus, tempore diuinitus praestituto, & a Prophetis multis ante seculis prædicto, nostram humanam naturam nn fibiaf sumpsisse & vniuiiffe,&eam quidem vere vero coe pore constantem ex Marię Virginis fubib bftanti conflato,veráque etiam anima humanaiaa purif- fima sanctissimáque,& quidem tam ardádto vin- culo , vt vnaquaque natura suam effentiatiam & proprietates suas essentiales retinente s s fine vl- la confusione,verus Deus fit,vt erat antetetequam humanitatem affumeret, idémque verærrus ho- mo nobis in omnibus excepto peccato o o factus simillimus , siquidem corpus eius ex t f sanctæ Virginis substantia factum & formatummm est:ac proinde, verum Deum & verum homiiinem in vnitate personæ permanere, (cuius doooctrinæ testimonia sumus in hac potissimum hiiiistoria si vspiam alibi maximè conspicua & exxxpressa visuri,)vt ita nobis ille, Sapietia, Iustitiiaa,San- ctificatio & Redeptio fiat, sicut docet / AApost, 1. Cor.1.30. Vt igitur ad propositam quaaaæstio- nem reuertamur,ille,cuius hæ fune perpppessio- nes, vnicus est Filius Dei , qui natura nooo stram assumpsit vt in ca noster apud Deum P?atrem vas atque sponsor fieret, & abfoluriffimaúu tum in anima tum in corpore pretium redemnpptio- nis. Quæ verò mens , aut quis Intelle&tuus , ne Angelicus quidem assequatur,aut quæ lli ingua efferat tantum hoc incarnationis & vrnnionis hypostaticæ mysterium , eius , qui quunmm esset in forma Dei fine rapina, id est verus & cessen- tialis Deus , sic formam serui assumsit ,, ı id est naturam nostram veram & essentialem ,, vt se exinaniuerit vsque ad mortem, mortemm autem crucis? Quis, inquam, mente humana capiat, qui fieri hoc potuerit, vt æternus Dei filius, voluerit Adami filius fieri, & in Virginis vtero concipi, vix adhuc elapsis mille sexcentis amis ex quo infinitus, finito, Creator, creatura, nuifibilis, visibili: Omnipotens omnium hominũ abiectissimo, Vita denique sese morti vniuit & coniunxit? O ingens mysterium, vel ipsis Angelis incomprehensum & plus quàm admirandum: vt ipse docet Apostolus. 1. Tim. 3.16. & Ephes. 3. 18. mysterium quod non caro & sanguis, sed ipse nobis pater revelat. Matth. 16. 17. per Filium qui est in sinu patris, Ioh. 1. 18. vt de venit vt nobis ipsemet illud patefaceret, Rom. 16.25. sicut loquutus erat per os sanctorum qui à seculo fuerunt Prophetarum suorum, Luc. 1.70. & 1. Pet. 1.11. & 2. Pet. 1.21.
units.tr: Opposing all those impure and abominable blasphemies with this one pure and simple truth, we openly profess that the only and unique Son of God, coeternal and coessential with the Father and the Holy Spirit, the second person of the Trinity (for in the one Trinity there are three persons, one and the same God, by no means divided in their essence, yet distinguished by their hypostatic properties), this second person, I say, by the will of God the Father, through the operation of the Holy Spirit, at the time divinely appointed and foretold by many Prophets long before, assumed and united to himself our human nature. He did so in such a way that it is truly a body consisting of real flesh, formed from the substance of the Virgin Mary, and also a true human soul, most pure and most holy. And he did so with such a close bond that each nature retains its own essence and its essential properties, without any confusion, so that he is true God, as he was before he assumed humanity, and likewise became for us in all things, sin excepted, a true man most like us, since his body was made and formed from the substance of the holy Virgin. Therefore, true God and true man remain in the unity of one person (we shall see the testimonies of this doctrine most clearly expressed in this history, if anywhere else), so that he becomes for us wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption, as the Apostle teaches (1 Cor. 1:30). To return, then, to the question proposed: he whose these sufferings are is the only Son of God, who took our nature so that in it he might become our surety and bondsman before God the Father, and the most complete price of redemption both in soul and in body. But what mind, what intellect, not even an angelic one, can grasp, or what tongue can express, this mystery of the incarnation and the hypostatic union: that he who, being in the form of God without robbery, that is, being true and essential God, thus took the form of a servant, that is, our true and essential nature, so that he emptied himself even unto death, the death of the cross (Phil. 2:6–8)? Who, I say, can grasp with the human mind how this could come to pass: that the eternal Son of God willed to become a son of Adam, and to be conceived in the womb of a Virgin, scarcely more than sixteen hundred years having elapsed since the world was created? That the infinite should be made finite, the Creator a creature, the invisible visible, the Almighty made the most abject of all men, and finally Life itself joined and united itself to death? O immense mystery, incomprehensible even to the angels and more than admirable, as the Apostle himself teaches (1 Tim. 3:16; Eph. 3:18), a mystery which flesh and blood did not reveal to us, but the Father himself (Matt. 16:17), through the Son who is in the bosom of the Father (John 1:18), who came to make it known to us himself (Rom. 16:25), as he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets who have been since the world began (Luke 1:70; 1 Pet. 1:11; 2 Pet. 1:21).

units.la: Accedo iam ad secundum caput, ad causas primum perscrutandas quibus Pater vt Filium suum nobis daret adductus sit, filius vero tanta nos charitate complecteretur, vt sefipsum morti pro nobis traderet, Spir. verò S. tum hanc Incarnationem perficeret, tum praetiosam istam veritatem nobis patefaceret. Sed quasego hic causas vel possum vel debeo perscrutari alias quàm ipsius Dei egregiam in nos voluntatem, infinitam sapientiam, immensam bonitatem, denique profundissimam vnius Dei miserationum abyssum, qua Pater adductus tale de nobis decretum faceret, Filius vero & Spiritus S. illud exequerentur pari voluntate, quum eorum vna sit, & eadem essentia, operationes autem indiuisç ac infepambi-les. Nam quid, obsecro, vel intus vel foris inerrat in homine, quo Creatorem suum Creatura demereretur & sibi deuinciret, licet in priore illa in qua fuerat condita dignitate periti-tisset: quandoquidem conformitas illa quę inter Deum & eius imaginem erat, qua Deo gratus erat præ reliquis omnibus rebus terrenis creatis, non aliunde quàm ab eadem eius bonitate promanabat, qua sola impellente ipsum hominem prius ad suam imaginem crearat & condiderat? Posteaquam vero homo, ingrato animo & spontanea voluntate, imaginem illam ad quam à Deo fuerat conditus, ita fœdauit & deturpauit, vt quum ante illam deformationem Deus Creator nihil nisi sibi gratum & acceptum in homine conspiceret, iam vero vice versa nihil nisi abominandum & quod iram aduersus illum prouocet offendat, quis absque insigni mendacio dixerit Deum aliquid vidisse aut præuidisse in tam deformi & modis omnibus deturpata creatura quod eius sauorem & benevolentiam illi conciliaret, ac non contrà potius ad hominem perdendum prouocaret? Nam, obsecro, quinam humani ingenij tenebræ, voluntatis prauitas, & modis omnibus miserandi corporis sordes, Lucem illam immensam, Bonitatem & Puritatem in sui amorem pellexissent? amorem, inquam, illum ineffabilem quo tam arcto sibi Deus hominem vinculo coniunxit, vt in Filij persona, per admirandam illam hypostaticam vnionem,de qua suprà mentione feeimus,humana natura ad sui Creatoris imagine nó mo do perfectissime fuisse redintegrata & instaurata,sed etiam Homo ille verus,solus,coëssentialis & coæternus filius Dei factus fuisse vere dici possit & debeat? Caue autè putes humanâ nostram naturâ in illo solo ad tantâ gloriam supra omnes Angelos vsq; ad dextrâ patris evectam fuisse, Phil.2.9. quùm eam gloriâ velit ipse communicare cum iis omnibus qui in ipsum insiti corpus illud mysticû efficiût,quod est Ecclesię.cuius caput est Christus,vt fiant vnusquisque pro sua mensura æternę illius hęreditatis & gloriæ coheredes. Eph.4.16.&5.30. Nam & hoc ipse Patrem rogauit. Iohan.17.24. & talis est vltimi iudicij forma futura. Matth.25.34. quam etiam ob causam Iesus Christus ab Apostolo Filius primogenitus inter plurimos fratres nun cupatur. Rom.8.28. Et iam spe cum eo in locis cœlestibus colloca ti sumus. Eph.2 6. tantisper exspectantes dum id quod sumus apparuerit. 1. Iohan.3.2. Quid igitur ad hæc tanta mysteria, fratres, dicturi sumus, nisi quòd hic nobis arcanum arcanorum Dei revelatur? hic immensæ ipsius & plus quàm admirandæ bonitatis secreta patefiunt, cuius causam reperit in se vno is qui sibi soli merito Custodis hominum nomen vindicat? Iob.7.20. 1. Timoth.4.2. Hac igitur impul- sus est sola charitate tanta vt suos etiam inimicos complecteretur, Roman.6.8. vt ad eos redimendos Filio vnigenito suo non
units.tr: I now come to the second chapter, to examine first the causes which moved the Father to give us his Son, and moved the Son to embrace us with such love that he delivered himself to death for us, while the Holy Spirit both accomplished this incarnation and revealed to us this precious truth. But what causes could I or should I investigate here, other than God's own outstanding will towards us, his infinite wisdom, his immense goodness, and finally the most profound abyss of the mercies of the one God, by which the Father, moved, made such a decree concerning us, and the Son and the Holy Spirit carried it out with equal will, since their will is one and the same essence, and their operations are undivided and inseparable? For what, I beg you, whether within or without, could there be in man by which the creature might deserve and bind to itself its Creator, even though it had perished from that dignity in which it had been created? For that conformity which existed between God and his image, by which man was pleasing to God above all the other earthly created things, flowed from nothing other than that same goodness of his, which alone moved him to create and form man first in his own image. But after man, with an ungrateful mind and of his own free will, so defiled and disfigured that image to which he had been made by God, that whereas before that deformation God the Creator saw nothing in man but what was pleasing and acceptable to him, now, on the contrary, he sees nothing but what is abominable and what provokes his anger against him and offends him, who, without a notable lie, could say that God saw or foresaw anything in such a deformed creature, and one defiled in every way, that might win him his favour and goodwill, and not rather provoke him to destroy man? For, I ask you, what darkness of the human mind, what perversity of the will, what filth of a body wretched in every way, could have enticed that immense Light, Goodness and Purity into love of itself? I mean that ineffable love by which God joined man to himself with so close a bond, that in the person of the Son, through that admirable hypostatic union of which we have spoken above, human nature was not only restored and renewed most perfectly to the image of its Creator, but that man himself could truly be said and ought to be said to have been made the true, only, coessential and coeternal Son of God. Do not think, however, that our human nature was raised in him alone to such glory, above all the angels, even to the right hand of the Father (Phil. 2:9), when he wills to share that glory with all those who, grafted into him, form that mystical body which is the Church, of which Christ is the head, so that each one, according to his measure, may become a co-heir of that eternal inheritance and glory (Eph. 4:16; 5:30). For this very thing he asked of the Father (John 17:24), and such will be the form of the last judgement (Matt. 25:34). For this reason too the Apostle calls Jesus Christ the firstborn among many brethren (Rom. 8:29). And already in hope we are seated with him in the heavenly places (Eph. 2:6), waiting until what we shall be is revealed (1 John 3:2). What, then, brethren, shall we say to these great mysteries, except that here the secret of God's secrets is revealed to us? Here the secrets of his immense and more than admirable goodness are laid open, whose cause he found in himself alone, he who alone rightly claims for himself the name of Keeper of men (Job 7:20; 1 Tim. 4:10)? Impelled by this love alone, so great that he embraced even his enemies (Rom. 5:8), he did not only not spare his only-begotten Son to redeem them (Rom. 8:32; John 3:16),

units.la: modò non pepercerit, Rom.8.33.Ioh.3.16. sed etiam aduersus ipsorum inimicos ira vehementi exarserit, & aduersus eos causam ipsorum tutatus sit.Isa.37.32.& Zach.8.2. omnium peccatorum oblitus quibus eius iram exacerbarant, & contra foederis illius memor, quod sancitum est fore vt benedicat Abrahami seminì benedicentibus, & maledicentibus maledicat?Genes.12.3. Filium verò vnicum illum Dei,obsecro, quæ tandem impulit causa vt seipsum formam serui assumens sic exinanirer. Phil.2.7. vt ab hominibus neglectus & reiectus; propter delicta nostra vulneraretur,&ob iniquitates nostras atteretur, & in se vnum omnium nostrum iniquitatem deriuaret? Esa.53.3.& seq. Quo,inquam, impulsore; se ipsum eousque demisit vt in nostra quam assumpsit carne, non homo sed vermis haberetur? Psal.22.7. immò, quod longè maius est pro nobis κατάρα & maledictio fieret, nisi æterno illo Patris decreto & beneplacito, & eadem illa inenarrabili etiam erga eos à quibus in crucem tollebatur dilectione? Luc.23.3. Annon eadem illa charitate commotus est misericordia super populo dissipato & disiecto, & Pastorem non habente?Matth.9.36. & super Hierosolymatempus visitationis suæ non agnoscente? Luc.19.44. Quid de Spiritu S.dicam,per quem Pater & Filius tanquam per coëssentialem & coæternam suam potentiam totum hoc mysterium operati sunt? Nimirum eadem causa dicam adductum ad nos regenerandos, Ioh.3.6.do6.docendos,Ioh.16.13. consolandos. Ioh.14.& 15.& 16. immò etiam sic subleuandos in infir- mitatibus, vt ipse Spiritus in corda nostra immittat suspiria inenarrabilia. Rom. 8.25. & os aperiat, vt cum omni fiducia clamemus ad Deum, Abba,id est Pater. Vt rem igitur totam in pauca conferam, tenete animis, totum redemptionis nostrae mysterium ab vnius Dei Patris, Filij & Sp.S.charitate profectum esse, cuius fuerit obiectum, hominis modis omnibus miseranda conditio, qua Deus ad misericordiam commotus est. Euge verò, qui fieri hoc potuit, quum miseria in quam inciderunt homines à peccato sit, quo iustus Dei furor aduersus eos potius quàm fauor excitatur? Sola nimirum egregia in nos eius voluntas id effecit, testatam hac in re faciens omnibus plus quàm immensam suam sapientiam, eo quod in nobis miserrimum illum & deploratissimum statum in quo iacebamus intueri maluit & miserari, quàm illius causam spectare, putà iniquitates nostras, de quibus seuerissimas à nostro vade & sponsore, Domino nostro Iesu Christo poenas exegit, qui solus tanto par fuit oneri ferendo, vt sub illo non fatiscere t. Erat enim non tantum homo, sed verus etiam Deus omnipotens. Vt igitur quod reseft eloquamur, fratres, non Satan, non Iudas ille prodi- tor, non Caiaphas, non Iudæi, non Pilatus, non denique carnifices illi, qui cruci affixerunt cum qui de vindice & vltore scelerum factus est sceleratorum Seruator & Redemptor, tam sunt accusandi, quàm nos ipsi. Nos enim, fra-tres, nos inquam ij sumus qui tâ multis modis indigne cruciandi, vinciendum & ligandum, qui tanquam blasphemum, reúmque læsæ ma-iestatis, tum humanæ tum diuinæ condemnâ-dum, qui irridendum, colaphis & virgis cæ-dendum, crucifigendum, perfodiendum tradi-dimus, qui denique ad mortem crudelissimam & summa cum ignominia atque adeò cum i-psa Dei maledictione. Deut.21.23. Gal.3.13. con-iunctam impulimus: & in ipsas denique se-pulchri cauernas detrusimus. Merito quidem igitur Satanam, & quotquot ad nefarium illud perpetrandum flagitium satellites adhibuit, damnamus, cuius etiam scimus illos pœnas quàm cumulatissimè daturos quum olim eum quem confixerunt in throno gloriæ suæ se-dentem conspecturi sunt: Zachar.12.10. & Ioh. 19.39. Verùm ne sic ipsi succenseamus, quin e-tiam aduersus nos ipsos ira incendamur: quin peccata & iniquitates nostras abominari de-testemur, quin ingratum animum nostrum contumaciam & stuporem vt par est agnoscé-tes, ad ipsos inferos vsque deiiciamur, & in no-bis nihil nisi summopere pudendum intuen-tes, serio pœnitentiæ sensu tangamur, miseriâ nostram in illo crucifixo contemplati, non au-tem peccatorum illecebris decepti, quibusta-men nos iste mundus iniquitatis nimium proh dolor! fascinare consueuit. Porrò, fratres, oro vos & obtestor vt me patienter feratis admo-nentem, nullam hodie Gentem magis hac in-digere digere doctrina, quàm populum Genevensem: nullúmque esse populum cui maior incumbat cura seriò de se cogitandi, gemendi: & votis assiduis à Deo spiritum illum demissum & contritum postulandi, quam esse primam verae poenitentiae partem, vel ipse Propheta testatur. Psal. 51.19. Vtinam igitur, atque vtinam hac vobis mentem Deus Opt. Max. largiatur. Nam in quos, obsecro, melius & convenientius quàm in nos populum Genevensem quadrat illa Dei per Prophetam Mich. 6. 3. grauis querimonia, Popule mi, quid feci tibi? & quo fatigaui te? te-stificare contra me. Quum educens te è terra Ægypti, & domo servorum redemisssem te, & praemisissem tibi Mosen & Aaronem. Quae fuit enim Ægyptus illa ex cuius immensa servitute in libertatem asserti sumus? quos Moses, quos Aarones libertatis vindices ipse Deus excitatos misit: quàm fuit abominandum scortum illud Babylonicum, cuius illecebris erepti sumus? quàm immensum mare persecutionum euasimus? Vos vero nominatim appello fratres, quos ex tot nationum cloacis & lupanaribus extractos virgula divina huc non per defectum aliquod maceratos, sed recta in terram Gosen deduxit, veris ipsius deliciis affluentem, & in qua nobis etiam ad voluptatem quae ad victum cultúmque corporis pertinent, affatim suppeditantur, quanta sunt, inquam, quámque admiranda illa in nos Dei beneficia? Quid interim putamus Dominum in hac à se tam diligenter exculta vinea aliud quàm labrusca s & acerbissimos amarissimósque fructus esse re-perturum, hoc præsertim tempore quo vide-tur, siquis inest nobis sensus, si aures ad audie-dum, satis apertis indiciis ostendere, sepost longam patientiam qua nos tolerauit ad vin-demiam accessisse, minimè quidem, (nisi me-liorem mentem induamus) vinitoria falce v-uas colleƈturum, vinum optimum ex iis ex-pressurum, sed gladio semel vites amputaturū. Quem quum videamus illū iam ardete dextra, non eminus vt antea, sed in omnium nostrum oculis sub ipsa nostra mœnia vibrare, an vs-que adeo obsurdescimus, vt & vociferantem, & monentem quæ quondam aduersus dileƈtâ suam ciuitatem vociferatus tandem etiam per-fecit iudicia non audiamus, sic frustra Do-mino per Prophetam Esa. 5. 3. ciues Hierufal. increpante, Nunc autem habitatores Icrus-chalaimorum, imò viri Iehudæ singuli, iudi-cate quæso inter me & vineam meam. Quid faciendum amplius fuerit vineæ meæ quod non fecerim in ea. Quamobrem quum expe-ƈtassem vt ederet vuas, edidit labruscas? Iam i-taque notum faciam nunc vobis quid fa-ƈturus sim vineæ meæ: amouebo sepem eius vt sit depastioni, disrumpam maceriam eius vt sit conculcationi: Et exponam eam desolationi: non putabitur, neque resarrietur, sed assurget sentis & vepres: insuper nubibus interdicam, ne demittant in eam pluuiam. Agnoscamus, igitur fratres, agnoscamus, inquam, nostra culpa faƈtum vt in hanc vineam apri irrum-perent perent Psal. 80. 14. Deum his verbis deprecemur, O Deus exercituum conuertere, obsecro, respice de cœlis, vide & visita tuam istam vineam. Sed, quos apros hanc vineam ingressos & late depopulatos dicemus? Nimirum, auaritiam, diffidentiam, gulæ immensitatem, scortationem, perfidiam, iniustitiam, superbiam, arrogantiam, cædes, denique quotquot fructus rebellionis à carne producuntur, quos recenset Apostolus Gal. 5. v.19. & seq. etsi nos Dominus & monere & hortari non destitit, & castigare etiam tanta quidem huc usque cum lenitate, ut immensa ipsius misericordia, longe iudiciorum severitatem superarit. Quousque tandem igitur Christum Dominum nostrum crucifigere non desinemus? quousque tandem eius abusi patientia, nostri similes parum cutabimus quæ sint maximæ partis terrarum, quā ausim dicere in Geneuefem populū oculos coniicere, futura de nobis iudicia? Quòd si mortales, si etiam nostra ipsorum conscientia nos condemnat, quale futurum putamus eius iudicium, qui solio alto suo insidens, corde nostro longe maior est? 1. Ioh. 3. 20. & quem iamiam paratum esse ad decreti sui aduersus nos promulgationem aspicimus, quale olim aduersus ficum illam sterilem pronunciauit, Luc. 13. 7. quum præsertim non vnum aut alterum, sed permultos iam annos, summa cum patientia nos ad pœnitentiam hortatus, à nobis fructus aliquos expectarit? Quando, inquam, nos pudebit nostri, & ad mentem meliorem reuersi nostri misereri incipiemus? de-nique quando sincerè colere discemus eum cuius egregiæ in nos voluntatis & beneuolentiæ, tot támque illustria sunt testimonia,& eũ venerari coram Maiestate cuius ipsi Angeli vultú operiunt?Isa.6.Faxit Deus ille Opt.Max. fratres, vt primo quoque tempore nos ad id accingamus, ne nobis procrastinantibus, & nullum crebris admonitionibus locum dantibus, vt solemus, licet nos etiam crebris miraculis à Deo in nostrum fauorem editis satis prouocemur, tandem occlusa ianua, responsum istud auferamus quod describit Matth. 7. 23.Non noui vos, discedite à me omnes qui facitis iniquitatē. Tu verò Deus Optime secundū immensam tuam misericordiam hoc à nobis malum auerte: largire verò potiùs vt seria & sincera dućti pœnitentia chirographum peccatorum nostrorum aduersus nos, laceratum ac deletū,& cruci affixū Domini nostri,Col.2. remissionémque peccatorum nostrorū ipsius scriptam & obsignatam sanguine,ad nóminis tui gloriam,& tuorum omnium consolationem vi-deamus & sen-tiamus.
units.tr: Not only did he not spare his only-begotten Son (Rom. 8:33; John 3:16), but he also burned with fierce anger against their enemies and took up their cause against them (Isa. 37:32; Zech. 8:2). Did he forget all the sins by which they provoked his anger, and did he not remember that covenant, sworn to Abraham's seed, that he would bless those who bless them and curse those who curse them (Gen. 12:3)? And that only Son of God, I beg you, what finally moved him to take the form of a servant and empty himself in this way (Phil. 2:7), so that, neglected and rejected by men, he was wounded for our transgressions and crushed for our iniquities, and laid upon himself alone the iniquity of us all (Isa. 53:3ff.)? By what impulse, I ask, did he humble himself so far that in the flesh he assumed he was regarded not as a man but as a worm (Ps. 22:7)? Indeed, what is far more, he became a curse [κατάρα] and a malediction for us, had it not been for that eternal decree and purpose of the Father, and for that same inexpressible love even toward those by whom he was lifted up on the cross (Luke 23:34)? Was he not moved by that same love with compassion for the people scattered and dispersed, having no shepherd (Matt. 9:36), and for Jerusalem, which did not recognise the time of its visitation (Luke 19:44)? What shall I say of the Holy Spirit, through whom the Father and the Son worked this whole mystery, as through their co-essential and co-eternal power? Surely by the same cause, I say, he is brought to regenerate us (John 3:6), to teach us (John 16:13), to comfort us (John 14–16), and even to be so present to us in our weaknesses that the Spirit himself breathes into our hearts unutterable groanings (Rom. 8:25) and opens our mouth, so that we may cry out to God with all confidence, "Abba," that is, Father. To sum up the whole matter in a few words, hold this in your minds: the whole mystery of our redemption proceeded from the love of the one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and its object was the human condition, wretched in every way, which moved God to mercy. But how could this come about, since the misery into which men have fallen through sin ought rather to have aroused the just fury of God against them than his favour? Surely his singular will toward us alone brought this about, making his more than immense wisdom known to all in this matter, in that he preferred to look upon and pity us in the most wretched and utterly hopeless state in which we lay, rather than to regard the cause of it, namely our iniquities, for which he exacted the most severe penalties from our surety and guarantor, our Lord Jesus Christ, who alone was equal to bearing so great a burden that under it he did not faint. For he was not only a man but also true and almighty God. Therefore, to speak what is right, brothers, Satan, that traitor Judas, Caiaphas, the Jews, Pilate, and finally those executioners who fixed him to the cross, are not to be accused any more than we ourselves, for he who was made the avenger and punisher of sins has become the Saviour and Redeemer of sinners. For it is we, brothers, I say it is we, who have brought it about that he should be tormented in so many unworthy ways, bound and tied, handed over as a blasphemer and a traitor to majesty, condemned both by human and by divine law, mocked, struck with fists and rods, crucified, pierced through, and finally driven to a most cruel death, with the greatest disgrace and joined even with God's own curse (Deut. 21:23; Gal. 3:13), and at last thrust into the very caves of the tomb. Rightly, indeed, we condemn Satan, and all the satellites whom he employed to commit that wicked crime, and we know that they will pay the penalties in full when they shall look upon him whom they pierced, sitting on the throne of his glory (Zech. 12:10; John 19:37). But lest we merely rage against them, and not also be kindled with anger against ourselves; lest we fail to abhor our sins and iniquities, and to confess, as is fitting, our ungrateful mind, our obstinacy and our stupor; lest we be cast down even to the depths, and, seeing in ourselves nothing but what is most shameful, be seriously moved by a sense of repentance, contemplating our misery in that crucified One, and not be deceived by the allurements of sins, with which, alas, this world is wont too much to bewitch us. Moreover, brothers, I beg and entreat you to bear patiently with me admonishing you that no nation today has more need of this doctrine than the people of Geneva, and that there is no people to whom greater care falls of thinking seriously about themselves and mourning, and of asking God with constant prayers for that spirit of contrition and humility, which the Prophet himself testifies is the first part of true repentance (Ps. 51:19). Would that, then, God Most Good and Great may grant this mind to you! For upon whom, I ask, does that grave complaint of God through the Prophet Micah 6:3 fit better and more fittingly than upon us, the people of Geneva: "My people, what have I done to you, and how have I wearied you? Testify against me. When I led you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of servants, and sent before you Moses and Aaron"? For what was that Egypt from whose immense servitude we have been claimed for liberty? Whom did God himself send, raised up as deliverers of liberty, Moses and Aaron? How abominable was that Babylonian harlot by whose allurements we were snatched away? What immense sea of persecutions have we escaped? But I address you by name, brothers, whom the divine rod drew out of so many sewers and brothels of nations, and led straight, not in any want, but into the land of Goshen, flowing with its true delights, where all the things that pertain to food and bodily care for our pleasure are supplied in abundance: how great, I say, and how admirable are those benefits of God toward us! Meanwhile, what do we think the Lord will find in this vineyard, which he has so diligently tended, but wild grapes and the most bitter and sour fruits? Especially at this time, when it appears, if any sense is in us and if our ears are open to hearing, to show by sufficiently clear signs that after the long patience with which he has borne with us, he has come to the vintage. Surely, unless we put on a better mind, he will not gather the grapes with the pruning-hook, nor press from them the best wine, but will cut down the vines once for all with the sword. Since we see him now brandishing that sword in his right hand, not from afar as before, but in the sight of all of us, right under our walls, can we be so deaf that we do not hear him crying out and warning us, and that we do not hear the judgments which he once pronounced against his beloved city, and finally carried out? Thus in vain the Lord rebukes through the Prophet Isaiah 5:3 the citizens of Jerusalem: "Now, then, inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, between me and my vineyard. What more was there to do for my vineyard that I did not do in it? Why, when I looked for it to bring forth grapes, did it bring forth wild grapes? And now I will make known to you what I will do to my vineyard: I will remove its hedge, that it may be grazed, and break down its wall, that it may be trodden down; and I will lay it waste; it shall not be pruned or dug, but briars and thorns shall come up; I will also command the clouds not to send rain upon it." Let us acknowledge therefore, brothers, let us acknowledge, I say, that it is by our fault that the boars have broken into this vineyard (Ps. 80:14). Let us beseech God with these words: "O God of hosts, turn again, I beseech you, look down from heaven, behold and visit this your vineyard." But which boars shall we say have entered this vineyard and laid it waste far and wide? Assuredly, avarice, distrust, immoderate gluttony, fornication, treachery, injustice, pride, arrogance, murders, and in short all the fruits of rebellion that are produced by the flesh, which the Apostle lists (Gal. 5:19ff.). Although the Lord has not ceased to admonish and exhort us, and even to chastise us, hitherto with such great gentleness that his immense mercy has far surpassed the severity of his judgments. How long then shall we not cease to crucify the Lord Jesus Christ?
