units.la: Absit autem sic istud intelligamus, quasi vis vlla spiritualis intrinseca in iltius Verbi sono insit, nec etiam in additis illi signis Sacramentalibus, vt somniant magi & venefici & quotquot illos imitantur: neue in iis qui verbum illud ore proferunt, vel administrant Sacramenta: quum contrà vis in eo sita sit omnis, quòd sola Deitatis virtus coëssentialis Spiritus Sanctus reipsa perficit in nobis quod verbi sonus ad aures nostras defert, & Sacramenta sensibus offerunt. Act.3.12.1.Cor.3.7.
units.tr: Yet let no one understand this as if some spiritual power were inherent in the sound of that Word, or in the sacramental signs added to it, as magicians and sorcerers and all who imitate them dream, nor in those who utter that word with their mouths or administer the sacraments. On the contrary, all the power lies in this: that the Holy Spirit, who is of the same essence as the Deity, alone accomplishes in us, in very deed, what the sound of the word carries to our ears and what the sacraments offer to our senses (Acts 3:12; 1 Cor. 3:7).

units.la: Sed alia Domini vis est, alia seruorum. Sic enim iste Dominus fuit minister & administrator paternæ voluntatis, quatenus erat homo, & seruus in forma serui, vt ab Esa. vocatur cap. 53.1. vt tamen Filius sit in domo paterna, cui præest tanquam dominationem & imperium in ea habens. Heb.3.6.adeò vt idem qui in terris ore suo loquutus est, & intus & foris sit operatus, vt voluit per suam coëssentialem virtutem Spiritum Sanctum. Ioh.24.32. Quomodo verò verbo suo id non faceret, quum solo aspectu Petrum tam miro modo commutauerit? Matth.26.75 & solo vestimenti sui attactu tam potenter operatus sit? Matth.9.21. non quòd, vt sibi fingunt idololatræ sepulchrorum & reliquiarum veneratores, vis illa vel sono Verbi, vel aspectui, vel vestimento inesset, sed quòd ab eo virtus egrederetur tanquam Deo, per omnipotentiam sic Deitati propriam vt alteri non sit communicabilis. Longè minùs igitur Prophetæ vel Apostoli miraculum vllum ediderunt, aut vi sua aliqua intrinseca, aut natura, aut gratia. Act.3.12. sed Deo tantùm per eos operante & eousque approbante virtute & efficacia propria suorum seruorum ministerium & doctrinam quod de omnibus in genere miraculis prædicatur. Marc.16.20.
units.tr: But the power of the Lord is one thing, and the power of the servants another. For this Lord was the minister and administrator of the Father's will, insofar as he was man and a servant in the form of a servant, as he is called by Isaiah in chapter 53 (Isa. 53:1). Yet as the Son he is in the Father's house, over which he presides, having lordship and rule in it (Heb. 3:6). So the same one who spoke with his mouth on earth also worked both within and without, since he willed to work by his co-essential power, the Holy Spirit (John 18:6; 18:32). And how would he not have done this by his word, when by a look alone he changed Peter in so marvellous a way (Matt. 26:75), and by the mere touch of his garment worked so powerfully (Matt. 9:21)? This was not because, as the idolaters who worship tombs and relics imagine, that power resided in the sound of the word, or in the look, or in the garment; rather, virtue went out from him as from God, through an omnipotence so proper to the Deity that it cannot be communicated to another. Much less, therefore, did the prophets or apostles work any miracle either by some intrinsic power of their own, or by nature, or by grace (Acts 3:12). Rather, God alone worked through them, and approved their ministry and doctrine by the power and efficacy proper to his servants, as is proclaimed of all miracles in general (Mark 16:20).

units.la: Cæterum hæc Iesu Christi verba Ego sum, si rite expendantur summam totius verbi diuini continent. Nam quòd ad Legem, si Ceremonialem intelligimus, fuit illa pædagogi instar Patribus ad contemplandam & apprehendam in his figuris veritatis Lucem quæ in Domino nostro Iesu Christo sita est, Gal.3.24. & Hebr.10.1. Moralis verò Lex, vt nos transgressores illius occidit, addita vt ait Apostolus Transgressionum gratia. Gal.3.19. sic etiam eadem in Iesu Christo iustificat. Rom.3.30. vt qui poenam quam à nobis Lex requirebat exsoluerit. Gal.3.13. & eam perfectè quum adimplerit, in omnibus credentibus eius promissiones firmas ac ratas fecerit. 2.Cor.1.20. vt non immeritò Paulus nihil aliud scire decreuerit nec docere, nisi Iesum Christum, eumque crucifixum. 1.Cor.2.2. quam etiam ob causam proprium nomen Iesus adeptus est, id est, Seruator, Matth.1.21. & ideò etiam Iesu Christi cognitio gnitio est salutis scientia. Luc.1. 77. & vita æ- terna. Ioh.17.3 quòd nimirum, ait Petrus, habeat æternæ vitæ verba. Ioh. 6.68. quo sensu etiam ab Apostolo Euangelij doctrina vocatur Potentia Dei ad salutem, putà,potens Dei instrumentum ad salutem cuiuis credenti. Rom.1.16.
units.tr: Moreover, these words of Jesus Christ, "I am," if they are rightly weighed, contain the sum of the whole divine Word. For as to the Law, if we understand the ceremonial law, it was like a schoolmaster to the fathers, to contemplate and grasp in these figures the light of truth which lies in our Lord Jesus Christ (Gal. 3:24; Heb. 10:1). But the moral law, which kills us as its transgressors, was added, as the apostle says, "because of transgressions" (Gal. 3:19); so too it justifies in Jesus Christ (Rom. 3:30), since he paid the penalty which the Law demanded from us (Gal. 3:13), and, having perfectly fulfilled it, has made all his promises firm and valid in all believers (2 Cor. 1:20). Thus not without reason Paul decided to know and teach nothing but Jesus Christ, and him crucified (1 Cor. 2:2). For this reason too he obtained the proper name Jesus, that is, Saviour (Matt. 1:21), and therefore the knowledge of Jesus Christ is the knowledge of salvation (Luke 1:77) and eternal life (John 17:3). This is so, as Peter says, because he has "the words of eternal life" (John 6:68). In this sense too the doctrine of the Gospel is called by the apostle "the power of God unto salvation" (Rom. 1:16), that is, a powerful instrument of God for the salvation of every believer.

units.la: Ex hac probè intellecta doctrina veros Pastores, quos audiri oportet, agnoscemus, & falsos quos vitare: verum Euangelium à falso distinguemus, ac proinde verà Ecclesiam extra quam non est salus, à falsa quæ regnù est perditionis discernemus. Quum igitur verus ille fit Christus quem nobis Propheta rum & Apostolorum scripta plenè & perfectè patefaciùt, sequitur Iesum Christum aliquem mutû,qualia sunt idola illa quos Crucifixos vocant,hominum manibus formatos aut depictos, non autem Dei spiritu: quos adorant quibus verae vitæ sensus nó inest maior quàm in idolis quæ colùt,nó verum illum & vnicum Iesum Christum in Scripturis depictum & in iis loquente, Gal.3.1. sed esse ridiculum spectrum. Nec verò pro vero Christo recipiendus is est què Satan & eius ministri se in Lucis Angelos transformantes proponunt,ostentantes quidem egregia ista & mirificè iactantes,bonâ intentione, deuotionem, bona opera, humilitatè, preces, abstinentiam,eleemosynas, Patres, quibus se callidè insinuant,vt tandem sub speciosa voce Traditionum sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ latitates omnia sua deque ferant. Siquis enim penitius in rhimorum istorum inquirat arcanæ, sucum eos facere comperiet, speciosam quid em ostentantes monetam sed adulterinam, qua miseros & incautos fallant, quod sit manifestissimum quum ad verum examen, puta purum Dei verbum, & fidei nostræ articulorum essentialium perpetuam analogiam exploran-tur, quæ sunt verus ille Lydius lapis ad quem est eorum examinanda doctrina, non solla antiquitas, non consuetudo, non vllius denique quisquis ille sit autoritas, vt verus scripturarum sensus a falso discernatur. Ad hanc regulam si diligenter examinentur doctrinæ, nemo nisi volens in veroꝛum & fidelium pastorum, ac proinde verae & falsae Ecclesiae differentia decipietur.
units.tr: From this doctrine, rightly understood, we shall recognise the true ministers whom we ought to hear, and the false whom we ought to avoid. We shall distinguish the true Gospel from the false, and therefore discern the true Church, outside of which there is no salvation, from the false, which is the kingdom of perdition. Since that is the true Christ whom the writings of the prophets and apostles reveal fully and perfectly, it follows that the Jesus Christ whom they call "crucified," the images formed or painted by human hands, are mute, like those idols; they are not of the Spirit of God. Those who adore them have no more sense of true life than the idols they worship have. They do not have the true and only Jesus Christ, depicted in the Scriptures and speaking in them (Gal. 3:1); they have a ridiculous phantom. Nor is that to be received as the true Christ whom Satan and his ministers, transforming themselves into angels of light, put forward, displaying indeed these excellent and wonderfully boasted things: good intention, devotion, good works, humility, prayers, abstinence, almsgiving, and the Fathers, by which they cunningly insinuate themselves, so that at last, under the specious name of the Traditions of holy mother Church, they may hide and carry off all their goods. For if anyone searches more deeply into these hidden mysteries, he will find that they are counterfeiters: they show off a fine coin, but it is adulterated, with which they deceive the wretched and the unwary. This is most evident when they are tested by the true touchstone, namely the pure Word of God and the perpetual analogy of the essential articles of our faith. These are that true Lydian stone against which their doctrine must be examined, not antiquity, not custom, not the authority of any man whatsoever, in order to distinguish the true sense of the Scriptures from the false. If doctrines are carefully examined by this rule, no one will be deceived about the difference between true and false pastors, and so between the true and the false Church, unless he wishes to be.

units.la: Porrò vt vnde digressi sumus reuertamur, obseruandum Deo vtenti suo verbo duos contrarios effectus tribui, nempe, credentibus vitæ odorem, incredulis verò, mortis odorem.
units.tr: Now, to return to where we digressed: it should be observed that when God uses his word, two contrary effects are produced: for believers it is the fragrance of life, but for unbelievers the fragrance of death.

units.la: 2.Cor.2.15.& 16. quorum alterum, vita nempe cum omni benedictione coniuncta, verè à Christo promanat, qui nihil in se nisi vita & salus est; & verbo suo vtitur tanquam gladio, quo pertingit vsque ad diuisionem animæ simul ac spiritus Heb. 4.12. vt mortiferum vulnus infligat contumacibus, & electos vetere homine caeso, viuificet Deo: alterum verò quod ad mortis causam ἀποτελεσματικῶ ab incredulorum rebellione prorsus emanat, iustum in se Dei iudicium attrahentium atque accersentium. Hoc miseris istis accidisse videmus, qui quum in malitia occalluissent, illius virtute sunt humi prostrati, qui vt Iudex ipsos percussit, quòd nollent eum agnoscere Seruatorem, per hoc ipsum Verbum, si tanquam verum Iesum & verum Nazarenum, vt eum ipsi nominarant, essent amplexati, quod non nisi volentes & sponte,toties & tam serió moniti, poterant ignorare.Ioh.9.41. & 15.25.24.
units.tr: (2 Cor. 2:15–16), of which the first, namely life joined with every blessing, truly flows from Christ, who in himself is nothing but life and salvation; and he uses his word as a sword, by which it pierces even to the dividing of soul and spirit (Heb. 4:12), so as to inflict a deadly wound on the obstinate, and to quicken the elect, the old man having been slain, to God. The second, however, which flows entirely from the rebellion of unbelievers as its effective cause, draws down upon them and summons the just judgment of God. We see this has happened to those wretches who, having grown hardened in wickedness, were cast to the ground by the power of him who struck them as Judge, because they would not acknowledge him as Saviour. They could ignore this only if they were willing and of their own accord, having been warned so often and so earnestly, when they could have embraced him through this very Word as the true Jesus and the true Nazarene, as they themselves named him (John 9:41; 15:24–25).

units.la: Age verò, si Christus examinationis suę tempore, & quum se iudicandum vltro capientibus offerret, suos hostes etiam tâ leniter compellans verbo tamen suo tantam vim indidit, quid futurum putas, quando mundum iudicaturus in gloria & Maiestate vocem suam illam metuendam, & horrendam instar tonitru proferet, Matth.25.41. Maledicti, abite in ignem æternum qui Diabolo & Angelis eius præparatus est? Tunc quum fractra dicetur montibus & petris, Cadite super nos, abscondite nos ab eius conspectu qui insidet throno, & ab ira Agni. Apoc 6.16. Quum cœli & terra cum stridore præteribunt: 2.Pet.3.10. Ecquid verò tunc erit quo fulciantur ij qui videbunt eum quem transfixerunt, & qui non tantum humi ad momentum statim surrecturi proster nentur, sed in æternum in inferorum abyssum præcipites immergentur? Quotus verò quisque,obsecro,hęc tam seria cogitat & animaduertit, ecquis non in vtramque aurem securus dormit? quàm multi sunt ex eorum contemptorum numero de quibus agit Apostolus 2. Pet.3 4. qui suo tandem experientur periculo
units.tr: Come now, if Christ, at the time of his examination, when he offered himself to be judged by those who willingly seized him, addressed even his enemies so gently yet put such power into his word, what do you suppose will happen when he, about to judge the world in glory and majesty, utters that dreadful voice of his, terrible as thunder: "Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels" (Matt. 25:41)? Then, when it will be said in vain to the mountains and rocks, "Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him who sits on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb" (Rev. 6:16), when heaven and earth will pass away with a roar (2 Pet. 3:10), what then will there be to support those who will see him whom they pierced, and who will not merely be cast to the ground, to rise again at once for a moment, but will be plunged headlong into the abyss of hell for ever? Yet, I beg you, how few think about and take note of these serious matters? Who does not sleep soundly, careless of either ear? How many are among the number of those scoffers of whom the Apostle speaks (2 Pet. 3:4), who will at last learn by their own peril

units.la: Deum in comminationibus non minùs quàm in promissionibus veracem: qui licet Solem suum ad tempus exoriri facit super malos ac bonos Matth. 5. 45. mundi tamen aliquando iudex futurus erit, Rom. 3 6 & incautos deprehensos tandem perditurus. Luc. 17. 27. Nam qui tam sapienter Solis ortum & occasum, & anni tempestates dispouit, quomodo non etiam impiis perpetuas tenebras, suis vero Lucem praefixit? Verùm enim verò, sceleratos acccontemptores etiam multa manent intermedia iudicia, licet in ultimum illum diem summa differatur executio, quae tam quam inferorum portae sunt, quotquot nimirum aerumnas & calamitates impij sine solatio perferunt. Immo quotquot benedictionibus temporariis illos longa Dei patientia sine dono Sancti Spiritus afficit, totidem in eorum capita horrenda sua iudicia cumulat, ut ipsi proprij sui exitij fiant instrumenta. Nec iuvat eos quòd ij quorum hic fit mentio, prostrati licet, confestim viribus receptis surrexerunt. Nam, ut aiunt, e craticula in carbones inciderunt: cuius rei fidem faciunt quae post Dominum & haeredem vineae eiectum tandem ipsis evenerunt. Matth. 21. 41. Idem Pharaoni novies obdurato contigit. Idem Niniuae tandem oblitae protestationis Ionae tempore factae. Idem Babyloni sua magnitudine & mole ruenti. Idem magno illi Romano Imperio Gentium vocationem recusanti. Quid verò nobis fiet miseris abortiuis, si dicentem Ego sum,contemnere perrexerimus? Et ne longius in perquirendis veteribus historiis abeam, quibus flagellis hodie Deus maximos Monarchas exercet à Septentrione in Meridiem, & ab ortu in occasum, quòd ab annis septuaginta plus minus ad nos velut è cœlis reuersum Dominum, & clara voce Ego sum cunctis mortalibus inclamantem audire recusent? Quæ verò quotidie cernimus & intus & foris, & propè & procul rerum discrimina, & horrenda Dei in mundum vniuersum iudicia?
units.tr: that God is no less true in his threats than in his promises. Although he makes his sun rise for a time on the evil and the good (Matt. 5:45), he will one day be the judge of the world (Rom. 3:6), and will at last destroy the careless when he catches them unawares (Luke 17:27). For he who has so wisely ordered the rising and setting of the sun and the seasons of the year, how should he not also appoint perpetual darkness for the wicked and light for his own? Indeed, for the wicked and scorners many intermediate judgments remain, although the full execution is deferred to that final day. These are like the gates of hell, namely all the afflictions and calamities which the ungodly bear without consolation. Indeed, however many temporary blessings God's long patience bestows on them without the gift of the Holy Spirit, so many dreadful judgments he heaps upon their heads, so that they become the instruments of their own destruction. Nor does it help them that those of whom mention is made, though cast down, rose at once with their strength restored. For, as they say, they fell from the grill onto the coals. The truth of this is shown by what befell them afterwards, when the Lord and heir of the vineyard was cast out (Matt. 21:41). The same happened to Pharaoh, hardened nine times. The same happened to Nineveh, which at last forgot the warning given in the time of Jonah. The same happened to Babylon, falling by its own greatness and bulk. The same happened to that great Roman Empire, which refused the calling of the Gentiles. What, then, will become of us wretched abortions, if we persist in despising him who says, "I am"? And, not to go on at length searching out ancient histories: with what scourges does God today afflict the greatest monarchs, from north to south and from east to west, because for about seventy years now they refuse to hear the Lord, who has returned to us as it were from heaven, crying with a clear voice to all mortals, "I am"? And what dangers, both within and without, and near and far, which we see every day, and what dreadful judgments of God upon the whole world?

units.la: Mature igitur, fratres, metuamus horrendum iræ diem. Oramus vos Christi nomine & secundum nostram legationem, Deo reconciliamini. 2. Cor. 5. 20. Maiore in pretio quàm hactenus sacrosanctum illud Verbum habeamus, Verbum, inquam, quod aures nostras personat, & vobis prædicamus, Roman. 10. vers. 8. si in bonam terram ceciderit fructus iustitiæ prolaturum: si verò in saxa & terras steriles, aduersus easdem maledictionem quæ fert ad interitum accumulaturum. Diligenti memoria repetamus quanta cum lenitate nos verbum illud visitarit nobis parcendo, & quanta benignitate nos adhuc toleret, quantam vix pauci alij sunt experti, immo vix vlla Ecclesia in toto terrarum orbe. Quandiu itaq; nos allo quitur, attentas ac dociles aures præbeamus, ne in magni illius viuentis Dei manus, vt Capernaum & Bethsaida ingratæ ciuitates, incidamus, deteriore futura nostra conditione quâ Sodomæ ac Gomorrhæ. Matth. 11. 24. aut vt Ierusalem terrestris, quòd tempus suæ visitationis non nouerit. Luc.19.44. Quod vtinam atque vtinam Deus Opt.Max.propter immensam bonitatem à nostris ceruicibus auertat.
units.tr: Therefore, brethren, let us hasten to fear the dreadful day of wrath. We beg you in Christ's name and as ambassadors, be reconciled to God (2 Cor. 5:20). Let us hold that most holy Word in greater esteem than we have hitherto done, the Word, I say, which sounds in our ears and which we proclaim to you (Rom. 10:8): if it falls on good ground it will bring forth the fruit of righteousness, but if on rock and barren land, it will accumulate curse upon those very places, which bears to destruction. Let us recall with careful memory how gently that word has visited us, sparing us, and how great its kindness still is towards us, a kindness that few others have experienced, indeed scarcely any church in the whole world. So long, therefore, as it speaks to us, let us offer attentive and teachable ears, lest we fall into the hands of that great living God, like the ungrateful cities of Capernaum and Bethsaida, our condition then being worse than that of Sodom and Gomorrah (Matt. 11:24), or like earthly Jerusalem, which did not know the time of its visitation (Luke 19:44). May God, the best and greatest, in his immense goodness, turn this from our necks, and again and again we pray that he will do so.

units.la: HOMILIA octaua.
units.tr: HOMILIA octaua.

units.la: MATTH. 26.
units.tr: MATTHEW 26.

units.la: 47. Et adhuc eo loquente, ecce, Iudas vnus ex duodecim, venit, & cum eo turba multa cum gladiis & fustibus, à principibus sacerdotum & senioribus populi.
units.tr: 47. And while he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders of the people.

units.la: 48. Is vero qui prodebat eum dederat eis signum, dicens, Quemcunque osculatus fuero, is est: prehendite eum.
units.tr: 48. Now he who was betraying him had given them a sign, saying, Whomever I kiss, that is he; seize him.

units.la: 49. Itaque statim quum venisset ad Iesum, dixit. Aue rabbi. Et deosculatus est eum.
units.tr: 49. And so, immediately, when he had come to Jesus, he said, Hail, rabbi. And he kissed him.

units.la: 50. At Iesus dixit ei. Amice, quorsum ades?
units.tr: 50. But Jesus said to him, Friend, why have you come?

units.la: MARC. 14.
units.tr: MARK 14.

units.la: 43. Et statim adhuc eo loquente adest Iudas qui erat vnus e duodecim: & cum eo turba multa cum gladiis & fustibus, à principibus Sacerdotum & Scribis & Senioribus.
units.tr: 43. And immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas came, who was one of the twelve, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and scribes and elders.

units.la: 44. Dide-
units.tr: 44. Dide-

units.la: 44. Dederat autem eis iste qui eum prodebat, commune signum, dicens, Quemcunque osculatus fuero: is est, comprehendite eum, & abducite tuto.
units.tr: 44. Now he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying: Whomever I kiss, that is the one; seize him and lead him away safely.

units.la: 45. Quum igitur venisset, statim accedit ad eum, dicitque ei, Rabbi, rabbi: ac deosculatus est eum.
units.tr: 45. When therefore he had come, immediately he goes up to him and says to him, Rabbi, rabbi; and he kissed him.

units.la: LVC. 22.
units.tr: LUKE 22.

units.la: 47. Adhuc autem eo loquente, ecce turba & is qui dicebatur Iudas, unus e duodecim, praibat eis, & appropinquauit Iesu ut oscularetur eum.
units.tr: 47. While he was still speaking, behold, a crowd, and he who was called Judas, one of the twelve, went before them, and approached Jesus to kiss him.

units.la: 48. Iesus autem dixit ei, Iuda, osculo Filium hominis prodis?
units.tr: 48. But Jesus said to him, Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?

units.la: IOH. 18.
units.tr: JOHN 18.

units.la: 3. Iudas ergo quum accepisset cohortem, & a Pontificibus ac Pharisaeis ministros, venit illuc cum laternis & facibus & armis.
units.tr: 3. Judas therefore, having taken a band of soldiers, and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, came there with lanterns and torches and weapons.

units.la: ACTENVS quomodo se ad tam tum certamen Dominus accinxerit audiuimus: nunc quis fuerit apparatus hostium, primusq; adeo certaminis istius conflictus in hac nobis historia proponitur. Adest igitur ab hostibus ingens caterua gladiis & fustibus instructissima cum mandatis primariorum Sacerdotum & Seniorum populi. Quorsum vero tantus hic apparatus? Nec enim ignorabat non esse sibi nec a Christo nec ab eius discipulis ab vlla vi externa quicquam metuendum. Sin autem occultam illam & inuisibilem po-
units.tr: So far we have heard how the Lord girded himself for so great a struggle; now we are shown in this history what the enemy's equipment was, and the first clash of that conflict. There comes, then, from the enemies a huge band, armed to the teeth with swords and clubs, under the orders of the chief priests and elders of the people. But why this great display? For they did not fail to know that neither from Christ nor from his disciples was there anything to fear from any external force. But if they feared that hidden and invisible power, whose many proofs they had felt, how great, I ask, was the madness of trying to do violence to him with iron weapons, men of flesh? And when all had been thrown prostrate to the ground by a single little word of Jesus Christ, and that the gentlest, it was enough, and more than enough, to perceive their own folly from this one argument, and as it were to feel it with the hand. But what can you do? An evil conscience never rests secure, and the more it relies on its own inventions, the more it betrays its blindness.

units.la: 1. j. tentiam timebant, cuius tot testimonia sense-rant,quantæ quæso fuit dementiæ carneos homines, ferreis armis instructos illi vim facere conari?Et quū vno Iesu Christi verbulo, soque lenissimo in terram omnes prostrati fuissent, satis superque vel ex hoc vno argumento suā ipsorum vesaniam deprehendere, & quasi manu palpare ipsos oportuit. Sed quid agas?nunquam mala conscientia tuta quiescit, quóve magis suis figmentis innititur, hoc magis suam cæcitatem prodit.
units.tr: ...feared his power, whose so many testimonies they had perceived. How great, I ask, was the madness of mortal men, armed with iron weapons, to attempt to do violence to him! And when all of them had been thrown to the ground by a single word of Jesus Christ, and that the gentlest of words, it was enough and more than enough to detect their own frenzy from this one argument alone, and, as it were, to feel it with the hand. But what can you do? An evil conscience never rests safely, and the more it relies on its own inventions, the more it betrays its blindness.

units.la: Obtinuerunt, fateor, quod agendum suscepe- rant. At ne sic quidem illis tribui quasi victoribus quicquam potest. Nec enim suaipso- rum vi Christum Iesum iniectis manibus abripuerunt: sed is ipse dese ita statuit. Quòd si de hac re tota iudicium ab exitu, sicuti par est, feramus, non autem ab iis simpliciter quæ intéruenerunt, heu miseri & infelices Iudæi, contra quem arma cepistis? Contra vos ipsos. Captiuus enim iste vos cœpit, vinctus iste vos aliis compedibus constrinxit, vestra audacia plusquàm vesana, certa fuit ratio, certum instrumentum, vera causa vestri vltimi exitij. Sic enim prehendentes Christum qui vestras manus effugit, Sacerdotes, certè vestram sacerdotij vestri dignitatem amisistis: tu verò Israël Deo quondam dilecte, odium ipsius in te vltro concistis, vt qui antea erat Non populus in tuum locum sufficeretur, quod olim disertis ve rbis ab Osea tibi prædictū fuerat. Cfe. 2.
units.tr: I grant that they achieved what they had undertaken. Yet not even so can anything be credited to them as victors. For they did not seize Jesus Christ by laying hands on him through their own strength; he himself so decided. But if we pass judgment on this whole matter from its outcome, as is right, and not simply from the events that intervened, what, unhappy and wretched Jews, did you take up arms against? Against yourselves. For this captive took you prisoner; this bound man shackled you in other fetters. Your audacity, more than mad, was the sure reason, the certain instrument, and the true cause of your final ruin. For in seizing Christ, who escaped your hands, you priests certainly lost the dignity of your priesthood. And you, Israel, once beloved of God, you of your own accord incurred his hatred, so that the one who was formerly "Not my people" was to be substituted in your place, as Hosea had foretold to you long ago in plain words. Hos. 2.

units.la: 2. Denique contrà quàm cogitasti, quoquot erant crant in tuam gratiam scripturæ Prophetiæ, à te ipso contra teipsum impletæ & ratæ cuaserunt.
units.tr: 2. Finally, contrary to what you intended, all the prophetic Scriptures that were in your favour were fulfilled and confirmed, by you yourselves, against yourselves.

units.la: Æquum vero non est vt seruorum melior sit quàm Domini conditio. Quapropter quum hac nostra tempestate, vt & omnibus seculis contigit, eadem hostium rabie exagitari filios Dei videmus, quid trepidi pauemus, ac non potius nobis de illa capitis cum membris conformitate, cuius idem erit proculdubio exitus gratulamur? Quum enim nulla sint magis idonea in suam ipsorum perniciem instrumenta, quàm ij ipsi qui nobis vltimum exitium minantur, idque tum maximè quum se vt otorum copotes factos iactitant, quid causæ est cur reformidemus? Hoc tamen non impedit quominus Deus iustis etiam humanis ad suos tutandos rationibus, vbi & quando libuit, vtatur, sicut hac nostra ætate non semel contigisse videmus, & hoc ipso loco nunc experimur. Sed quoties ita Deo visum est, meminerimus si- quid inde subsidij & solatij percipimus, non magis id viribus nostris aut armis ascribendū, quàm muscis aut ranis, Ægypti vastationem tribuendam. Ac sanè hoc nostro seculo talem sese Deus hic nobis præstitit, vt necessario fa- tendum sit, illi vni, qui paruis rebus, magna conficit, Ecclesiæ salutem acceptam esse fe- rendam.
units.tr: Indeed, it is not fair that the condition of the servants should be better than that of the Master. Therefore, since in our own time, as in all ages, we see the sons of God harassed by the same raging of enemies, why do we tremble in fear, and not rather rejoice in that conformity of the head with the members, whose outcome will undoubtedly be the same? For since there are no instruments more suited to their own destruction than those very people who threaten us with final ruin, and that especially when they boast that they have become masters of the world, why should we be afraid? Yet this does not prevent God from using, where and when it pleases him, even just human means to protect his people, as we have seen happen more than once in our own age, and as we are experiencing now in this very place. But whenever it has seemed good to God, let us remember that whatever help and comfort we receive from this is to be ascribed not so much to our own strength or arms as the devastation of Egypt was to be ascribed to flies or frogs. And indeed, in this our age God has so shown himself to us here that we must necessarily confess that the salvation of the Church has been received from him alone, who accomplishes great things by small means.

units.la: Quæ porrò sit humanę mentis prauitas hinc maximè perspicimus, quum sic aduigilent im- probi & omnes animi cogitationes adiiciant
units.tr: Moreover, we see most clearly from this how perverse the human mind is, when the wicked keep watch so diligently and apply every thought of their minds

units.la: Quæ capiti contra membris fiduciam adferunt. Deus non vetat suam Ecclesiam iustis se armis tueri. Pios ad bonum alacriores.
units.tr: to bringing about what gives the head confidence against the members. God does not forbid his Church to defend itself with just arms. The pious are made more eager for good.

units.la: nefariis suis conatibus perficiendis, ita interim altum stertentibus Apostolis, vt ne experiegescieri quidem possint. Et quemadmodum o-lim factum, & hodie fieri videmus, plus saris illud esse verum experimur, Filios huius seculi prudentiores esse in suo genere filiis Lucis. At oportet tamen discrimen aliquod inter filios Lucis esse, quales tandem Apostoli fuere, & tenebrarum filios. Oremus igitur Dominum vt & pastoribus & gregibus altum illum corpo-rem ac veternum magis ac magis demonstret, ac simul emendet, ne somno sicut reliqui mortales opprimantur, sed excubent potius, induti thorace fidei & charitatis, & pro galea, spe salutis, vt monet Apost. 1. Thess. 5. 8. Nec vero nobis sit satis, quod ad nos vsque externa illa Lux Euangelij peruenerit, sacrosancto inter nos ministerio vigente: sed oculos ab eo pestulemus penes quem eorum est potestas, ad lucem illam excipiendam Ps. 146. 7. & sapientiam ab eo qui cunctis illam benigne largitur nec exprobrat. Iacob. 1. 5. Quid enim Sol, licet serenissimus & limpidissimus caecos iuuat, aut vltro claudentes oculos ne lucem aspiciant? nempe quantum miseris illis Iudaeis, lux externa profuit, caecutientibus interim ad veritatis lucem quae se oculis illorum ingerebat: & hic quidem laternas & faces preferentibus, vt annotat Iohan. sed veram lucem respuentibus, vnde factum est vt etiamnum hodie tenebrarum plus quam Cimmeriarum caligine premantur.
units.tr: to carrying out their wicked attempts, while the apostles sleep so deeply that they cannot even be roused. And as was done of old and as we see done today, we find by experience that the saying is more than true, that the sons of this age are more prudent in their own kind than the sons of light. Yet there ought nonetheless to be some difference between the sons of light, such as the apostles at last were, and the sons of darkness. Let us therefore pray the Lord that he may show more and more to both ministers and flocks that deep bodily drowsiness and lethargy, and at the same time cure it, so that they are not overcome by sleep like the rest of mortals, but rather keep watch, clothed with the breastplate of faith and love, and with hope of salvation for a helmet, as the Apostle warns: 1 Thess. 5. 8. Nor should it be enough for us that that outward light of the Gospel has reached us, while the most holy ministry flourishes among us; rather let us ask him, in whose power it lies, to open our eyes to receive that light: Ps. 146. 7. and let us ask for wisdom from him who gives it generously to all and does not reproach: Jas. 1. 5. For what good does the sun, however serene and clear, do to the blind, or to those who of their own accord shut their eyes so as not to see the light? Indeed, how much did the outward light profit those wretched Jews, while they remained blind to the light of truth which was presenting itself to their eyes; and they were carrying lanterns and torches, as John notes, yet rejected the true light, whence it came about that even today they are oppressed by a darkness thicker than the Cimmerian gloom.

units.la: Verùm
units.tr: But

units.la: quàm in pios ad malum esse oportet.
units.tr: than they ought to be against the pious for evil.

units.la: Verùm age quos putas homines tanta rabie Christum adortos? Næ, non Pilatus, non Herodes, non Græci, non Romani, non ipsum denique proprie vulgus imperitum, non sua sponte sed a magnatibus impulsum & adornatum: sed ipsi Sacerdotes hoc fecerunt Aaronico sanguine oriundi, qui soli altari admovebantur, offerebant & precabantur pro populo, ex quorum labiis petenda fuit sapientia, Deut.17.8. ipsi etiam præ cæteris Pharisæi, magni illi iustitiæ cultores, Legis enarratores, traditionum auctores, secta inter Iudæos omnium exquisitissima. Act.26.5. Quænam igitur tunc erat vera Ecclesia? num ex istis hominibus conflata? Minimè vero. Nam, inquit, Dominus noster Iesus Christus, Oves meæ vocem meam audiunt. Ioh. 10.27. isti vero contra mandata Dei suis traditionibus cuertebant. Matth.15.6. à quibus etiam cauere nos iubet. Matth.15.14.
units.tr: But come, what men do you think assailed Christ with such rage? Certainly not Pilate, not Herod, not the Greeks, not the Romans, nor finally the unlearned common people themselves, who were not driven and set on by their own will but by the great men. No, it was the priests themselves who did this, descended from Aaron's blood, who alone approached the altar, offered sacrifice and prayed for the people, and from whose lips wisdom was to be sought: Deut. 17. 8. Also the Pharisees above all others, those great cultivators of righteousness, expounders of the Law, authors of traditions, the most exact sect among the Jews: Acts 26. 5. What then was the true Church at that time? Was it formed of these men? By no means. For, says our Lord Jesus Christ, "My sheep hear my voice": John 10. 27. But these men, against God's commands, overturned them by their own traditions: Matt. 15. 6. from whom he also bids us beware: Matt. 15. 14.

units.la: Adeste igitur, vos Antistites, qui ad vestra peda & tiaras sacrosanctum Ecclesiæ nomen extra quam non est salus, transfertis, cedò vero, num vestrum illud Petri templum, Romæ ex Dei mandato sicut alterum illud Hierosolymitanum conditum est & constructum? Sed esto sane, vestrone magis astrictus & alligatus fuerit Sp. S. quàm illi Hierosolymitano? Personalis illa vestra Successio num validiore fundamento fulcitur quàm Leuitica illa & maxime Aaronica? Fateor igitur lubens, Deû quidem in Ecclesia sua per sanctum suum regnare ministerium: verum & illud agnosco, quan-
units.tr: Come forward then, you bishops, who transfer the sacrosanct name of the Church, outside which there is no salvation, to your feet and your tiaras. Tell me, is that temple of yours, Peter's at Rome, founded and built by God's command, just as the other one at Jerusalem was? But grant it: is the Holy Spirit more firmly bound and tied to yours than to that Jerusalem one? Does that personal succession of yours rest on a firmer foundation than the Levitical one, and especially the Aaronic? I therefore gladly confess that God rules in his Church through his holy ministry; but I also acknowledge this, how far

units.la: {a} Qui Ecclesiæ ædificationi præsunt sæpissimè membra quidem sunt Ecclesiæ, sed illius potius destructores quantum in ipsis est, tum vita tum doctrina. doquidem fides est ex auditu verbi, & Ecclesia superstructa est fundamento Apostolorum ac Prophetarum Ephes.2.10. Apocalyp.2.14. eam nunquam fuisse nec esse, nec fore veris doctoribus, ac veris discipulis destitutam. Stat & illud, ordinem a Christo in Ecclesia sua constitutum, ad finem vsque seculi perduraturum: At non tamen dicitur futurum, ut haec Ecclesia, haec verbi praedicatio, hic ordo semper eodem & pari statu decurrat: ut qui sedluri sunt in cathedra veritatis: semper etiam veritatis sint praecones: ut hic ordo religiose semper retineatur, quasi Spiritus Sanctus successioni ordinariae & personali adhaerescat. Immo Aaron, licet imprudens, tamen in praecipua sui muneris parte peccasse deprehenditur, utpote in eo positum, ut idololatriam omnem prohiberet. Exod.32.2. & 21. Sed & duo ex ipsius libertis, primi omnium temere alienum ignem altari Iehouae admouerunt. Levit.10.1. Ac ne totam primae illius Israeliticae Ecclesiae historiam retexamus, quod nam ore, Prophetae acrius increpant, quam sui temporis Sacerdotes, non solum in eorum mores inuecti, sed hoc unum maxime vrgentes, quod praecaeteris populum a vero Dei cultu abducerent, & Prophetas ipsos persequerentur. Eius enim rei luculentum duplex testimonium habemus: unum in altari Damasceno ab Uria sacerdote erecto 2. Reg.16.11. & 16. alterum vero in illo Pascha summo in Ieremiam furore percito Ier. 20.2. & 16.8. Denique ut ad illud accedamus quod susuperiora exempla longè lateque omni atrocitate superat, quinam filium & hæredem vineæ occiderunt?lj nempe de quibus post Dauidem Psalm. 118. 22. & Esaiam cap.28.29.Simeon ante vaticinatus fuerat Luc.2. 34. Quoties verò ante & post captiuitatem Babyloniam Ecclesia in cum statum redacta est,ut nulli esset,vt ita dicam,nisi soli Deo cognita, cuj perspicua sunt quæ quanlibet lynceis & perspicacibus hominibus aliquando quòd ad externam saltem formam attinet, sunt prorsus incomperta, velut ipsi Eliæ 1. Reg. 19. 18. Qui tunc igitur Ecclesiæ administrationem obtinebant, Ecclesiæ membra non erant, nedum vt eam constituerent: sed potius improbi vinitores,quibus proinde Dominus suam quum ipsi libuit vineam abstulit. Matth.21. 1. At fortassis Ecclesiæ Christianæ præsules, peculiari quapiam & certiore promissione nituntur. Immò nulla prorsus. Quinetiam tam sedulò nos Iesus Christus de falsis Christis & pseudoprophetis cauendis commonefecit Matth.24. 5.& 24. & Apostolus Act. 20. 29. 1. Thess. 2. 4. 1.Timoth.4 3.& Ioan.in Apocal. diserte quoque vrbem sepiticollem, id est, Romam, illius insignis meretricis futuram sedem designauit. Denique etiamsi nullum de his vaticinium antiquius extaret, quid apertius nobis testatur Ecclesiastica tota historia, quàm vastationes illas Ecclesiæ præcipuas sese mutuò excipientes, à falsis pastoribus in primis exortas?
units.tr: {a} Those who preside over the building up of the Church are very often members of the Church, but, so far as lies in them, rather its destroyers, both by their life and by their teaching. For faith comes by hearing the word, and the Church is built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets (Ephes. 2.10; Apoc. 2.14). It has never been, nor is, nor will it ever be, left destitute of true teachers and true disciples. It also stands that the order instituted by Christ in his Church will endure to the end of the age. Yet it is not said that this Church, this preaching of the Word, and this order will always run on in the same and equal state, so that those who sit in the chair of truth will always be heralds of truth, and this order is religiously kept as if the Holy Spirit clung to ordinary and personal succession. Indeed Aaron, although imprudent, is found to have sinned in the chief part of his office, since it was his duty to prohibit all idolatry (Exod. 32.2, 21). Moreover, two of his own sons were the first of all to offer strange fire on the altar of Jehovah (Lev. 10.1). Not to retrace the whole history of that first Israelite Church: who did the Prophets denounce more sharply than the priests of their own time, attacking not only their morals but insisting above all on this, that they were drawing the people away from the true worship of God and persecuting the Prophets themselves? We have a clear double witness to this: one in the Damascene altar erected by the priest Uriah (2 Kings 16.11, 16), and the other in that great uproar against Jeremiah (Jer. 20.2; 16.8). Finally, to come to that which far and wide surpasses the earlier examples in every atrocity: who killed the son and heir of the vineyard? Namely those of whom, after David, it is said (Ps. 118.22; Isa. 28.16, 29), and whom Simeon had foretold (Luke 2.34). Often, before and after the Babylonian captivity, the Church was reduced to such a state that it was known, so to speak, only to God, whose eyes alone can see what, even to the keenest and most sharp-sighted men, is sometimes wholly unknown, at least as far as outward form is concerned, just as it was to Elijah himself (1 Kings 19.18). Those who then held the administration of the Church were not members of the Church, let alone its founders; rather they were wicked vinedressers, from whom the Lord therefore took away his vineyard when it pleased him (Matt. 21.1). But perhaps the leaders of the Christian Church lean on some particular and surer promise? Not at all. Indeed Jesus Christ warned us so earnestly to beware of false Christs and pseudo-prophets (Matt. 24.5, 24), and the Apostle (Acts 20.29; 1 Thess. 2.4; 1 Tim. 4.3), and John in the Apocalypse, clearly designated the city of the seven hills, that is Rome, as the future seat of that notorious harlot. Finally, even if no older prophecy about these things survived, what does the whole of ecclesiastical history testify to us more plainly than those chief devastations of the Church that have followed one another, first brought about by false pastors?

units.la: b. iiij.
units.tr: b. iiij.

units.la: Sed alia multa praeterea nobis in hac veterum illorum & nostrorum sacerdotum collatione consideranda proponuntur. Erat enim Leuiticum Sacerdotium à Deo constitutum, adeò vt vitium in personis non autem in ipso sacerdotali munere inhaereret. At vero intetra illa & execranda Babylone Romana, egregia illa nimirum, quam vocant, Hierarchia, cuius tanpore successionem personalem iactitant, vnde tandem obsecro totus ille fiue spiritualis siue temporalis Episcopi œcumenici Romani primatus ortum duxit? vnde tota illa Cardinalitia dignitas? vnde omnes illi Primatuum & Archiepiscoporum ordines? vnde, inquam tota illa colluuies emersit quàm ex imo ambitionis & Orci, barathro?
units.tr: But many other things are also to be considered by us in this comparison of those ancient priests with our own. For the Levitical priesthood was instituted by God, so that the fault lay in the persons and not in the priestly office itself. But within that detestable and accursed Roman Babylon, that outstanding so-called Hierarchy, whose personal succession they boast of, from where, I beg you, did that whole spiritual or temporal primacy of the ecumenical Bishop of Rome arise? From where all that cardinalate dignity? From where all those orders of Primates and Archbishops? From where, I say, did that whole sewer emerge, if not from the bottom of the pit of ambition and of Hell?

units.la: Nam in Apostolicis quidem scriptis, nulla ne tenuissima quidem illarum rerum mentio, & à veteribus quos citant canonibus (de quibus etiam quaeri potest ac debet) quàm procul isti aberrarint abundè fuit à nostris iam pridem demonstratum. Quod autem ad alias functiones Ecclesiasticas attinet, quae scripturae authoritate nituntur, quales sunt Episcopi, Pastores, quos Curatos vocant, Doctores & Diaconi, quid in his omnibus praeter sola nomina superest? Sunt enim hodie tanquam umbratiles quaedam laruae quae vix ac ne vix quidem umbrae nomen mercantur. Quid vero? detestandum illud Sacerdotium quod prepresbyterium vocant, vnico summi nostri & perpetui Pontificis sacerdotio quo semel defunctus seseadnos Patri suo reconciliandos obtulit oppositum ex diametro, vnde successionis initium quàm ex Satana vero ipsius parente ducet?
units.tr: For in the apostolic writings there is not even the faintest mention of those things, and how far they have strayed from the canons of the ancients, whom they cite (and this too can and should be inquired into), has long since been amply demonstrated by our people. As for the other ecclesiastical functions, which rest on the authority of Scripture, such as bishops, pastors (whom they call curates), teachers and deacons, what remains of all these except the bare names? For today they are like certain shadowy ghosts, which scarcely, if even scarcely, earn the name of a shadow. And what of that detestable priesthood which they call the pre-presbyterate, set diametrically against the unique priesthood of our highest and perpetual High Priest, who once for all offered himself, having died, to be reconciled to his Father on our behalf? From where would it derive the beginning of its succession, if not from Satan, its true parent?

units.la: Denique vt tandem aliquando ex hac sententia emergamus, si tum quoque quum ordo functionum in Ecclesia Dei constitutarum retinetur, non simpliciter quorumcunque patrum praedicationi credendum, sed explorandi sunt Spiritus. Ephes.5.ver.17. Philipp.1. ver.10. 1.Thess.5.21. 1.Iohan.4.1. quanto magis illud requiritur, vbi quicquid erat diuinitus recte constitutum, funditus euersum cernitur? Facillimè autem discernentur alii ab aliis, si Dei monitis veterem populum compellantis, Deut.13.ver.2. ad inter nosce ndos falsos Prophetas à veris obsequamur, & rursum Matth.7.16. & quidem in primis si quod nobis praescribitur de analogia & perpetuo articulorum fidei nostrae, & totius scripturae interpretationis consensu retineamus.
units.tr: Finally, that we may at last emerge from this opinion: even if the order of functions instituted in the Church of God is still retained, the preaching of any fathers whatever is not to be believed simply, but the spirits must be tested (Eph. 5.17; Phil. 1.10; 1 Thess. 5.21; 1 John 4.1). How much more is this required when whatever was rightly ordained by God is seen to be overthrown from the foundations? The one may be distinguished from the other quite easily if we obey God's warnings, which address the ancient people, for distinguishing false prophets from true ones (Deut. 13.2), and again (Matt. 7.16), and especially if we hold to what is prescribed to us concerning the analogy and perpetual agreement of the articles of our faith and of the interpretation of all Scripture.

units.la: Haudabs re vero Euangelistae inter effera-tos istos Iesu Christi persequutores, nominatim Iudae proditoris meminerunt, vt qui non solum vnus quispiam de sceleratorum istorum numero fuerit, sed coru etiam dux & antesignanus, tanta tamq; Satanica audacia praeditus, vt exequendi sui sceleris rationes apud se excogitarit quibus perfidus non haberetur, certis datis signis quibus prodebat dignoscetur, ne forte Iudæi in eius prehensione in mediæ noctis caligine fallerentur: atque adeo Christum inuasuros sic exhortatus vt diligenter eum custodirent. O scelus, o deploratam audaciam cum summè ingrati animi crimine sceleratissimo coniunctam, quæ facile omnes omnium improbitates superat, si modo facinoris iltius per se tam terri & detestandi circumstantias omnes, tum Domini tam boni & clementis tam perfidè proditi, tum servi Dominum ac discipuli magistrum tam exiguo præsertim pretio prodentis expendamus.
units.tr: Indeed the Evangelists mention by name, among those savage persecutors of Jesus Christ, Judas the traitor, who was not only one of that wicked company but also its leader and standard-bearer, endowed with such great and Satanic audacity that he devised for himself means of carrying out his crime by which he would not be thought a traitor, and gave certain signs by which he would be identified as the betrayer, lest perhaps the Jews should be mistaken in seizing him in the darkness of midnight; and so he urged them to guard him carefully, as they were about to attack Christ. O crime, O desperate audacity, joined with the most wicked sin of an ungrateful mind, which easily surpasses all the wickedness of all men, if only we weigh all the circumstances of that deed, so terrible and detestable in itself: on the one side a Lord so good and gentle, so treacherously betrayed; on the other a servant and disciple betraying his Master and Teacher, especially for so small a price.

units.la: At ilta sic accidere oportuit, vt quæ sit inter prioris Adami culpam & eius expiationem per alterum Adamum præstitam analogia perspici posset. Ecce igitur primus ille noitri generis parens à suo conditore tanquam œconomus quidam, & ipsius domus in hoc mundo constitutus, cum Satana coniurat, montes aureos sibi pollicitus. En ex aduerso noster secundus Adamus poenam talionis quam vocant subiens, ab eo similiter proditur, quem crumenæ custodem & suæ familiæ administratorem constituerat, eò nimirum impulso magni alicuius lucri expectatione, vel ex pecunia promissa ac iam forte numerata, vel ex gratia quam se maximam à principibus populi sui illo patrato facinore consecuturum sperabat.
units.tr: But it had to happen in this way, so that the analogy between the fault of the first Adam and its expiation, accomplished through the second Adam, might be perceived. Here then is that first parent of our race, appointed by his Creator as a kind of steward and administrator of his household in this world, who conspired with Satan, having been promised golden mountains. Opposite him, our second Adam, undergoing the penalty of retaliation, as they call it, is likewise betrayed by one whom he had appointed keeper of the money-bag and administrator of his household, driven of course by the expectation of some great gain, either by money promised and perhaps already counted out, or by the favour which he hoped to win in the highest degree from the leaders of his people once the deed was done.

units.la: Sed Iudæ tamen scelus profecto primi parentis nostri culpam longe superauit. Nec enim ille vltrò sed ab vxore incitatus, nec eius vxor vltrò peccauit, sed ab eo qui cum ea sub ser-penpentis specie colloquebatur decepta : Iudas vero minime dicitur à Sacerdotibus quæsitus, sed eos potius prior adiisse, & vltrò sic compellasse. Quid vultis mihi dare, & ego vobis cum tradam? Matth.26.15. Itaque Deus non eodem modo vtrumque accepit. Nam in Adamo quidem poenam quâ nihil grauius cogitari potest inflixit, sed tamen cui certum simul remedium adhibuit. In Iuda vero summè horrendi nulla venia condonandi diuini iudicij exemplum habemus, duobus paribus exemplis graphicè expressum: uno videlicet in Saule contra propriam conscientiam obdurato. 1. Sam.24.21. & 31.4. altero in Achitophele, de quo tam acerbè conqueritur Dauid Psal.41. 10. vt qui exemplum perdito isti proditori videatur imitandum præbuisse. 2.Sam.27.23.
units.tr: But Judas's crime certainly far surpassed the fault of our first parent. Adam did not sin of his own accord but was urged on by his wife, and his wife did not sin of her own accord but was deceived by the one who talked with her under the form of a serpent. Judas, however, is not said to have been sought out by the priests; rather, he approached them first, of his own accord, and addressed them thus: "What will you give me, and I will hand him over to you?" Matth.26.15. So God did not deal with the two in the same way. In Adam he inflicted a punishment than which nothing more grievous can be imagined, yet he at the same time applied a remedy. In Judas, however, we have an example of the most dreadful judgment of God, with no pardon granted, set forth vividly through two parallel examples: one in Saul, hardened against his own conscience, 1. Sam.24.21 and 31.4; the other in Ahithophel, over whom David complains so bitterly, Psal.41.10, as one who seems to have offered that lost traitor an example to imitate, 2.Sam.27.23.

units.la: Est igitur profecto facinus istud immane ac horrendum, quod vt in vsum nostrum vertamus, attentius est nobis etiam atque etiam considerandum quomodo perditus ille in tantum præcipitium lit prolapsus, vt eius exemplo commonefacti, tempestiuè nobis ab eiusmodi præcipitiis caueamus. En igitur Iudam suâ sorte minime contentum, & diro illo auaritiæ vitio infectum, quæ merito ab Apostolo, atque adeo ab ipsis prophanis hominibus, radix malorum omnium appellatur. 1. Tim. 6.10. Videtur tamen Iudas principium aliquod boni motus habuisse, quo impulsus fuerit ad Christum non tantùm audiendum vt plerique alij, sed etiam cum perseuerantia sequendum, vnus videlicet ex eorum numero qui omnia deseruisse dicuntur, vt illum assectarentur, Matth. 19. vers. 27. Hinc factum vt à Christo admissus non modo in numerum duodecim illorum domesticorum cooptaretur, & vnus ex iis esset quos ingentibus donis Spiritus S. ornatos ad promulgandum Euangelium misit. Matth. 10. vers. 8. Sed etiam loculos gestaret, & coëmendis ad vsus domesticos necessariis velut œconomus præficeretur. Iohan. 12. vers. 6. Sed quum dira illa auaritiæ pestis in ipso sensim incrementum caperet, eò tandem deuenit, vt quicquid ex suo magistro tot monitis, præceptis & miraculis didicerat oblitus, Dominum illum suum triginta numulis polthaberet, & ita ipse sibi mentis oculos eruit, vt immemor eius in quem reluctante conscientia coniurabar, sceleratam suam cogitationem vltro indurare, ac etiam execui sustinuerit, idque tanto studio & ardore vt in hoc vnum totus esset intentus.
units.tr: Certainly that deed is monstrous and horrible. So that we may turn it to our own use, we must consider it again and again, and more attentively, how that lost man fell into such a precipice, so that, warned by his example, we may in good time guard ourselves against such precipices. Here, then, is Judas, by no means content with his lot and infected with that dreadful vice of avarice, which the Apostle rightly calls the root of all evils, as do even the profane themselves, 1. Tim.6.10. Yet Judas seems to have had some beginning of good motion, which moved him to follow Christ, not merely to hear him as many others did, but to follow him with perseverance. He was one of those who are said to have left everything to follow him, Matth.19. vers.27. Hence, admitted by Christ, he was not only enrolled among the twelve, his intimate household, and made one of those whom he sent out, adorned with the great gifts of the Holy Spirit, to proclaim the Gospel, Matth.10. vers.8. He also carried the money-bag and was placed over the buying of necessities for the household, as its steward, Iohan.12. vers.6. But when that dreadful plague of avarice gradually grew in him, he came at last to such a state that, forgetting all he had learned from his master through so many admonitions, precepts and miracles, he held his Lord of little account for thirty pieces of silver. So he blinded the eyes of his own mind, and, unmindful of him against whom his conscience struggled, he willingly hardened his wicked intention and even endured to carry it out, and with such zeal and ardour that he was wholly intent on this one thing.

units.la: Huc igitur aures arrigite, auari, huc animum aduertite: quos si Deus adhuc prohibuit in tantum scelus prolabi, scitote tamen voscandem præcipitij viam insistere. Nam Iudas quidem augendarum facultatum cupiditate flagrabat, vos autem oro quid captatis? Næ id luce clarius est ex vniuscuiusque ciuium, tum potentiorum, tum plebeiorum moribus, ex fœnerationibus, ex monopolis mercaturis mercatorum, ex annonæ caritate malis artibus illata, ex illicitis pactis & contractibus, frustra nobis reclamantibus, & ex hoc ipso loco resipiscentiam inculcantibus. Vos igitur, aio, & palàm denuntio eandem atque Iudam iustum præcipitij viam non modò insistere, sed longissimè iam esse progressos, & iisdem Satanæ compedibus irretitos teneri, Sapientis illius immemores præmonentis eum qui turpe lucrum captat suam ipsius domum turbare. Proverb. 15. verf. 27. nec impunitum illum fore qui cito vult ditescere: & Apostoli diserte monentis. 1. Timoth. 6. v. 9. eos qui volunt ditescere incidere in tentationem, & laqueum & cupiditates multas inutiles, & damnosas quæ demergunt homines in exitium & interitum. Iudas certè recto quodam animi motu impulsus fuit ut posthabitis omnibus Christum sequeretur. Quinetiam in eius familiam fuit adscitus, & ad honorificum munus vocatus. Hæc in vobis similia omnia animadverto.
units.tr: Prick up your ears here, misers; pay attention here. God has so far kept you from falling into such a crime, but know that you are treading the same path to the precipice. Judas indeed burned with desire to increase his possessions; but what, I ask, are you aiming at? This is clearer than light from the conduct of every citizen, both powerful and humble: from usury, from monopolies, from the trading of merchants, from the dearness of provisions brought about by evil arts, from unlawful pacts and contracts. We protest in vain, and from this very pulpit we urge repentance. Therefore I say to you, and openly declare, that you are not only treading the same path to the precipice as Judas, but have already advanced far along it, and are held fast in the very fetters of Satan. You forget that wise man who warns that he who seeks base gain troubles his own house, Prov.15. vers.27, and that he will not go unpunished who wishes to grow rich quickly; and you forget the Apostle who plainly warns, 1. Timoth.6. v.9, that those who want to be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and harmful desires which plunge men into ruin and destruction. Judas, certainly, was moved by a certain right impulse of mind to follow Christ, setting aside everything. He was even taken into his household and called to an honourable office. I notice that all these things are similar in you.

units.la: Sunt enim ex vobis qui ab initio, neglectis priuatis suis commodis Deum vocantem sequuti sese ipsius Ecclesiæ adiunxerunt: alij in ipsa domo Dei nati sunt, & in ea magnos honores consecuti. Sed quorsum hæc? Eheu multæ plures sunt quàm par sit, qui in medio Ecclesiæ sinu Mammonæ inseruiant, ut ex tota eorum vitæ ratione liquet, nedum ut charitati studeant, quæ certa est eorum nota & testera qui veri sunt domestici filij Dei, à cuius familia nunquam desciscant. Matth.22. 12. & participes tandem eximiæ illius promissionis suturi quæ habetur,Matth.19.29. Quid vero tandem auaris istis fiet? Nempe Deo exosi, hominibus inuisi & execrandi, ipsi sibi carnifices alij laqueum induunt, & initar Iudæ sese dant præcipites:alij infinitis sese molestissimis curis ma cerantes,neque suis illis opibus quarum causa tam miserè suam conscientiam Sataną man ciparunt, non magis fruentes quàm si nullas possiderent, ac tandem quum ab eadem con-scientia vadimonium ipsis sui in iudicio Dei sistendi causa denuntiatur, nusquam solatium inuenientes,miserrimè intereunt.Sed &quàm nimium multi iam olim fuêre & etiam num hodie reperiuntur, qui quod Iudas in Christo prodendo fecit, in eius membris faciant, non animaducentes miseri, præcipuum hoc esse caput eius pactionis quam cum Diabolo & eius administris ineunt, vt illi sese totos mancipatos addicant,eius compedibus constricti, vt sese nunquam ex iis expedire possint. Hic igitur sese quisque sibi nihil assentatus circumspiciat, ne vana huius mundi species quempiam seducat 1. Cor.7.31. & 1.Ioh.2.15. Reputemus apud nos, quaso, quanto pluris æstimanda sit benedictio Iacobi, quàm iusculum illud Esaui.Et quum huius vitæ cómoda creata sint in hominum gratiam,cogitemus quàm turpe sit iis tanquam dominis parêre,& vt durissimis tyrannis seruire,quæ nobis esse subiecta oportuit. Neque vero nos ipsos viuos in terram defodiamus, quum nos Deus in coelos ipsos inuitet: neve ex eorum numero simus qui commodum suum quaerunt propriarum animarum dispendio, quas ita curis istius vitae irretiunt, vt ex iis quibus semel astrictae sunt vinculis extricare sese postea nulla ratione possint. Ne stultos illos (inquam) & amentes homines imitemur, qui potu sitim accendentes, eam restinguere se amplius potando posse somniat. Quod ad huius vitae commoda, sciamus esse Domini ea quibus velit distribuere & dimetiri: ac proinde insanis illis cupiditatibus quibus aestuamus, procul a nobis ablegatis: quum Dei vnius imperio coelum & terra subiaceant, non autem perditi illius inuasoris huius mundi Principis, cui nec potestas nec voluntas adest nobis vel in minima vlla re suc-currendi: in eiusmodi rerum inopia, ad illum vnum verum istorum omnium bonorum auctorem ac benignissimum distributorem confugiamus: eam denique rei familiaris augendae ratione sequamur quam ille nobis optimam instituit, nempe vt intra nostrae vocationis fines maneamus, & praesentibus bonis ad nominis sui gloriam, & proximi vtilitatem cum omni gratiarum actione fruamur, & vere nostrae incorruptae & sempiternae haereditatis fruitionem animis placidis expectemus.
units.tr: For some among you from the beginning, neglecting your private advantages, followed God's call and joined yourselves to the Church itself; others were born in the very house of God and attained great honours in it. But why say these things? Alas, there are far more than is fitting who serve Mammon in the very bosom of the Church, as is clear from the whole course of their lives, let alone that they study charity, which is the sure mark and token of those who are true domestic children of God and never desert his household, Matth.22.12, and who at last share in that notable promise found at Matth.19.29. But what will become of these misers? Surely they are hated by God, odious and detestable to men. Some put a noose round their own necks, becoming their own executioners, and, like Judas, hurl themselves headlong. Others, tormenting themselves with endless and most wretched cares, enjoy their riches no more than if they had none, and for the sake of those riches they have so miserably enslaved their conscience to Satan. At last, when that same conscience summons them to appear for judgment before God, they find comfort nowhere and perish most miserably. But how many, alas, there were long ago, and how many are found even today, who do in the members of Christ what Judas did in betraying him! They do not realise, wretched men, that this is the chief article of the pact they make with the Devil and his ministers: to hand themselves over wholly as slaves, bound in his fetters, so that they can never free themselves from them. Let each one, then, look around without flattering himself, lest the vain show of this world deceive anyone, 1.Cor.7.31 and 1.Ioh.2.15. Let us consider how much more to be valued is Jacob's blessing than that mess of pottage of Esau. And since the comforts of this life were created for the benefit of men, let us think how shameful it is to obey them as masters and serve them as the harshest tyrants, when they ought to be subject to us. Nor should we bury ourselves alive in the earth when God invites us to heaven itself. Nor should we be among those who seek their own advantage at the cost of their souls, entangling them in the cares of this life so that, once bound by the chains, they can by no means extricate themselves. Let us not imitate (I say) those foolish and mad men who, kindling their thirst with drink, dream that they can quench it by drinking more. As for the comforts of this life, let us know they are the Lord's, to be distributed and measured out as he wills. Therefore let those mad desires with which we burn be banished far from us, since heaven and earth lie under the rule of the one God, and not under that lost invader, the prince of this world, who has neither the power nor the will to help us in the least thing. In such want, let us flee to that one true author of all these goods and most kind distributor. Finally, let us follow that method of increasing our household means which he has set up as best for us: to remain within the limits of our calling, and with all thanksgiving to enjoy present goods, for the glory of his name and the usefulness of our neighbour, and with calm minds to await the enjoyment of our true, incorruptible and everlasting inheritance.

units.la: Vt autem ad historiam nostram reuertamur, diligenter etiam est considerandum quo modo sese in hoc toto negotio gesserit Iudas, quod vel maxime ostendit quanta eius fuerit impudentia, vt qui tantæ sibi perfidiæ con‑scius, non dubitarint ipsè propius ad ipsum etiâ filium Dei deosculandum accedere: deinde quòd bis etiam Magistri nomen repetere sit ausus, velut ipsi blandiens: denique quòd illi sit verbo bene precatus, quem in hostium manus reipsa nefariè tradebat. Illud verò sceleus quum hodie quoque nimium multi aduersus Christi membra patrare non verentur: ij videlicet de quibus nuper egimus, magnates nempe non fulciendæ (sicuti iactant) diuinitus constituti, sed euertendæ potiùs Ecclesiæ veræ Catholicæ à Satana excitati, hypocritæ inquâ isti ore quidè Christum & salutem hominum, cuius studiosissimi videri volunt, profitentes, sed reipsa animas hominum cauponatur, causa non est cur nouum hoc nobis & insolens videatur: sed à Deo postulanda est illa patientia & constantia quam hoc loco nobis in sese spectandam Christus exhibuit: nostra spe omni in eum defixa qui suo tempore Iudam vltus, specimen in eo nobis edidit eius vltionis quam suo loco & tempore luituri sunt, qui hac nostra ætate Iudam moribus exprimunt.
units.tr: But to return to our story, we must also consider carefully how Judas conducted himself in this whole affair, which above all shows how great his impudence was. Aware of such treachery, he did not hesitate to draw near and kiss the Son of God himself; then he dared to repeat the name of Master twice, as if flattering him; and finally he blessed him in words while in fact he was wickedly handing him over into the hands of enemies. Since even today very many do not hesitate to commit that crime against the members of Christ, namely those of whom we have lately spoken, magnates who were raised up not, as they boast, by God to support the Church, but rather stirred up by Satan to overthrow the true Catholic Church, hypocrites who profess with their mouths Christ and the salvation of men, of whose zeal they wish to appear most eager, but who in fact trade in men's souls, there is no reason why this should seem new and strange to us. Rather, we must ask of God that patience and constancy which Christ here showed us to behold, with all our hope fixed on him who in his time avenged Judas and gave us in him a specimen of the vengeance which those will suffer in their time and place who in our age imitate Judas in their conduct.

units.la: Cæterùm duo hîc ora in hac deosculatione, mutuò sibi occurrunt tam repugnantia quàm verbis bellè inter se consentire viderentur. Nam vnum quidem est os veritatis, alterum verò dissimulatæ perfidiæ: & vox quidem Iudæ vox est ementiti Iacobi, eiusdem verò manus sunt yeri Esaui manus. Et licet hæc ora mutuò fe exosculata sint, illud tamen tenen-dum & notandum est, Christum nullum Iudæ osculum præbuisse(nam osculum filij Dei vi-tam simul inspirat) sed Iudam osculum istud Christo impressisse quo suum ipsius exitium sanciret, nempe ex ipsius hypocrisi, non ex Dei spiritu promanante. Hoc igitur Iudæ factum minimè respondet illi exhortationi,qua iubemur Pfal.2.12.filium exosculari nequando irascatur:hoc est,clientelarem illi fidem & obsequium foris simul & introrsum ex sincero & integro animo præstare,osculo à Iuda præbito prorsus repugnans. Idcirco sponsa in præstantissimo illo Cantico Canticorum, à suis illis basiis & suauiis non exorditur, sed orat vt ipsius oris sponsi baiis basietur. Prior enim ipse nobis oscula porrigat oporter, vt qui nos prior elegerit & quidem ante iacta mundi fundamenta, & gratuita sua beneuolentia. Ephef.1.4. is, inquam,nos prior dilexit.1. Ioh. 4.10.is est qui sese præbet iis inueniendum à quibus nó quæritur.Esa.65.1.Rom.10.20.Quinam vero sunt illi Iudæ imitatores ? nempe ij de quibus Dominus expostulans,Esa.29.13.Ore,inquit,isti ad me accedunt,& me labiis honorant, sed cor eorum procul abest à me. Hi sunt denique quos his ipsis verbis Dominus compellat. Matth.15. 8. Denique, vt quod res est, dicam ,tales quidem sunt illæ Pontificiæ larvæ, & otiosi ventres illi, cæteriique hypocritæ, quibus adhuc scatet orbis terrarum:sed quo iure totum hoc onus in ipsos reiecerimus
units.tr: Moreover, two mouths meet here in this kiss, as contrary to each other as they might seem to agree well in words. One is the mouth of truth, the other of feigned treachery. The voice is the voice of Judas, the voice of the deceitful Jacob, but the hands are the hands of the true Esau. And although these mouths have kissed one another, it must still be held and noted that Christ gave Judas no kiss (for the kiss of the Son of God breathes life at the same time). Rather, Judas pressed that kiss upon Christ so as to sanction his own ruin, springing from his own hypocrisy and not from the Spirit of God. Therefore this act of Judas by no means corresponds to that exhortation by which we are bidden to kiss the Son, lest he be angry (Pfal.2.12), that is, to render him a client's faith and obedience, outwardly and inwardly, from a sincere and whole heart, which is wholly opposed to the kiss given by Judas. For this reason the bride, in that most excellent Song of Songs, does not begin with her own kisses and sweetnesses, but prays to be kissed with the kisses of the bridegroom's mouth. For he must offer kisses to us first, since he chose us first, indeed before the foundation of the world, and loved us by his free goodwill (Ephef.1.4). He, I say, loved us first (1. Ioh. 4.10). He is the one who presents himself to those who do not seek him (Esa.65.1; Rom.10.20). Who, then, are the imitators of Judas? Namely, those of whom the Lord complains (Esa.29.13): "With their mouth these people draw near to me and honour me with their lips, but their heart is far from me." Finally, these are the ones whom the Lord addresses in these very words (Matth.15.8). To say plainly what is the case: such indeed are those Papist masks, those idle bellies, and the other hypocrites with whom the world still teems. But with what right would we have cast this whole burden upon them,

units.la: m. j. quum ad nos quoque hæc accusatio maxime pertineat. Quàm enim multi inter nos velut artem peccandi exercent, in ore tamen illud frequenter habentes, Domine,Domine: quibus ipse vicissim Dominus respondebit ex Matth. 7.22. Non noui vos,discedite à me qui iniustitiæ datis operam.Quid amplius?quoties huc Dei verbo erudiendi conuenimus, annon apud Deum peccatores nos esse verbo profitemur? nonne illud, Domine, Domine inclamamus? Sed quotusquisque hic est discipulus, diligens & proficiens auditor? Atqui non simpliciter dicit scriptura, beatum illum esse qui audiat sermonem Dei,sed qui auditum obseruet. Luc.11.28. Et,quæso, quid cuipiam profuerit si vocanti in vineam suam Christo respondeat se abiturum, nec tamen eò proficiscatur? Matth.21.30. Sic nostrum certè non pauci hoc ipso loco Deum compellant & Dominum, quibus ille iam olim per os Malachiæ respondet.Malach.1.6.Si ego sum pater,vbi est honor mihi debitus? Si Dominus, vbi timor mei?Enimuerò, fratres, nullus hic responset, nullus tergiuersetur:sed veniam omnes potius à Domino deprecemur, vt pote tanto granioris quàm cæteri homines criminis rei quanto turpius contaminauimus & adhuc quotidie fœdamus purissimum illud sacrosanƈti ipsius oris osculum, & supplices ab eo petamus, vt tandem aliquando seriò illum osculemur,colamus & spiritu ac veritate veneremur.
units.tr: since this accusation applies most of all to us too. For how many among us practise, as it were, an art of sinning, and yet often have on their lips, "Lord, Lord," to whom the Lord himself will in turn reply (Matth. 7.22): "I never knew you; depart from me, you who work iniquity." What more? As often as we gather here to be taught by the word of God, do we not profess with our words that we are sinners before God? Do we not cry out, "Lord, Lord"? Yet how few here are diligent disciples and progressing hearers? And yet Scripture does not simply say that blessed is he who hears the word of God, but he who keeps what he has heard (Luke 11.28). And, I ask, what would it profit anyone if, when Christ calls him into his vineyard, he answers that he will go, and yet does not go there (Matth. 21.30)? So surely not a few of us address God here as Lord, and to them he long ago answered through the mouth of Malachi (Malach. 1.6): "If I am a father, where is the honour due to me? If I am the Lord, where is the fear of me?" Truly, brothers, let no one answer here, let no one evade. Rather, let us all beg pardon from the Lord, as those guilty of a crime all the heavier than other men, in proportion as we have more shamefully defiled, and still daily foul, that most pure kiss of his most holy mouth. And as suppliants let us ask him that at last we may kiss him in earnest, honour him, and venerate him in spirit and truth.

units.la: Et hæc quidem Iudas. Cedo verò, quid ei rerespondet Dominus? Amice, inquit, aut si ma-uis, Socie, h.e. familiarissime & mihi coniunctissime, quorsum hic ades? o vocem comitate in-genti & suauitate inenarrabili conditam, non tamen sine aculeis qui grauiter animum Iudae quantumuis obduratum pungerent, (ed quae mihilominus isti perdito salutaris fuisset, si quo modo aut voluisset aut potuisset in peccatus suum admittere. Verum quum aduersus Spiritum S. peccaret, hoc est, non contra unum tantum aliquod Dei mandatum, nec sola infirmitate, nec simpliciter contra conscientiam & veritatem cognitam, sed vniuersali apostasia, & capitali odio insurrexisset in magistrum suum, filium illum Dei viuentis, qualem illum fuerat ore Petri professus, Matth. 16. 16. non fuit amplius in ipsius potestate illud velle recipere, quod tam scelerate proculcatum plane repudiarat. Heb. 6. 7. Eouque igitur sensim prolabuntur, qui suae conscientiae obluctari pergunt, & longius semper progrediendo, tam procul tandem a recta via excurrunt, vt in eam postea reuerti nunquam possint. Hic vero quaerat aliquis, num quopiam amore Deus eum prosequeretur, quem optime noflet, nec etiam eorum inscius quae sibi ab ipso impenderent, quae facile fuit ipsi cuitare sicut antea praedixerat. Matth. 26. 24. Respondeo posse quidem sic istam vocem accipi, ac si Dominus de praeterito tempore duntaxat loqueretur, quasi his illum verbis exciperet. Quid agis? & quorsum hic ades tu cui tam benevolum me praebui,
units.tr: Such are the words of Judas. But tell me, what does the Lord answer him? "Friend," he says, or if you prefer, "Companion," that is, most intimate and most closely joined to me, why are you here? O voice seasoned with immense courtesy and inexpressible sweetness, yet not without stings which would sharply prick the mind of Judas, however hardened it was, and which would nevertheless have been salutary for that lost man, if he had in any way been willing or able to admit them into his conscience. But since he sinned against the Holy Spirit, that is, not against any single commandment of God, nor merely through weakness, nor simply against conscience and the truth known to him, but rose up with universal apostasy and deadly hatred against his master, that Son of the living God whom he had professed with Peter's mouth (Matth. 16.16), it was no longer in his power to accept that will which he had so wickedly trampled and utterly rejected (Heb. 6.7). Therefore those who persist in struggling against their conscience slip gradually, and by always advancing further they run so far from the right way that they can never return to it afterwards. But here someone may ask whether God pursued with any love the one whom he knew best, and who was not ignorant of the things impending over him, which it would have been easy for him to avoid, as he had foretold (Matth. 26.24). I answer that this word may indeed be taken as if the Lord spoke only of past time, as if he received him with these words: "What are you doing, and why are you here, you to whom I have shown myself so kind,

units.la: m. ij. & quo tam familiariter sum vsus? Nam hoci-pfum etiam proculdubiò significare voluit. Sed nihil obstat quominus hic etiam adda-mus, Christum, licet Iudam minimè diligeret eo amore quo solet eos demum complecti quos à Patre accepit, tamen ex infinita illa & inenarrabili clementia, qua generaliter homines vt missus à Patre salutis praeco prosequebatur, adeò vt singulos etiam homines mili ipsi sibi obstitisse nt, seruare studeret, in hanc vocem praemagno dolore erupuit, quemadmodum alibi de veteri populo loquens Dominus eas effundit querelas, quae homines quantumuis saxeos & ferreos plus satis commouere possint.Mich.6.3. Populeme, inquiens, quid in te admisi? qua in re te fatigaui? Respondemihi. Sic etiam quanuis sciret, atque adeò praedixisset illud inevitabile urbis Hierosolymitanae exitium, fleuit tamen super ea, & ista luctuosissima querimonia lamentatus, Ierusalem, Ierusalé, inquit, quoties volui congregare tuos liberos, quemadmodum gallina congregat pullos suos sub alas? O si tu nosses, vel hoc saltem tuo die, quae ad pacem tuam pertinent. Matth.23.37. Luc.19.42.
units.tr: and with whom I have used such familiarity? For he surely meant this very thing too. But nothing hinders us from adding here as well that Christ, although he did not love Judas with that love with which he is wont at last to embrace those whom he received from the Father, nevertheless, out of that infinite and inexpressible clemency by which, as the messenger of salvation sent by the Father, he embraced men in general, so that he was eager to save even single men who had set themselves against him, burst forth in this word with great grief. Just as elsewhere, speaking of the old people, the Lord pours out those complaints which could move men however stony and iron-hearted (Mich. 6.3): "My people, what have I done to you? In what have I wearied you? Answer me."
