Indeed, we ought so greatly to revere his most holy name that, if we suspect that the one to whom an oath has been offered will forswear himself, we should set the glory of God and our neighbour's salvation above all earthly things, even the most precious and dearest. Here the place itself compels me to say that some magistrates, in many places, commit a great sin in admitting capital defendants to an oath. For experience itself has proven that men of any kind, and especially of a dissolute life, will say and do anything to preserve their lives. Add that, when all other arguments have at last failed, there ought to be room for an oath, which will settle the dispute once and for all.

units.la: Vt igitur ad ea quæ textus propria sunt recurramur, quid Caiaphaм ad hanc adiurationem impulit? Duo nimirum arbitror, illo &ociis ipsius dignissima. Primum, vt prætenti-bus videretur ingenti zelo cognoscendi quæ Christum interrogabat hic loquutus: Alterum, vt ita falso persuaderet cum quicum illi res erat, nunquam perspicue nisi coactum respondere: faliflimum vtrumque, vel ipsius teste & ipsum coarguente conscientia. Nam ipse quidem nihil minus quàm certam de Christo notitiam quærit: & contrà Christus adeo semper ad se patefaciendum paratus fuit, quis nimirū, & à quo missus esset, vt vel ob hoc vnicum scelerati isti & flagitiosi homines ferre ipsum amplius nō potuerint. An verò cum Caiapha & eius sociis genus istud hominū extinctū est? Annon si cum illis est mortuum, nostro tamen seculo reuixit? & quidem ita reuixit vt superiorum omnium temporum crudelitatem & suas persecutiones nostri temporis carnifices & falsi iudices, nostrorum martyrum historia teste, longè superarint? Accedamus igitur ad hanc quæstionem, cuius summa hæc est, vt aliquid sit ipse Christus, Dei filius aperte eloquatur: Hic vero minime putem alienum a proposito quaerere, cur hoc potius quam quidvis aliud interrogarit. Nam praeterquam quod falsas eorum interpretationes mandatorum Dei tam expresse Christus reprehenderat, & traditiones eorum detestatus erat, annon etiam flagello ex templo mercatores eorum abegerat, Annon etiam eos hypocritas, dealbatos parietes, latrones appellarat? annon aperte satis de ipsis dixerat, nec ipsos intrare coelorum regnum, nec aliis ut introeant permittere? Non deficiebat cum igitur materia, sed animo non respondebat. Nam licet admissos auditores, consueto sermone, Christus esset alloquutus, coram omnibus attoniti & confusione perfusi essent. Malitiose igitur hanc quaestionem proposuit, tum minime in dubium revocans quin admitteret Iesus Christus, quod tam saepe palam erat audiente populo, Deum Patrem professus: tum ut cognosceret quid plebi videretur de Nomine Filij Dei, quod sibi arrogarat, quoque iam tum offensi tantopere fuerant, ut morte dignum eum iudicarent, & ad mortem raperent. Ioh.5.v.18. Et tamen hic error, quo Dei foedus cum hoc populo penitus violabatur, à Caiapha & sociis Sacerdotibus, Scripturarum praecipuum caput adulterantibus manabat: hac illis caecitate iam olim Esa.29. 14. praedicta, & eiusdem exitu Psalm. 118.22.
units.tr: To return, then, to the things that belong to the text itself: what drove Caiaphas to this adjuration? I think there were two reasons, both most fitting for him and his associates. First, he wished to appear to those present to be moved by great zeal to learn what Christ was saying. Second, he wished to persuade the man he was dealing with that he would never answer clearly unless compelled. Both were utterly false, and his own conscience, which bore witness and condemned him, proves it. For he sought no certain knowledge of Christ at all, whereas Christ was always so ready to reveal himself, who he was and who had sent him, that these wicked and shameless men could not bear him any longer, if only for this reason. Was this kind of men extinct with Caiaphas and his associates? Did it not, if it died with them, revive in our own age? And indeed it has revived in such a way that our executioners and false judges, as the history of our martyrs bears witness, have far surpassed the cruelty and persecutions of all earlier times. Let us come, then, to this question, the sum of which is this: that the Son of God, Christ himself, plainly declares that he is something. Here I think it is not out of place to ask why he chose this question rather than any other. For besides the fact that Christ had so expressly rebuked their false interpretations of God's commandments and had detested their traditions, did he not also drive their merchants out of the temple with a whip? Did he not call them hypocrites, whitewashed walls, and robbers? Had he not said plainly enough about them that they neither entered the kingdom of heaven themselves nor allowed others to enter? There was therefore no lack of matter, but their spirit did not answer to it. For although Christ addressed the hearers admitted to him in his usual manner, they were stunned and overwhelmed with confusion before everyone. Therefore Caiaphas put this question maliciously, not at all doubting that Jesus Christ would admit what he had so often openly professed, in the hearing of the people, that he was the Father's Son; and in order to learn what the common people thought of the name of the Son of God, which he had claimed for himself, and at which they had already been so offended that they judged him worthy of death and dragged him to it (John 5:18). Yet this error, by which the covenant of God with this people was utterly violated, flowed from Caiaphas and the priests his associates, who corrupted the chief point of the Scriptures. This blindness had been foretold long before (Isa. 29:14), and its outcome likewise (Ps. 118:22).

units.la: Idcirco etiam improbus hic Iudex non X. j.
units.tr: For this reason also this wicked judge was not

units.la: contentus ex eo quæsiuisse an esseт Christus, simul etiam hanc Filij Dei qualitatem adiicit, & quidem ea loquendi forma quæ speciale m Filij Dei qualitatem notet, nulli tribuendam nec Angelis, nec Regibus, nec personis, vllis quantumuis excellentibus, nec Israelitico populo, quem tamen Deus honore primogeniti filij dignabatur.
units.tr: content with asking whether he was the Christ; at the same time he adds this quality of the Son of God, and indeed in a form of speech that marks a special quality of the Son of God, which is to be ascribed to no one, neither to angels, nor to kings, nor to any persons, however excellent, nor to the people of Israel, whom God nonetheless honoured with the dignity of the firstborn son.

units.la: Verùmenimuero, Dei se Prouidentia prgbet hic etiam admirandam. Nam hac ratione voti factus compos flagitiosus iste, hoc nempe prætextu Christo ad mortem damnato, vt Ioh.9.7. quid tamen effecit? Seipsum nimirum suo gladio, & populum iugulauit, & excellentissimam apertissimamque confessionem ex ore Domini nostri Iesu Christi elicuit, ipsum esse verum Christum, verum Dei Filium, & vnicum nostrum Seruatorem. Denique seque suoisque in inferos præcipites dedit, nobis vero quodammodo cœlos, præter intentionem tamen patefecit. Quomodocunque tamen Caiaphas hanc Filij Dei qualitatem intellexerit, (etsi quid diceret non satis eum intellexisse sit verisimile) quod dixit verissimum est, quum Filij Dei nomen proprio & speciali modo de Messia dicatur ab omni æternitate Psal.2.7. & 45.7. & 110.2. & passim alibi. Nam revera nisi talis esset, nec remissio peccatorum ab eo, nec æterna vita sperarentur: & idololatræ forent ipsi Angeli qui iubentur eum adorare Psal.97.7. Heb.1 6. Quis non igitur crassam hanc ignorantiam cum summa coniunctam malitia meritò tito miretur?
units.tr: Indeed, here the providence of God shows itself to be wonderful. For by this means the wicked man obtained his wish: under this pretext Christ was condemned to death (cf. John 9:7). Yet what did he achieve? He destroyed himself with his own sword and slew the people, and he drew from the mouth of our Lord Jesus Christ the most excellent and clearest confession, that he is the true Christ, the true Son of God, and our only Saviour. Finally, he plunged himself and his people headlong into hell, but he opened heaven to us in a certain way, though beyond his intention. However Caiaphas understood this quality of the Son of God (although it is likely he did not understand well what he was saying), what he said is most true, since the name Son of God is used in a proper and special sense of the Messiah from all eternity (Ps. 2:7; 45:7; 110:2, and elsewhere). For indeed, unless he were such, neither forgiveness of sins nor eternal life could be hoped for from him, and the angels themselves, who are commanded to worship him (Ps. 97:7; Heb. 1:6), would be idolaters. Who therefore would not rightly wonder at this gross ignorance joined with the greatest malice?

units.la: Quid futurum igitur est iis qui Sanctum Spiritum personis, vocationibus, locis deniq; quibuslibet ad suum arbitrium alligant? & illis nituntur ac nominibus Præiatorum Ecclesiæ, & sola externa professione Iesu Christi quem quidem Filium Dei suumque Redemptorem vocant, sed quem minus, saltem bona pars ipsorum, quàm Caiaphas norunt?
units.tr: What, then, will become of those who bind the Holy Spirit to their own will by persons, callings, and finally by any places whatever? They rely on these and on the names of the prelates of the Church, and on the bare external profession of Jesus Christ, whom indeed they call the Son of God and their Redeemer, but whom at least a good part of them know less than Caiaphas did.

units.la: Et sane sunt illi quàm simillimi, quòd in miseros Dei filios capitis iudicia exercentes, precipuas controuersias ne leuiter quidem attingunt, sed quærunt, An credant Panem illum incantatum esse Iesum Christum, in propria persona, realiter: An Papam Ecclesiæ caput fateantur: quòd fi negatum erit, actum est, dicta sententia, nihil superest nili vt Pilato miseri tradantur: Caiaphan imitati, in eo quòd semper Principium errore maximo petunt.
units.tr: And indeed they are very much like him, in that, while exercising the judgement of the head over the wretched sons of God, they do not even lightly touch upon the chief controversies, but ask whether they believe that the bread has been enchanted into Jesus Christ himself, in his own person, really; or whether they acknowledge the Pope as head of the Church. If it is denied, the matter is done; the sentence has been given, and nothing remains but that the wretched are handed over to Pilate. In this they imitate Caiaphas, in that they always beg the principle with the greatest error.

units.la: Christus verò, licet probè perspectum hostium suorum animum haberet, & futurum euentum cognosceret, non tamè vt antea siluit: verè Christianos omnes suo exemplo docens, omnia sine vlla exceptione purœ sinceræque diuini Nominis, & eius veritatis, quum eius cognitione nos dignatur, poltponere. At videri possit simpliciter ita respondens. Tu dixisti nec inficiari nec etiam admittere propositam interrogationem: sed ex Marco perspicuum satis est, idem illud significasse acsi disertis verbis expressisset, Ego sum: vt forta ssis etiam v-
units.tr: Christ, however, although he had a thorough view of the minds of his enemies and knew the outcome to come, nevertheless did not keep silent as before. Teaching all true Christians by his example, he sets aside, without any exception, everything for the sake of the pure and sincere name of God and of his truth, since he deigns to make us partakers of that knowledge. But it might seem that he answered simply in this way: "You have said it," neither denying nor admitting the question put to him. Yet it is clear enough from Mark that he meant the same thing as if he had expressed it in plain words, "I am," so that perhaps he even

units.la: X. ij trumque dixit:quanquam illa loquendi phra-sis, affirmatio sit quadam modestia tempe-rata, qua libenter utuntur, qui modeste de se sentientes, aliquid admittunt quod ipsis sine honore & laude tribui non potest.Sic Dominus ipse non semel editis miraculis,eos qui sanati fuerant ea vulgare prohibuit, etsi miracula non ederet, ut lateren t. En igitur excellentem confessionem qua nostra fides nititur hoc uno Seruatore, tanquam vero Dei filio Patri coessentiali, & simul etiam vere fratri nostro anima & corpore, excepto peccato.
units.tr: said both. Although that form of speech is an affirmation tempered by a certain modesty, which those use willingly who, thinking modestly of themselves, admit something that cannot be ascribed to them without dishonour or praise. Thus the Lord himself, after performing miracles more than once, forbade those who had been healed to make them known, so that they would remain hidden, even though he did not perform miracles in order to hide them. Here, then, is the excellent confession on which our faith rests: this one Saviour is the true Son of God, co-essential with the Father, and at the same time truly our brother in soul and body, apart from sin.

units.la: Sed quoniam praesens ille Seruatoris nostri tam vilis & abiectus status, diuinae gloriae Maiestatique repugnabat, atque adeo splendori & magnificentiae quam de aduentu Messiae Prophetae praedixerant, necesse fuit Christum, tum ut improbos illos iudices lanciaret, tum ut scandalo Crucis, quae aliis quidem fuit offendiculo, aliis autem ludibrio, manifestum esse testimonium quo ignominiam illam breui in tantam gloriam commutandam ostenderet, ut sublimis super ipsos etiam Angelos ferretur, & Crux etiam medium esset, quo super caelos euheretur, sicut antea non semel praedixerat. Ioh.6.62.&12.28.&38.Haec igitur loquendi phrasis, Sedere ad dextram omnipotentiae Dei, id est Dei Omnipotentis, est metaphorica, ducta ab huius saeculi Monarchis, ad dextrum suum latus, Gubernatores suos collocantibus, quibus eandem ac sibi ipsis potestatem statem deferunt. Et ita de Iofepho Scriptura loquitur Genef. 41. His igitur verbis illud ipsum intelligitur quod discipulis suis perspicuè dixit à resurrectione, nempe, Datam ipsi à Patre omnem potestatem in cœlo & terra. Matth.28.18.& priùs etiam Ioh.5.27.
units.tr: But since that present state of our Saviour, so mean and abject, was at odds with the divine glory and majesty, and so with the splendour and magnificence which the prophets had foretold of the coming of the Messiah, it was necessary for Christ, both to confound those wicked judges and to make a clear testimony to the scandal of the cross, which was indeed a stumbling block to some and a mockery to others, showing that this ignominy would soon be changed into such glory that he would be raised high above even the angels, and that the cross itself would be the means by which he was lifted above the heavens, as he had foretold more than once before (John 6:62; 12:28, 38). This form of speech, "to sit at the right hand of the power of God," that is, of the Almighty God, is metaphorical, taken from the monarchs of this age, who place their governors at their right side and give them the same power as they have themselves. So Scripture speaks of Joseph (Gen. 41). Therefore by these words is understood that very thing which he plainly told his disciples from his resurrection: that all power in heaven and earth had been given to him by the Father (Matt. 28:18; and earlier also John 5:27).

units.la: Quoniam autem huius gloriæ prætextu nonnulli hodie sibi & aliis persuadent Christi corpus vbique præsens esse, tam secundùm humanitatem quàm diuinitatem,& præsertim in Sacrosancta Cœna, vel vt alij loquuntur, in Missa, notandum est in nostro Symbolo, priùs quàm de Sessione ad dextram fiat mentio, dici ipsum ascendisse in cœlos, inde tandem ad viuos & mortuos iudicandos venturum. Inde autem necessariò duo sequuntur, nempe thronum istius iurisdictionis qui cœlum ac terram continet in cœlis collocatum: & Christum secundùm suam humanitatem, (in qua & per quam diuinitas hanc dignitatem exercet per hunc vnicum Mediatorem) in ipsis residere, nunquam recessurum donec in gloria sua viuos & mortuos iudicaturus adueniat, vt non solùm iste locus, sed tota passim Scriptura testatur: quoniam vt bene quidam ex veteribus dixit, gloria nihil in humanitatis substantia mutauit, sed tantùm infirmitatem in hunc Maiestatis gradum mutauit, quo super ipsos etiam Angelos effertur. Phil.2.9. & 10.Ex illis etiam Apostolum in terra iacentem alloquutus est. Act.9.3.In iisdem vidit eum D.Stephanus. Act. 7.55. Eò nos etiam remittit ApostoloIus, Coloss.3.v.1.minimè repugnante eiusdem Christi dicto, fore nimirum se nobiscum vsque ad mundi consummationem. Matth. 28. 20. nempe, non tantùm essentiali diuinitatis suæ præsentia, & potentia sua generali & vniuersali: sed virtute & efficacia peculiari sui Spiritus, cuius respectu in suis agens, non relinquit eos orphanos. Ioh. 14.16.& 18.inhabitans in ipsis hac ratione. Ioh.14.23.Ephes.3.17. cœlitus æternæ vitæ & spiritualis arrhabonem tanquam Ecclesiæ caput inspirans Ephes.4.12. & 16. pro donorum suorum mensura.1.Cor.12.27.
units.tr: Since, however, some today, under the pretext of this glory, persuade themselves and others that the body of Christ is present everywhere, both according to his humanity and his divinity, and especially in the most holy Lord's Supper, or, as others say, in the Mass, it must be noted that in our Creed, before mention is made of his sitting at the right hand, it is said that he ascended into heaven, and thence at last will come to judge the living and the dead. From this two things necessarily follow: that the throne of that jurisdiction, which contains heaven and earth, is set in the heavens; and that Christ, according to his humanity (in which and through which the divinity exercises this dignity through this one Mediator), sits there and will never depart until he comes in his glory to judge the living and the dead. This is attested not only by this passage but by the whole of Scripture throughout. For, as one of the ancients rightly said, glory changed nothing in the substance of his humanity, but only changed his weakness into this degree of majesty, by which he is raised above even the angels (Phil. 2:9, 10). From there he addressed the apostle lying on the ground (Acts 9:3); from there Saint Stephen saw him (Acts 7:55). The apostle also refers us thither (Col. 3:1), not at all contradicting the saying of Christ himself that he will be with us to the end of the world (Matt. 28:20), namely not only by the essential presence of his divinity and his general and universal power, but by the peculiar virtue and efficacy of his Spirit, by whose agency in his own people he does not leave them orphans (John 14:16, 18), dwelling in them in this way (John 14:23; Eph. 3:17), breathing from heaven the pledge of eternal and spiritual life as head of the Church (Eph. 4:12, 16), according to the measure of his gifts (1 Cor. 12:27).

units.la: Qui quærunt igitur in terris humanitatem Christi, alij quidem eam Vbique esse affuerantes alij cam Sacrosanctæ Cœnæ Panis & Vino, alij autem accidentibus(vt loquuntur) Panis & Vini in Missa sua Transsubstantiatis alligantes, quantum in ipsis est, tres præcipuos articulos fidei penitus euertunt, quibus eorum falsitas manifestè deprehenditur: veram putà perpetuámque Filij Dei incarnationem, à conceptione in Virginis vtero inchoatam, & nunquam definentem: etsi hanc humanitatem in duplici statu nos oporteat considerare, quorum prior est exinanitionis status à conceptione initium, & in resurrectione, & supra cœlos Ascensione finem habens: alter est, summa eius & immensa gloria, ducens initium à Sessione à dextris, quum in Patris gloriam ingressus est. Alterum articulum fidei, Ascensionem supra omnes cœlos, tum Vbiquitarij, tum Transsubstantiatores ac Consubstantiatores euertunt,
units.tr: Those who therefore seek the humanity of Christ on earth are wrong. Some hold that it is everywhere present, others bind it to the bread and wine of the holy Supper, and others, the Papists, bind it to the accidents (as they call them) of bread and wine, which they transubstantiate in their Mass. In doing so, as far as they can, they utterly overturn three chief articles of faith, by which their falsehood is clearly exposed: namely the true and perpetual incarnation of the Son of God, begun in the Virgin's womb at the conception and never ending. We must consider this humanity in a twofold state. The first is the state of humiliation, which begins at the conception and ends with the resurrection and the ascension above the heavens. The second is his supreme and immeasurable glory, which begins with his session at the right hand, when he entered into the glory of the Father. The ascension above all the heavens, the second article of faith, is overturned by the Ubiquitarians, the Transubstantiators and the Consubstantiators alike.

units.la: { } Ascensione. cunt. Tertius est eiusdē reditus, visibilis & realis, coniunctus cum eius in cœlis inhabitatione vsque ad secundū aduentū, cuius hic metio fit: velipsis testibus Angelis. Act. 1. 9. & 11. & D. Petro, verbis difertissimis, Act. 3 21. articulus ille nimirum quo dicitur VENTVRVS, & quidem visibiliter, testibus his vocibus, VIDEBITIS quibus Matth. & Marcus vtuntur: & VIDEBVNT. Ioh. 19. 37.
units.tr: Ascension. The third article is his return, visible and real, joined with his indwelling in heaven until the second coming, which is what is spoken of here. The angels bear witness to it, Acts 1:9 and 11, and St Peter too, in the plainest words, Acts 3:21. That article, I mean, by which it is said that he is COMING, and indeed visibly, as the witnesses of the words YOU WILL SEE, which Matthew and Mark use, and THEY WILL SEE, John 19:37.

units.la: Ad textu autē reuersi, videmus in falsis iudicibus, & in hac tota Iudæorū gete in vniuersum consideratā, vnam ex causis præcipuis quibus increduli nec Luce ista conspiciant impediuntur, quod nimirū iudicium tantū naturale sequantur in vero à falso discernēdo, perinde facientes ac siquis de Luce supernaturali iudicet ex tenebris. Et in hoc errore Iudæi versantur adhuc, existimantes fieri nō posse vt qui adeo est exinanitus, Filius esse Dei potuerit: & à Crucifixo vitam hauriendā: licet à Prophetis vterque status iste Redeptoris dilucidissimis & expressissimis verbis sit ipsis prænuntiatus, quorum in hac historia testimonia profert Euangelista: sed nominatim Psalm. 22. & 69. & lōgè clarius apud Esa. 53. adeo vt noui Rabbini antiquioribus impudentiores, coacti gloriā & ignominiā eidē Messię tribuere, quę tamē duo cōtraria nō posse in vnā personam cadere sibi persuaderi non patiuntur, duos Messias, miserrimum vnum, gloriosum alterū & magnificum somniarint in eo suam cæcitatē & stupore patefacientes de quo Paulus agit. I.Cor. 2. 14.
units.tr: But returning to the text, we see in the false judges, and in the whole Jewish nation considered in general, one of the chief causes by which unbelievers are prevented from beholding this light: namely that they follow only natural judgement in distinguishing the true from the false, acting just as if someone should judge the supernatural light from darkness. The Jews still remain in this error, thinking it impossible that one who is so humbled could be the Son of God, and that life must be drawn from one who was crucified. Yet both states of the Redeemer were foretold to them by the Prophets in the clearest and most express words, and the Evangelist brings forward testimonies of these in this story, especially Psalms 22 and 69, and far more plainly in Isaiah 53. So much so that the newer rabbis, more shameless than the older ones, were forced to ascribe both glory and ignominy to the same Messiah. Yet, unable to bear that two contraries could not fall into one person, they dreamed up two Messiahs, one most wretched and the other glorious and magnificent. In this they reveal their blindness and stupor, of which Paul speaks, 1 Cor. 2:14.

units.la: x. iiij. Sed miseram illam miseram facientes nationem, quam vtinam Deus suo tempore respiciat, quod quasi nobis seculum hoc Atheos & Epicureos omnem religionem habentes ludibrio protulit, quod nullam suo sensui congruentem inuenant? Quot sunt μωρὸ(ὸφοι qui Sacras Scripturas ex Platone & Aristotele meditantur, vt ex suo sensu nobis nouam religionem cudant? Quot denique sunt à Religione non prorsus alieni, quos Conscientia paulò vehementius vellicat, qui tamen multitudine nobis aduersantium, & potentiam admirati: suorumque Praelatorum pompam & magnificentiam, & sui tam bene culti & exornati Iesu Christi, obstupescunt, & ab hoc Christo spinis coronato, & Euangelio cum cruce coniuncto perterriti resiliunt?
units.tr: x. iiij. But why do we, who are now made a laughing stock by atheists and Epicureans who have no religion, wish that God would look upon that wretched nation in his time? Do they not find nothing that agrees with their own sense? How many are there who are so-called wise fools [μωρόσοφοι], who study the Holy Scriptures through Plato and Aristotle, so that they may forge for us a new religion from their own sense? Finally, how many are there who are not altogether strangers to religion, whom conscience pricks rather sharply, yet who, astonished at the multitude of those opposing us and at their power, and at the pomp and magnificence of their prelates, and at their own Jesus Christ so well cultivated and adorned, shrink back in terror from this Christ crowned with thorns and from the Gospel joined to the cross?

units.la: Hic vero cauendum aliud extremum, ne nimirum ex arbitrio nostro fidei nobis articulos confingamus, & quicquid captum nostrum superat Religionis nomine velemus. Nam vt vera Fides non minus credit quàm Euangelium docet, sic etiam nihil amplius credit. At vnde praeterea non tantum pertinax non recipiendi Euangelij Religio, sed etiam immanis quaedam Dei filios persequendi nascitur audacia, nisi quòd Iesus Christus tam humilis & abiectus in membris suis crucifixus contemnitur?
units.tr: Here, however, we must guard against the other extreme, namely that we should not, at our own pleasure, invent articles of faith for ourselves, and wish to veil under the name of religion whatever exceeds our grasp. For as true faith believes no more than the Gospel teaches, so it believes nothing further. But from what else does not only a stubborn refusal to receive the Gospel arise, but also a certain savage audacity to persecute the sons of God, except that Jesus Christ, so humble and abject, is crucified and despised in his members?

units.la: Quid porrò fumus aliud omnibus istis offendiculis, tum hisce hominibus confusione obruendis, tum nobis aduersus istud scandalum
units.tr: What, moreover, are we to oppose to all these stumbling blocks, both to overwhelm these men with confusion, and to strengthen ourselves against this scandal,

units.la: confirmandis, nisi illustrem illum Domini no-stri secundum aduentum opposituri? Fateor non magis eos propterea quàm iis de quibus agimus commouendos, & quemadmodum Christus licet istis interminatus, nihilominus damnatus & crucifixus est, sic quicquid istis occinatur, non desituram tamen ab humeris nostris Crucem: at vicissim verum esse non desinet quod modo contemnunt: & suo tempore quod sanunis excipiunt in suum detestandum caput deuolui sentient, nobis contra promissam quietem & tranquillitatem in aeternum fruentibus. Agite igitur in ea spe quae nunquam confundit quiescamus, & inanem illam arrogantiam sese illa pascentibus relinquamus.
units.tr: except the illustrious second coming of our Lord? I admit that they are no more moved by this than those of whom we are speaking. And just as Christ, though threatened by them, was nevertheless condemned and crucified, so whatever is sung to them will not remove the cross from our shoulders. Yet conversely, what they now despise will not cease to be true, and in its time they will feel that what they now greedily receive as healthy is rolled back upon their own detestable head, while we enjoy the rest and tranquillity promised for eternity. Come then, let us rest in that hope which never disappoints, and leave that empty arrogance to those who feed on it.

units.la: Quoniam verò Dominus nominatim hic de ultimo illo die loquitur, quem Apostoli Petri temporibus irrisores multum tardare dicebant 2. Pet. 3. 4. tenendum nobis est, quem-admodum Dei iudicium non diu dilatum est quin Caiaphan cum sociis suis obtutum pessundaret, ita nostri temporis homines idem manere iudicium, Domino improborum poenas non semper in illum diem differente, cui tamen anima & corpore damnandis reseruantur. Nam huius vitae excessum (qui quando futurus sit incertum est) horrenda interlocutoria sententia excipit, cuius apud Lucam 16.22. mentio fit: adde quòd etiam in hac vita coguntur homines iusmodi lugere & dentibus stridere, in illorum etiam oculis quos antea tamen irridebant. Atque, oro vos,quot iam ante oculos nostros hodie conspicimus ciuf- modi iudicia, & quàm multa nostro seculo i- mo ab hinc anno, aduersus summæ & infimæ conditionis homines conspeximus? Ergo vi- gilemus, diémque illum Domini particula- rem aut vniucrfalem exspectemus, vt filij Lu- cis cum lampadibus nostris ardentibus incc- dentes, vt sapientes illæ virgines, de quibus mentio fit, Matth. 25. 7. & 10. & improbis ri- dentibus & exsultantibus, huius diei nos ex- spectatione in fletu nostro & lachrymis,eo de- mum die siccandis,consolemur.
units.tr: Since the Lord here speaks expressly of that last day, which the mockers in the time of the Apostle Peter said would be long delayed (2 Pet. 3:4), we must hold that, just as God's judgement was not long deferred before it overthrew Caiaphas with his companions, so the same judgement remains for the people of our own time. The Lord does not always defer the punishment of the wicked to that day, to which, nevertheless, the condemned are reserved, both in soul and in body. For at the departure from this life (when it will be is uncertain) there follows a dreadful interlocutory sentence, mentioned in Luke 16:22. Add to this that even in this life such people are compelled to mourn and gnash their teeth, in the sight of those whom they had earlier mocked. And, I beg you, how many such judgements do we see today before our eyes, and how many have we seen in our own age, indeed only this year, against men of the highest and the lowest condition? Therefore let us watch, and let us await that day of the Lord, whether particular or universal, so that, walking as sons of the light with our lamps burning, like those wise virgins mentioned in Matthew 25:7 and 10, while the wicked laugh and exult, we may console ourselves in our weeping and tears, which will at last be dried on that day, by the expectation of this day.

units.la: Euangelistæ deinceps narrant istum hypo- criram,quem ad Domini responsum oportue- rat horrescere,purà,cum irreuocabili commi- natione coniunctum, vestimenta laceraffe, quod erat in summo luctu tantum vsitatum, quum tamen improbus corde magnopere læ- taretur, quasi consilij fui detetlandi ad finem deducendi nactus quam quærebat occasio- nem. Erat igitur non tantum apud Orientales populos, sed apud alias exteras gentes iftc ge- ftus in maximis luctibus vsitatissimus,vt vete- res testantur historici, velut in lugendis mor- tuis, quod ex Iacobi, Iofephum deflentis hi- storia fatis est conspicuum, Genef.37. 34. Etsi veroDominus mortuorum luctui inter popu- lum suum modum posuit, Leuit.19.verf.27. & Deut.14.1.hanc tamen veitium laceratiouem fohis Sacerdotibus hoc casu prohibitam fuisse colligi videtur ex Leuit.10.6. Idcirco Dauid in
units.tr: The Evangelists next relate that this hypocrite, who ought to have shuddered at the Lord's answer, joined with a plain and irrevocable threat, tore his garments. This was the common sign of the deepest mourning, although the wicked man in his heart was greatly rejoicing, as if he had found the occasion he sought for bringing his detestable purpose to an end. This gesture was therefore very commonly used in the greatest mourning not only among the Eastern peoples but among other foreign nations also, as the ancient historians testify, as in the mourning for the dead. This is clear enough from the history of Jacob lamenting Joseph, Gen. 37:34. Yet although the Lord set a limit to mourning for the dead among his people, Lev. 19:27 and Deut. 14:1, it seems to be gathered from Lev. 10:6 that the tearing of garments was forbidden to the priests alone in that case. Hence David, in

units.la: Abneri (epultura 2.Sam.3.verf.31.populum ad vestium lacerationem inuitat. At hic de re longè maioris momenti,de Dei nimirum honore & gloria, quam hic hypocrita sibi fingit à Domino Iesu Christo fuisse læsam agitur: quo calu tantùm abest, vt tristitiæ & ægritudinis testimonium Domino displicuerit, vt contrà, qui Prophetæ librum scalpello vidfirst rant à Regè Iohachino lacerari, & in ignem abiici, nec tamen expauerant, veltéfue lacerauerant grauiter reprehendantur, Ier.36.24. & Iofias contrà coram Domino laceratis vestibus fe abiiciens magnopere commendetur. 2. Reg.22.19.
units.tr: the burial of Abner, 2 Sam. 3:31, urges the people to tear their clothes. But here the matter concerns something of far greater importance, namely the honour and glory of God, which this hypocrite imagines has been injured by the Lord Jesus Christ. In this case the sign of sorrow and grief is so far from displeasing the Lord that, on the contrary, those who saw the Prophet's book cut with a knife by King Jehoiakim and cast into the fire, and yet did not tremble, or even tore it, are severely rebuked, Jer. 36:24. And Josiah, on the contrary, who cast himself down before the Lord with torn garments, is greatly commended, 2 Kings 22:19.

units.la: Ac sanè quo vulnere magis affici saucia- ríque nos decet quàm quum Dei gloriam læ-di vel aspicimus, vel audimus? Sic iustum Lotum habitantem inter Sodomitas, in dies animam iustam iniquis illorum factis & videndo & audiendo excruciasse dicit Apostolus 2.Petr.2.verf.8. Sic Dauid de fe tettatur, fe quum ab hostibus hæc audiret, Vbi nunc Deus tuus est, veluti pugionibus pectus & imas medullas fuisse traiectum.Pfalm.42.verf.3.Et reuera quum de Deo, fiue priuatim fiue publicè honorando agitur: fiue de zelo palàm testando quo quum dedecoratur ardere nos oportet,Deo & hominibus fieri conspicuos exteriore aliquo signo interiores motus æquum est: vt Dauidi coram arca Domini extraordinariè saltanti contigisse legimus. 2. Sam. 14. verf. 6. Verùm hac in re certus adhibendus modus & ædificationis habenda ratio: quòd plerumque contingat eos qui pluribus iftiuf-modi gestibus abundant, parum tamen adferre veri zeli ac religionis, quod ipsum Dominus per Prophetam arguit his verbis, Frangite, inquit, corda vestra, non autem vestimenta. Ioel.2.13. At, fratres, quid hic oro vos, dicturi fumus? Annon est iste perfidus hypocrita in summo illo & ultimo iudicio aduersum nos iudex surrecturus? Tempus fuit, & illud memoria repeto, quum, fi Geneuæ quis, vel peregrinus deieraffet, omnes commouerentur, terramque ille deosculari cogeretur: noftis, inquam, probè, etiam ex vicinis nobilibus quosdam in carcerem propterea coniectos. At, ô tempora, ô hominum mores, præsertim à coepto bello, quot modis sacrosanctum Dei nomen impune polluitur? quot horrendæ deierationes, blasphemiaque abominandæ passim audiuntur? Quis verò commouetur? quis reprehendit? quis deferet? quis etiam rogatus testatur? Scio fuisse publicum in miseris duobus & ignaris editum exemplum: sed quid duo illi ad aliorum prorsus inexcusabilium tantam multitudinem? Excipiat aliquis, illos non dignosci: & non inuitus credo parui fieri deierantes, tantum abest vt reprehendantur aut deferantur, sic iam paucis annis istis flagitiis assueuimus. An verò putamus coram Deo locum excusationi fore? Legimus in historia celebrati illius Achabi, quum Nabotho in medio populo Israëlis blasphemiæ fuisset crimen per calumcalumniam impactum, etsi desciuerat populus à vero & legitimo Dei cultu, tamen indictum publicè fuisse ieiunium ad blasphemiæ illius Nabotho tamen per calumniam impositæ detestationem. Quam igitur excusationem nos qui Reformatam Religionem profitemur, coram Domino fumus allaturi? Atque adeò si ab hoc malo prorsus immunes essemus, quum tamen hodie & procul & ad mœnia nostra fœteat aër impurissimis & horrendissimis deierationibus & blasphemiis omnium hinc inde nationum, quales nunquam vel ipse tartarus cogitauit, aut audiuit, an non illis percelli & vri nos oportuit, ad exemplum Apostoli 2. Corinth. 11. 29. an non, inquam decuit nos lachrymis & gemitibus iram Dei, Ezechiæ Regis ad exemplum auditis Rapsaces blasphemiis auertere? 2. Reg. 19. 15. & 16. & Esa. 37. 3. & 4. Vah, quàm multæ nos ad id ipsum, fiquid alias, vnquam, impellunt? Sed quàm metuo ne nobis illa potius Domini Ichouæ exercituum verba conueniant, Vocaui vos in illo tempore ad fletum & ad planctum, & ad calluitium, & ad cincturam cilicij: Ecce vero lætitiam & gaudium: occiduntur boues & iugulantur pecudes, comeduntur carnes & bibitur vinum, dicendo, edamus, & bibamus, cras enim moriemur. Quid ad hæc vero Dominus? Si vnquam, inquit, expietur ista iniquitas vobis, donec moriamini. Annon, inquam, nos ij sumus. Nam etsi non idem est omnium sermo, non eædem voces, an non tamen vitæ ratio quid quisque corde premat satis apertè testatur? Euge verò, si vestes hoc luctuosissimo & calamitosissimo tempore non laceramus, nec ciliciis induimur, quum ignari Papistæ supplicationes diis suis nudis pedibus decernant, saltem ne tot nouarum vestium, tot nouas formas ostentaremus, & vanitatibus vanitatum indulgeremus, quarum testes oculati fumus omnes, nec tamen commouemur: eò iam erumpente vel tenuiorum & infimæ sortis hominum lasciuia, vt passim in holosericis vestibus conspiciantur. Admitto non omnes qui sericis induuntur, pretio argenti numerato coemisse: at fortasse prius quàm hic ludus desinat, magno sibi constitutae sentient. Denique, nonne similes fumus temporibus Noachi? Siquis verò fuit ab initio bonus ordo tot rebus superfluis & indecentibus, immo calamitosis istis temporibus penitus intolerandis, constitutus emendandis & corrigendis, qui factum est vt in quorundam superborum gratiam, tum virorum tum mulierum tam repente concideret? Quid profuit certum menis numerum præscripsisse, nisi vt in petenda venia plus esset laboris? Faxit verò Deus, vt terras inundante diluuio, Noachus cum sua familia saluus enatet. Ad textum autem reuersi, videamus vt Dei prouidetia, perditus iste hypocrita sibi maculam indelebilem inflerit. Blasphemiam detestatus vestimeta sua lacerat. Et sane blasphemia hic tanta fuit quanta vix in mente hominis nis veniat: non quidem à Christo, sed ab ipso Caiapha, blasphemiâ Dei æterno filio impingente, qui tamen sine macula vlla fuit, & contrà blasphemiarum est rigidus vltor ac vindex. Quamobrem hæc vestium laceratio est, & erit perpetuum coram Domino & sanctis eius Angelis, & coram Ecclesia Dei, testimonium Caiaphæ aduersus scipsum, sic in ipsum à Domino retorto flagitio. Obseruandum præterea horrendum Dei aduersus perditum istum & eius socios iudicium. Quid enim, Caiapha, laceratis vestibus effecisti? Nimirum præter opinionem & ambitionem tuam Sacerdotio teipsum exuisti. Tu iterum ignarus & præter mentem vt loquitur Apostolus, Act.13.27. quod erat paulo post perficiendum, nempe Sacerdotij Aaronici finem prædixisti, quod tu tuique similes tam multis annis miserè polluepaтis: & præter mentè eū, quē nefariè tanquā blasphemum condemnasti, verum & æternū sacerdotem, secundum ordinem veri Melchisedeci constituisti. Adeò est Dominus Deus noster tam in misericordiis suis ex mera ipsius gratia, quàm in horrendis iudiciis aduersus impios, per eosdem quoties sic illi visum est admirandus.
units.tr: Indeed, with what wound ought we to be more affected and wounded than when we see or hear that the glory of God is injured? The Apostle says that the righteous Lot, living among the Sodomites, tormented his righteous soul day by day with their lawless deeds, both by seeing and by hearing them (2 Pet. 2:8). David, when he heard from his enemies, "Where now is your God?", describes himself as pierced to the heart and to the innermost marrow, as with daggers (Ps. 42:3). And truly, when the honour of God is in question, whether privately or publicly, and when we speak of the zeal that we ought to burn with when God is dishonoured, it is right that our inner feelings should be made visible to God and men by some outward sign, as we read happened to David when he leapt and danced before the ark of the Lord (2 Sam. 6:14, 16). Yet in this matter a certain measure must be observed, and regard must be had for edification. For it commonly happens that those who abound in many gestures of this kind bring little true zeal or religion, which the Lord himself rebukes through the Prophet in these words: "Rend your hearts, not your garments" (Joel 2:13). But, brethren, what, I ask you, are we about to say here? Will not that treacherous hypocrite rise up as judge against us at the last and great judgment? There was a time, and I recall it to memory, when, if anyone at Geneva, even a stranger, swore an oath, all were stirred, and he was made to kiss the ground. You know well, I say, that some of the noble men from the neighbourhood were thrown into prison for this very reason. But, O the times, O the manners of men, especially since the war began, in how many ways is the holy name of God polluted with impunity? How many horrible oaths and abominable blasphemies are heard everywhere? Who is moved? Who rebukes? Who reports it? Who, even when asked, bears witness? I know that a public example was made of two wretched and ignorant men; but what are two men against so vast a multitude of others who are utterly inexcusable? Someone may object that those men were not recognised, and I do not doubt that many swear unwillingly, though they are not rebuked or reported at all, so much have we in these few years grown accustomed to these crimes. But do we really think there will be room for excuse before God? We read in the history of that famous Ahab that when blasphemy was falsely laid against Naboth in the midst of the people of Israel, although the people had fallen away from the true and lawful worship of God, nevertheless a public fast was proclaimed in detestation of that blasphemy falsely imputed to Naboth. What excuse then shall we who profess the Reformed religion bring before the Lord? And if we were wholly free from this evil, yet today, when the air both far and near, even at our very walls, reeks with the most foul and horrible oaths and blasphemies of all nations on every side, such as not even Tartarus itself ever imagined or heard of, ought we not to be struck down and burned by them, after the example of the Apostle (2 Cor. 11:29)? Ought we not, I say, with tears and groans, to turn away the wrath of God, after the example of King Hezekiah, when he heard the blasphemies of Rabshakeh (2 Kings 19:15-16; Isa. 37:3-4)? Alas, how many things drive us to this very thing, if anything ever did! But I fear that rather those words of the Lord of hosts, Jehovah, apply to us: "In that day I called you to weeping and to mourning, and to baldness and to girding with sackcloth. Behold rather joy and gladness: oxen are slain and sheep are killed, flesh is eaten and wine is drunk, saying, Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die." What does the Lord say in reply? "Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till you die" (Isa. 22:12-14). Are we not, I say, those people? For although not everyone speaks the same words, and the voices are not the same, does not the manner of life clearly enough show what each one hides in his heart? Well then, if we do not rend our garments in this most mournful and calamitous time, nor clothe ourselves in sackcloth, while the ignorant Papists decree supplications to their gods with bare feet, at least let us not display so many new clothes and so many new fashions, and indulge in vanities of vanities, of which we are all eyewitnesses, and yet are not moved. Now the wantonness even of the poorer and lowest sort of people has broken out so far that they are seen everywhere in silken garments. I grant that not all who wear silk bought it with silver counted out; but perhaps, before this game ends, they will find it has cost them dearly. Finally, are we not like the times of Noah? And if there was once a good order established to correct and restrain so many superfluous and unseemly things, which in these calamitous times are utterly intolerable, how has it come about that it has fallen so suddenly, for the favour of some proud men, both men and women? What good was it to prescribe a fixed number of ... unless it were to make the obtaining of pardon more difficult? May God grant, however, that when the earth is flooded by the deluge, Noah with his family may swim safe through. But returning to the text, let us see how that lost hypocrite, through God's providence, has inflicted on himself an indelible stain. He tears his clothes, detesting the blasphemy. And indeed the blasphemy here was so great that it can scarcely come into a man's mind; not, indeed, uttered by Christ, but by Caiaphas himself, who hurled blasphemy against the eternal Son of God, though Christ was without any stain, and is, on the contrary, the stern avenger and punisher of blasphemies. Therefore this tearing of the garments is, and will remain, before the Lord and his holy angels, and before the Church of God, a testimony of Caiaphas against himself, the crime being turned back by the Lord upon him. Moreover, we should observe the dreadful judgment of God against this lost man and his companions. For what, Caiaphas, did you accomplish by tearing your garments? Surely, contrary to your own opinion and ambition, you stripped yourself of the priesthood. Again, ignorant and beyond your own intention, as the Apostle says (Acts 13:27), you foretold what was to be accomplished shortly after, namely the end of the Aaronic priesthood, which you and those like you have so wretchedly polluted for so many years; and beyond your intention, you appointed as the true and eternal priest, according to the order of Melchizedek, him whom you wickedly condemned as a blasphemer. So great is our Lord God, admirable both in his mercies, which flow from his pure grace, and in his dreadful judgments against the wicked, whenever it pleases him to act in these ways.

units.la: De Blasphemiæ crimine verò, vox ipsa Blasphemandi, quum in Dei maiestatem directè feratur, satis oltendit idem esse ac famam lædere, aut detrahere & iniurium esse, aut Deo detrahendo quod illi proprium est & Maiestatis plenum: aut contra tribuendo quod ab eius natura penitus est alienum. Crimen igitur est læsæ Maiestatis diuinæ, siue id verbis, siue gestu fiat, vt scriptum est Leuit.24. 15.&16. & Num.15 30. vbi manus elatæ mentio fit, quod minantium signum est. Fateor non quicunque blasphemiam dicit, reipsa necessario blasphemum esse. Sæpe fit enim vt alterius inducta persona quis loquatur, vt quum dicit Dauid, impium in corde suo dicere, Non esse Deum. Hic vero magnum requiritur iudicium, ne temere sæpius repetatur quod semel dictum nimium est: Dauide nos docente religioni nobis esse debere vel falsorum nomina deorum ore pronuntiare. Psal.16.4. Nec etiam ille mendax habendus est, qui falsum aliquid dixerit, quod vel ipse non affirmet, vel quod esse verum existimet. Fieri etiam potest vt Turca vel Iudæus, minime quidem animo mentiendi, sed religionem suam veram arbitratus aliquid effutiat sine blasphemia, quod Christianus, licet imperitus non possit dicere sine blasphemia. Sed quicquid sit, in se blasphemia semper est blasphemia: teste Apostolo, sei-psum blasphemum agnoscente, licet ignoras, in Pharisaismo peccasset. 1.Timoth.1. 13. prædicente etiam Domino, multos istiusmodi homines zelo sine scientia peccantes, se Deo cultum præstare putaturos. Iohan.16.2. At quum Deus hominem istiusmodi melius edocuit, & ad agnitionem peccati adduxit, tantum abest vt excusare se debeat, quin eum cum Apostolo lugere potius oporteat. Quod si centesimam partem eius studij collocarent homines in cognoscendis iis quae de Deo & eius cultu sciri oportet, quod huius mundi honoribus & bonis cumulandis impendunt, nullus esset in blasphemia locus ignorantiae. Ac sane quisquis repugnans aliquid effutit ei quod naturaliter homines de Deo norunt, & de quo loquitur Apostolus. Act. 14. verf. 17. & Rom. 1. verf. 20. blasphemus est inexcusabilis.
units.tr: Concerning the crime of blasphemy, the very word "to blaspheme", when it is directed straight against the majesty of God, sufficiently shows that it means to injure or defame, and to do wrong, either by taking away from God what is proper to him and full of majesty, or on the contrary by ascribing to him what is wholly alien to his nature. Blasphemy is therefore a crime of injured divine majesty, whether it is committed by words or by gesture, as is written in Leviticus 24:15-16 and Numbers 15:30, where mention is made of a raised hand, which is the sign of those who threaten. I grant that whoever speaks blasphemy is not necessarily in fact a blasphemer. For it often happens that someone speaks in the person of another, as when David says that the impious man says in his heart, "There is no God" (Ps. 14:1). Here, however, great judgment is required, lest what has once been said too rashly be repeated too often; David teaches us that it ought to be a matter of religion for us not even to pronounce the names of false gods with our mouth (Ps. 16:4). Nor should he be held a liar who says something false which he himself does not affirm, or which he thinks to be true. It may also happen that a Turk or a Jew, with no intention of lying at all, but believing his own religion to be true, utters something without blasphemy which a Christian, even an unlearned one, could not say without blasphemy. But whatever the case, blasphemy is always blasphemy in itself: the Apostle bears witness that he acknowledged himself a blasphemer, though he had sinned in ignorance in his Pharisaism (1 Tim. 1:13), and the Lord also foretells that many such men, sinning from zeal without knowledge, will think they are offering service to God (John 16:2). But when God has taught such a man better and led him to the knowledge of his sin, it is so far from his being able to excuse himself that he ought rather to mourn with the Apostle. If men devoted even a hundredth part of the effort to knowing what ought to be known about God and his worship that they spend on heaping up the honours and goods of this world, there would be no room for blasphemy through ignorance. And indeed whoever utters anything contrary to what men naturally know about God, of which the Apostle speaks (Acts 14:17; Rom. 1:20), is an inexcusable blasphemer.

units.la: At vicissim fi Regibus & Magistratibus ini- essêt vel millesima particula, zeli illius quo in sua dignitate tuenda, & merito quidem flagrant, in laesae Maiestatis diuinae crimine puniendo, nae longe graviores & seueriores poenas blasphemis positas, & longe maiorem in iis obseruandis diligentiam videremus. Nihilominus tamen si quod Legislatoris auctoritas pondus habet, annon ipse Iehoua, Deus aeternus Legem capitis aduersus blasphemiam, etiam in ira pronuntiatam posuit? Leuit. 34. 14. & 23. Quod si ex criminis natura poena etiam est constituenda, quis, nisi summa cum impudentia negauerit, (quum Dei Maiestas longe sit rebus omnibus quantumuis excellentibus pretiosior) blasphemiam omnium criminum quibus ab hominibus homines laedi possunt atrocissimum? Ergo vt volent homines de blasphemia iudicium ferant: & pro arbitrio suo poenas moderentur, aio tamen aliter Deum de blasphemis, & de iis qui tamopere ipsis parcunt, esse iudicaturum.
units.tr: On the other hand, if kings and magistrates had even a thousandth part of that zeal which they rightly feel in defending their own dignity, and in punishing the crime of injured divine majesty, we would see far heavier and more severe penalties laid down for blasphemers, and much greater diligence in enforcing them. Yet if the authority of the Lawgiver carries any weight, did not Jehovah, the eternal God himself, enact a capital law against blasphemy, pronouncing it even in anger? Lev. 24. 14. & 23. And if the penalty must be fixed according to the nature of the crime, who, unless he denies it with the utmost shamelessness, would not admit that blasphemy is the most atrocious of all crimes by which men can injure one another, since the majesty of God far surpasses all things, however excellent and precious? Let men, then, pass judgment on blasphemy as they wish, and moderate the penalties at their own pleasure; I maintain, however, that God will judge otherwise concerning blasphemers, and concerning those who spare them so readily.

units.la: Sed prae reliquis omnibus horrenda quaedam est & stupenda blasphemia in Spiritum . Sanctum nunquam remittenda. Matth.12. 31. & 32. Marc. 3. 29. Luc.12. 10. 1.Ioh. 5.13.de qua suum aliquid dicturus, tum vt sibi quisque caueat ne in tam horrendum peccatum incidat, tum ad conscientias, quas haec tentatio premit, consolandas. In primis autem tenendum peccatorum omnium, etiam leuissimorum, si quae dici leuia possunt, stipendium esse mortem aeternam, Apostolo teste, Rom.6.23. & Iac. 1.15. contra vero gratiae & misericordiae Dei respectu, nullum adeo magnum esse peccatum quod non delcat is qui mundi peccata tollit. Ioh.1.29. & qui peccata nostra pertulit in corpore suo super lignum.1.Pet.2. 24. ita vt nulla sit in iis condemnatio qui sunt in Christo Iesu.Rom.8.1. & Coloss.1. 22. excepto vnico illo Peccato in Spiritum Sanctum, quod peccatum ad mortem vocatur: non quod sua natura reliqua omnia mortalia non sint, sed quod quum illud nunquam remittatur, mortem aeternam secum necessario trahat: quum reliqua sua natura mortalia fiant venalia, & ab eo remittatur qui pro peccatis nostris est propitiatio. 1.Ioh.2.2. Vt vero quale illud sit nouerimus, & ab eo nobis caueamus, sic nominari sciendum est non simpliciter Sancti Spiritus personae respectu. (Nulla enim est inter Diuinitatis personas inaequalitas: & qui ex tribus vnam laedit, Diuinitatem laedit) sed operationis S. Spiritus propriae, qua mentes nostras in veri Dei Patris, Filij & Sp. Sancti cognitionem illustrat, & doctrinam nostrae salutis in Domino nostro Iesu Christo Hcb. 6. 13. Peccatum igitur illud veritatis cognitionem præsupponit, vt discrte docet Apostolus ad Heb. 6. 4. Præterea voce Blasphemiæ notatur tam horrendum illud peccatum, nö in eorum esse numero quæ aduersus secundam tabulam admittuntur, nimirum contra proximum, etsi non læditur proximus quin Deus etiam offendatur: nec præterea comprehendi peccata quæ recta in primam tabulam feruntur, peccantibus hominibus infirmitate, quod iustissimis & maximè regeneratis sæpe contingit, vel illis testibus lapsibus, in quos incidisse Iobus, Abraham, Sara, Iacobus, Moses, Aaron, Dauid, Petrus in sacris memorantur, ex quorum numero se nemini liceat eximere, vel ipso teste dilecto Domini discipulo, seipsum hoc numero non eximente. 1. Ioh. 1. 8. Absit igitur vt quicunque contra conscientiam peccat huius peccati, nūquam remittendi, reus esse dicatur. Quis enim si hoc ita foret, seruaretur? Quorsum vero singulis momentis Remissionem peccatorum implorare doceremur, si nunquâ illa remitterentur? His ita positis non erit intellectu difficile quale sit peccatum istud, nēpe esse nō alicuius mandati certam transgressionem sed generalem apostasiam à Deo, ex certa & destinata malitia profectam, & cum odio Dei & veritatis eius coniunctam ad quodlibet facinus & flagitium aduersus eum admittendum. Exempli gratia, Satan & eius Angeli sola sua destinata malitia & peruicaci-
units.tr: But beyond all others there is a certain horrible and astonishing blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, which is never to be forgiven. Matt. 12. 31. & 32. Mark 3. 29. Luke 12. 10. 1 John 5. 13. I shall say something about it, both so that each of us may take care not to fall into so dreadful a sin, and so that consciences oppressed by this temptation may be comforted. Above all, we must hold that the wages of all sins, even the slightest (if any sins can be called slight), is eternal death, as the Apostle testifies, Rom. 6. 23. and James 1. 15. Yet, with regard to the grace and mercy of God, there is no sin so great that he who takes away the sins of the world does not blot it out, John 1. 29., and he who bore our sins in his own body on the tree, 1 Pet. 2. 24., so that there is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, Rom. 8. 1. and Col. 1. 22. The one exception is that sin against the Holy Spirit, which is called a sin unto death. This is not because by its nature it is not mortal, as all the others are, but because, since it is never forgiven, it necessarily draws eternal death after it; whereas the rest, though mortal by nature, become venial and are forgiven by him who is the propitiation for our sins, 1 John 2. 2. So that we may know what that sin is, and guard ourselves against it, we must understand that it is named not with respect to the person of the Holy Spirit simply (for there is no inequality among the persons of the Godhead, and whoever injures one of the three injures the Godhead), but with respect to the proper operation of the Holy Spirit, by which he enlightens our minds to know the true God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and the doctrine of our salvation in our Lord Jesus Christ, Heb. 6. 13. That sin therefore presupposes knowledge of the truth, as the Apostle clearly teaches in Heb. 6. 4. Moreover, by the word blasphemy that horrible sin is marked as not belonging to the number of those committed against the second table, namely against one's neighbour, although a neighbour is not injured without God also being offended. Nor are included those sins that are directed straight against the first table and are committed through human weakness, which very often happens even to the most just and most regenerate, or those well-known falls into which Job, Abraham, Sarah, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, David and Peter are recorded in Scripture as having fallen, and from whose number no one may think himself exempt; indeed the beloved disciple of the Lord himself, as his own witness, does not exempt himself from this number, 1 John 1. 8. Far be it, then, that whoever sins against conscience in this sin, which is never to be forgiven, should be called guilty. For if this were so, who would be saved? And why would we be taught to pray daily for the remission of sins, if they were never remitted? With these things laid down, it will not be hard to understand what sort of sin this is: it is not a certain transgression of some commandment, but a general apostasy from God, arising from a fixed and deliberate malice, and joined with hatred of God and his truth, so that one is ready to commit any crime or outrage against him. For example, Satan and his angels, by their deliberate malice and stubborn obstinacy alone, assail God and his truth, which from the beginning has tempted the first man to his fall.

units.la: y. ij. tate Deum eiúsque veritatem oppugnant, qua iam inde ab initio primum hominem ad lapsum sollicitauit. Tales fuerunt etiam ílli scelerati, quos, quum plus satis tum operibus tum Christi doctrina conuincerentur, solo Dei tamen & veritatis eius odio compulsos, malitiosè seipsos & alios excæcantes, non puduit horrendam illam blasphemiam euomere, Iesu Christo cum Diabolis conuenire. Talis & improbus ille fuit Caiaphas, & longè adhuc peior, vt ita dicam, cum reliquis illis suis sociis, vt qui Dei Filium blasphemiæ arguere & condemnare aulus sit, & iustorum iustissimum, qualem ipsum vel inuiti cognoscebat. At quinam, obsecro, feruntur homines in tam profundum abyssum præcipites? Seipsos nempe indurantes paulatim, & ita Sanctum Spiritum contristantes vt non modò ad tempus docere & consolari desinat (quod ipsi Dauidi peccato suo tam diu indormienti contigit. Psal.51.12.& 77.3.& 4) sed etiam nunquam rediturus discedat, adeò vt peior sit hominum istiusmodi conditio posterior priore, quæ satis istos Christus Dominus præmonuerat. Matth. 12.43.
units.tr: Such also were those wicked men who, though they were more than sufficiently convicted both by his works and by the teaching of Christ, yet, driven only by hatred of God and his truth, maliciously blinding both themselves and others, were not ashamed to vomit forth that horrible blasphemy, that Jesus Christ was in league with the devils. Such, too, was that wicked man Caiaphas, and, to put it so, far worse than the rest of his companions, since he dared to charge the Son of God with blasphemy and to condemn him, the most just of the just, whom even against his will he knew to be such. But, I ask, into what depths of this abyss do men plunge headlong? Clearly, by hardening themselves gradually, and so grieving the Holy Spirit that he not only ceases for a time to teach and comfort them (as happened to David himself, who slumbered so long in his sin, Ps. 51. 12. & 77. 3. & 4.), but departs and never returns; so that the later condition of such men is worse than the earlier, as Christ the Lord had already warned them, Matt. 12. 43.

units.la: Quid igitur opus est facto? Nempe vigilandum, orandū, electio & vocatio magis ac magis à nobis confirmanda, tanquam Dei filiis & Lucis.2.Pet.1.10. Lapsus verò si quis aut negligentia, aut alio errore quodam contigerit, minime desperandum, sed colligendæ vires, & licet non is sit ardor, quem adesse oporteret, subinde tamen nouis stimulis excitandus est, dum ille Consolator reuertatur. An vero re-uersurus est? Omnino sane. Nam quum electio sola Dei voluntate nitatur immutabili, esse-ctum suum sortiatur necesse est ac proinde licet electi graui lapsu cadant, nunquam tamen excidunt, ac proinde nunquam illis à peccato lethale vulnus infligitur, etsi Satan filiorum Dei coniuratus hostis hac eos plurimum ten-tatione sollicitet: cui consolatio illa quam Dauid ipse nobis in sua persona patefacit est opponenda, Psal. 42. toto. & Psal. 77. 6. & sequent. & firma conclusio faciend̄a ex salutis certitudine & Spiritus sancti rediuiua gratia, quod quum donum illud Dei, Spiritus nimi-rum adoptionis solis electis datur. Rom. 8.16. nunquam etiam tollatur ab eis, licet ad tempus non magis quàm in infante ratio, aut intellectus ac ratiocinatio in ebrio conspiciatur En, quibus armis illa propulsanda tentatio sit, cuius non poterit non esse felix exitus, quum qui suos in inferos demittit, eosdem etiam ipse reducat 1.Sam.2.6. ex boni illius ac summi Pastoris promissione, qui nullam ouium quas Pater ei donauit, foras eiicit, Ioh. 17. 12. & 20. & 24. Nam qui eius se ouili subducunt, verè nunquam ex eo sed specie tenus fuerunt, hoc testante dilecto illo discipulo, de Iuda prodi-tore & eius similibus verba facientc. 1. Ioh. 2. 19. Quid amplius igitur? Nempe propria ipsa nobis conscientia licet peccati sensu grauiter afflicta, resurgendi simul & nouas vires recipit. piendi modum suppeditat. Quisquis enim in hac tentatione Deum à se offensum dolet, & cum in se poenitentiae & precationis ardorem ac motum qualem vellet non sentit, ex hoc ipso mœrore certò potest colligere, fe ex Dei filiorum esse numero, & ab eius Spiritus gratia non alienum. Quis enim dolere nos ex Dei offensa docet, quis mœrere quod bonum non faciamus quod volumus, nisi Dei Spiritus? Huius rei testis esto luGta illa quam in seipso Paulus nobis proponit. Rom. 7. 19. 24. & 25. Et hæc quidem de graui hac quæstione hactenus.
units.tr: What, then, must be done? Clearly, we must watch and pray, and make our election and calling more and more sure, as children of God and of the Light, 2 Pet. 1. 10. If anyone falls through negligence or some other error, he must by no means despair, but must gather his strength; and although the ardour that ought to be present may not be there, he must nevertheless be roused from time to time with fresh goads, until that Comforter returns. But will he return? Certainly. For since election rests solely on the unchangeable will of God, it must necessarily obtain its effect; and therefore, although the elect may fall with a grievous fall, they never fall away, and so a deadly wound from sin is never inflicted on them, even though Satan, the sworn enemy of the sons of God, harasses them greatly with this temptation. Against this we must set the consolation that David himself reveals to us in his own person, Ps. 42. throughout, and Ps. 77. 6. and following, and we must draw a firm conclusion from the certainty of salvation and the renewing grace of the Holy Spirit, since that gift of God, namely the Spirit of adoption, is given to the elect alone, Rom. 8. 16., and is never taken away from them, although for a time it is no more visible than reason is visible in an infant, or understanding and reasoning in a drunken man. Behold the weapons by which this temptation is to be repelled, and its outcome cannot fail to be happy, since he who casts his own down to the depths also brings them back again, 1 Sam. 2. 6., according to the promise of that good and chief Shepherd, who casts out none of the sheep that the Father has given him, John 17. 12. & 20. & 24. For those who withdraw from his fold were never truly his, but only in appearance, as the beloved disciple testifies when speaking of Judas the traitor and his like, 1 John 2. 19. What more, then? Conscience itself, though grievously afflicted by the sense of sin, both rises again and receives new strength, and it supplies the manner of rising. For whoever in this temptation grieves that God is offended by him, and does not feel in himself the ardour and motion of repentance and prayer such as he would wish, may certainly infer from this very sorrow that he is among the number of God's children and not estranged from the grace of his Spirit. For who teaches us to grieve at God's offence, who makes us sorrow that we do not do the good we want, unless it is the Spirit of God? Let the struggle that Paul sets before us in his own person be a witness to this, Rom. 7. 19. 24. & 25. And so much for this grave question.

units.la: Narrant deinceps Euangelistæ Christum Dominum nostrum, communibus istius Consessus suffragiis, ad capitis supplicium tanquam blasphemum condemnatum. Quid ad hæc dicturi sunt igitur, qui Concilia non posse errare iactitant, quæ tamen Sanctus ille Pater Romanus convocaverit, & quibus præfuerit? Quid inquam, refutatione dignum allaturi sunt? Nisi forte, tam sunt insigniter periti, ut impudentissimum mendacium, purissimam esse veritatem persuadere nobis possint: Sacerdotium nimirum secundum ordinem Melchisedeci, quod primo finem attulit, nempe Leuitica, successioni esse obnoxiu, ut fuit primum illud Leuiticum: hanc successionem firmioribus nixi promissionibus Sancti Spiritus sine vlla distinctione quàm priorem illam Leuiticam: Petrum huius esse Successionis caput: hanc Successionem vrbi Romæ inhærere: denique Sancti
units.tr: The Evangelists next relate that our Lord Christ was condemned to the punishment of the cross as a blasphemer, by the common votes of that assembly. What, then, will those say who boast that councils cannot err, councils which that holy Roman Father convened and presided over? What, I ask, will they bring forward that is worth refuting? Unless perhaps they are so remarkably skilled that they can persuade us that the most shameless lie is the purest truth: namely, that the priesthood according to the order of Melchisedec, which at first had the Levitical priesthood as its end, is subject to succession, just as that first Levitical priesthood was; that this succession rests on firmer promises of the Holy Spirit, yet without any difference from that earlier Levitical succession; that Peter is the head of this succession; that this succession clings to the city of Rome; and, finally, that

units.la: Abusus circa Patrorum & Conciliorum absque autem auctoritate. Sancti Spiritus esse testimonia, Cruces, bullas, galeros, lituos, mitras, pileos rotundos, lineos amictus, coronas à tonsore in capite notatas. Tam pudenda haec omnia ut illa verisimile sit Satanam ipsum & impuros Spiritus ridere.
units.tr: The abuse of the Fathers and Councils, without any authority. The testimonies of the Holy Spirit are crosses, bulls, galeros, crosiers, mitres, round caps, linen vestments, and crowns marked on the head by the barber. All these things are so shameful that it is likely Satan himself and the unclean spirits laugh at them.

units.la: Isti tamen, ut paulo ante diximus, quantumuis improbi, festuri sunt olim iudices aduersus eos qui blasphemiam crimen esse capitale negant. Non enim in eo peccarunt isti quod blasphemiam capitali iudicio damnarunt, qua in re minimè decipiuntur: sed quod blasphemiam esse iudicant quod procul aberat à blasphemia, sed erat contra Dei maxima gloria: & blasphemum eum dicunt, qui os sacrosanctum erat Dei Patris sui. Nam, obscuro, quodnam est in omnibus Dei operibus summum & maximè admirandum, nisi hoc, ut qui verus absque rapina Deus est, eòque se demiserit ut frater noster fieret, ut sua obedientia usque ad mortem Crucis nos ex inferis ereptos in coelos inducheret? Cuius verò proprium est istud utrumque, nisi eius qui testimonium è coelis, voce ipsa Patris è coelis intellecta accepit? Matth. 3. 17. & 17. 5. At lapidem angularem à prauis aedificantibus oportuit reiici. Antequam igitur de blasphemia iudicium ferrent, quòd se Dei Filium aliquis diceret, & priusquam hunc iudicaret tanquam falsò sibi Messiae, filiíque Dei nomen tribuentem, horum duorum prius fuit ex Mosis & Prophetarum scriptis inuestigandum: alterum ex diligenti
units.tr: Yet these men, as we said a little earlier, however wicked they are, will one day sit as judges against those who deny that blasphemy is a capital crime. For those men did not go wrong in condemning blasphemy to capital judgment, a point on which they are by no means mistaken; they went wrong in judging to be blasphemy what was far from blasphemy and was rather to the greatest glory of God, and in calling a blasphemer the one who was the most holy Son of his Father. For, I ask, what is the highest and most admirable of all God's works, except this: that he who is true God, not grasping at equality with God, humbled himself so far as to become our brother, so that by his obedience unto the death of the cross he might lead us, snatched from the depths, into heaven? And whose own are both of these things, except his who received the testimony from heaven, spoken by the very voice of the Father from heaven? Matth. 3. 17. and 17. 5. But the cornerstone had to be rejected by the wicked builders. Before, therefore, they pronounced judgment on blasphemy, because someone called himself the Son of God, and before they judged this man as one who falsely claimed for himself the name of Messiah and Son of God, the first of these two matters ought to have been investigated from the writings of Moses and the Prophets, and the other ought to have been learned from a careful

units.la: y. iiij. natiuitatis Iesu Christi, doctrinę factorúmque ipsius inquisitione cognoscendum, quod si ab ipsis factum esset sanè quod vt blasphemum condemnarunt, tanquam pretiosissimam veritatem essent amplexati. Iam verò si quomodo se nostri aduersarij aduersus haereses & haereticos gerant considereres, nae facilè fuerit animaduertere nam qui se iudiciis illis immiscet veri Caiaphae successores merito dicendi sint. At prouocamus & prouocaturi sumus ab iniquis eorum iudiciis ad eum, qui, vt nostri capitis ignominiam, in illam gloriosam Sessionem a dextris omnipotentiae suae commutauit, idem est de iudiciis aduersus ipsius cohaeredes datis tandem aliquando praestiturus.
units.tr: ...inquiry into the birth of Jesus Christ, his teaching and his deeds (page y. iiij.). If they had done this, they would surely have embraced as most precious truth what they condemned as blasphemy. Indeed, if you should consider how our adversaries conduct themselves against heresies and heretics, you would easily notice it; for whoever mixes himself into those judgments may rightly be called the successor of the true Caiaphas. But we call upon, and shall continue to call upon, from their unjust judgments to him who, in exchange for the shame of our head, exchanged that ignominy for that glorious Session at the right hand of his omnipotence; the same one will at length deliver judgment on the judgments passed against his co-heirs.

units.la: Caeterum, si hoc excepto incarnationis Filij Dei mysterio, horrenda blasphemia est, Deitatem homini tribuere, testibus D. Paulo & Barnaba, Act.14.15. quanta putas est quamque miris modis itupenda blasphemia, crustum panis existimare essentialiter esse Transsubstantiatum in hunc verum Iesum Christum, verum Deum & verum hominem: & vt talem adorare & inuocare, in vero & essentiali corpore? Quàm est etiam blasphemum, si nomen, aliqua tamen ituis potentiae & virtutis partem incommunicabiliter soli Deitati propriae, non tantum Angelis tribuere, qui tamen nunquam illud passi sunt, Apoc.19.10. & 22.9. non minus quàm sancti olim viri, Act. 10.26. nec Sanctorum manibus qui suo semel decurso stadio res humanas non curant Esa.63.16.& 16. & Act. 16.36. sed mortuorum reliquiis, aquę lustrali, chrismati, oleo, cerę, imagunculis, &c ut uno verbo rem totam complectar, omnibus quęcunque falsa fides ac superstitio potest imaginari? Sancta illa tamen omnia: quę qui reprehendat haereticus sit. Iterum vero provocamus ad Dei tribunal, qui vtinam nobis hanc gratiam largiatur ut & animo & corpore, in spiritu & veritate nos ipsum veneremur & colamus. Amen.
units.tr: Moreover, if, apart from the mystery of the incarnation of the Son of God, it is a horrible blasphemy to attribute deity to a man, as Paul and Barnabas bear witness, Acts 14. 15., how great, think you, and how astonishingly monstrous is the blasphemy of believing that a crust of bread is essentially transubstantiated into this true Jesus Christ, true God and true man, and of worshipping and invoking it as such, in a true and essential body? How blasphemous too it is to attribute to the angels, not merely a part of God's power and might, which belongs incommunicably to the Deity alone (though the angels never accepted this, Rev. 19. 10. and 22. 9.), nor even to holy men of old, as in Acts 10. 26., nor to the hands of saints who, once they have finished their race, no longer care for human affairs, Isa. 63. 16. and Acts 16. 36., but to the relics of the dead, lustral water, chrism, oil, wax, little images, and so on; in a word, to embrace the whole matter, to everything that false faith and superstition can imagine? Yet all these holy things, whoever finds fault with them is a heretic. Again we call upon the tribunal of God, who grant us, I pray, this grace: that we may worship and honour him in spirit and in truth, both in mind and in body. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA decimaquinta.
units.tr: HOMILIA decimaquinta.

units.la: MATTH. 26.
units.tr: MATTH. 26.

units.la: 67. Tunc insputerunt in faciem eius, & colaphos ei influxerunt: alii vero bacillis eum ceciderunt.
units.tr: 67. Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists; others slapped him with the palms of their hands,

units.la: 68. Dicentes, Vaticinare nobis Christe, quis sit qui te percussit.
units.tr: 68. saying, "Prophesy to us, Christ, who is it that struck you?"

units.la: 69. Petrus autem sedebat extra in aula: & accessit ad eum quaedam ancillula, dicens, Et tu cum Iesu Galilaeo eras.
units.tr: 69. Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a certain servant girl came up to him, saying, "You too were with Jesus the Galilean."

units.la: 70. Ipse vero negavit coram omnibus, dicens, Nescio quid dicas.
units.tr: 70. But he denied it before them all, saying, "I do not know what you are saying."

units.la: 71. Eum autem egredientem in vestibulum vidit alia(ancilla) & dixit iis qui(erant) illic, Et iste erat cum Iesu Nazareno.
units.tr: 71. When he had gone out into the porch, another servant girl saw him and said to those who were there, "This man too was with Jesus the Nazarene."

units.la: 72. Tunc rursus negauit cum iureiurando, dicens, Non noui hominem.
units.tr: 72. Then again he denied it with an oath, saying, "I do not know the man."

units.la: 73. Paulo post autem accesserunt qui astabant, & dixerunt Petro, Vere & tu ex ipsis es: nam & locutio tua te manifestum facit.
units.tr: 73. A little while later those who were standing by came up and said to Peter, "Surely you too are one of them, for your speech also makes you plain."

units.la: 74. Tunc coepit seipsum denouere, & iurare, dicens, Non noui hominem. Et statim gallus misit vocem.
units.tr: 74. Then he began to curse and swear, saying, "I do not know the man." And immediately the cock crowed.

units.la: 75. Et recordatus est Petrus Verborum Iesu, qui dixerat ei, Priusquam gallus vocem mittat, ter me abnegabis. Et egressus extra fleuit amarè.
units.tr: 75. And Peter remembered the words of Jesus, who had said to him, "Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times." And going out he wept bitterly.

units.la: MARC. 14.
units.tr: MARC. 14.

units.la: 54. Petrus autem longinquo interuallo sequutus est eum intrò vsque in aulam Pontificis Maximi: & considebat cum ministris, & calefaciebat sese ad ignem.
units.tr: 54. Peter, however, followed him from a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest; and he sat down with the servants and warmed himself at the fire.

units.la: 66. Quum vero Petrus esset in aula inferius, venit quaedam ex ancillis Pontificis maximi.
units.tr: 66. While Peter was down in the courtyard, one of the maidservants of the high priest came up.

units.la: 67. Et quum vidisset Petrum se calfacientem, intuita in eum, dixit, Et tu cum Nazareno Iesu eras.
units.tr: 67. And when she saw Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, "You too were with Jesus of Nazareth."

units.la: 68. Ipse vero negauit, dicens, Non noui, neque scio quid tu dicas. Et exiit extra inuestibulum, & gallus vocem emisit.
units.tr: 68. But he denied it, saying, "I neither know nor understand what you are saying." And he went out into the forecourt, and the cock crowed.

units.la: 69. Tunc ancilla quum rursus vidisset eum, coepit dicere astantibus, Hic est (vnus) ex ipsis.
units.tr: 69. When the maid saw him again, she began to say to the bystanders, "This man is one of them."

units.la: 70. Ipse vero rursum negauit, Et rursus paulo post qui adstabant dixerunt Petro, Vere ex ipsis es: etenim Galilaeus es: & loquutio tua similis est. Ipse
units.tr: 70. But he denied it again. And a little later those who stood by said to Peter, "Surely you are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech is like theirs." Ipse

units.la: 71. Ipse autem coepit execrari & iurare, dicens, Non noui hominem istum quem dicitis.
units.tr: 71. But he began to curse and swear, saying, "I do not know this man you speak of."

units.la: 72. Tunc secundo gallus vocem emisit, & recordatus est Petrus verborum quae dixerat ei Iesus, Priusquam gallus vocem bis miserit, ter me abnegabis. Et quum se proripuisset, fleuit.
units.tr: 72. Then the cock crowed a second time, and Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken to him: "Before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times." And when he had broken down, he wept.

units.la: LVC. 22.
units.tr: LVC. 22.

units.la: 54. Petrus vero sequebatur procul.
units.tr: 54. Peter, however, followed at a distance.

units.la: 55. Quumque accendissent ignem in medio aulae atque una consedissent, sedit & Petrus inter eos.
units.tr: 55. When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter also sat down among them.

units.la: 56. Quum autem eum vidisset ancilla quaedam sedentem ad ignem, intentis in eum oculis dixit, Et iste cum eo erat.
