This is called repentance [resipiscentia], and it goes much further: it is the same as returning from thoughtlessness to a better mind, and going back from error to the right way. Thus this affection looks not only at the punishment but hates and condemns the evil itself, because it is evil, and so brings about a complete change of the whole man for the better. Let us therefore leave the penitence of Judas and those like him, and consider in Peter true repentance, also following the traces of the evangelists in this matter, who used two different Greek words, [μεταμέλειας] and [μετάνοιας].

units.la: Quibus positis de vera Resipiscentia tracta-turi,veram illius ex hoc exemplo inuestigabi-mus causam : tum quid sit, quósque producat effectus differemus. Causa igitur ipsius πνεῦμα Spiritus Sanctus est. 2. Tim. 2. 25. & 26. ideo Consolator dictus, adducens conscien-tiam ad cognitionem & apprehensionem beneficij Domini nostri Iesu Christi, peccatoribus in eius verbo & Sacramentis oblati.
units.tr: With these things laid down, when we treat of true repentance, we shall investigate its true cause from this example; then we shall defer discussing what it is and what effects it produces. The cause of it, then, is the Holy Spirit [πνεῦμα] (2 Tim. 2:25–26). He is therefore called the Comforter, bringing the conscience to the knowledge and apprehension of the benefit of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is offered to sinners in his Word and Sacraments.

units.la: Inde sequitur Fidem & Refipiscentiam indiuiduas esse, etsi hæc illa non sit, nec etiam proprie pars alterius. Nam, exempli gratia, quis malum ideò quòd malum sit, non autem pœnæ aut inferorum formidine detestari potest, nisi qui virtutis amore ducitur, & vt bonum amplectitur ? Ecquis vero præstiturus hoc ipsum est nisi in eius cognitione doctus, qui Patrem nobis & seipsum exhibet, quis sit ipse nimirum, & quid ab ipso sit exspectadum docès? Ioh.1.15. & à Patre vi Sp.S. cooperantis ad ipsum tractus fuerit? Ioh.6.44. & 65. quum ex nobis ipsis idonei non simus ad ea quæ Dei sunt cogitanda? Denique nullus vero Dei ducitur amore nisi qui de eius in se benevolentia in Iesu Christo per eundem Sanctum Spiritum certus est.Rom.8.1.& 7.& 16. At si verum est(vt est sanè verissimum)Resipiscentiam voluntatis & vitæ mutationem adferre, peccatore ad Deum converso quem prius aversabatur, (quam etiam ob causam Resipiscentia Conuersio dicitur) & Sanctus Spiritus is est qui efficit in nobis vt velimus & vt efficiamus immutata nostra natura, Philip.2.verf.13. quinam tandem à Fide Resipiscentia, & Fides ab eo discerpetur cui nos ipsa coniungit & incorporat, quíque nobis à Patre Sapientia, Iustitia & Sanctificatio factus est? 1. Cor.1.30.
units.tr: It follows that faith and repentance are inseparable, although the one is not the other, nor properly a part of the other. For example, who can detest evil because it is evil, and not out of fear of punishment or of hell, unless he is led by the love of virtue and embraces the good? And who will do this unless he has been taught in the knowledge of him who shows us the Father and himself, that is, who he is and what is to be expected from him (John 1:18); and unless he has been drawn to him by the Father through the power of the Holy Spirit working together with him (John 6:44, 65), since we of ourselves are not fit to think the things of God? Finally, no one is led by the love of God unless he is certain, through the same Holy Spirit, of God's goodwill towards him in Jesus Christ (Rom. 8:1, 7, 16). But if it is true (as it certainly is, most true) that repentance brings about a change of will and of life, when the sinner is converted to God whom he previously turned away from (for which reason repentance is also called conversion), and if the Holy Spirit is the one who works in us both to will and to accomplish, our nature being changed (Phil. 2:13), then how could repentance be torn away from faith, and faith from him to whom it joins and incorporates us, and who has been made to us by the Father wisdom, righteousness and sanctification (1 Cor. 1:30)?

units.la: Hoc ipsum nos textus iste noster docet, quû dicitur Christus Petrum respexisse, & quidem eo vultu quem toties Dauid in suis calamitatibus expostulat: cuiusque præsentiæ excellens extat illa promissio Psal.34.16. Oculi Iehouæ sunt super iustos, qualis fuit in electione Dei Petrus, tum quum ea se maximè indignum redderet: vt eodem contra Psalmo v.16. dicitur Vultus esse Iehouæ super facientes malum, vt exscindat è terra memoriam eorum. Hic igitur aspectus in cor Petri penetravit, & iis gradibus de quibus deinceps acturi sumus veram in ipso Resipiscentiam produxit.
units.tr: This very thing our text teaches us, when it says that Christ looked upon Peter, and indeed with that look which David so often begs for in his troubles, and whose excellent promise of presence stands in Psalm 34:16: "The eyes of Jehovah are upon the righteous." Such was the case with Peter in God's election, at the very time when he made himself most unworthy of it; and on the contrary, in the same psalm, verse 16, it is said: "The face of Jehovah is against those who do evil, to cut off their memory from the earth." This look, then, penetrated into Peter's heart, and by those steps which we shall discuss afterwards, it produced in him true repentance.

units.la: Quoniam verò Christus iam à terris abest supra cœlos omnes euectus: & quoties se ex cœlis conspiciendum præbuit, vt Sancto Stephano, Act.7.36. aut in ipsis cœlis, vt in eos Apostolo rapto. 2.Cor.12.2. aut visione in ecclesi, quod eidem contigit Act.22.17. extraordinarium fuit, hodie minime exspectandum, vt corporeis ipse nos oculis intueatur, sed Sancti Spiritus energia in nobis operantis & oculos dantis quibus eum contemplemur & audiamus, tam in eius sacrosancto verbo legitime in ipsius Ecclesia prædicato, quàm in sanctis Sacramentis, picturis non mutis, sed vivis, Christum nobis prædicantibus, & in nostris cordibus, vt loquitur Apostolus, Gal.3.1. depingentibus: vt tandem huius promissionis Thomæ à Domino factæ, Beati qui non viderunt & crediderunt, Ioh.20.29. participes fiamus. Illa igitur ipsa vox, cuius sono Lazarus iam putidus prioris mortis vinculis solutus est, in offensis & peccatis spiritualiter mortuos deprehendens, in vitam æternam viuificat. Ephes.2.1. & 5. seu nobis illuminatis ab initio nostræ regenerationis, & à tenebris ad Lucem conuertis, Act.26.18. seu restituta nobis lætitia salutis ipsius nostra culpa veluti tenebris obnoluta. Psal.51.12. & in memoriam quæ tradideramus obliuioni reuocatis. Idem Petro contigit, sic ab initio sua temeritate excæcato, deinde vero tanto metu perculso, vt mille licet Gallis millies cantantibus, abnegationem abnegationi fuerit additurus, nisi vultus ille reuocasset in memoriam ipsi quæ cito nimis obliuioni tradiderat. Agite igitur, fratres, absit monente nos vel conscientia, vel etiam ipso per seruos suos Domino, restitemus. Ecquis enim nouit an semel inuitati denuo fimus inuitandi? Iu‑uenes caucte ne moniti, sapientiam in seniles annos reiiciatis. Non omnes enim ad fene‑ctam perueniunt: nec senes omnes sapiunt. Nos vero quos tanta patientia Deus tam multos annos tolerat, & vix vocanti respondi‑mus, quid moramur adhuc ac fegnefcimus? Deus enim, inquit Apostolus, decipi non po‑teft. Nulli vero magis Deum contemnunt quam dicentes, Permaneamus in peccato vt gratia fiat auctior. Rom.6. verf.1. Fateor quacunque hora peccator ingemuerit exaudiendum a Domino, & propinquum esse Iehouam omnibus inuocantibus eum. At solis iis contingit qui‑bus speciali Dei gratia conceditur, Spiritu Dei pro ipsis interpellante suspiriis inenarra‑bilibus, Rom.8. verf. 26. & clamare docente, Abba, Pater, Gal.4.6. non exauditis Efaui vlu‑latibus; Hebr.12.17. Agite igitur, quandiu fa‑pientia vociferatur in plateis, Prouerb.1.20. vocem illam nos inuitantem audiamus cum timore & reuerentia Spiritus Sancti tam fo‑nora voce nos ad id cohortantes admonitio‑nibus. Pfal.95.8. locum dantes.
units.tr: But since Christ is now absent from the earth, carried above all the heavens, and since as often as he showed himself to be seen from heaven, as to St Stephen (Acts 7:36), or in the heavens themselves, as to the Apostle caught up (2 Cor. 12:2), or in a vision in the temple, as happened to him (Acts 22:17), that was extraordinary, today we should not expect that he will look upon us with bodily eyes. Rather, through the energy of the Holy Spirit working in us and giving us eyes by which we may contemplate and hear him, both in his most holy Word lawfully preached in his Church and in the holy sacraments, which are pictures not mute but living, presenting Christ to us and painting him in our hearts, as the Apostle says (Gal. 3:1), we may at last become partakers of that promise made by the Lord to Thomas: "Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed" (John 20:29). That very voice, by whose sound Lazarus, already stinking, was loosed from the bonds of his former death, finds us spiritually dead in offences and sins and quickens us to eternal life (Eph. 2:1, 5); whether we are illuminated from the beginning of our regeneration and turned from darkness to light (Acts 26:18), or the joy of salvation is restored to us, which our own fault had as it were overshadowed with darkness (Ps. 51:12), and things we had committed to oblivion are recalled to memory. The same happened to Peter, who was first blinded by his own rashness and then struck with such fear that, though a thousand cocks crowed a thousand times, he would have added denial to denial, unless that look had recalled to his memory what he had all too quickly consigned to oblivion. Come, then, brothers, let us not delay, while either conscience admonishes us or the Lord himself through his servants. Let us return. For who knows whether, once invited, we shall be invited again? Young men, take care lest, though warned, you put off wisdom until your old age; for not all come to old age, and not all old men are wise. But we, whom God so patiently bears with for so many years, and who scarcely answer when he calls, why do we still delay and dawdle? For God, as the Apostle says, cannot be mocked. Yet no one despises God more than those who say, "Let us remain in sin so that grace may abound" (Rom. 6:1). I grant that whatever hour a sinner groans, he will be heard by the Lord, and that Jehovah is near to all who call upon him. But this happens only to those to whom special grace of God is granted, with the Spirit of God interceding for them with unspeakable sighs (Rom. 8:26), and teaching them to cry "Abba, Father" (Gal. 4:6), with the cries of Esau not being heard (Heb. 12:17). Come, then, while wisdom cries out in the streets (Prov. 1:20), let us hear that voice inviting us, and with the fear and reverence of the Holy Spirit, let us give place to those admonitions which urge us to this with a voice so loud (Ps. 95:8).

units.la: En veram & vnicam μετανοίαν Resipi‑scentiae causam. Ipsa vero quid fit age expen‑damus. Tribus illam essentialibus partibus conflare nostri temporis Ecclesia Romana docet, cordis Contritione, Confessione & Satisfactione: tam vera, si bene intelligatur doctrina, licet adhuc imperfecta, quàm falsa est & Diabolica, ex eorum mente intellecta, vt sumus paulò post exposituri.
units.tr: Here, then, is the true and only cause of repentance [μετανοίαν]. Let us now weigh what repentance itself is. The Roman Church of our time teaches that it is made up of three essential parts: contrition of heart, confession, and satisfaction. This teaching is true, if it is rightly understood, though still imperfect; but as their minds have understood it, it is as false as it is diabolical, as we shall set out shortly.

units.la: Tres istas igitur partes admitto, & agno-sco Refipifcentiam initium capere à contrito illo corde cuius Pfalm. 51. & passim alibi scriptura meminit: cuius testimonium nobis tam multi sanctorum virorum gemitus & lamentationes certissimum reliquæ sunt. At Contritionis voce, non quemlibet conscientiæ à peccato vulneratæ sensum intelligo, sed eam demum tristitiam, quam fecundum Deum tristitiam dicit Apostolus. 2. Corinth. 7. verf. 10. quæ salutem efficit, tristitiæ mundi oppositam quæ mortem parit: illis inter fe modis omnibus, tum in origine, tum obiectis, & effectis differentibus. Mundi enim tristitia post offensum Deum à veneno peccati manat, ex quo sequitur morsus & pauor conscientiæ, ante oculos sola peccato debita pœna, Deóque vehementer irato obuersante, tandem aut stupor lethalis aut desperatio consequitur. Contrà fecundum Deum tristitia, etsi à peccati sensu iudiciorumque Dei apprehensione capit occasionem, non inde tamen tanquam ab origine prima proficiscitur, sed contrà ad aliam expellendam à gratiæ & bonitatis Dei pura sanctaque origine dimanat, Deo nos ab isto terrore tanquam ab inferis eductos in coelos euchente per Consolatorem illum suum Sanctum Spiritum, pedetentim de peccatorum remissione certiores facientem, & non paruam aegritudinem de laesa Dei nostri bonitate in nobis, odiumque peccati, tum praeteriti tum in posterum producendi, generantem, quae tandem in gaudium & inenarrabilem consolationem desinat. Hac enim ratione Dominus in nobis Lucem salutis ex peccati & maledictionis tenebris, eductam ut perfectissimus & excellentissimus opifex producit. Ea contritio est cuius exemplum hic nobis in Petro proponitur, quem non tantum aegritudine affectum sed etiam fleuisse, & quidem amare fleuisse legimus.
units.tr: I accept these three parts and acknowledge that repentance begins from that contrite heart which Psalm 51 and many other passages of Scripture mention. The groans and laments of so many holy men that have been left to us are the most certain witness to it. By contrition, however, I do not mean any sense of conscience wounded by sin, but that sorrow which the Apostle calls "godly sorrow" (2 Cor. 7.10), which produces salvation, and which is opposed to the sorrow of the world, which produces death. These differ in every respect, in their origin, their objects, and their effects. The sorrow of the world flows from the poison of sin, after God has been offended. From this come the sting and terror of conscience, with the punishment due to sin alone before its eyes and God standing against it in great anger; and at last there follows either deadly stupor or despair. Godly sorrow, by contrast, although it takes its occasion from a sense of sin and from the apprehension of God's judgements, does not proceed from these as its first origin. Rather, it flows from the pure and holy origin of God's grace and goodness, to drive out that other sorrow. God, through his Comforter, the Holy Spirit, lifts us up from this terror as if from the depths into heaven, gradually making us more certain of the forgiveness of sins. It produces in us no small grief at the injury done to the goodness of our God, and hatred of sin, both past and to be committed in future, and at last it ends in joy and inexpressible consolation. For in this way the Lord, as the most perfect and excellent craftsman, brings forth in us the light of salvation, drawn out of the darkness of sin and curse. This is the contrition of which Peter is set before us here as an example, for we read that he not only was affected by grief but also wept, and indeed wept bitterly.

units.la: Confessio vero necessario superiora comitatur, quum fieri non possit quin vere Christianus in ipsa sancta aegritudine: tantae beningnitatis divinae suavitate perceptae, seipsum horis omnibus immo & momentis, tum privatim tum in Christianorum publico & ordinatio coetu, miserum coram Domino peccatorem agnoscat, qui maxime semper offenditur, quemque praecipue conscientia reformidat: deinde, quum ita feret casus, privatim ergo laesum, proximum, Matth. 5. 24. Tertium quoddam est confessionis genus quod ad disciplinam Ecclesiae pertinet, seu coram Senioribus, seu publice in totius Ecclesiae conspectu ex disciplinae canonicae instituto fiat: quum non co vsque semper in priuatis lapsibus sit proprogrediendum, sed obseruandi gradus à Domino præscripti. Matth. 18. 15. Huius igitur Confessionis exemplum insigne nobis hic proponitur ad finem vsque seculorum duraturum. Etsi enim erat vnicus Christus cum Petro facti istius conscius, Petrus tamen illud amarissimis suis lachrymis patefecit, & proculdubio non texit ore, quum illud etiam voluerit à condiscipulis ad Domini gloriā scriptis mandari.
units.tr: Confession necessarily accompanies what has gone before, since it cannot happen that a true Christian, in that holy grief, having perceived the sweetness of such great divine kindness, does not acknowledge himself, at every hour and indeed every moment, to be a wretched sinner before the Lord, both privately and in the public and ordered assembly of Christians. He is always offended most of all by himself, and conscience dreads him above all. Then, when circumstances so require, he confesses to the one he has wronged, privately, as his neighbour (Matt. 5.24). There is a third kind of confession, which belongs to church discipline, and which is made either before the elders or publicly in the sight of the whole Church, according to the rule of canonical discipline. For it is not always right to proceed so far in private faults, but the steps prescribed by the Lord must be observed (Matt. 18.15). Therefore this remarkable example of this confession is set before us here, to last until the end of the ages. For although Christ alone was a witness to that deed together with Peter, Peter nevertheless revealed it with his most bitter tears, and without doubt did not hide it with his mouth, since he also wished it to be written down by his fellow disciples for the glory of the Lord.

units.la: Satisfactio etiam ad veram Respipiscentiam accedat oportet, sed vario respectu. Nam Deo quidem (cuius reuera natura quum suæ iustitiæ non possit obliuisci perfectissimam, seuerissimamque peccati punitionem efflagitat, quod qui non agnoscit Deum in horrendum idolum transformat) quale tandem offeremus pro peccatis nostris pretium, nisi vnicum Seruatorem nostrum Dn. Iesum Christum, traditum propter offensas nostras, & excitatum propter iustificationem nostri? Rom. 4. 25. Nostrum igitur hic nihil est, sed illud omne ab vnico Iesu Christo fidei instrumento est hauriendum, quod Deo patri nostro offeramus, quatenus nimirum in nobis ipsis coram eius Maiestate foedi apparentes, peccatorum gravitate sordidati postulamus, vt nos in hoc Sacrificio semel pro nobis ipsi reconciliandis, oblato respiciat gratiosque habeat. At proximorum & Ecclesiæ respectu, præterquam quòd libera peccatorum agnitio, de qua superius apud laesos minimeque vindictæ cupidos satisfactionis locum obtinet, extra omne dubium est, si adsit facultas detrimentum illatum proximo compensandi, seu restituto quod erat ablatum, sed alia ratione pensato, veram Resipiscentiam id etiam cum quadruplo, si fieri poterit ad Zachaei exemplum Luc. 19.8. postulare. Porro quod ad istud Satisfactionis caput attinet, quid aliud vita Petri fuit a conversione, nisi perpetua, ut ita dicam, erga condiscipulos, totamque Ecclesiam, pro negationibus illis trinis compensatio?
units.tr: Satisfaction too ought to accompany true repentance, but in different respects. For with regard to God (whose nature, since it cannot forget his most perfect and severe justice, demands the punishment of sin; and whoever does not acknowledge this turns God into a horrible idol), what price shall we offer for our sins, other than our one Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ, who was delivered up for our offences and raised for our justification (Rom. 4.25)? Nothing of ours is here, but all that we offer to God our Father must be drawn from the one Jesus Christ by the instrument of faith. That is, we, appearing in ourselves before his Majesty as guilty and defiled by the weight of our sins, ask that he look upon and regard with favour that one sacrifice, once offered, by which we are reconciled to him. But with regard to our neighbours and the Church, apart from the free acknowledgement of sins (which, as said above, has its place with those we have injured, who are not at all eager for revenge), it is beyond doubt that if there is the means to make up for the harm done to a neighbour, by restoring what was taken away or by otherwise making amends, true repentance will demand this, even fourfold if it can be done, after the example of Zacchaeus (Luke 19.8). Moreover, as far as this head of satisfaction is concerned, what else was the life of Peter after his conversion, but a continual making amends, so to speak, to his fellow disciples and to the whole Church, for those three denials?

units.la: Reliqua sunt huius Resipiscentiae effecta, quae Sanctus Iohannes Baptista vocat fructus convenientes resipiscentiae. Matth. 3.8. Ea sunt in summa, vitae immutatio, omnibus bonis effectibus testata, quos etiam fructus Spiritus dicimus, carnis oppositos fructibus, quorum amplam enumerationem instituit Paulus, Gal. 5.19. Quod iterum nobis in hoc exemplo proponitur: quum dicitur Petrus, vbi ad se rediisset infaustis aedibus illis exiuisse, & amare fleuisse. Haec vnica via est quam qui constanter insistunt, ut ab initio remissionem peccatorum in hoc mundo receperunt, ita tandem ad aeternam salutem perueniunt. Testis esto Petrus qui sic immutatus, & ipsius ore Domini in Apostolatum a quo trina negatione velut exciderat, trina illi opposita confessione restitutus Ioh. 21.15. & 16. & 17. ipsas etiam oues Domini tum voce, tum vitae exemplo, & scriptis deinceps feliciter rexit.
units.tr: There remain the effects of this repentance, which St John the Baptist calls "fruits worthy of repentance" (Matt. 3.8). In sum, these are a change of life, attested by all good effects, which we also call the fruits of the Spirit, opposed to the fruits of the flesh, of which Paul gave a full list (Gal. 5.19). This is again set before us in this example, when Peter is said, once he had come to himself, to have gone out of that unlucky house and wept bitterly. This is the one way which those who keep to it steadily, as they received forgiveness of sins in this world from the beginning, so at last come to eternal salvation. Peter is a witness to this, who, so changed, and restored to the apostolate, from which he had as it were fallen by his threefold denial, was restored by the Lord himself with a threefold confession set against it (John 21.15, 16, 17). He afterwards happily ruled the very sheep of the Lord, by voice, by the example of his life, and by his writings.

units.la: En quae vera sit Resipiscentia (quam illi poenitennitentiam vocant) cum peccatorum remis- sione, nostráque salute inseparabiliter con-iuncta: cui si doctrinam hodiernorum Catholicorum Romanorum opponamus,sus de-que omnia ferri in illa compericmus. Primum enim in vera Pœnitentiæ origine duobus modis peccant grauissimè. Primus est, quòd quum ca vnicæ Dei gratiæ accepta ferenda sit,singunt aliquam in peccatoribus esse dispositionem ac præparationem naturalem,quam gratia præueniat & excitet, vt cum illa tandem cooperetur. Non minus sanè ridiculè quàm si quis in corporum resurrectione diceret reliquam fore aliquam præparationem in natura corporis cum potentia Dei cooperantem, vt partim naturalis sit resurrectio, partim à gratia & potentia Dei promanans. Quis verò comparationem istam eludat? Nec enim minus anima nostra mortua est, omníque potestate & spirituali motu, ad resurrectionem spiritualem priuata, Ephes. 2. 1. quàm ad corpoream resurrectionem corpus.
units.tr: Here, then, is what true repentance is, which they call repentance, inseparably joined to the forgiveness of sins and to our salvation. If we set against it the doctrine of the Roman Catholics of today, we shall find everything turned upside down. First, in the very origin of true repentance, they go wrong in two very serious ways. The first is this: whereas contrition is to be received as the sole gift of God's grace, they imagine that there is in sinners some disposition and natural preparation, which grace comes before and stirs up, so that it may at last cooperate with it. This is no less ridiculous than if someone were to say, in the resurrection of bodies, that there will remain in the nature of the body some preparation, cooperating with the power of God, so that the resurrection will partly be natural and partly flow from the grace and power of God. And who would not laugh at such a comparison? For our soul is no less dead, and deprived of all power and spiritual motion for spiritual resurrection (Eph. 2.1), than the body is for bodily resurrection.

units.la: Ad primum istum errorem alter accedit. Nam pro vera Contritione cordis,tum à Sancto Spiritu, tum ab odio peccati & Dei dilectione promanante Conscientiæ morsum illum, solum Dei iudicium apprehendentem ponunt, quod perinde est ac si pro vita, mortem, & pro luce, tenebras elegeris. Præterea, quod longè adhuc peius est, huic Contritioni Meriti cuiusdam præparatorij speciem aliquam attribuunt. Sed indigna re- sponso est doctrina: Et ita quidem in priore Poenitentiae parte, quam vocant Cordis contritionem, hallucinantur.
units.tr: A second error is added to the first. For in place of true contrition of heart, which flows from the Holy Spirit, from hatred of sin and love of God, they put that sting of conscience which apprehends only God's judgement. This is just as if you were to choose death for life and darkness for light. Moreover, what is far worse still, they attribute to this contrition some appearance of a kind of preparatory merit. But the doctrine is unworthy of a reply. Thus, in the first part of repentance, which they call contrition of heart, they go astray.

units.la: Confessionis vero cuius tres species constituimus, primam apud Deum, singulis proinde Christianis communem, seu privatim domi, seu in coetu publico Deum precentur, & eius verbum audiant: Alteram erga laesum proximum: Tertiam apud Ecclesiam quum disciplinae Ecclesiasticae locus est, sive illa fiat tantum in Seniorum & presbyterorum, id est Ecclesiasticae disciplinae moderatorum consessu, sive publice & solenniter coram tota Ecclesia, ut offensae ratio postulare videbitur, Catholici Romani nostri primam quidem partem in specie retinuerunt, sed prorsus depravatam, primum quod eius formula peregrino & incognito miseris ipsorum quibus sermone concipitur. An non vero id est aperte Deo illudere, quum eadem plane sint, quae non intelligas loqui, & omnino non loqui? Deinde, quod in hac formula, quae vulgo vocatur CONFITEOR, miseros peccatores quos ad unicum Patrem in Christo Iesu Mediatore nostro confugere oportuerat, ad Mariae Virginis, Sanctorum ac Sanctarum intercessionem, quae tribui ipsis sine blasphemia in Christum non poterat, ablegant. Primum enim Confessio Deo soli, tanquam honos ipsi & debita fides, exhibenda est: deinde cum idololatria coniuncta est, tu quod ipsimet ad sua idola procumbant, bant, tum quòd beatorum spiritus recumbant in Domino, cursu suo peracto, rerum humanarum curam aut cognitione à Domino nullum habentes nec gerétes: corpora verò diem vltimum exspectantia iaceant in puluere, cum reliquis fratribus, ac proinde Confessio illa sit inanis apud nec videntes nec audientes, quod tamen dum in his terris degerent poterant, fratrum miserias agnoscentes, mutuásque cum illis preces coniungentes. At lògè peius quidam adhuc hic subest. Nam alteri quàm vnico Deo cognitionem eorum quæ in terris aut cœlis fiunt dicuntúrue tribuere, rei creatæ est ascribere quod Creatoris incommunicabiliter proprium est. Nec etiam in sacris vsquam, nec exemplum, nec mandatum eiusmodi quo talis confessio vel inuocatio nitatur inuenias.
units.tr: As for confession, of which we have set up three kinds, the first is before God, and therefore common to all Christians, whether they pray to God privately at home or in the public assembly, and hear his Word. The second is towards a neighbour who has been wronged. The third is before the Church, when there is a place for church discipline, whether this takes place only in the assembly of elders and presbyters, that is, the governors of church discipline, or publicly and solemnly before the whole Church, as the nature of the offence seems to require. Our Roman Catholics have indeed kept the first kind in form, but wholly corrupted it. First, because its formula is composed in a foreign and unknown language, to the wretches for whom it is meant in their own speech. Is it not plainly to mock God, when the words are exactly those you do not understand, and in effect not to speak at all? Second, because in this formula, which is commonly called the Confiteor, they send miserable sinners, who ought to have fled to the one Father through Christ Jesus our Mediator, to the intercession of the Virgin Mary and of the holy men and women, which cannot be ascribed to them without blasphemy against Christ. For confession must first be made to God alone, as the honour due to him and the faith owed to him. Second, it is joined with idolatry, both because they fall down before their own idols, and because the spirits of the blessed rest in the Lord, having finished their course, and have no care or knowledge of human affairs from the Lord, while their bodies, awaiting the last day, lie in the dust with the rest of the brethren. And so that confession is empty, made to those who neither see nor hear, whereas while they lived on this earth they could, recognising the miseries of their brothers, join prayers with them. But something even worse than this lies hidden here. For to ascribe to any other than the one God the knowledge of what is done on earth or in heaven is to ascribe to a created thing what is incommunicably proper to the Creator. Nor will you find anywhere in the sacred writings either an example or a command on which such confession or invocation rests.

units.la: Secundam Confessionis speciem particularem erga læsum proximum tam diserte à Domino mandatam, Matth. 5. 23. nominatim in oratione Dominica, Matt. 6. 12. & 14. & 15. boni isti scilicet Vicarij parum admodum aut omnino nihil curant.
units.tr: The second particular kind of confession, toward a neighbour wronged, is so plainly commanded by the Lord (Matt. 5. 23), and by name in the Lord's Prayer (Matt. 6. 12, 14, 15), yet those good vicars of theirs care very little, or nothing at all, for it.

units.la: Tertiam vero quæstuosissimam, & aptissimam arcanis omnium detegedis habent, concientiis vel attonitis vel pacatis ad suū arbitrio, hac ratione non tantū ad Pharisæorum exceptum viduarum domos vorates, Matt. 12. 40. sed etiam maximos orbis terrarum Status & opulentiam compilantes. Cui res fidè faciunto, præter maximam bonorum temporalium in orbe Christiano parte, quam in peras suas isti mendici deriuarunt, immensae illae opes quas, qui sibi toti Ecclesiae commune nomen Iesuitarum proprium faciunt, annorum minus quadraginta spatio confessionum iltarum praetexta corraserunt, & adhuc hodie corradunt? Confessionis igitur partem tertiam iis peculiarem qui censuram excommunicationis incurrerat, & Poenitentes vocabantur, in generalem & universalem Legem transformarunt, docentes nullum peccatum nisi expressè agnitum & ore profitum, condonari. Deinde pro eo quod haec Confessio publice coram tota Ecclesia fiebat, paulatim Seniorum & Ecclesiasticae disciplinae Gubernatorum collapsis coetibus & administratione a Pastorum & Doctorum ministerio distincta. 1. Cor. 12. 28. haec cura primum ei commissa fuit quem Poenitentiarium dixerunt, deinde ad Curiones, eorum Vicarios, Sacrificulos, tandemque ad Monachos, illam pecunia redimentes deuenit. Intolerandam miseris conscientiis tyrannidem, nullo nec Sacrae Scripturae Veteris, aut Novi Foederis, nec verae veteris multorum saeculorum Ecclesiae fundamento nixam!
units.tr: They keep the third kind, the most profitable and best suited for uncovering the secrets of all men, of consciences either terrified or at peace, to their own discretion. By this method they not only devour the houses of widows under the pretext of Pharisaical prayers (Matt. 12. 40), but also plunder the greatest states and the wealth of the world. Do the facts bear this out? Apart from the greatest part of the temporal goods in the Christian world, which those beggars have drained into their own purses, do those immense riches, which those who make the common name of Jesuits their own for the whole Church, have scraped together in less than forty years under the pretext of these confessions, and still scrape together today? So they have transformed the third part of confession, which was peculiar to those who had incurred the censure of excommunication and were called penitents, into a general and universal law, teaching that no sin is forgiven unless it is expressly acknowledged and professed by mouth. Then, because this confession was made publicly before the whole Church, the assemblies of elders and the governors of ecclesiastical discipline gradually collapsed, and the administration was separated from the ministry of pastors and teachers (1 Cor. 12. 28). This care was first committed to the one they called the penitentiary, then passed to parish priests, their vicars and sacrificers, and finally to monks, who bought it back with money. An intolerable tyranny over wretched consciences, resting on no foundation of Holy Scripture, of the Old or New Covenant, nor of the true Church of many centuries past!

units.la: At tam horrendis iltis abusibus viam tantum sibi Satan ad veram Satisfactionem cuertendam fecit, quamin re quid poslet pro viribus eam aggressus satis ostendit. Quum illius enim species tres sint, praecipua nimirum & fundamentalis erga Deum: altera erga laesum proximum, tertia denique erga Ecclesiam, quum EcEcclesiæ censuram quis incurrit, harum trium nullam intactam reliquit. Primam enim quòd attinet, vt omittam impietatis plena illa quæ sibi fingunt Sanctorum merita, numerata pecunia redempta, quæque cum Christi Domini nostri merito coniungunt, tantum suis fraudibus promouerunt, vt pœnas à Canonibus præscriptas Pœnitentibus, minimè quibus Deo, vel ex parte, vel in solidum satisfieret: nec quibus apud eum remissio peccatorum obtinere-tur, sed quæ veræ Resipiscentiæ signa & probationes essent ad Ecclesiæ ædificationem, transformarint in satisfactiones apud Deum meritorias. Quòd autem multa sæpe in prima illa Ecclesia inciderent, quibus censurarum Ecclesiasticarum administratores nonnihil de veterum Canonum rigore cogebantur remittere, Paulum imitati in moderatione illa qua incestuosum recipi iussit, 2. Cor. 2. 6. & 7. quod Indulgentias vocabant, eò deuenit istorum animas cauponantium audacia, cum summa & incredibili impudentia coniuncta, vt ex eo suum Purgatorium & Indulgentias fabricati sint: quasi Christi sanguine sola Culpa delea-tur, Pœna verò ex æterna temporalis facta sit: horrenda sanè ac detestandam & satis scelsam confutantem blasphemiam. Nam id si esset, ne Purgatorium iis puniendis destinaretur, quos nulla Culpa vrgeret: quod quid aliud est quàm Deum in tyrannum inexcusabilem coram ipsis hominibus transmutare? His porrò pedetentim iactis fundamentis, tandem cuique peccato fuit suum tempus præfigendum, quam suo arbitrio æstimationem reseruatam, vt e re-ipsorum est dispensant in illis suis Indulgentiis ac Iubilæis, adhibitis ad hoc mysterium quæcunque tandem sibi ridicula & ludicra fingunt, suis interim ita subductis rationibus, vt mundo licet ad annorum multas myriades durante, miseras animas in Purgatorio sibi semper tributarias retinent: hoc ipso tamen suam absolutionem irritam facientes, quam non minus quàm confessionem illam auricularem necessariam volunt, à Sacrificulo administratam: exceptis iis quos suis Episcopis aut ipsi Pontifici reseruant calibus: iis adhibitis ritibus, quibus hanc quam describimus Pœnitentiam faciunt Sacramentum, non minus ridiculè quàm malitiosè euerterunt quicquid Sacra Scriptura de vera Christianáque Resipiscentia docet. Denique hic ad mensuram cumulus accedit oratiunculårum quæ Pater noster dicunt, & Missarum certus numerus, ieiunia, eleemosynæ in Conuentum, peregrinationes, quibus noltrorum Romanorum Pœnitentia peragitur, & conscientiæ tranquillitas quæritur.
units.tr: But by these horrible abuses Satan has merely opened a way for himself to pervert true satisfaction, as his undertaking of the task shows well enough. For there are three kinds of satisfaction: the chief and fundamental one toward God; the second toward the neighbour wronged; and the third toward the Church, when someone incurs its censure. He has left none of these three untouched. As to the first, to pass over that impious invention of theirs, that the merits of the saints can be bought with money and joined to the merit of Christ our Lord, they have so advanced by their frauds that the penalties prescribed by the canons for penitents, which were never meant to satisfy God either in part or in full, nor to obtain forgiveness of sins from him, but were signs and proofs of true repentance for the building up of the Church, they have turned into meritorious satisfactions before God. Since many things often happened in that early Church, by which the administrators of ecclesiastical censures were compelled to relax somewhat the rigour of the ancient canons, imitating Paul in that moderation by which he ordered the incestuous man to be received (2 Cor. 2. 6, 7), which they called indulgences, the audacity of these hucksters of souls went further, joined with the greatest and incredible impudence, so that from it they fabricated their Purgatory and indulgences. As if by Christ's blood only guilt were blotted out, while punishment became temporal instead of eternal! This is a horrible, detestable and utterly wicked blasphemy. For if that were so, Purgatory would not be destined for those who are punished but are burdened by no guilt; and what is that but to transform God, before men themselves, into an inexcusable tyrant? Having laid these foundations step by step, at last a time had to be fixed for each sin, its valuation reserved to their own judgment, which they dispense as their own in those indulgences and jubilees of theirs, employing for this mystery whatever ridiculous and playful inventions they devise. Meanwhile they so calculate their accounts that, though the world lasts for many myriads of years, they keep the wretched souls in Purgatory always tributary to them. Yet by this very act they make their own absolution void, which they insist, no less than that auricular confession, must be administered by the sacrificer, except in those cases they reserve to their bishops or to the Pontiff himself. By the rites with which they make this penance, which we describe, into a sacrament, they have subverted, no less foolishly than maliciously, whatever Holy Scripture teaches about true and Christian repentance. Finally, the full measure is reached with the heap of little prayers they say as the Our Father, a fixed number of Masses, fasts, almsgiving to the convent, and pilgrimages, by which the penance of our Romanists is carried out and tranquillity of conscience sought.

units.la: Porrò vera Resipiscentia ex diametro pugnat cum Impœnitentia, in iis puta qui se illa, opus habere, quòd iusti sint, non arbitrantur, quales iis temporibus Pharisæi, & quos Iudas hic accessit: quibus in Ecclesia Christiana Cathari olim, & noltro seculo Anabaptistæ successerunt. Adde & in iis qui sic occalluerunt, vt
units.tr: Moreover, true repentance is diametrically opposed to impenitence, in those who do not think they need it because they are righteous, such as the Pharisees of that time, and those whom Judas here resembled. In the Christian Church the Cathari once, and in our own age the Anabaptists, have succeeded them. Add also those who have grown so hardened that

units.la: Collatio vera Resipiscentia cum impœnitentia, & pœnitentia simulata.
units.tr: Comparison of true repentance with impenitence, and with feigned repentance.

units.la: vt malum à bono minimè discernant, & adversus Dei iudicia, quibus eos par erat territos ad meliorem frugem reuerti, potius fremant & obmurmurent, donec tandem eos Dei furor obruat, aut in eam desperationem præcipites ferantur, quàm exitium vltimum consequatur. Hoc Sauli contigisse verisimile est: & in historia Ecclesiastica nobis etiam horrendum istiusmodi proponitur exemplum in perdito illo Iuliano Imperatore Apostata cognominato, quem blasphemantem & in aërem sanguinem spargentem cœlum versus extinctum fuisse memoriæ proditum est: cuius etiam contrarium exemplum & singulare in Manasse habemus, in quo Dei summam infinitamque misericordiam contemplemur. 2. Chron. 33, 13.
units.tr: that they cannot tell evil from good, and rage and mutter against God's judgments, by which they ought to have been terrified into returning to better conduct, until God's fury overwhelms them, or they are hurled headlong into that despair which brings final ruin. This seems to have happened to Saul. In church history, too, a horrible example of this kind is set before us in the notorious Julian the Apostate, who is recorded to have died blaspheming and sprinkling blood into the air toward heaven. We also have the opposite and singular example in Manasseh, in whom we behold the highest and infinite mercy of God (2 Chron. 33. 13).

units.la: Idem hypocritis omnibus accidit, quorum alii aliud foris ostentant, aliud corde clausum occultant, quod toties à Prophetis nominatim reprehendi conspicimus: in aliis verò, quorum murmuratores in deserto per annorum quadraginta spatium. Psal. 95. 10. & Achabus. 1. Reg. 21. 27. exemplo sunt, Resipiscentiæ quidem initium inest, sed quod statim, effluat, nimirum vero nimis proverbio, Præterito periculo Sanctum irrideri: Et hactenus de Impœnitentia verè Resipiscentiæ ex diametro oppositæ. At inter hæc duo extrema, falsæ Resipiscentiæ mediæ sunt, quarum alij, superstitiosæ puta, quales de quibus paulò ante eginus, in hominibus spem quandam salutis ingenerant, sed frustrà: nam somnia sibi fingunt, quum vera fides & spes in sacrosancto Dei verbo scriptis promissionibus nitantur. Aliæ verò,quum solum ante oculos Dei iudicium illis obuersetur, in horrendam desperationem incidunt, quam Iudæ Pœnitentiam diximus, cuius effecta sunt eadem cum falsis & superstitiosis Pœnitentiis. Frustra enim aliquid sperare, & nihil sperare, vnum & idem consequuntur effectum, illa quidem in spe vana, hac verò in desperatione manente.
units.tr: The same happens to all hypocrites, some of whom display one thing outwardly and keep another hidden shut up in the heart, which we see the prophets rebuke by name so often. In others, whose murmurers in the desert over forty years are examples (Ps. 95. 10), and Ahab (1 Kings 21. 27), there is indeed a beginning of repentance, but it immediately drains away, in accordance with that all too familiar proverb: once the danger has passed, the holy man is mocked. So far on impenitence, which is diametrically opposed to true repentance. But between these two extremes lie the middle kinds of false repentance. Of these, some, superstitious ones such as those we spoke of a little earlier, engender in men a certain hope of salvation, but in vain, for they invent dreams for themselves, whereas true faith and hope rest on the promises written in God's sacred word. Others, when only God's judgment is set before their eyes, fall into a horrible despair, which we have called the repentance of Judas. Its effects are the same as those of the false and superstitious repentances. For to hope in vain and to hope for nothing bring about one and the same result, the former remaining in empty hope, the latter in despair.

units.la: Agè verò iam hanc Iudæ Pœnitentiam excutiamus, qua cum Petri Resipiscentia collata & eodem ordine seruato, primùm ex qua causa promanarit perpendamus: deinde qualis in fe fuerit: ac tertio loco qualis eius effectus: vt maximo inter has discrimine perspicuè cognito, Deum suppliciter oremus, vt Petri pœnitentiam nobis largiatur: Iudæ verò misericors à nobis auertat. Primùm igitur aio Petri lapsum à causa in se laudabili promanasse, pio nimirum affectu, sed immoderato, & cum summa temeritate coniuncto. Sceleratù verò illum Iudam statim ab initio, summa & deploratissima malitia, cum immensa desperata auaritia coniuncta sic excæcauit & transuersum egit, vt ad tempus, omnem illi Magistri sui apprehensionem, & beneficiorum quę immensa ab illo acceperat memoriam extinxerit. Deinde aio, tandem à peccato quidem vtriusque conscientiam excitatâ & attonitam: sed Iudæ omnè pœnitentiam à sensu peccati sui, & horrore iudicij diuini, cum eius fugestiogestione qui cor eius intrauerat. Luc. 22. 3. exortam: quum contrà Petro quidem tristitia & lachrymas peccatum extorserit: at benignus Iesu Christi aspectus in ipso vi & efficacia sancti sui Spiritus agens, tristitiam illam secundùm Deum, initium Resipiscentiæ produxerit. Tam bene igitur inter se contritio cordis Iudæ, & Petri contritio conueniunt, quàm quod à Satana, malitia nostra, & peccatis promanat, cum eo quod nobis à Deo Patre in Domino nostro Iesu Christo per Sanctum Spiritum gratis donatur.
units.tr: Come now, let us examine this repentance of Judas, comparing it with Peter's repentance and keeping the same order: first let us weigh from what cause it sprang; second, what it was in itself; and third, what its effect was. Having clearly grasped the greatest difference between these, let us humbly pray God to grant us Peter's repentance and to turn away from us the wretched repentance of Judas. First, then, I say that Peter's fall sprang from a cause praiseworthy in itself, namely a pious feeling, but immoderate and joined with great rashness. That wicked Judas, however, from the very beginning, by the greatest and most desperate malice joined with immense and despairing avarice, so blinded and perverted himself that for a time he extinguished all regard for his Master and all memory of the immense benefits he had received from him. Then I say that in the end the conscience of each was stirred and stunned by sin; but in Judas repentance arose from a sense of his sin and horror at God's judgment, together with the suggestion of him who had entered his heart (Luke 22. 3). In Peter, by contrast, sin wrung out sorrow and tears, but the kindly look of Jesus Christ, working in him by the power and efficacy of his Holy Spirit, produced that sorrow according to God, the beginning of repentance. So well, then, does the contrition of Judas's heart agree with Peter's contrition, as what springs from Satan, our malice and sins, agrees with what is freely given to us by God the Father, in our Lord Jesus Christ, through the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Idem de vtriusque Confessione sentiendū, etsi non satis attente historiam consideranti Iudæ speciosior quàm Petri fuisse videatur. Iudas enim apertè & serio tam sui sceleris atrocitatem quàm Iesu Christi innocentiam profitetur. Quod fieri minimè potuit nisi falsi iudicij damnato Caiapha, totóque Hierosolymitano consessu: quum Petri lachrymas tantum legamus. At praeterquàm quod extra dubium est Petrum ad condiscipulos reuertum rem totam illis vt erat gesta cum magnis singulibus enarrasse & condemnasse (nam alioquin ex quo didicissent quæ tam accuratè & distinctè describunt?) vtriusque considerandus est Confessionis ortus, non eodem fonte manans, nec eandem viam insistens, nec ad eundem scopum collineans. Iudam enim non Dei & Iesu Christi amor ad suam proditionem, proditores, auaritiam, argentum ipsum condemnandum impulit, sed solus tam
units.tr: The same judgment should be made of the confession of both, even though to someone who does not examine the story closely, Judas's seems the more striking. For Judas openly and earnestly professes both the atrocity of his own crime and the innocence of Jesus Christ. This could hardly have happened unless Caiaphas had condemned him in a false trial and the whole Jerusalem assembly had heard it, whereas we read only of Peter's tears. Yet, apart from the fact that it is beyond doubt that Peter, when he returned to his fellow disciples, related the whole affair to them as it had happened, with great detail, and condemned himself (for otherwise how would they have learned what they describe so accurately and distinctly?), the origin of each confession must be considered: they did not flow from the same source, follow the same path, or aim at the same goal. For the love of God and of Jesus Christ did not drive Judas to condemn his betrayal, his betrayers, his greed, and the silver itself; rather, only a sense of the unworthiness of his deed [impelled him], just as you may see a murderer, who has been caught and is in the hands of the executioner, abhorring the killings he has committed, under the force of torture. That same sense drove him to proclaim the innocence of Christ, whom at that time he would have wished never to have known, indeed not even to have come into the world. Peter, on the other hand, while no less detesting his own fault, though it was by no means comparable, nevertheless, from the atrocity of it, seeks and implores the mercy and clemency of his Lord, which he came to recognise more and more, and he receives himself back to his remaining fellow disciples.

units.la: β. iiij. indigni fui facinoris sensus: veluti sicarium deploratum in lictoris manibus cædes à se factas, vi cruciatuum adactum detestari videas. Illud ipsum eum ad Christi quem tunc nollet vnquam cognitum, imo ne in mundum quidé vnquam venisse, prædicandam innocentiam adegit. Petrus vero contra culpam suam, etsi longè disparem non minus detestatur, sed ex eius atrocitate, Domini sui misericordiam & clementiam magis ac magis agnitam, requirit & implorat, seque ad reliquos condiscipulos recipit.
units.tr: ...the sense of his own unworthy crime: just as you may see a condemned murderer in the executioner's hands, forced by the agony of torture to detest the murders he has committed. That same sense drove him to proclaim the innocence of Christ, whom at that time he would never have wished to be known, indeed whom he would have wished had never even come into the world. Peter, on the other hand, though his guilt was far different, detests his own sin no less, but from its atrociousness he seeks and implores the mercy and clemency of his Lord, which he comes to acknowledge more and more, and so he takes himself back among his fellow disciples.

units.la: Tertia supererat Satisfactio, quæ Domini quidé & pacis ac tranquillitatis conscientiæ respectu, in Iuda, sicut dictum est, nulla fuit, nulla nimirum nec fide nec spe veniæ consequendæ prædito. Nec magis de hominibus satisfaciendo Iudas reddita pecunia cogitauit.
units.tr: A third element remained, satisfaction. With respect to the Lord, and to peace and tranquillity of conscience, there was none in Judas, as has been said, since he had neither faith nor hope of obtaining pardon. Nor did Judas, by returning the money, think any more about making satisfaction to men.

units.la: Nam contra capitale aduersus eos cum quibus coniurarat odium fouebat à quibus se grauiter offensum putabat: & pro eo quod Magistrum suum ab ipso veniam postulaturum requirere ipsum oportuerat, aut alios discipulos, saltem affectu si coram non poterat, tantum abest vt hanc viam ingrediatur vt contra ex templo de ibi manibus inferendis, scelus scelere cumulans, cogitet. Contra plorans Petrus, seque simul etiam consolatus, repente se infausta illa domo proripit, ad Dominum suum supplex in discipulorum cœtu confugit, salutisque viam quæsitam, inuenit. Iudas igitur seipsum à principio ad finem vsque in inferos fetos immersit: contrà Petrus eximiani gur- gite, sola cius qui erat cum suo aspectu dignatus gratia & misericordia emersit.
units.tr: On the contrary, he nursed a deadly hatred against those with whom he had conspired, and by whom he thought himself gravely wronged. Although he ought to have sought out his Master, who would have granted him pardon, or the other disciples, at least in feeling if he could not do so in person, he is so far from taking this way that, on the contrary, he thinks straight away of laying hands on them, heaping crime upon crime. Peter, on the other hand, weeping and at the same time consoling himself, suddenly tears himself away from that unhappy house, takes refuge as a suppliant with his Lord in the company of the disciples, and finds the way of salvation that he sought. Judas, therefore, plunged himself from beginning to end into the foul depths of hell; Peter, on the contrary, rescued from the deepest abyss, emerged by the grace and mercy of the one who deigned to look upon him.

units.la: Non abs re igitur, fratres, hanc materiam fufius sum perfequutus, vt exempla quae nobis hic ob oculos proponuntur tam expressa tulerunt, vt eum qui non minus est in suis iudiciis seuerus quàm in misericordia facilis ac benignus reuereamur. Ergo ex iis omnibus quae copiosè exposuimus primum confidere- mus vtriusque culpam ex hoc fonte manasse, putà verbi Domini obliuione: quo nos excitari vehementer oportet ad dies noctesque Deo preces fundedas, nos, inquam, quos Deus ante multos annos iam alloquutus est, & adhuc hodie voce sua compellat, vt aures ad audiendum, & cor ad retinendum largiatur. Deinde huius perditi exemplo cauti, sciamus nihil tam occultum esse nec suscipi quod Deus in lucem aliquando, quum ipsi videbitur, non educat: nullisque adeo aliis nec testibus opus esse ipsi, nec iudicibus, nec carnificibus ad sceleratos cruciados quàm ipsimet, quum horrendum sit in Dei viuentis manus incidere, Heb.10. 21. Obseruemus praeterea saepe in Dei Ecclesiam, immo in ipsum veluti finum Ecclesiae multos recipi, quibus tamen nulla sit in Ecclesia pars, tantum ingressis ipsis vt egredentur. Ioh.2.19. Ad conuiuium igitur vocati & ingressi, nuptialibus vestibus induamur, ne foras vbi ploratus est & dentium stridor eiciamur. Matth. 22. verf.13. Denique quum in ipsa Filij Dei familia tam horrendum scandalum acciderit, licet ab ipsa propria Dei sapientia edocta, de qua dictum est, Vos estis Lux mundi. Matth. 5. vers. 14. absit, istiusmodi scandalis in Ecclesia contingentibus offensi, vel à Christo ipso, vel ab eius sacrosancto verbo, vel ab eius vera Ecclesia resiliamus: sed diligenter caucamus ne in partem eorum veniamus, quum minime nouum sit aut inusitatum Satanam in sanctissimos etiam greges, aliquem vorraturum irrumpere, quod accidisse familiis Abrahami, Isaaci, Iacobi, Davidis & aliorum ex historia sacra conspicuum est: quum iam olim Apostolus diligenter praemonuerit fore ut ex pastoribus lupi egrediantur. Act. 20. 29. quod ipsum etiam tota passim Ecclesiastica historia probat, & nos hodie nimium saepe, proh dolor! in ipso sinu Ecclesiae contingere conspicimus.
units.tr: It is not without reason, brothers, that I have pursued this matter at greater length, so that the examples set before our eyes here might bear such clear witness that we may revere him who is as severe in his judgments as he is easy and kind in mercy. Therefore, from all that we have expounded at length, let us first grasp that the guilt of both sprang from this source, namely forgetfulness of the Lord's word, by which we ought to be vehemently stirred to pour out prayers to God day and night: we, I say, whom God addressed many years ago and still today speaks to with his voice, that he may grant ears to hear and a heart to retain. Next, warned by the example of this lost man, let us know that nothing is so hidden or undertaken that God will not at some time, when it seems good to him, bring it into the light; and that there is no need of any other witnesses, judges or executioners to torment the wicked than themselves, since it is a dreadful thing to fall into the hands of the living God (Heb. 10. 21). Let us observe, moreover, that often many are received into the Church of God, indeed into the very bosom of the Church, who yet have no part in it, having entered only in order to go out (Joh. 2. 19). Therefore, having been called to the feast and having entered, let us put on wedding garments, lest we be cast out where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth (Matth. 22. 13). Finally, although in the very family of the Son of God so dreadful a scandal has occurred, and although we are taught by God's own wisdom, of which it was said, "You are the light of the world" (Matth. 5. 14), let us be far from abandoning Christ himself, his most holy word, or his true Church, offended by scandals of this kind arising in the Church. Rather, let us take careful heed that we do not come to share in their part, since it is by no means new or unusual for Satan to break in upon even the most holy flocks to devour someone. This happened in the families of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, David and others, as is plain from sacred history, since the Apostle long ago carefully forewarned that from among the ministers wolves would arise (Act. 20. 29). Ecclesiastical history as a whole proves this everywhere, and we too see it happening all too often today, alas, in the very bosom of the Church.

units.la: HOMILIA decimaseptima.
units.tr: Homily 17

units.la: MATTH. 27.
units.tr: Matthew 27.

units.la: 3. Tunc Iudas qui eum prodiderat, videns eum damnatum esse, poenitens retulit triginta argenteos (numos) ad primarios Sacerdotes & Seniores.
units.tr: 3. Then Judas, who had betrayed him, seeing that he was condemned, repenting, brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,

units.la: 4. Dicens, Peccavi prodito sanguine innoxio. At illi dixerunt, Quid ad nos? tu videris.
units.tr: 4. Saying, I have sinned, in that I have betrayed innocent blood. But they said, What is that to us? See thou to it.

units.la: 5. Ipse vero proiectis (illis numis) argenteis in templum, secessit: & abiens strangulavit (se.)
units.tr: 5. And he cast down the pieces of silver into the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.

units.la: 6. Principes autem Sacerdotes acceptis (numis) illis argenteis dixerunt, Non licet eos mittere in Corbanan, quoniam pretium sanguinis est.
units.tr: 6. And the chief priests took the silver pieces and said, It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.

units.la: 7. Consilio autem capto, emerunt ex eis agrum illum figuli ad sepulturam hospitum.
units.tr: 7. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in.

units.la: 8. Quapropter vocatus est ager ille, ager sanguinis usque in hodiernum diem.
units.tr: 8. Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.

units.la: 9. (Tunc impletum est quod dictum est per Ieremiam Prophetam, dicentem, Et acceperunt triginta (numos) argenteos, pretium aestimati, quem aestimatum fuit a filiis Israel.
units.tr: 9. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, And they took thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value;

units.la: 10. Et dederunt eos ad emendum agrum illum figuli, sicut constituit mihi Dominus.)
units.tr: 10. And gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord appointed me.

units.la: VVM sermone superiore satis copiosè de vera Resipiscentia ex sola immensa Dei gratia ad salutem promanante, & contrà de Poenitentia cuius initium est solus peccati sensus ad desperationem ac mortem, diflerucrimus, multa supersunt nobis in hac historia sigillatim, tum de infelici Iudae exitio, tum de Sacerdotibus apud quos suum facinus professus est excutienda.
units.tr: Since in the previous sermon we have discussed at sufficient length the true repentance that flows from the immense grace of God alone unto salvation, and on the other hand the repentance whose beginning is nothing but a sense of sin leading to despair and death, there remain many things in this history to be examined one by one: both the unhappy end of Judas and the priests before whom he confessed his crime.

units.la: Ac primùm quidem dicitur Iudas tandiu exspectasse dum aduersus Christum latam audiuisset sententiam, hoc est, morte dignus esset à Caiapha & alijs iudicatus, quorum in potestate non esset nec pronuntiare nec exequi capitale iudicium, quorsum enim ad Pilatum confugisset? Ex quo apparet Iudam suum Dominum prodentem, sibi persuasisse nunquam eò deuenturum ipsum, sed è manibus hostium quando & qua ratione vellet facillimè, vt sepiùs alias, elapsurum: qua quum excidisset opinione, nec amplius dubitaret quin Sacerdotes voti fierent compotes ex immensa illa in quam se praecipitem dederat abysso, nulla potuisse ratione amplius emergere.
units.tr: And first, it is said that Judas waited so long until he had heard the sentence pronounced against Christ, that is, until he was judged worthy of death by Caiaphas and the others, who had no power either to pronounce or to carry out a capital sentence. For otherwise, why would he have fled to Pilate? From this it appears that Judas, who betrayed his Lord, had persuaded himself that it would never come to that, but that he would easily escape from the hands of the enemies whenever and however he wished, as he had often done before. When this opinion failed him, and he no longer doubted that the priests would obtain their desire, he thought there was no way at all to rise again out of the immense abyss into which he had thrown himself.

units.la: At quo fundamento nitebatur haec opinio? Nempe, quod istis maiora Iesum Christum posse nosset, & cogitaret Christum vitae suae gloriaeque cupidum, nunquam hanc potestatem suis inimicis in se permissurum. At cur non renocat in memoriam, quae huic opinioni ni contradicebant, tam expressas, tam claras & perspicuas, in hac præsertim vltima Cœna, Domini, non tantùm de suis vinculis, sed de in Gentilium potestatem traditione, & cruce ipsa prædictiones? Nimirum illa quidem Magistro prædicente, curabat scilicet Iudas ac credebat pro arbitrio. Et in hoc peccatum incurrunt quicunque fidem partim humanis iudiciis partim Dei verbo miscent, vt aquam vino, 2.Corinth.2.17. & aquam cisternarum hominum manu cauatarum cum puro fonte aquæ viuæ, Ierem.2.vers.13.aut fermentum Pharisaicum pura farina, Luc.12.vers.1. quum Dei verbum fidei misceri ad credentis viuificationem oporteat. Hebr.4.2. Non errauit igitur Iudas in potentiæ Christi apprehensione: at suæ rationis sensum sequutus, de eo quod esset Magister facturus ex sua fantasia, non ex ipsius verbis iudicans præceps ruit, immemor infelix causæ ob quam in mundum Dei Filius aduenirset, & eorum quæ præter superiora tam disertè, támque dilucidè prædixerat Ioh. 12.vers.32.se nimirum è terra sublatum, omnes esse tracturum ad seipsum, & de figura serpentis æneî. Iohan.3. vers.14. & de ligno Ionæ, Matth.12. vers.40. Denique, non animaduerterat infelix immensam illam Domini sui charitatem, qua non modò suæ gloriæ sed vitæ etiam erat quos Pater ei donauerat antepositurus, Iohan.10.11.& 15.Rom.5.v.8. Nec solus Iudas ita se perdidit, sed iam ante (quod ipsum memoriæ mandasse oportuit) Petrus hac impulsus opinione melius Domino suo cognoscendi quid ipsum deceret, ausus fuerat his verbis Dominum compellare, Propitius sis tibi Domine, nequaquam hoc erit tibi. Quod quidem Iesu Christo tantopere displicuit, ut ad eum conuersus diceret, Abscede à me Satana, scandalo es mihi. Matth. 16 22. Iudas igitur icro nimis animaducrtens vlterius negotium praeter suam opinionem processisse, nullumque apparere remedium, in desperatione cadit. Sic initio à recta deflectentes via, facilem in eam regressum sibi persuadent: sic qui alterius parui momenti rem abstulit sibi ingit se nunquam in furé euasurum: sic qui fur est, nunquam in latronem, quum plerumque tamen à minimis ad maxima deueniatur, nisi Domino pro immensa illa sua misericordia nos immutante resipiscamus, ut Iudam ex fure proditorem factum, mortisque Domini sui reum conspicimus.
units.tr: But on what foundation did this opinion rest? Surely on this: he knew that Jesus Christ was able to do greater things than these, and he thought that Christ, who loved his own life and glory, would never permit this power to be given to his enemies over himself. But why did he not call to mind the things that contradicted this opinion, so explicit, so clear and so plain, especially in this last supper of the Lord, both concerning his bonds and concerning his being handed over into the power of the Gentiles, and concerning the cross itself? Of course, while the Master was foretelling these things, Judas was caring for and believing in his own judgment. And into this sin fall all who mix faith partly with human judgments and partly with the word of God, as one mixes water with wine (2 Cor. 2.17), and the water of cisterns hollowed out by human hands with the pure spring of living water (Jer. 2.13), or Pharisaical leaven with pure flour (Luke 12.1), whereas the word of God ought to be mixed with faith for the quickening of the believer (Heb. 4.2). Judas therefore did not err in grasping Christ's power, but, following the sense of his own reason, and judging from his own fancy what the Master would do, and not from his words, he rushed headlong, unhappy and forgetful of the cause for which the Son of God had come into the world. He had forgotten what the Lord had foretold so plainly and so clearly, beyond the things mentioned above: that he would indeed be lifted up from the earth and draw all men to himself (John 12.32), and concerning the figure of the bronze serpent (John 3.14), and the sign of Jonah (Matt. 12.40). Finally, the unhappy man did not notice that immense love of his Lord, by which he was about to set those whom the Father had given him before his own glory and even before his life (John 10.11; 15; Rom. 5.8). Nor was Judas alone in losing himself in this way. Earlier still (and this too ought to have been kept in memory), Peter, driven by this same opinion, thought he knew better than his Lord what was fitting for him, and dared to address the Lord with these words: "Be it far from you, Lord; this shall never happen to you." And this so displeased Jesus Christ that, turning to him, he said, "Get behind me, Satan; you are a stumbling block to me" (Matt. 16.22). Judas, therefore, realising too late that the business had gone beyond his opinion and that no remedy appeared, fell into despair. Thus those who at the beginning turn aside from the right way persuade themselves that a return to it will be easy: thus he who has taken something of small worth promises himself that he will never become a thief; thus a thief is never made a robber, although as a rule people advance from the smallest things to the greatest, unless, by the immense mercy of the Lord changing us, we repent, as we see Judas, from a thief made a traitor, and guilty of the death of his Lord.

units.la: Eodem sane qui sacrosanctum Dei verbum suis glossematibus depravant, incidunt quo Iudas, ex suo sensu quae Dominus de sibi Hierosolymis eventuris praedixerat exponens. Sic suo sensui nimium dediti, Trinitatis doctrina, vnionis hypostaticae, duarum in vno Iesu Christo naturarum, ac pene omnes fidei articulos adulterarunt.
units.tr: Into the same error fall those who corrupt the most holy Word of God with their own glosses, as Judas did when he explained in his own sense what the Lord had foretold about what was to befall him at Jerusalem. Being so devoted to their own sense, they have corrupted the doctrine of the Trinity, the hypostatic union, the two natures in the one Jesus Christ, and almost all the articles of faith.

units.la: Hic porro Satanae nobis ingens metuendus dolus, nos ab extremo in aliud impellentis extremum, quae totidem praecipitia sunt. Ut igitur vehementer hallucinantur qui Dei verbum bum naturali suo sensui subiiciunt, sic nō minus aberrant toto cœlo, qui, quòd fides sensus naturales in ordinem cogere debet, articulos fidei supernaturales ex suo sensu sibi fingunt, quum tamen fidem, qua ratio nostra sensuíque captiuandi sunt, solo Dei verbo bene intellecto, non autem omniis noltris veteribus aut nouis oporteat niti.
units.tr: Here, moreover, is a great snare of Satan that we must fear: he drives us from one extreme to the other, and both are precipices. So those who subject God's Word to their natural sense go terribly astray, but no less far astray are those who, because faith must bring our natural senses into order, invent for themselves supernatural articles of faith from their own sense. Yet faith, by which our reason and senses are to be taken captive, must rest on the Word of God rightly understood alone, not on any of our old or new notions.

units.la: Exempli gratiâ, quæ controuersia magni est hodie momenti: negantibus nobis Iesu Christi corpus realiter & essentialiter in his terris esse: vel in Missa panem & vinum in corpus & sanguinem essentialem Iesu Christi commutari: vel esse in Cœna aut alibi cum hoc pane vel hoc vino: contrà vero dicentibus Iesum Christum secundùm humanam naturam, esse in cœlo, ibique esse quærendum & fide amplectendum, quò nos tum simplex verbum tum Sacramenta deducunt (nimirum quòd vere humanum corpus nec sit inuisibile, nec fine suis dimensionibus, ac proinde quantum sit, nec plurib9 simul locis) itaque exprobratur Dei Omnipotentiâ à nobis humanis sensibus subiici. Excipimus contrà fundamentum illud absentiæ corporis essentialis Iesu Christi, non hac sola naturali ratione fulciri, sed quatenus hæc naturalis ratio tribus articulis nostræ fidei nititur. Horum primus vera filij Dei incarnatio. Alter realis & essentialis eius quòd ad humanitatem è terris excelsus, & ascensus supra cœlos omnes, quibus eum oportere contineri dicit Petrus, Act. 3. 8. vsque ad diem vltimum, ita vt coelestis illa gloria, nec naturam illi, nec essentiales proprietates verè humani corporis ademerit, vt verè Catholica & Apostolica Ecclesia aduersus Eutychianorum & Monophysitarum errores ex Sacris optime constituit. Tertius est, ipse eum venturum vivos & mortuos iudicatum: cum quorum articulorum veritate non magis potest praesentia essentialis humanitatis Christi in coelis & in terra, aut pluribus locis simul, quàm lux cum tenebris consistere. Huius igitur doctrinae haec clto conclusio, ad tam perniciosum vitandum errorem, credenda quidem quae supra sensum nostrum scriptura docet non tamen sibi articulos supernaturales ex sui sensus naturalis opinione fingendos: propterea quod tanto interuallo inter se quae Deus dixit, & quae nobis somnia finximus distent, quanto veritas & mendacium. Facile vero supernaturalia, quae credenda discernentur ab imaginariis & fanaticis, si vera esse dicamus supernaturalia, quae sine contradictione cum fidei nostrae articulis conspirant: falsa vero quae vel leuissime repugnant, sic docente nos Apostolo. Rom.12.6. & Esaia ad Legem & testimonium ablegante, Esa.8.20.
units.tr: Take, for example, the controversy which is today of great importance. We deny that the body of Jesus Christ is really and essentially on this earth, or that in the Mass the bread and wine are changed into the essential body and blood of Jesus Christ, or that it is in the Supper, or elsewhere, together with this bread or this wine. On the contrary, others say that Jesus Christ, according to his human nature, is in heaven, and that there he is to be sought and embraced by faith, to which both the plain word and the Sacraments lead us (namely, that a truly human body is neither invisible nor without its dimensions, and therefore neither as large as it is nor in several places at once). Thus, they charge us with subjecting God's omnipotence to human senses. We, on the contrary, take exception to that foundation of the absence of Jesus Christ's essential body: it is supported not by this natural reason alone, but insofar as this natural reason rests on three articles of our faith. The first of these is the true incarnation of the Son of God. The second is his real and essential exaltation from the earth as to his humanity, and his ascension above all the heavens, where Peter says he must be received until the last day (Act. 3. 8.), so that that heavenly glory has taken from him neither the nature nor the essential properties of a truly human body, as the truly Catholic and Apostolic Church has rightly established from the Scriptures against the errors of the Eutychians and Monophysites. The third is that he himself will come to judge the living and the dead. With the truth of these articles the essential presence of Christ's humanity in heaven and on earth, or in several places at once, cannot any more consist than light can with darkness. Therefore the immediate conclusion of this doctrine, to avoid so pernicious an error, is that we must indeed believe what Scripture teaches above our sense, but must not invent supernatural articles from the opinion of our natural sense, because the things God has said and the dreams we have invented are as far apart as truth and lie. Indeed, supernatural things to be believed are easily distinguished from imaginary and fanatical ones: we say those supernatural things are true which agree without contradiction with the articles of our faith, and those are false which conflict with them even in the slightest way, as the Apostle teaches us (Rom. 12.6), and as Isaiah sends us away to the Law and the testimony (Esa. 8.20).

units.la: Ad hunc igitur primum scopulum Iudas impegit: deinde multo crassius & fine praetextu quum sopita magis magisque conscientia & ad Domini sermone auribus obseratis, sibi persuasit Dominum suum quicquid acciderit nihilominus semper cuasurum, se vero suis rebus
units.tr: Judas stumbled on this first rock. Then, much more crudely and without any pretext, when his conscience was more and more lulled to sleep and his ears were closed to the Lord's word, he persuaded himself that his Lord would always provide whatever happened, while he himself would always look after his own affairs.

units.la: Quàm exiiosa sit auaritia in ipsi aliis, saro, tum aliis. rebus auctis loculis semper consulturum. Heu nimium caecos hac in parte mortales, quasi Deo illudentes in gratiam eius semper sint reddituri? Istud igitur alta mente defigamus, & singulis horis ac momentis pensitemus, omne peccatum inter Deum & homines diuisionem efficere: duobus inter se repugnantibus Dominis neminem seruire posse, praesertim Deo ac Mammonae, quod Iudas tamen hic, licet praemonente Domino tentauit, Matth. 8. 24. Quid vero nisi verissimum ad haec eloquar? Nec pelicet Regni coelorum esse participes nequeant in quibus qualecunque peccatum regnat. Gal. 5. 21. non tamen frustra Mammonis mentionem fieri, & auaritiam ab Apostolo idololatriam dici. Col. 3. 5. malorumque omnium radicem, non solum ab Apostolo. 1. Tim. 6. 10. sed ab ipsis etiam prophanis? Sed sane siquid est a quo nobis exitium imminet, illud est. Utinam vero Deus Opt. Max. a quo nostram diu tamque variis modis edocti sumus ab ipso solo pendendum, & hic veluti theatrum erectum est in quo omnes quid sit Deo soli fidere doceantur, hanc nostris mentibus doctrinam, ad ipsius honoris gloriam, & no stram salutem altius infigat.
units.tr: How dangerous avarice is, both in itself and in others. Once his goods were increased he would always look to his purse. Alas, how very blind mortals are in this matter, as if mocking God, they will always be reconciled to his favour! Let us therefore fix this firmly in our minds and weigh it every hour and moment: every sin creates a division between God and man, and no one can serve two masters who are opposed to each other, especially God and Mammon. Judas nevertheless tried this here, though the Lord had warned him, Matth. 8. 24. What could I say that is more true than this? Nor can those be partakers of the kingdom of heaven in whom any sin at all reigns, Gal. 5. 21. Yet the mention of Mammon is not made in vain, and avarice is called idolatry by the Apostle, Col. 3. 5, and the root of all evils, 1 Tim. 6. 10, not only by the Apostle but even by profane writers. But surely, if there is anything by which ruin threatens us, it is this. Would that God Almighty, from whom we have been taught for so long and in so many ways to depend on him alone, and here set up as a kind of theatre in which all are taught what it is to trust in God alone, would fix this doctrine more deeply in our minds, to the glory of his own honour and our salvation.

units.la: Narratur deinceps non tantum in genere Iudam fallum se peccasse, sed suum peccatum diserte expressisse. Ne vero nos ab improbo licet aliquid hic discere pudeat, procul tamen eius vestigia refugientes. Primum enim sola Iudam hic premit conscientia, & tamen non
units.tr: Next it is told that Judas not only sinned in general, but plainly stated his sin. Yet, lest we be ashamed to learn anything here from the wicked man, let us nonetheless flee far from his footsteps. For first, here conscience alone oppresses Judas, and yet not

units.la: C. j. tantum admittit,sed etiam promulgat, in ipso templo, coram insignibus viris miserum se peccatorem, immo in omnibus perditissimū. At contra quàm multos reperias, etiam inter eos quos praeterita vita satis coarguit, qui vocati, conuictíque peccatorum se illorum vel minimo sensu tangi demonstrent? Quos, vi veritatis aliquam confessionem extorquentes, audias mussitare, Peccatores sumus, Homines sumus, etiam in eos à quibus monentur illud ausuros retorquere, ni quodam metu cohibentur? Longè verò fuit Iudae amplior confessio, minimè se aliis hominibus aequantis, sed se proditorem, perfidè iusti sanguine pecunia diuendito confitentis. Ita sunt nimirum ore aperto peccata detestanda, primum coram Deo sine exceptione, deinde longius etiam, quum ita ferret Dei gloria, & e re proximorum erit.
units.tr: C. j. only admits his sin but publishes it, in the temple itself and before distinguished men, declaring himself a wretched sinner, indeed the worst of all. But on the contrary, how many will you find, even among those whom their past life sufficiently convicts, who, when called and convicted of their sins, show that they are touched by the least sense of them? Hearing them, when the power of truth forces some confession from them, you will hear them mumble, "We are sinners, we are men," and even turn this back on those by whom they are admonished, unless they are held back by some fear. Judas's confession was far fuller: he did not equate himself with other men but confessed himself a traitor, who treacherously sold innocent blood for money. Thus sins are indeed to be openly detested: first before God without exception, and then further still, when the glory of God requires it and it will serve the good of our neighbours.

units.la: At quum praeterea veritas huic homicidae proditori tam apertum innocentiae nostri Servatoris testimonium extorserit, qua ratione putas falsorum iudicum notam effugituros qui sententiam mortis aduersus cum vt reum tulerunt?
units.tr: But since truth has moreover extorted from this murderer and traitor so clear a testimony to our Saviour's innocence, by what means do you think those false judges will escape the stain of their guilt, who pronounced the sentence of death against him as a guilty man?

units.la: Abiectum à Iuda in templum argentum addit Euangelista, Sacerdotibus illud recipere nolentibus: ex quo discendum: (etli aliam quàm Iudae noltram mentem esse oportet) quousque malum sit detestandum: nempe vt non tantum à malo abstineatur, aut malum admissum animi aegritudo sequatur quatur:sed etiam male parta sic abiiciantur,vt ne leuiter quidem attingantur, etiam male quæsita.Iud.23.vt sub Lege olim,idipsum erat pollutum quod à polluto contactum fuerat: & ipse Dominus nō modò suo templo procul esse iubebat,scortum, sed etiam scorti mercedem est abominatus, Aggæ. 2. 14. Deut. 23. v. 18. Quare Dauidem etiam protestantem audiamus sibi esse religioni falsorum Numinum nomen enuntiare. Psal. 16. 4.
