units.la: errorisha nc omnem idololatriam fuga sua ad signum Crucis, & ad aquam lustralem obfi- gnauit, mille animas inuadens, dum fe ab ali- quo Dæmoniaco simulat illis rebus eiici vel fugari.Ecquis enim istorum hominum & Spi- rituum Coniuratorum fraudes & impofturas non nouit.Agite igitur,fratres,Deo quàm ma ximas gratias agamus, quòd ex abominanda illa crucis idololatria nos per immensam suam misericordiam ereptos Crucifixum ipsum & quicquid ab illo bonorum expectamus docuit:illáque omnia instrumenta,vnà cum car-nificibus & eorum crudelitate detestemur. At veram Crucem Euangelicæ professionis indi-uiduam comitem, quæcunque tandem illa sit, & quantumlibet onerosa subeamus alacres ad exemplum Apostoli,& tanquam insignia nostri Ducis nobis præuntis sequamur. Gal. 6.14. & 17. illius suffulti virtute qui fidelis est, & nunquam nos supra vires quas ipsemet suppeditat tentari patietur,1. Cor.10.13.Nam & per Crucem in dilectissimis conformitas inter caput & membra ipsius obsignatur,restante Domino,passiones quas cum illo perpetimur certissimum esse pignus illius promissionis,simul cum ipso patientes etiam simul regnaturos. Rom.8.17.& 2.Tim.2.12,Exemplum ç̃lto miser ille Cyrenæus, qui quum hominum respectu forte in carnifices istos incidisset,à Deo tamen electus omnibus Domini fidelibus discipulis repræsentandis,hunc honorem est allequutus, vt ex ignoto & humili rustico, celebris factus V. iij. fit tantorum testium in hac historia commen-datione, nec tantum suo nomine & patria sed vtrorumque etiam liberorum nomine desi-gnatus: minimè nominaturis eos Euangelistis nisi Ecclesiæ deinceps ex Dei gratia peculiari quadam ratione innotuissent.
units.tr: ...by his flight to the sign of the cross and to holy water sealed up all idolatry, attacking a thousand souls while pretending to be cast out or put to flight from some demoniac by those things. For who of these men and conjurers of spirits does not know their frauds and impostures? Come then, brothers, let us give the greatest thanks to God, who by his immense mercy has rescued us from that abominable idolatry of the cross and taught us to look to the Crucified himself for all good things. Let us detest all those instruments together with the executioners and their cruelty. But the true cross, the inseparable companion of the evangelical profession, whatever it may be and however burdensome, let us undertake cheerfully after the example of the Apostle, and follow it as the insignia of our Leader who goes before us. Gal. 6.14 & 17. Supported by the virtue of him who is faithful, and who will never allow us to be tempted beyond the strength he himself supplies. 1 Cor. 10.13. For through the cross the conformity between head and members is sealed in his beloved ones, and the Lord remains. The sufferings we undergo with him are a most certain pledge of that promise, that suffering together with him we shall also reign together with him. Rom. 8.17 & 2 Tim. 2.12. Consider the example of that poor Cyrenian. He may have fallen by chance into the hands of those executioners, so far as men were concerned, but God chose him to represent all the Lord's faithful disciples. He obtained this honour: from an unknown and humble countryman he became famous, and in this history he is commended as one of such great witnesses. He is named not only by his own name and country but also by the names of both his sons. The evangelists would not have named them unless they had later become known to the Church by a special mode of God's grace.

units.la: Sequitur apud historiam magnam populi multitudinem cum sequutam esse, & nomi-natim quasdam slentes & lugentes eum fœmi-nas. Est autem verisimile immo extra omne du-bium in tanto populi concursu, varia homi-num fuisse genera, quorum alij eiusdem fue-rint cum Caiapha farinæ, alij Christum ex ze-lo, sed sine scientia condemnarint, pro quibus etiam Christus moriens orauit, Luc. 23.34. & exauditus est, Act. 2. 37. & 38. alij fortasse me-liùs edocti, factum istud, cum fœminis de qui-bus hic agitur, nequaquam approbarint. In-terea tamen nullus sceleratis istis arguendis os aperuisse memoratur, ac ne ipse quidem, de quo postea, dilectus discipulus. Tanta fuit tùc quorundam ignorantia, & piorum infirmitas in hoc Crucis scandalo. At in hoc, vt & in hac historia tota nobis altiùs ad Dei consilium ele-uandi sunt oculi, volentis cum qui pro mundo vitam dabat, putà pro electis omnibus ex omni gente & natione collectis, minimè clàm in remoto aliquo angulo, sed in aperto velut in omnium hominum conspectu mori, in tam magna tamque populosa ciuitate, tam solenni festo: ad quod non tantùm Iudæorum omnium ex omni Iudæa patresfamilias conuenire, sed etiam in longius remotis orbis terrarum plagis habitantes oportuit, quantum quidem ab illis fieri potuit, profanis etiam eo multis concurrentibus, quod ex sequenti festo Pentecostes satis est conspicuum.
units.tr: The history goes on to say that a great multitude of people followed him, and certain women who wept and lamented him by name. It is probable, indeed beyond all doubt, that in so great a crowd there were various kinds of men. Some were of the same stripe as Caiaphas; others condemned Christ out of zeal but without knowledge, and for these Christ prayed as he died, Luc. 23.34, and was heard, Act. 2.37 & 38. Others, perhaps better taught, did not approve of that deed, together with the women of whom we speak. Yet no one is recorded as having opened his mouth to accuse those wicked men, not even the beloved disciple, of whom more later. So great was the ignorance of some and the weakness of the pious in this scandal of the cross. But in this, as in this whole history, our eyes must be raised higher to God's counsel. He willed that the one who gave his life for the world (that is, for all the elect gathered from every people and nation) should not die secretly in some remote corner, but openly, as in the sight of all men, in so great and populous a city, at so solemn a feast. To that feast it was necessary that not only the heads of households from all Judea should gather, but also those living in the more distant regions of the world, as far as they could come. Many profane people also came together, as is clear from the feast of Pentecost that followed.

units.la: Quòd verò nullus in tam multis Christum palàm cófessus est, testari sic voluit Dominus totam illorum omnium salutem à sola mera- que eius esse gratia & misericordia, quorum nullus non se indignū ea præberet, aliis quidem scelere suo perditis, & gratia reiicietibus, aliis non immerito abnegatibus Crucifixu iftu non dissimilib. vt qui hominū metu suo filetio bonā causam proderent, quā tueri illos decuerat, quos tamen sua gratia Christus dignatus est quum libuit, non ita multò post, vt sumus, in historia sepulturæ pluribus audituri.
units.tr: Because none of so many openly confessed Christ, the Lord wanted to show that the salvation of all of them rests on his sheer mercy and grace alone, since none of them deserved it. Some were destroyed by their own crime and rejected grace. Others, not undeservedly, disowned him, much like those who crucified this man. Some betrayed the good cause by silence, through fear of men, though it became them to defend it. Yet Christ deigned to favour these, by his grace, when it pleased him, as we shall hear more fully in the history of the burial, not long after.

units.la: De mulieribus verò præterquàm quòd sexus est ad fletum & misericordiam procliuior, cóstat aliquas fuisse, præsertim ex iis quæ fuerant eum à Galilæa sequutæ Luc. 23. 49. peculiari à Christo fauore exceptas, dignatásque vt non vno loco sacra scriptura testatur: Christo vicissim & ipsius familiæ necessaria ministrates ex suis facultatibus Luc. 8. 2. & 3. quo loco quædam etiam nominantur, vt & in historia sequenti sepulturæ. Lugebant igitur hæ fœminæ: fletu suo satis testantes factum sibi non probari: & sic aliquid amplius quàm viri ipsi, ac ne ipse quidem dilectus discipulus præstantes: Etsi verò laude dignus quidem est ille misericordiæ affectus, tam iusta ratione nixus, V. iiij. tamen nihil nisi humanus affectus & male compositus fuit.Quorsum enim hi gemitus ac lamenta, nisi vt Christum veluti perditum deflerent, de resurrectione mox istam morte sequutura nihil cogitarent, nec fructus ex ea proventuros pensitantes: adeo vt vere dici posset nō modò nullam fidem in ipsis fuisse, sine qua tamē placere Deo nemo poterat,sed etiā contrā nihil tūc mentē earū occupasse nisi contraria omnia iis quæ de Christo sunt ad salutē necessaria. At vero Dominus ea quæ fidei semina prius earū cordibus indiderat penitus suffocari passus non erat.Reliquas vero mulieres quod ipse cōpellat Dominus,vt patet ex eo quod Filias Hierusalē appellat,obseruandū in primis, Iesum Christū qui prius quū de sui priuata defensione ageretur altū silentium egerat, ob eas quas suo loco causas indicauimus,contrà quum vel de munere ad quod erat vocatus ageretur obeundo, ipso infirmitatis suæ tempore durissimo, tamen os palā aperuisse, vel gloriæ Patris tuendæ,primum apud Caiaphā, Matth.26.64. Marc.14.62. Luc 22.70. deinde apud Pilatum. Ioh.18.36.& 37.& 19.11. vel docedis iis qui opus habebat,vt Petrus,Matth.26.50. & seruus Maximi Pontificis.Ioh.18.23.& hoc loco mulieres iltæ: quod & ipsum in Cruce fecit,qua re veris & fidelibus Ecclesiarū Pastoribus in ministerij sui fideliter exercendo munere præiuit exēplo.
units.tr: As for the women, besides the fact that their sex is more inclined to weeping and pity, it is clear that some of them, especially those who had followed him from Galilee, were singled out for special favour by Christ and held in honour, as Scripture testifies in more than one place (Luke 23:49). They also served Christ and his household with their own means (Luke 8:2–3), and some of them are named in that passage, as also in the following history of the burial. So these women mourned, sufficiently showing by their weeping that what had been done to him did not meet with their approval. In this they did something more than the men themselves, not even the beloved disciple excepted. Yet although that feeling of pity deserves praise, being grounded in so just a reason, it was nothing more than a merely human emotion, and badly directed. For why these groans and laments, unless they wept for Christ as one lost, thinking nothing of the resurrection that would soon follow his death, and not weighing the fruit that would come from it? So much so that it could truly be said that not only was there no faith in them, without which no one can please God, but also that their minds were then occupied with nothing except things contrary to all that concerns Christ's saving work. But the Lord did not allow the seeds of faith that he had earlier sown in their hearts to be utterly suffocated. As for the other women, whom the Lord addresses as he does, as is clear from his calling them daughters of Jerusalem, we must note above all that Jesus Christ, who earlier, when his own private defence was at issue, had kept a deep silence for the reasons we indicated in their place, on the contrary, when the discharge of the office to which he was called was at stake, even in the most severe time of his weakness, opened his mouth openly. He did so either to defend the glory of the Father, first before Caiaphas (Matt. 26:64; Mark 14:62; Luke 22:70), then before Pilate (John 18:36–37; 19:11), or to teach those who needed it, as with Peter (Matt. 26:50) and the servant of the High Priest (John 18:23), and in this place the women. He also did this on the cross. By this means he went before the true and faithful pastors of the Churches as an example in faithfully discharging the office of their ministry.

units.la: Notandū deinde Dominū mulieres istas minimè increpasse quasi aliquid mali seriò patrates, cum cui tā insignis fiebat iniuria miseratæ. ratæ, vt res ipsa per se loquebatur: sed duo voluisse ipsas longè iustis gemitibus & plancitibus magis necessaria docere, de quibus illæ tamen parum aut nihil cogitaret. Primum, nequaquam esse de se tanquam de homine perdito ex statu in quo ipsum intuebantur iudicandum. Breui enim illas contra cospectuas quanta vis eius esset ac seuera potetia, suos hostes vindicta persequentis, & in eorum capita suam ira contorquentis. Alte rum sibi ipsis de se potius, quam de illo cogitandum, vtpote quæ in horrendæ iustius vindictæ iusto Dei furore immittendæ parte essent venturæ. Quas eius minas non irritas fuisse tristis gentis illius, post elapsos annos circiter triginta quatuor, exitus comprobauit.
units.tr: Next, we must note that the Lord did not rebuke these women as if they had seriously done anything wrong, since such a notable wrong was being done to him that they pitied him, as the matter itself spoke for itself. Rather, he wished to teach them two things, far more necessary than their weeping and wailing, of which they thought little or nothing. The first: that he was not to be judged by them, as a man lost, from the state in which they saw him. For he would soon show them how great his power was, and how severe his might, when he pursues his enemies with vengeance and turns his wrath upon their heads. The second: that they ought to think about themselves rather than about him, since they would be among those who must bear the fury of the just vengeance of God, which is to fall upon that dreadful day. That his threats were not empty was proved by the outcome for that sad nation, some thirty-four years later.

units.la: Nec vero solas illas Hierosolymitanas fœminas, aut ea tantum tempora, designauit, sed totum peregrinationis filiorum Dei in hac vita tempus, quo Iesu Christo factos coformes hac se solari ipse oportet, Dominum olim de ipsorum causa iudicaturum, deque ipsorum hostibus vindictam sumturum. Et quæsto quam multa iam nostris oculis obuersantur horum iudiciorum exempla, præsertim in Galliarum Hierosolyma, etiam hactenus oblata misericordia væsano Diabolico que furore despuente? Nec sane satis scio, an excepto vltimo illo excidio maior inter duas vllas vrbes esse queat conformitas, quam inter illa Iudæorum & hac de qua loquor Hierosolymam: & profecto, licet sero, tandem tamen eandem scelera-tos omnes eadem malitia ramque væsano furore sanctos persequentes vindicta manet.
units.tr: Nor did he point only to those Jerusalem women, or only to that time. He pointed to the whole time of the pilgrimage of the children of God in this life, in which we must be conformed to Jesus Christ and console ourselves with this: that the Lord will one day judge their cause and take vengeance on their enemies. And indeed, how many examples of these judgments already meet our eyes, especially in this Jerusalem of France, where mercy has been offered until now, though the mad, diabolical fury spits it out! Nor do I really know whether, apart from that final destruction, any greater likeness can exist between two cities than between that Jerusalem of the Jews and this one I am speaking of. And certainly, though late, vengeance awaits all the wicked who, with the same malice and the same mad fury, persecute the saints.

units.la: Obseruandum denique licet videantur omnis generis calamitates & afflictiones quas hoc loco Dominus igni comparat, solis Dei filiis, vt illud copiose Propheta canit Psal.73. præ filiis huius seculi, reseruari, fore tamen vt exitus ostendat tantum inter eos esse discrimé quantum inter lignum aridum & viride, quum hoc minime ad flammam comparetur, & licet in flammam iniectum, se tamen ab ea tueatur, contrà vero lignum illud aridum, facinorosi nimirum homines quos hæc similitudo præsentat, ligni viridis ignem accendentes, tandem suo tempore sint in flammas immittendi, tanquam illis debiti & destinati, quibus cum posteris absumantur quòd ad huius mundi distatum, & inde in alium ignem ἀσβεστον coniiciendi. At contrà lignum illud viride cuius hic mentio fit, igni quidem & flammis est obnoxium, sed castigationis & probationis, quo si fuerit expolitum & confirmatum, non autem absumptum, in perpetuum coram Deo manet in benedictionem, qua via tandem in veram suam & perpetuam requiem ac beatitatem perducitur. Obsecro vero vos, fratres, annon ista fidei oculis intuentes, dicturi sumus eos prorsus amentes qui dubij hærent sint-ne partes Ecclesiæ vel mundi sequuturi: quíque in Dei Ecclesia coronæ illius spinæ aculeos sentientes, purpuram ad finem vsque perseuerantibus præparatam non recordantur, Esau non absimiles, benedictionem paternam vel offula Iacobo diuendentis? Deum Opt.
units.tr: Finally, we must observe that although all kinds of calamities and afflictions, which the Lord here compares to fire, seem reserved only for the sons of God, as the Prophet sings at length in Psalm 73, yet the outcome will show that there is as great a difference among them as between dry wood and green. Green wood is hardly comparable to a flame, and even if it is thrown into the fire, it protects itself from it. On the other hand, the dry wood, that is, the wicked men whom this comparison portrays, kindling the green wood, will at last, in their time, be thrown into the flames, as if they were owed and destined to them, to be consumed with their offspring, when the state of this world is ended, and then to be cast into another, unquenchable fire. But that green wood of which there is mention here is indeed liable to fire and flames, but for chastisement and testing. If it has been refined and strengthened by these, and not consumed, it remains before God for ever for a blessing, and by this way is at last brought to its true and everlasting rest and blessedness. And I beg you, brothers, shall we not, looking at these things with the eyes of faith, say that those are utterly mad who hang in doubt, uncertain whether they will follow the side of the Church or of the world? Those who, feeling the prickles of that crown of thorns in God's Church, do not remember the purple prepared for those who persevere to the end, are not unlike Esau, who sold his father's blessing for a morsel to Jacob.

units.la: Huius fe-culi filii sunt lignum aridum, quod arde-t flamis ire Dei. Filii vero Dei sunt lignum viride, quos ignis castigatio nis & probationis paulatim perficit. Opt. Max. precor, vt quemadmodum huc nos in Ecclesiam suam ex variis terrarum nationibus coegit, & hactenus mirabili quadam ratione tuitus est, sic pro immensa ipsius bonitate in posterum conseruet, & ita corroboret, vt eum qui nobis eandem viam ingressus exemplo praeit, suo sanguine paratam sequamur, vt tandem quo peruenit ipse tandem etiam peruenia-mus ad illius nimirum Regni fruitionem, in quo sumus illi cohaeredes futuri, quandoquidem illud nobis ita dispositum est, vt est illi à Patre dispositum. Luc.22.29.
units.tr: The sons of this age are the dry wood, which burns in the flames of God's wrath. But the sons of God are the green wood, which the fire of chastisement and testing gradually perfects. I pray to God, best and greatest, that just as he has gathered us here into his Church from the various nations of the earth, and has hitherto protected us in a wonderful way, so by his immense goodness he will preserve us in the future and strengthen us, so that we may follow him who has gone before us on this way, the way prepared by his own blood. Thus at last we may arrive where he has arrived, that is, to the enjoyment of that Kingdom, in which we shall be his co-heirs, since it has been arranged for us just as it has been arranged for him by the Father (Luke 22:29).

units.la: HOMILIA VICESIMAOCTAVA.
units.tr: HOMILY XXVIII.

units.la: 33. Et quum venissent in locum qui dicitur Golgotha, quod est Calvariae locus.
units.tr: 33. And when they had come to the place called Golgotha, which is called the place of the skull.

units.la: 34. Dederunt ei acetum bibendum cum felle mistum: & quum gustasset noluit bibere.
units.tr: 34. They gave him vinegar mixed with gall to drink, and when he had tasted it, he would not drink.

units.la: 35. Postquam autem crucifixerunt eum, partiti sunt eius vestimenta, sortem iacientes, vt impleretur quod dictum est à Propheta, Partiti sunt sibi vestimenta mea, & super vestem meam miserunt sortem.
units.tr: 35. After they had crucified him, they divided his garments, casting lots, that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: They divided my garments among them, and upon my vesture they cast lots.

units.la: 36. Et sedentes servabant eum illic.
units.tr: 36. And sitting down, they kept watch over him there.

units.la: 37. Et imposuerunt super caput eius crimen ipsius scriptum, HIC EST IESVS REX ILLE IVDÆORVM.
units.tr: 37. And they put over his head his accusation written, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

units.la: 38. Tunc crucifiguntur cum eo duo latrones: unus ad dextram, & alter ad sinistram.
units.tr: 38. Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on the right and the other on the left.

units.la: MARC. 15.
units.tr: MARC. 15.

units.la: 22. Deduxerúntque eum in locum Golgotha, quod est si interpreteris, Caluariæ locus.
units.tr: 22. And they brought him to the place Golgotha, which, if you translate it, is the place of the skull.

units.la: 23. Et dederunt ei bibendum myrrhatum vinum: ipse vero non sumpsit.
units.tr: 23. And they gave him wine mingled with myrrh to drink, but he did not take it.

units.la: 24. Quúmque crucifixissent eum, partiti sunt vestimenta eius, iactα sorte super ea quis quid tolleret.
units.tr: 24. And when they had crucified him, they divided his garments, casting lots upon them to see what each should take.

units.la: 25. Erat autem hora tertia quando crucifixerunt eum.
units.tr: 25. Now it was the third hour when they crucified him.

units.la: 26. Eráтque inscriptio criminis ipsius inscripta his verbis, REX ILLE IVDÆORVM.
units.tr: 26. And the inscription of his accusation was written in these words: THE KING OF THE JEWS.

units.la: 27. Crucifixerunt etiam cum eo duos latrones: vnû ad dextram, & alterum ad sinistram eius.
units.tr: 27. They crucified with him also two robbers, one on his right and the other on his left.

units.la: 28. Et impleta est Scriptura quæ dicit, Et cum sceleratis numeratus est.
units.tr: 28. And the Scripture was fulfilled which says, And he was numbered with the wicked.

units.la: LVC. 23.
units.tr: LVC. 23.

units.la: 32. Ducebantur autem etiam alij duo (qui erant) malefici, cum eo necandi.
units.tr: 32. Two others also, who were malefactors, were led away with him to be put to death.

units.la: 33. Quum igitur venissent in locum qui vocatur Caluaria, illic crucifixerunt eum, & maleficos illos: vnum ad dextram, alterum ad sinistram.
units.tr: 33. When therefore they had come to the place called Calvary, there they crucified him and those malefactors, one on the right and the other on the left.

units.la: 34. Iesus autem dicebat, Pater, remitte hoc ipsis. Nesciunt enim quid faciant. Partientes vero vestimenta eius iecerunt sortem.
units.tr: 34. Then Jesus said, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do. And dividing his garments, they cast lots.

units.la: 38. Erat autē etiam inscriptio scripta super eum literis Græcis, & Romanis & Hebraicis, HIC EST
units.tr: 38. There was also an inscription written over him in Greek, Latin and Hebrew letters: THIS IS

units.la: EST REX ILLE IVDÆORVM.
units.tr: That is the King of the Jews.

units.la: IOH. 19.
units.tr: JOHN 19.

units.la: 16. Tunc ergo tradidit eum ipsis ut crucifigeretur. Assumpserunt autem Iesum, & abduxerunt.
units.tr: 16. Then therefore he delivered him to them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.

units.la: 17. Et ipse baiulans crucem suam inde venit in eum locum qui dicitur Caluariæ, Hebraice autem Golgotha.
units.tr: 17. And he, bearing his own cross, went out into a place called the place of a skull, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha.

units.la: 18. Vbi crucifixerunt eum, & cum eo alios duos, hinc & hinc, medium autem Iesum.
units.tr: 18. There they crucified him, and two others with him, one on either side, and Jesus in the middle.

units.la: 19. Scripsit autem etiam titulum Pilatus, & posuit super crucem. Erat vero scriptum, IESVS NAZARENVS REX ILLE IVDÆORVM.
units.tr: 19. And Pilate also wrote a title and put it on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

units.la: 20. Hunc ergo titulum multi Iudæorum legerunt: quia prope ciuitatem erat locus vbi crucifixus erat Iesus: & erat scriptum Hebraicè, Græcè & Latinè.
units.tr: 20. Many of the Jews therefore read this title, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, Greek and Latin.

units.la: 21. Dixerunt igitur Pilato Primarij Sacerdotes Iudæorum, Ne scribito, Rex ille Iudæorum: sed illum dixisse, Rex sum Iudæorum.
units.tr: 21. So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, Do not write, The King of the Jews; but that he said, I am King of the Jews.

units.la: 22. Respondit Pilatus, Quod scripsi, scripsi.
units.tr: 22. Pilate answered, What I have written, I have written.

units.la: 23. Milites ergo quum crucifixissent Iesum, acceperunt eius vestimenta, (& fecerunt quatuor partes, vnicuique militi partem) & tunicam. Erat autem tunica insutilis, à summo contexta tota.
units.tr: 23. Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments (and made four parts, a part for each soldier) and his tunic. Now the tunic was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

units.la: 24. Dixerunt ergo inter se, Ne findamus eam, sed sortiamur de illa cuius futura sit: vt Scriptura impleretur, dicens, Partiti sunt vestimenta mea sibi, & super vestem meam miserunt sortem. Milites igitur hæc fecerunt.
units.tr: 24. So they said among themselves, Let us not tear it, but cast lots for whose it shall be: that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which says, They parted my garments among them, and for my vesture they cast lots. The soldiers therefore did these things.

units.la: HACTENVS intelleximus quomodo, qui pro Ecclesia sua vera oblatio factus est, modo quodam cum iis congruo & conuenienti quibus in veteribus Legis sacrificiis adumbrabatur, captus sit, vinctus, ad summum Pontificem deductus, & ab eodem quidem immolatus quantum in ipso fuit, ad mortem eum condemnante, sed non tamen exequente, quod diuina prouidentia voluerit, vt qui seipsum offerebat ad salutem omnium electorum, ex vniuerso terrarum orbe colligendorum, non tantum Iudæorum, sola sua gratia tum Iudæos tum Gentes seruaret, ab vtrisque reiectus & modis indignissimis tractatus, vt superius est a nobis expositum. Deinceps igitur attendendum quomodo adductus sit & immolatus super altare Crucis, quod quum quatuor Euangelistæ summo consensu copiosissime descripserint, nobis illud sedulò meditandum & expendendum reliquerunt. Primum igitur locus in quem adductus est diligenter notatur ex nomine Golgotha, voce toti illi genti tunc visitata, quæ idem est, vt exprimit ipse contextus, atque Caluariæ locus: sicut in historia Iesabelis, 2.Reg.9.35. Quæ sanè vox variis expositionibus ansam dedit. Exciterunt enim iam pridem fanatici quidam homines audacissimi, qui somniarunt, atque aliis persuadere conati sunt, Caluariam illa ex qua locus ille denominabatur, fuisse ipsius Adæ Caluariam, eo loco sepultam, adeo vt ipsa crux Christi
units.tr: So far we have understood how he who was made the true offering for his Church, in a manner suited and fitting to those things that were foreshadowed in the sacrifices of the old Law, was seized, bound, and led to the high priest, and was indeed sacrificed by him as far as lay in his power, the high priest condemning him to death but not carrying it out, as divine providence willed; so that he who offered himself for the salvation of all the elect, to be gathered from the whole world and not only from the Jews, might by his grace alone preserve both Jews and Gentiles, though he was rejected by both and treated in the most unworthy ways, as we have set out above. Next, therefore, we must consider how he was led away and sacrificed upon the altar of the Cross. The four Evangelists have described this with the greatest agreement and in the fullest detail, and they have left it to us to meditate on and weigh carefully. First, then, the place to which he was led is carefully noted from the name Golgotha, a word then in common use among that whole nation, which, as the context itself expresses, is the same as the place of Calvary; compare the history of Jezebel, 2 Kings 9:35. This word has indeed given occasion to various explanations. For some very bold fanatics long ago stirred up notions, dreaming and trying to persuade others, that the skull from which that place was named was the very skull of Adam, buried in that spot, so that the cross of Christ was fixed in the same place where Adam's skull had been buried,

units.la: Cur locus ipse Caluaria dictus sit. Christi eodem loco fixa sit quo Adæ Caluaria defossa fuerit, cum multis aliis non minus ridiculis fabulis, qualis illa est arboris ex qua Christi Crux decisa fuit: quibus omnibus contemplationum doctorum fabulis etiam indignis recitatione Satan harum sacrarum historiarum veritatem eleuare conatus est, licet ab istis delirisHominibus illorum plena volumina conscripta sint, multæque effictæ imagines, vel illis ipsis testibus, quibus ad Crucis imam partem, mortui caput effingitur. Alij existimarunt in hunc locum fuisse mortuorum ossamenta congesta, ut plerunque fit in Ecclesiæ Romanæ cœmeteriis, ut Christus in eum locum, tanquam in locum pollutum ac profanum deductus sit, quod in Legalibus pollutionibus mortuorum etiam contactus nominatim reponatur. Alij vero locum fuisse putant in quo ex more de facinorosis supplicia sumerentur, sic dictum propter ea quod colliculus esset rotundus in speciem humani capitis, ut plerunque patibula non procul ab vrbibus in locis eminentioribus conspiciuntur. Et sane talis adhuc est hodie locus ille, ut memorant qui loca illa visitarunt, atque adeo nomen illud Caluariæ apud Christianos retinet. Quæ posterior expositio magis ad veritatem videtur accedere.
units.tr: Why the place itself was called Calvary. together with many other fables no less ridiculous, such as the one about the tree from which Christ's cross was cut. By all these fables of the contemplations of the teachers, fables unworthy even of being recited, Satan has tried to undermine the truth of these sacred histories. Although those madmen have filled whole volumes with them, and many images have been made, even by those same witnesses, in which the head of a dead man is depicted at the foot of the Cross. Others have thought that the bones of the dead were heaped up in that place, as often happens in the cemeteries of the Roman Church, so that Christ was led to that spot as to a polluted and profane place, since contact with the dead is expressly listed among the legal pollutions. Others, however, think it was the place where, by custom, the punishments of criminals were carried out, and that it was so called because the little hill was round in the shape of a human head; as gallows are often seen not far from cities, on rather high ground. And indeed that place is still today such, as those who have visited it report, and so it keeps the name of Calvary among Christians. This latter explanation seems to come closer to the truth.

units.la: Sed ne in nominis istius explicatione diutius hæreamus, duo magni momenti capita quæ nos hic Spiritus Sanctus docet agediscipiamus. Primum est, ratione situs istius loci (qui tunc erat vrbi proximus, vt Ioh. 19. 20. dicitur, sed extra vrbem, intra quam deinceps à Christianis Hierosolymam incolentibus inclusus est) hoc mysterium in hac circumstantia, sicut in aliis multis, fuisse complementum eorum quae in Lege figurate praedicebantur. Nam, ait Apostolus loco supra citato, Lege vetabantur Sacerdotes eorum animalium vesci corporibus quorum sanguis inferebatur per Pontificem in Sacrarium pro peccatorum expiatione, Leuit. 6. verf. 20. & 16. verf. 17. sed extra castra quae tunc in deserto erant comburi iubebantur illa corpora: ita praenuntiante Spiritu Sancto eum qui vera est pro peccatis expiatio extra vrbem offerendum: & Sacerdotes reliquosque omnes quotquot post hanc Iesu Christi oblationem vetera Sacrificia & Legales ceremonias retinere studerent, non ventu-ros in partem huius oblationis, quod hoc unico agno standum sit, ita semel in Cruce oblato, vt ad verum usque coelorum sanctuarium ascenderit, ad nostram reconciliationem. Porro si allegorica haec expositio vera est & firmo fundamento nititur (quod negari non poterit, quum illius auctor sit Spiritus Sanctus) quinam Christi particeps erit hodierna Romana Ecclesia, quae non modo maximam partem Iudaicarum Ceremoniarum in vsum reduxit, sed aliarum praeterea numerum immensum inuexit? quae sanguinem istius agni miscet non modo cum Martyrum sed cum cuiusuis meritis, aut etiam cum quacunque re voluerit, eo vsque vt oblationem huius agni semel factam quotidie repetat? Quousque verò tandé Christianismus tam multis abominationibus polluetur? Alterum est, Apostolum cōsiderantem Christum extra vrbem per contumeliam pulsum, tanquam coetu hominum indignum (qua in re conspicimus Christum reuera nostris peccatis debitas poenas luisse, quibus indigni Dei facie & conspectu reddimur) nos admonere ne nouum nobis sit ac insolens, si ab huius mundi ciuitate ferri non possumus: & contrà potius ad gaudium & laetitiam nos exhortari, si capiti nostro simus in hoc opprobrio conformes, infamati vt spectaculo simus Angelis, mundo & hominibus & tanquā purgamenta habeamur, 1. Cor. 4. 13. nullam hic habentes ciuitatem permanentem, sed eam quaerentes quae ventura est, Heb.13. 14. quéadmodū à terrena Ierusalem Iesus Christus extra portas eiectus, nullū propterea passus est detrimentum. Contrà verò Ierusalem expulsa Luce, sua ipsius culpa in tenebras perditionis ruit: quod omnibus talia patrantibus hactenus contigit, & continget in posterum.
units.tr: But, not to linger longer over the explanation of that name, let us take up the two heads of great importance that the Holy Spirit teaches us here to consider. The first is that, by reason of the situation of that place (which at that time was near the city, as John 19:20 says, but outside the city, within which it was later enclosed by Christians who inhabited Jerusalem), this mystery, in this circumstance as in many others, was the fulfilment of what was foreshadowed in the Law. For, says the Apostle in the passage cited above, the priests were forbidden by the Law to eat the bodies of those animals whose blood was carried by the high priest into the sanctuary for the expiation of sins (Lev. 6:20 and 16:17); but those bodies were commanded to be burned outside the camp, which at that time was in the wilderness. So the Holy Spirit foretold that he who is the true expiation for sins must be offered outside the city; and that the priests and all others who, after this offering of Jesus Christ, sought to keep the old sacrifices and legal ceremonies would not have a share in this offering, because we must stand by this one Lamb, offered once on the Cross, which ascended to the true sanctuary of heaven for our reconciliation. Moreover, if this allegorical explanation is true and rests on a firm foundation (which cannot be denied, since its author is the Holy Spirit), who will share in Christ in today's Roman Church? It has not only brought back the greater part of the Jewish ceremonies into use, but has also introduced an immense number of others besides. It mingles the blood of this Lamb not only with the merits of the martyrs but with the merits of anyone whatever, or even with whatever thing it pleases, to such an extent that it repeats daily the offering of this Lamb, which was made once. But how far, finally, will Christianity be polluted by so many abominations? The second is that the Apostle, considering that Christ was driven outside the city with contempt, as unworthy of the company of men (in which we see that Christ indeed paid the penalties due to our sins, by which we are made unworthy of the face and sight of God), admonishes us not to find it strange and unusual if we cannot be carried within the city of this world. On the contrary, he urges us rather to joy and gladness, if we are conformed to our Head in this reproach, made infamous as a spectacle to the angels, the world and men, and are counted as the offscouring of all things (1 Cor. 4:13), having here no abiding city but seeking the one that is to come (Heb. 13:14). In the same way, Jesus Christ, cast out beyond the gates of the earthly Jerusalem, suffered no loss on that account. On the other hand, Jerusalem, having cast out the Light, has fallen by its own fault into the darkness of destruction; which has happened to all who have done such things hitherto, and will happen in the future.

units.la: Eo igitur loci dicitur, vti ferebat lata sententia crucifixus. Vbi praeter ea quae de hoc supplicij genere diximus, non alienum est à propósito quod à quibusdam obseruatum est de conformitate quae incidit in huius oblationis Iesu Christi modum, & veterum Sacrificiorum ceremonias, ac praesertim holocausti, sicuti Leuit.1. describuntur. Nam quae à Sacerdote offerebantur, primùm eleuebantur, deinde à dextra ad sinistram mouebantur, veluti Crucis figuram repræsentarent, & Iesum Christum in ea extensum, qui fuit altare, non sanè templi illius Hierosolymitani, sed totius mundi, in quo sanguinem fudit, manantem à quatuor præcipuis corporis ipsius membris, vtroque nempe brachio, & vtrisque tibiis, ac tandem ipso suo corpore, iam prius lacero, & abluto, non aqua sanè, sed suo ipsius sanguine intra Prætorium. At quæ super altari templi offerebantur, quum caduca & corruptioni obnoxia essent, veraeque huius victimæ tantùm figura, ignis absumebat: quam ob rem etiam eiusmodi sacrificia sæpius repetebantur: & eo ipso satis prædicabant longè aliud perfectius holocaustum exspectandum, nempe Crucifixum illum, quem, minimè perpessionum ignis licet asperrimus, absumplit, sed qui potiùs in Cruce mortem ipsam absorpsit, & corruptionem in sepulchro, cœlos ipsos penetràs in reconciliatione nostrâ oblationis istius fragrátia, vt hac ratione priùs clausi nobis patefierent ac dicarentur. Magna est igitur in hac figuræ cum veritate congruentia verisimilitudo. Sed longè certius, quod ipse docet Apostolus, nempe pro eo quod sperarent Christi inimici eum crucifixum in nihilum redigendum, hac ratione contrà chirographum peccatorum quod erat aduersum nos peccatis nostris obsignatum, cruci affixum fuisse, & è media sublatum: mortémque ipsam morte affectam
units.tr: Therefore he was crucified in that place where, as the sentence pronounced, he was taken. Here, besides what we have said about this kind of punishment, it is not out of place to note what some have observed about the correspondence that falls upon the manner of this offering of Jesus Christ and the ceremonies of the old sacrifices, especially the burnt offering, as they are described in Leviticus 1. For the things that were offered by the priest were first lifted up and then moved from right to left, as if they represented the figure of the Cross, and of Jesus Christ stretched out on it, who was the altar not of that temple at Jerusalem but of the whole world, and on which he shed his blood, flowing from the four principal members of his body, namely both arms and both legs, and at last his very body, already torn and washed, not indeed with water but with his own blood, within the Praetorium. But the things offered upon the altar of the temple, since they were perishable and liable to corruption, and were only a figure of the true victim, were consumed by fire; for which reason such sacrifices were also repeated often, and by that very fact they proclaimed that a far different and more perfect burnt offering was to be expected, namely the Crucified One, whom the fire of sufferings, though very harsh, did not consume, but who rather swallowed up death itself on the Cross and corruption in the sepulchre, and penetrated the heavens themselves by the fragrance of this offering for our reconciliation, so that by this means those things that had been closed to us might be opened and consecrated to us. There is therefore a great likelihood of agreement between this figure and the truth. But far more certain is what the Apostle himself teaches: that, although Christ's enemies hoped to reduce the crucified one to nothing, in this way, on the contrary, the handwriting of sins, which stood against us, sealed by our sins, was nailed to the Cross and taken out of the way; and death itself, put to death by death,

units.la: Su Christi crucifixi. sectam, peccatum coudemnatum, & Principem ipsum mundi, viribus omnibus in cum impetu facto, corruisse : ipsum captū dum capere nititur, & victima vinctum maledictione dum vincit eum : tanta fuit huius crucifixi potentia,etiam in maxima sua infirmitate,tamq; est passionum eius immensa gloria, quibus ipsa Crux Dei tribunal factum est, & thronus iudicij quo mundus olim iudicandus est. Sed praeter superiora illa omnia,quaeso,quomodo Seruatoris nostri clementia potuit nostris oculis melius repraesentari, quàm sic expansis suis ad nos amplexandos brachiis? Agite igitur ad hunc crucifixum accurramus, ne cum hac misera natione censeamur, quam his verbis apud Esaiam 65. 2. graviter olim Dominus increpuit, Expenderam manus meas toto die ad populum rebellem, qui ambulant via non bona sequedo cogitationes suas. Ad populum qui provocant me in os iugiter: Non tacebo nisi rependero, atque rependero in sinum eorum. Supplices contrà petamus ab eo ut quotidie sancto suo Spiritu veterem nostrum hominum secum crucifigat ac mortificet, nosque sibi spiritu regenitos conformes reddat: in hunc crucifixum incumbentes, & ut ita dicam, os ori, oculos oculis, palmas palmis, ad illius Prophetae exemplar. 2. Reg. 4 31. applicantes.
units.tr: ...Christ crucified: sin, condemned in his flesh, and the Prince of this world himself. He attacked them with all his strength and fell. While he tried to seize Christ, he was seized; while he conquered him as a victim, he was himself conquered and bound by the curse. So great was the power of this crucified one, even in his utmost weakness, and so immense is the glory of his sufferings, that the Cross of God itself became the tribunal and throne of judgment by which the world is one day to be judged. But besides all these things, I ask, how could the mercy of our Saviour be more vividly set before our eyes than by his arms stretched out to embrace us? Come, then, let us run to this crucified one, lest we be counted with that wretched nation which the Lord once sharply rebuked in these words of Isaiah 65:2: "I have stretched out my hands all day long to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, following their own thoughts; a people who provoke me continually to my face. I will not keep silent but will repay, and will repay into their bosom." Let us rather pray to him that he would daily crucify and mortify our old man by his Holy Spirit with himself, and make us, regenerated by his Spirit, conformed to him. Let us lean upon this crucified one and, so to speak, apply mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, palms to palms, after the pattern of that prophet (2 Kings 4:31).

units.la: Caeterùm narrat deinceps historia duos cum illo latrones abductos & cruci affixos, a dextris unum, alterum a sinistris, de quorum accusatione & condemnatione quum nulla sit potest ex-
units.tr: Moreover, the history next relates that two robbers were led away with him and crucified, one on his right and the other on his left. Since no mention has been made of their accusation and condemnation before, ...

units.la: X. ij.
units.tr: X. ij.

units.la: antea facta mentio, stultæ curiositatis merito damnantur egregij illi Doctores cunctemplatiui, in eorum nomina & vitā amplius inquirentes, non modò curiosè sed etiam impiè, quę silentio regi longè melius est, & in genere detestari, quàm diutius in iis refutandis commorari: sicut etiam eorum ignorantiam qui de duobus latronibus duos fures fecerunt persequi nolo. Illis igitur omissis observanda est potiùs perditorum istorum hominum intolerranda nequitia, & Pilati maximum præter superiora peccatum, quòd quum toties palàm esset innocentiam Iesu Christi professus, etiam in ipso condemnationis eius momento, passus sit tamen illis comitibus Christum abduci crucifigique, quum rogatum de eo à Iudæis minimè legamus. Sed ita solet Deus conscientiæ vim facientes excæcare.
units.tr: those notable contemplative teachers deserve to be condemned for their foolish curiosity, who inquired further into their names and lives, not only curiously but even impiously. It is far better to pass over such things in silence and in general to reject them than to linger long in refuting them. I am also unwilling to pursue the folly of those who made the two malefactors into two thieves. Leaving those matters aside, we should rather observe the intolerable wickedness of these abandoned men, and the great sin of Pilate, beyond what has been said above: although he had so often openly professed the innocence of Jesus Christ, even at the very moment of his condemnation he allowed Christ to be led away and crucified with those companions, whereas we do not read that the Jews asked anything about him. But God is wont to blind those who do violence to their conscience.

units.la: Interea tamen Deus omnibus istis visus est, vt magis ac magis patefaceret, nihil eorum omissum, quæ ad nostram redemptionem requirerentur. Licet enim Christus latrocinij neque accusatus, neque damnatus sit, medium tamen inter duos latrones pendentem oportuit haberi latronū socium, & in iis numerari tanquam Ducem præcipuum, ita vices nostras sustinentem, qui in primi nostri Parentis persona Deum Creatorem gloria sua & honore spoliare sumus aggressi. Et hoc ipsum Dominus ipse prædixerat per Esaiam Prophetam. Esa.53.12.quod in hac historia Marcus ipse notauit, vt sciamus licet hæc omnia à sola istorum rum scelceratorum malitia promanarint, nihil hic tamen factum fortuito, sed prout erat ad nostram salutem diuinitus ordinatum.
units.tr: Meanwhile, however, God appeared to all these men in order to reveal more and more that nothing required for our redemption was left out. For although Christ was neither accused nor condemned as a robber, it was fitting that he, hanging in the middle between two robbers, should be held to be their companion and counted among them as their chief leader, thus bearing our place, he who in the person of our first parent had set out to despoil God the Creator of his glory and honour. The Lord himself had foretold this through the prophet Isaiah (Isa. 53:12), which Mark also noted in this history, so that we may know that although all these things sprang solely from the malice of those wicked men, nothing here was done by chance, but was divinely ordained as it was for our salvation.

units.la: Sed praeter illa superiora quae de duobus i- ftis latronibus deinceps audituri sumus, nos longe altius deducunt: nam admiranda qua- dam ratione Dei nobis sapientiam ac proui- dentiam patefaciunt in sceleratorum homi- num euertendis consiliis, & in gloriam suam conuertendis etiam tum maxime quum laxas habenas illis permittit, votisque sui compotes facit.
units.tr: But beyond those things above, which we are about to hear further concerning these two robbers, these matters lead us much deeper. For in a wonderful manner they reveal to us the wisdom and providence of God in overthrowing the plans of wicked men and turning them to his own glory, especially when he gives them loose reins and grants them the fulfilment of their wishes.

units.la: Lucas vero praeter superiora illa omnia quiddam summae consolationis plenum ad- iungit, quo non tantum inenarrabilem Domi- ni constantiam testatur dum pedes ac manus eius transfigerentur, sed etiam immensam il- lam quam Patri reddidit obedientiam, & infi- nitam erga nos inimicos suos charitatem, nun- quam Mediatoris quod sponte subierat mu- neris, ne in summis quidem & grauissimis cru- ciatibus oblitus, quod est a nobis in hac ipsa historia saepius obseruatum. Seu magnitudi- nem igitur eius quo de hic agimus consideremus, quis se cum Dei vnico & aeterno Filio au- sit aequare: seu meritum attendamus, quis vel ipsos Angelos ausit cum integritate & excel- lentia carnis Christi comparare? Sin autem iniuriam expendamus personae illius, vitae, di- gnitati factam mille modis indignissimam, ecquis vnquam grauiorem passus est aut est passurus in posterum? annon vero vindicandi X. iij. se potestatem etiam humanitus habebat, quū sola hac voce, Ego sum, dum caperetur potuerit hostes suos humi prostratos deiicere? Ioh.18.6. An vero iuris eum æquitas ad se vindicandum, aut ad vindictam à Patre flagitandam deficiebat? Minimè Gentium. Cur ergo non fecit? Nempe quia noluit. Quamobrem vero? Quod res suas priuatas immo res omnes gloriæ Patris in eorum misericordia pro quibus orabat glorificandi postposuerit. Vera igitur fortitudo est in suiipsius victoria, etsi non fuit in Christo quæ in nobis est rationis & passionum repugnantia. Ac Iesus Christus Dominus noster non ore suo tantùm, sed tot etiam perfectissimis exemplis, tres has virtutes Christianas docere nos voluit, mansuetudinem, qua irę ex iniuria nobis illata lenitur impetus: patientiam, qua vel maximè violentæ passiones reguntur: & charitatem in proximū quæ sic contemplatur iniuriam quam sibi ipse facit, & periculum in quod in nobis offendendis incurrit, ut ad eius misericordiam potius quàm ad vindictam persequendam commoueat.
units.tr: Luke, however, besides all those things above, adds something full of the highest consolation, which testifies not only to the Lord's unspeakable constancy while his hands and feet were pierced, but also to that immense obedience he rendered to the Father and his infinite love towards us, his enemies. He never forgot the office of Mediator, which he had undertaken of his own accord, not even in the greatest and most grievous torments, as we have often observed in this very history. If we consider the greatness of him of whom we speak here, who would dare to equal himself with the only and eternal Son of God? If we weigh his merit, who would dare to compare even the angels with the integrity and excellence of the flesh of Christ? But if we consider the injury done to that person, his life and dignity, in a thousand most unworthy ways, who has ever suffered, or will suffer in the future, a graver one? Did he not, even as a man, have the power of avenging himself, since by this one word, "I am he," while he was being seized, he could have struck his enemies to the ground? (John 18:6). Or did equity of right fail him, that he might avenge himself or demand vengeance from the Father? Not at all. Why then did he not do so? Simply because he was unwilling. And why? Because he preferred to set aside his private concerns, indeed all matters of the Father's glory, in favour of the mercy he was seeking for those for whom he prayed. True courage, therefore, lies in victory over oneself, even though in Christ there was not that conflict between reason and the passions which exists in us. And our Lord Jesus Christ wished to teach us these three Christian virtues not only by his word but by so many most perfect examples: meekness, by which the impulse of anger aroused by an injury done to us is calmed; patience, by which the most violent passions are restrained; and love towards our neighbour, which so regards the injury he does to himself and the danger he incurs in offending us, that it moves him to seek mercy rather than to pursue vengeance.

units.la: Quid vero sum ad hæc fratres dicturus? equis erit inter nos qui se cum hoc comparet, aut cui tanta sit vnquam illata iniuria? Annon igitur merito pudore suffundemur, Christianos dici velle nos, & tamen tam esse vindictæ cupidos? Diligite, aiebat ille, vestros inimicos: odio vos prosequentibus, bene facite: precamini pro iis qui vos infestant, & persequuntur vos,vt fitis filij Patris vestri qui est in cœlis:fa- cit enim vt Sol suus exoriatur super malos ac bonos.Matth.5.45. Quid autem pluribus opus est?Filij Dei omnes esse dicíque cupimus. Men daces ac hypocritas! Eò nos hodie deuenisse vt sibi inustam aliquam maculam arbitretur, qui malum malo, imò iniuriam duobus non compensarit,si fieri possit.Nec verò nos pudet sic precari, Dimitte nobis debita nostra,sicut & nos remittimus debitoribus nostris, id est, Ne nobis cõdona lapsus nostros qui fratribus condonare nolumus? Annon idem est ac si sic precaremur, Damna nos,quia damnari volu-mus.Discite ex me,inquit Dominus,quòd mi-tis sim & humilis corde,& inuenietis requiem animabus vesttis. Matth.11.29. Quis verò ha-ctenus in hac schola profecit vt debuit? Diffi-cillimum istud, aiunt, carni. Immo verò, in-quam,prorsus carni ἀδύνατον. At,quæso,sumus ne in carne vel in spiritu? Si sumus in carne, quorsum Dei filiorum nomine gloriamur? Si Spiritu Christi agimur, re ipsa illud testemur. Nec enim irrideri Deus se patitur. Nequis au-tem excipiat(etsi verissimum illud quidem sed non tamen ad malum ansam præbere debet) perfectius esse IesuChristi exemplum quàm vt illud perfectissimè possimus imitari : saltem sanctorum Prophetarum & Apostolorum exempla sequamur, qui homines & ipsi nobis simillimi fuerunt, & tamen ad vsum hanc doctrinam reuocarunt vt totum vitæ ipsorum curriculum nihil fuerit nisi perpetua praxis illius, malum bono compensantes & eorum à quibus persecutionem patiebantur salutem procurantes. Ecquid amplius? Quot praestantes inter ipsos Ethnicos viros reperias, quorum maníuetudine, patientia, dilectione, & aliis virtutibus quales in iis esse potuerunt, suis passionibus imperarunt, adeo vt etiam saepe malum bono compensarint? An igitur ipsos Ethnicos & prophanos homines non putabit nos iudices nostrae ἀσεληείας ἢ σχολασίας experiri? Quod si rationibus humanis agendum est, quae ratio tandem erit partes simul in sua causa sustinere accusatoris, testis, iudicis & executoris? Et tamen hoc faciunt qui quod Deo proprium est sibi vendicant: Nam mihi est ultio, inquit Dominus, ego rependam. Deut. 32. verf. 35. Rom. 12. verf. 19. Deo igitur causae nostrae bonitas & aequitas commendenda: ad Magistratus ad id ordinatos à Domino confugiendum est in his casibus, non quidem vt Deum ipsum aut Magistratus odiorum nostrorum executores aduersus proximos habeamus (nam haec atrocior foret iniuria) sed vt nostra nobis reddantur dicta causa, si eo usque deueniendum est, sincero tamen & non fucato erga proximos animo affectis.
units.tr: But what shall I, brothers, say to these things? Will there be anyone among us who compares himself with him, or to whom such a great injury has ever been done? Shall we not then rightly blush to wish to be called Christians, and yet be so eager for revenge? "Love your enemies," he said, "do good to those who hate you, pray for those who mistreat and persecute you, that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good" (Matt. 5:44-45). But why need there be more? We desire to be and to be called sons of God. Liars and hypocrites! Have we come to such a point today that a man thinks some stain has been put on him if he does not repay evil with evil, or rather injury with two injuries, if he can? Nor are we ashamed to pray thus: "Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors" (Matt. 6:12), that is, "Pardon our lapses," though we are unwilling to pardon our brothers. Is this not the same as praying, "Condemn us, because we want to be condemned"? "Learn from me," said the Lord, "that I am meek and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls" (Matt. 11:29). But who has so far made progress in this school as he ought? "That is very difficult," they say, "for the flesh." Indeed, I say, it is altogether impossible [ἀδύνατον] for the flesh. But, I ask, are we in the flesh or in the Spirit? If we are in the flesh, why do we glory in the name of the sons of God? If we are led by the Spirit of Christ, let us prove it in fact. For God does not allow himself to be mocked. Lest anyone object (though this is most true, yet it ought not to give occasion for evil) that the example of Jesus Christ is too perfect for us to imitate it perfectly, let us at least follow the examples of the holy prophets and apostles, who were men very like ourselves, and yet recalled this teaching to practice, so that the whole course of their lives was nothing but a constant practice of repaying evil with good and of seeking the salvation of those by whom they suffered persecution. What more? How many outstanding men among the heathen themselves you will find, whose meekness, patience, love and other virtues, such as they could have in them, governed their passions, so that they often repaid evil with good. Will not the heathen and profane men themselves think that we are testing them by our impiety or sloth [ἀσεληείας ἢ σχολασίας]? But if we must act by human reasons, what reason will at last allow one man to play the part of accuser, witness, judge and executioner all at once in his own cause? And yet those who claim for themselves what belongs to God do exactly this: "Vengeance is mine," says the Lord, "I will repay" (Deut. 32:35; Rom. 12:19). Therefore the goodness and equity of our cause must be commended to God; in these cases we must flee to the magistrates appointed for this by the Lord, not indeed so that we may have God himself, or the magistrates, as executors of our hatreds against our neighbours (for that would be a more atrocious injury), but so that our cause may be heard and our rights restored to us, if it must come to that, provided that we are disposed towards our neighbours with a sincere and not a feigned mind.

units.la: Christum vero non modo non seipsum vltum esse diligenter obseruandum est, sed etiam pro inimicis ardentes preces apud Deum fundere. Non igitur satis est si inuicem reconciliandi testentur, se non malo animo esse affectos stos erga proximos (quod sæpe nimium videmus à multis contrà id quod sentiunt dici) sed dicendum & reipsa præstandum est, se bono esse animo, nec se vinci à malo pati debet, sed potius bonitate vincere malitiam. Rom.12.21. Quînam enim alioqui Deum patrem nostrum diceremus, aut Iesum Christum fratrem, aut cur de Spiritu Iesu Christi, qui est Spiritus Sanctus gloriaremur?
units.tr: Christ, however, not only did not avenge himself, but also poured out fervent prayers to God for his enemies. It is therefore not enough for men to declare to one another, when they are reconciled, that they are not ill-disposed towards their neighbours (we often see too much of what many say that is contrary to what they feel). It must be said and also shown in fact that one has a good disposition, and one must not be overcome by evil, but rather overcome evil with good. Rom. 12.21. For by what other means could we call God our Father, or Jesus Christ our brother, or boast of the Spirit of Jesus Christ, who is the Holy Spirit?

units.la: At pro quibus Christus precatus est? Pro quid agerent ignorantibus, quod tamen dextrè intelligendum est, vt de iis nimirum dicatur qui omnino peccabant ignorantia, quales multi fuisse videntur in vulgo malè in Lege Dei edocto, Matth.9.36. & à furore Scribarum & Sacerdotum, vt mare à tempestate vetorum agitato, vt Petrus declarat, cuius ministerio precationis huius virtus & efficacia patefacta est. Act.3.17. & de seipso Paulus 1.Tim.1.13. & de sua natione indefinitè testatur, Rom.10.2. Sed vt varij sunt ignorantiæ gradus, in hoc ignorantium numero pro quibus hæc precatio facta est censendi sunt in quibus aliquid etiam amplius quàm simplex ignorantia fuit, sed tamen plus ignorantiæ quàm praue voluntatis.
units.tr: But for whom did Christ pray? For those who did not know what they were doing. This must be understood rightly, namely as referring to those who sinned purely through ignorance, such as many seem to have been among the common people, who were poorly taught in the Law of God (Matt. 9.36), and who were driven by the fury of the Scribes and Priests like a sea tossed by a storm, as Peter declares, through whose ministry the power and efficacy of this prayer was made known (Acts 3.17). Paul also testifies of himself (1 Tim. 1.13), and of his nation in general (Rom. 10.2). But just as there are various degrees of ignorance, those for whom this prayer was made must be counted among those ignorant persons in whom there was something more than simple ignorance, yet still more ignorance than wicked will.

units.la: At pro improbis illis, qui scientes prudentes ex mero furore quemuis alium quàm Cæsarè Regem eiurarant, & omnia aduersus conscien-tiam atque adeò contra Sanctum Spir. moliti erant, vt multis ante seculis Dominus prædixerat, quum scirèt Iesus Christus iam aduersum eos scriptam sententiam, precatus nō est. Excipe tamen quosdam ex praecipuis gubernatoribus, puta Nicodemum, Ioseph um Arimathaeensem, & alios illis siqui fuerunt similes, teste D. Petro. Act. 3 17. Et revera precibus istis debetur eorum conversio de quibus agitur Act. 2.37. quemadmodum etiam Pauli conversionem dixerunt veteres fuisse D. Stephani precum effectum. Act. 7.60.
units.tr: But he did not pray for those wicked men who, knowing and deliberately, out of sheer fury, renounced anyone other than Caesar as King, and who schemed everything against conscience and thus against the Holy Spirit, as the Lord had foretold many centuries before; since Jesus Christ already knew the sentence written against them. Yet make an exception for some of the principal rulers, such as Nicodemus, Joseph of Arimathea, and others like them, if there were any, as Peter bears witness (Acts 3.17). And indeed the conversion of those spoken of in Acts 2.37 is owed to these prayers, just as the ancients said that the conversion of Paul was the fruit of the prayer of Stephen (Acts 7.60).

units.la: Siquis autem quaerat, sit ne etiam pro malitiosis ipsis orandum, etiam in sua prauitate scienter prudenter pergentibus, contra conscientiam, aio nobis indefinite pro quibuslibet etiam maximis peccatoribus precandum, non ignaris singulis momentis quosdam a Domino vocari, cuius misericordia longe lateque diffunditur. Quod minime tamen impedit quominus ut merentur peccatores arguantur & reprehendantur. Sed horum omnium Charitas erit optima moderatrix. Sic videmus Samuelem diu multumque pro Saule precatum esse, donec illi Deus tandem silentium imposuerit 1.Sam.16.1. Praeterea licet iusta sint & irrevocabilia Dei iudicia, lugere tamen nos oportet quatenus quidem sine Dei offensa fieri id poterit, & vera in proximum charitas iubet, vel ipso teste Mose cuius exemplum legitur Exod.32.32. & ipso etiam teste Iesu Christo super Hierusalem lugente, Luc.19 44. & D. Paulo. Rom.9.3.
units.tr: If anyone asks whether we ought to pray even for the malicious themselves, who knowingly and deliberately persist in their wickedness against conscience, I answer that we must pray for all sinners without distinction, even the greatest, since we know that some are called by the Lord every moment, and his mercy is spread far and wide. This does not prevent sinners, as they deserve, from being charged and rebuked. But charity will be the best moderator of all these things. Thus we see Samuel prayed for Saul long and earnestly, until God finally imposed silence on him (1 Sam. 16.1). Moreover, although God's judgments are just and irrevocable, we ought nevertheless to mourn, insofar as this can be done without offence to God, and true charity toward our neighbour requires it, as Moses bears witness (whose example is read in Exod. 32.32), and as Jesus Christ bears witness when he lamented over Jerusalem (Luke 19.44), and as Paul did (Rom. 9.3).

units.la: Ab his tamen precibus excipiendum est peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum, ut docet D. Ioh. 1. Ioh. 5.16. cuius criminis erant maxime convicti uicti quos in istis Iesu Christi precibus dixi non cötineri:quod est generalis auersio à Deo cum eius odio ex proposito coiunćta:sed summopere nobis cauendum est ne in hunc aut illum hæc iudicia transferamus fine magna & attenta consideratione,& vt ita dicam fine rarissimis inspirationibus: quod Apostolo contigisse non est dubium, 2.Timot.4.14.& longè adhuc clarius Ecclesiæ veteri aduersus Arrium in summis angustiis oranti Deum, & aduersus Imperatorem Iulianum Apostatam,Deo suorum preces exaudiente ratásque faciente, horrendo illo quo periit Iulianus iudicio.Nostróque fœculo multa recenseri possent non absimilia exempla horrendorum Dei iudiciorum, à quibus tamen abstinebimus in præsentia, Deo gratias agentes quòd Ecclesiam suam à talibus inimicis liberarit,ex suæ voluntatis erga nos beneplacito, & rogantes eum vt fe misericordem erga reliquos, fiqui supersunt,fi ita ferat eius voluntas,præbeat.
units.tr: Yet from these prayers the sin against the Holy Spirit must be excepted, as St John teaches (1 John 5.16). Those who were most convicted of this crime, whom I said were not included in these prayers of Jesus Christ, were guilty of a general aversion from God joined with a deliberate hatred of him. But we must take great care not to apply these judgments to this or that person without much careful consideration and, so to speak, without very rare inspirations. That this happened to the Apostle is beyond doubt (2 Tim. 4.14). And much more clearly, the ancient Church, praying to God against Arius in great distress, and against the Emperor Julian the Apostate, saw God hear the prayers of his people and make them effective by that dreadful judgment by which Julian perished. In our own age many similar examples of God's dreadful judgments could be recounted, but we will refrain from them at present, giving thanks to God that he has delivered his Church from such enemies by the good pleasure of his will towards us, and asking him to show mercy towards the rest, if any remain, if his will so pleases.

units.la: Sed vt hanc absoluamus quæstionem, absit cogitemus ignorantia vel fimpliciffima peccantes venialiter peccare, id est peccata quibus non debeatur mors æterna committere, aut quæ alia vlla re quàm pretioso nostri crucifixi sanguine deleri possint. Nam,vt sæpe ex hoc pulpito vobis dictum est, etsi inæqualia quidem in fe peccata sunt, tamen,vt capitalia omnia crimina non sunt æqualia,attamen capitalia omnia, sic omne peccatum natura sua mortale est,fine exceptione, quo nimirum læfa est Dei Maiestas, quatenus iudicium exer-cet: vt contrà nullum peccatum est nonVenia-le (excepto eo solo quod nunquam remitti posse docuimus)id est,quod remitti condona-riquenon possit,iis quibus Deus ex misericor-dia fidem & refipiscentiam donat. Exempli gratia, licet per se fatis hæc clara sint ac dilu-cida, non tantùm generalis illa regula confi-deranda, Iuris ignorantiam non excusare pec-catum, etsi leuius facit, nec tantùm quod di-sertis verbis pronuntiat Apostolus, Rom.5.12. & 21. sed etiam attendenda sacrificia quæ Le-ge præscribebantur,pro quibuslibet per igno-ratiam admissis peccatis, quibus nobis ad illa delenda remedium vnicum ostenditur Chri-sti sanguis, quo mundi peccata sublata sunt. Denique quid opus erat Christum suis preci-bus patrem interpellare pro illis per ignoran-tiam peccantibus vt Pater eis ignosceret,mor-te illa placatus quam dum fundit preces istas patiebatur, si venia ipsos non opus habuisse putamus?
units.tr: But to conclude this question, let us not think that those who sin through the simplest ignorance sin only venially, that is, sins for which eternal death is not owed, or which can be blotted out by anything other than the precious blood of our crucified Lord. For, as has often been said to you from this pulpit, although sins are unequal in themselves, and not all capital crimes are equal, nevertheless all capital crimes, and indeed every sin by its nature, is mortal without exception, since by it the majesty of God is injured, insofar as it exercises judgment. On the contrary, there is no sin that is venial (except that one which we have taught can never be forgiven), that is, one that cannot be remitted or pardoned to those to whom God in his mercy grants faith and repentance. For example, although these things are clear and plain enough in themselves, we must consider not only that general rule, that ignorance of the law does not excuse sin, even though it lessens it, nor only what the Apostle states in plain words (Rom. 5.12 and 21), but also the sacrifices prescribed by the Law for any sins committed through ignorance, by which the only remedy for blotting them out is shown to us in the blood of Christ, by which the sins of the world have been taken away. Finally, why was there any need for Christ to plead with the Father by his prayers for those sinning through ignorance, that the Father might forgive them, appeased by that death which he suffered while pouring out these prayers, if we think they had no need of pardon?

units.la: Porrò in reliquo illo omni apparatu,expres-fa fit metio Tituli in summa cruce supra Chri-sti caput affixi, in quo continebatur causa, vt ait Matth. & Marc. condemnationis illius ad crucem à Pilato, quòd fuisset à Iudæis accusa-tus affectati regni. Eius tituli, verba ipsissima, Iohannes descripsit. Non sine maximis ratio-nibus hæc ab Euangelistis perscripta. Primùm igitur hinc obseruandus est illorum,licet cor-ruptissimorum temporum, forma & consue-tudo tudo iudiciorum: nempe fuisse populum de causis ob quas de reo sumeretur supplicium admonitum:quod repugnat Regum aut aliorum Magistratuum consuetudini, seu quosdam ad mortem sine vlla iudicij forma trahant, seu manus in eos iniiciant, & in eos inquirant, sua authoritate abutentes, quasi necesse non sit causas à quoquam cur id quó-vc modo fiat resciri. Non sic apud Dei populum illa gerebantur: quum contrà etiam in publico quaestio de reis haberetur, in portis quippe iudicia exerceri solita, quod in sacris conspicuum est ex illa iudicij forma aduersus Achan. Iosu. 7. aduersus blasphemum. Leuit. 24. Ionathanum. 1. Sam. 14. Atque adeò apud Romanos de publicis quae vocant criminibus apud populum agebatur:quam iudicij formam quum magnus ille vir & insignis Consul non omnino seruasset in causa quorundam Romanorum ciuium & Magistratuum manifestae aduersus Rempub. coniurationis conuictorum, exilio multatus est. Sic in hac aduersus Christum iudicij forma nihil occultum,aperte & palàm omnia. Absit autem dicamus in inquisitionibus eiusmodi requiri omnium praesentiam, ex qua mille incommoda & damna facilè orirentur, licet in plerisque locis mos ille inoleuerit: verùm tamen hoc saltem requiritur vt publicè causa supplicij & forma declaretur, vt tyrannidi praecidatur omnis occasio.Quę in hoc Statu consuetudo quòd in vsu sit, Deo gratias agamus,& religiosè ac diligenter eam observemus,quod non temerè dico,propter violatam nimirum illam hoc tempore, quod nequaquam est approbandum,nec imitandum.
units.tr: Furthermore, among all that other equipment, mention is expressly made of the title fixed on the top of the cross above Christ's head, in which was written the cause, as Matthew and Mark say, of that condemnation to the cross by Pilate, namely that he had been accused by the Jews of aspiring to kingship. John wrote down the very words of that title. These things were recorded by the Evangelists not without the greatest reasons. First, then, we should observe from this the form and custom of their judgments, however corrupt the times: namely, that the people were informed of the causes for which punishment was to be inflicted on the accused. This is contrary to the custom of kings or other magistrates, who either drag some to death without any form of trial, or lay hands on them and make inquiries against them, abusing their authority, as if it were not necessary for the causes of how this is done to be made known to anyone. It was not so among God's people; those things were done differently. On the contrary, even in public, an inquiry about the accused was held, since judgments were customarily exercised at the gates. This is evident in the sacred record from the form of judgment against Achan (Josh. 7), against the blasphemer (Lev. 24), and against Jonathan (1 Sam. 14). Indeed, among the Romans, what they call public crimes were dealt with before the people, and when that great and distinguished consul did not entirely observe this form of judgment in the case of certain Roman citizens and magistrates convicted of a manifest conspiracy against the commonwealth, he was punished with exile. So in this form of judgment against Christ nothing was hidden: everything was open and public. Let us not, however, say that inquiries of this kind require the presence of everyone, from which a thousand inconveniences and losses could easily arise, although that custom has become established in many places. Yet at least this is required: that the cause of punishment and the form of proceeding be declared publicly, so that every occasion for tyranny is cut off. We should give thanks to God that this custom is in use in this state, and observe it religiously and diligently. I do not say this rashly, since at this time that custom has been violated in some places, which is by no means to be approved or imitated.

units.la: At longè altius nos hac narratione Spiritus Sanctus deducit, fructum omnem qui ex hac historia colligendus est docens, & quàm admiranda sit Dei prouidentia in luce ex tenebris educenda. Non temerè igitur Dauid, Iesu Christi figura,scripsit,Psal. 2. 6. hunc Regem aduersus quem tum Reges ac Principes tum infimæ conditionis homines insurgerent & conspirarent, (quod magis expresse exponitur, Act. 4. 26. & 27. ) in regni possessionem venturum, usque ad vltimos orbis terræ fines, & in Sione Regem consecrandum. Rem in se admirandam, vt ait Psalt es Psal.118. 23. & in primis obseruandam si potissimum quibus instrumentis ad istud implendum vsus sit Dominus,attendamus,Herode primùm,à quo veste magnifica & Regia indutus est: deinde militibus, qui purpura illum quali Reges vtebantur, induerunt, qua deinde Iesus Christus exutus, ecce pro veste illa Pilatus supra caput eius titulum affigit,quo expressissimè declaratur hùc esse magnum illù à Prophetis Regem promissum, & nominatim Iudæis, sed etiam cunctis in orbe terrarum nationibus.Hanc ob causam hic titulus ab eodem Hebraicè, Græcè,Latinéque scriptus est,ad sceptrum quo regnum hoc administratur denotandum : doctrinam putà scriptis ac monumentis traditam,
units.tr: But the Holy Spirit leads us much more deeply through this narrative, teaching us all the fruit to be gathered from this history and how admirable God's providence is in bringing light out of darkness. It was therefore not without reason that David, a figure of Jesus Christ, wrote (Ps. 2:6) that this King, against whom kings and princes, and men of the lowest condition, would rise up and conspire (as is more expressly explained in Acts 4:26-27), would come into possession of the kingdom, to the furthest ends of the earth, and be consecrated King in Zion. It is a thing admirable in itself, as the Psalmist says (Ps. 118:23), and it is chiefly to be observed if we attend to the instruments the Lord used to accomplish it: first Herod, by whom he was clothed in a magnificent and royal robe; then the soldiers, who put on him the purple such as kings wore, and from which Jesus Christ was then stripped. And behold, in place of that robe, Pilate fixes a title above his head, by which it is most plainly declared that this is that great King promised by the prophets, named not only to the Jews but to all the nations of the world. For this reason the title was written by the same hand in Hebrew, Greek and Latin, to signify the sceptre by which this kingdom is administered, namely the doctrine handed down in writings and records,

units.la: Admirada Dei prouidentia Christus in possessionem regni euangelicalis, & per petuum mistus est, vtente Deo instrumentis ad id implendum Herode, Pilato, carnificibus ipsis nihil tale cogitantibus. tam, & omnibus in orbe terrarũ prædicata m, tribus illis tũ in orbe præcipuis linguis & cæterarum fontibus indicatam : hanc ob causam cœlitus in Apostolos, dono linguarum misso, tanquam futuris legatis ac præconibus huius Regis in yltimos vsque terrarum fines. Tantùm autem abest vt de istis cogitarét quorum hac in re perficienda Deus vsus est opera, vt alij contrà per ludibrium fecerint, quod Deus in tantam gloriam commutauit: alij, vt Pilatus in Iudæorum odium indignabundi fecerint. Et quidem perinde fuit istud acsi Dominus ipse de cœlo per os Pilati sic eos compellaret,Regem vobis à me promissum abnegastis, hoc adacto Iudice ad sententiam mortis aduersus eum ferendam,& ad eundem crucifigendum : at vobis licet repugnantibus hic Crucifixus dominabitur, quos virga illa sua ferrea contundat. Psal. 2. 9. iis tamen ex vobis exceptis quorum miserturus sum, regno meo ex Sione translato, Psal. IIo. 2. atque adeò Iudex ille quem ad eius condemnationem adegistis, scriba meus aduersum vos sententiam meam dicturus,dum vestram ascribit est futurus. Præterea quò hæc essent notiora, voluit diuina prouidentia Iudæos de hoc titulo queri,& tamen inu itis licet ac repugnantibus illis manere indelebilem in perpetuum, respondente Pilato,Quod scripsi,scripsi.
units.tr: The wonderful providence of God put Christ into possession of the evangelical kingdom and made it perpetual, God using as instruments for this purpose Herod, Pilate, and the executioners themselves, who thought of nothing of the kind. And that doctrine was to be proclaimed in all the world, indicated in those three languages which were chief in the world and the sources of the rest. For this reason the gift of tongues was sent from heaven upon the Apostles, as future envoys and heralds of this King to the uttermost ends of the earth. Yet these men, whose work God used to accomplish this, were far from thinking about these things: some acted in mockery, which God turned into great glory; others, like Pilate, acted in indignant hatred of the Jews. And indeed it was just as if the Lord himself were speaking to them from heaven through the mouth of Pilate: "You have denied the King promised by me. This judge has been driven to pronounce sentence of death against him and to have him crucified; yet, although you resist, this Crucified One will rule over you, and he will break you with his iron rod (Ps. 2:9). Nevertheless, from among you I will set apart those on whom I will have mercy, and my kingdom will be transferred from Zion (Ps. 110:2). And so that judge whom you forced to condemn him will be my scribe, about to declare my sentence against you, while he is set down as yours." Moreover, that these things might be better known, divine providence willed that the Jews should complain about this title, and yet, though they were unwilling and resisting, it should remain indelible forever, Pilate replying, "What I have written, I have written."

units.la: Ecquid igitur, fratres, amplius metuemus, quum infensissimos hostes huius veritatis qua nitimur,eandem quam maximè volunt funditus euersam, & quidem quum videaur voti compotes facti conspiciamus tamen ædificare & stabilire, vt historia sacra nobis elt huius rei testis locupletissimus? Nostro vero seculo licet Satan & fui satellites cœlum terræ miscere conati sint, quibus & eorum ignibus opposuimus Domini sacras chartas & tabulas, quid aliud tandem fecerunt nisi quòd ignem accenderunt quo absumuntur & magis ac magis in dies absumentur? Quæ nobis igitur amplius causa metus superest? Immo potiùs quid non possumus ac debemus in tantis istis probationibus merito à Domino sperare?
