Mansit igitur hic titulus cruci affixus, cuius patuit lectio cuilibet legere volenti, indignatibus frustra ac reluctantibus Iudæis, confirmante Domino Pilatum, cuius erat opera ad hunc scribendum titulum, vsus, licet eo nihil minus cogitante. Quid futurum igitur putamus hoc sacrosancto Verbo, quo huius tituli expositio continetur, quod Deus ipse verè sanctis suis & fidelibus scribis, Prophetis & Apostolis dictauit? An tanta vlla vis erit, tantæ fraudes quibus deleri vnquam possit? At contrà ne apex quidem eius est in seculum interiturus.
units.tr: Therefore, brothers, what more shall we fear, since we see the most bitter enemies of this truth on which we rest, who most of all want it utterly overthrown, and yet, though they seem to have gained their wish, it is built up and made firm, as sacred history is for us the most abundant witness of this? In our own age, although Satan and his henchmen have tried to mix heaven and earth, and we have opposed their fires with the Lord's sacred pages and tablets, what else have they done in the end but kindle a fire by which they are consumed, and will be more and more consumed day by day? What cause for fear therefore remains for us? Rather, what may we not, and ought we not, rightly hope from the Lord in such great proofs? This title, then, remained fixed to the cross, and its reading lay open to anyone who wished to read it, while the Jews raged and struggled in vain, the Lord confirming Pilate, whose work it was to write this title, though he was thinking of nothing of the kind. What then do we suppose will become of this most holy Word, in which the explanation of this title is contained, which God himself dictated to his true saints, the prophets and apostles, and wrote? Will there ever be such strength, such frauds, by which it could be destroyed? On the contrary, not even a stroke of its letter is going to perish forever.

units.la: Annon enim, obsecro, in tantis omnium totius orbis Statuum tempestatibus & mutationibus mille miris modis est conseruatum: vetere quidem Testamento in manus eorum qui subiecti quod eo continetur, putà Chriiti, fuerunt hostes infenfiffimi tanquam deposito fidelifideliter custodiendo tradito, & tanta fide conseruato, non sibi quidem hactenus propter indurationem, sed nobis, vt ne apex quidem detrahi possit, quin statim fraus detegatur, tanta fuit, tamque accurata ipsorum in hoc aliis conseruando thesauro diligentia. Ab hinc autem annis octoginta, annon Dominus populum suum e captiuitate Babylonica Romana educturus, titulum iltum veluti de nouo scriptum restituit Hebraicè, Græcè, & Latinè, trium illarum linguarum vsu renocato ad quarum fontes recurratur aduersus ignorantiam & barbariem quæ prius inualuerat? Quando vero sic operatus est? Christianis nimirum errantibus nostro seculo in tenebris sine pastoribus, vt olim Israële quum Christus in mundum veniret, Matth.9.36. & cæcis cæcos in fossam ac præcipitium ducentibus Matth. 15. 14. quo tempore boni illi Doctores palam prædicabant Hebraicis studiis vacare, idem esse ac ludæum fieri, Græcè studere idem ac hæreticum esse. Nihilominus tamen cœlitus linguarum donum denuo missum est, & sapientia à filiis suis agnita, Matth. 11. 19. Et quod scriptum est, scriptum est.
units.tr: For, I ask you, in such great storms and changes of all the states of the whole world, has it not been preserved in a thousand wonderful ways? In the Old Testament, the most bitter enemies of the Christ contained in it were entrusted with it as a deposit to be faithfully guarded, and it was kept with such faithfulness, and with such careful diligence, that though they did not, because of their hardness, use it for themselves, yet for us not even a stroke of it can be removed without the fraud being immediately exposed. Within the last eighty years, has not the Lord, about to lead his people out of Roman Babylonian captivity, restored that title as if newly written, in Hebrew, Greek and Latin, the use of those three languages being recalled, to whose sources one returns against the ignorance and barbarism that had previously prevailed? And when did he so work? Surely when Christians in our age were wandering in darkness without shepherds, as Israel once was when Christ came into the world (Matt. 9:36), and blind men were leading the blind into a ditch and a precipice (Matt. 15:14). At that time those good teachers openly preached that devoting oneself to Hebrew studies was the same as becoming a Jew, and studying Greek the same as being a heretic. Nevertheless the gift of tongues was sent again from heaven, and wisdom was recognised by her children (Matt. 11:19). And what has been written, has been written.

units.la: Verum quidem est eos de quibus hic ago, longè peius adhuc facientes quàm qui à Pilati responso quieuerût, sperasse sperarèque ad hucinuentam à se rationem qua fructum impediant, pro viribus reluctantes ne vulgata Latina versio, ex duarum linguarum originalium collatione repurgetur, quò singuli cre-
units.tr: It is true that those of whom I speak, doing far worse than those who were quieted by Pilate's answer, have hoped, and still hope, to find a way, devised by themselves, to prevent the fruit, struggling with all their might lest the Latin Vulgate be purified by collation with the two original languages. Their argument is that by this means, they say, each individual will attain knowledge of what to believe and do, and that in this way everyone would claim for himself the power of teaching and expounding the Scriptures. This argument is false in every respect.

units.la: Y. j. dendorum faciendorúmque sibi cognitionem assequantur, quòd hac ratione, inquiunt, omnes sibi docendi exponendíque scripturas potestatem sint arrogaturi. Falsum modis omnibus argumentum.Nec enim hætefibus ne nascantur itur obuiam, aut natæ cohibentur sacrarum Scripturarum lectione prohibita, quum ex solis Scripturis verum à falso distinguatur,quum de religione & conscientia agitur : sed fidelium Pastorum officium postulat vt oues suas hoc verbo Viuifico doceant, arguant, hortentur, & consolentur. Quoniam autem falsos Pastores quos caueri, cum veris quos oportet audiri, sepissimè misceri contingit, ideò Lucem hanc verbi diuini par est in singulis ædibus Domino sacris in locis eminentibus collocari, ex quo à singulis cuiuslibet ætatis ac conditionis voces eorum discernantur. At hoc ipsum boni isti viri metuunt, non ducentes religioni Dei verbo detrahere, mutare,addere,quæcunque voluntas & arbitrium illis dictauerit: quas eorum fraudes & sacrilegia nulla alia ratione detegi aut vitari quàm huius sacrosanctæ Lucis splendore certum est. Age verò, nonne Moses ipse, & omnes Prophetæ,atque adeò Christus ipse populum Dei sunt alloquuti vulgato suis temporibus idiomate, & eòdem idiomate dicta sua monumentis conscripta ad posteros transmiserunt ? Annon eadem, oro, scripta singulorum manibus voluebantur,& singulis sine exceptione in Synagogis prælegebantur?Quorsum vero Vetus Te-
units.tr: For the heresies that arise are not prevented by withholding the reading of the sacred Scriptures, nor are they checked once born; since truth is distinguished from falsehood by the Scriptures alone, when religion and conscience are at stake. The duty of faithful ministers requires that they teach, convict, exhort and console their sheep by this life-giving Word. And since it often happens that false ministers, whom one must beware of, are mixed up with true ministers, whom one ought to hear, therefore this light of the divine Word ought to be set up in every house consecrated to the Lord, in conspicuous places, so that the voices of each of them, of every age and condition, may be distinguished. But this very thing those good men fear, not thinking it a sin against God's Word to take away, change, or add whatever their will and judgment has dictated. It is certain that their frauds and sacrileges can be detected or avoided by no other means than by the brightness of this most holy Light. Come now, did not Moses himself, and all the prophets, and Christ himself, address the people of God in the language common in their times, and transmit their sayings, committed to writing in the same language, to posterity? Were not these same writings, I ask, turned over in the hands of individuals, and read aloud without exception in the synagogues?

units.la: Testamentum ex Hebraeo in Graecū sermonem translatum est à variis interpretibus, multisq; etiam vicibus, nisi vt qui populi ea lingua vterentur,quę tunc maximam orbis partem obtinebat,illud legerent & intelligerent? Cur etiam Euangelistæ Græcè scripserunt, docuerúntque, vulgatissimo tūc etiam inter Romanos idiomate, nisi vt ab omnibus intelligerētur,& scripta ipsorum legerentur? Immo verò, inquam, cur linguis omnibus, nisi ob istud ipsum prædicarunt? Cur verò sacri Fœderis Veteris & Noui in Latinum sermonē iteratis vicibus à variis patribus tabulęversæ sunt,nisi in eorū populoru gratiam quibus Lingua Latina esset propria & vulgata, vt ab iis legerentur ac intelligerentur? Gratias igitur immortales agamus Domino, quōd hoc beneficium tantum nobis largitus sit vt istorum fraudis conatibus & irritis factis, qui nec ipsi in regnum cœlorum introeunt nec alios introire sinunt, Matt.23.13. cognitionem istarum originalium linguarum nostro seculo reduxerit & instaurarit: & populo dederit aures ad eum vulgari loquentem idiomate intelligendum: Dei donum excellentissimum, hoc bene si homines norint & ad vsum suū reuocent:sed quo prorsus inexcusabiles reddantur qui eo abutūtur, alij in legendo negligentes,alij verò quæ perfunctorie legunt floccifacientes,quum tamen ex hoc sacrosancto cibo cupientes nutrimentum percipere,necesse sit eum manducare,gustum ex eo percipere,& eundem digerere.Atque hoc ipso loco visum est Deo trium illarum linguarum scholam erigere, scholam sane iam ita neglectam, ut pars & quidem maxima, negligat suos liberos vel elementa docere: pars vero suos liberos vix a limine salutata schola statim auocent, ut paucissimi studiorum cursum perseguantur, quo tandem aliquando in docetos viros cuadant, & vocationem aliquam adipiscantur: quam pauci vero ad sacrosanctum istud ministerium aspirant? Nempe vocatio illa est hodie omnium abiectissima, & tamen adeo necessaria, ut aer quem sorbemus & halitus quo respiramus non sit magis necessarius. Hinc fit ut inter nos, praeter maximum eorum numerum qui ex crebris quas audiuerunt cocionibus bonum norunt, quod non faciunt, maximus sit ignorantium numerus, ut non sine magno vestro pudore conspiciamus hoc loco ministros quorum vtimur opera peregrinos, quum hinc potius fidos pastores decuerit in vniuersum orbem terrarum propagari.
units.tr: Why was the Old Testament translated from Hebrew into Greek by various interpreters, and that many times, if not so that those people who used that language, which then held the greatest part of the world, might read and understand it? Why also did the Evangelists write and teach in Greek, the most widespread language then even among the Romans, unless it was so that their writings might be understood and read by all? Indeed, I say, why did they preach in all languages, if not for this very purpose? Why, again, have the books of the sacred covenant, Old and New, been translated many times into Latin by various Fathers, unless for the sake of those peoples to whom the Latin tongue was native and common, so that they might read and understand them? Let us therefore give immortal thanks to the Lord, that he has granted us so great a benefit, that in spite of the attempts and vain efforts of those who neither enter the kingdom of heaven themselves nor allow others to enter (Matt. 23:13), he has restored and renewed in our age the knowledge of those original languages, and has given the people ears to understand him speaking in the vernacular. It is God's most excellent gift, if men know it well and recall it to its proper use; but those who abuse it make themselves wholly inexcusable, some being negligent in reading, others despising what they read superficially, although, if they desire to receive nourishment from this most holy food, they must chew it, taste it, and digest it. And in this very place it has pleased God to set up a school of those three languages, a school indeed now so neglected that a part, and indeed the greatest part, neglects to have its own children taught even the rudiments; while another part, having scarcely greeted the threshold of the school, at once withdraws its children, so that very few follow the course of studies by which they might at last grow into learned men and obtain some calling. How few aspire to that most sacred ministry! Indeed that calling is today the most despised of all, and yet it is as necessary as the air we breathe and the breath by which we live. Hence it comes about that among us, besides the great number of those who, from the frequent sermons they have heard, know what is good but do not do it, there is a very large number of the ignorant; so that we see here, to our great shame, ministers whose work we use being foreigners, when rather faithful shepherds ought to have been spread from here throughout the whole world.

units.la: Superest in hoc titulo caput vnum adhuc obseruandum, ut in tota sacra scriptura, cuius est hoc summarium, nepe non tantum illu intelligendum, aut legendum, sed etiam intelligendum, meditandum & ad vsum suum referendum, vera & viua fide ab vnoquoque secundum suam vocationem & dignitatem. Quibus adde cauendum summopere ne sacrosanctae voces istae in magicas incantationes conuertantur, quae summa est impietas, in quam manifeste labuntur qui schedulas de iis conficiunt ut de
units.tr: There remains one point to observe in this title: in the whole of Holy Scripture, of which this is a summary, we must not only understand and read, but also grasp, meditate upon, and apply to our own use, with a true and living faith, each person according to his own calling and station. To these add that we must take the greatest care that these sacred words are not turned into magical incantations, which is great impiety, and into which those clearly fall who make slips of paper from them, as

units.la: Peculiaris expositio singulorum verborum huius tituli nostrae sacrae scripturae mysterium coniectis. vt de nonnullis aliis scriptvræ locis, quæ ex collo pendeant, & febribus cæterisque adeò morbis omnibus remedium præsentissimum adferat, aut ad eos propellendos amuleta sint, rem sanè detestandam, & graui animaduersione dignissimam.
units.tr: A detailed explanation of the individual words of this title is the mystery of our holy Scripture, not to be sewn into amulets, as is done with some other passages of Scripture that people hang from the neck and that they claim bring the most ready remedy for fevers and all other diseases, or that they use as charms to drive them away. This is truly a detestable thing, most deserving of severe reproof.

units.la: In sensu igitur & rebus per has voces signi- catis, non autem in elementis vel syllabis est inhærendum, quum in singulis istis vocibus suum inæstimabile pondus insit. Iesus igitur dicitur, nomine illi proprio & peculiari, id est Seruator, quoniam ait Angelus Iosepho, Matt. 1. 21. & sanctæ Virgini, Luc. 1. 31. populum suum à peccatis suis liberabit. Verù igitur esse Deum inde efficitur, quandoquidem vnius Dei proprium est potentia sua peccata condonare, Luc. 5. 21. Verus etiam homo est, (nec enim spectrum crucifixum est, sed verus homo) ac proinde verus Emanuel, id est Deus nobiscum, aut Homo Deus, Matth. 11. 23. Hac igitur vnica voce continetur quicquid de persona & officio Iesu Christi Domini nostri nobis tenendum est.
units.tr: One must therefore keep to the sense and the realities signified by these words, and not to the letters or syllables, since each of these words carries its own inestimable weight. Jesus is so called as a proper and peculiar name, that is, Saviour, since the angel said to Joseph (Matt. 1.21) and to the holy Virgin (Luke 1.31) that he would save his people from their sins. From this it follows that he is true God, since it is the proper power of God alone to forgive sins (Luke 5.21). He is also true man (for he is not a crucified phantom but a true man), and therefore the true Emmanuel, that is, God with us, or God-man (Matt. 11.23). In this one word is contained whatever we must hold concerning the person and office of Jesus Christ our Lord.

units.la: Nazarenus idem, & quidem per errorem dicitur, sic vulgo eum nominante, quasi vrbe Nazaretha esset oriundus. Sed diuina prouidentia nomen istud in alium vsum inuertit, vt apud Matt. exponitur 2. 13. vt qui sit verus Domini Nazaræus ab omni pollutione sanctificatus & separatus, vt Nazaræorum voti figura præmonstrabat. Num. 6. in quo etiam omnes sanctificamur & Deo consecramur.
units.tr: He is also called the Nazarene, though by an error, since people commonly name him so as if he had come from the city of Nazareth. But divine providence turned that name to another use, as is explained at Matt. 2.13, so that he might be the true Nazarite of the Lord, sanctified and set apart from all defilement, as the figure of the Nazarite vow foreshadowed (Num. 6), in which we too are all sanctified and consecrated to God.

units.la: Rex deinde declaratur, & quidem Rex ille Iudaeis promissus, Rex, inquam, omnem habes in coelo & terra potestatem, Matth.21.15.cuius in femore scriptum est, Rex Regum, & Dominus dominantium. Apocal. 19. 16. Rex coram quo res omnes superas, medias, infimas genu flectere oportet, Rom.14.11. & Philipp.2.10.& nominatim solus Rex spiritualis, caput, conseruator ac legislator suae Ecclesiae. Iac.4.v.12. Sed obseruandum Regiam hanc dignitatem, ex aeterni sacerdotij forma, inseparabilem in eo esse, cuius Melchisedecus fuit figura. Porrò Sacerdotium illud in Lege tribus capitibus continebatur, nimirum in offerendi, docendi ac benedicendi potestate, quod huius unius & Aeterni Sacerdotis, cuius figura fuit Summus Sacerdos secundum ordinem Aaronicum, proprium est ac peculiare. Hic igitur ille est qui oblatione sui semel in Cruce facta nos omnes in aeternum patri reconciliauit & sanctificauit. Rom.3.24.Heb.10.14. hic ille est per quem nos Pater doctrinam salutis semper docuit, cuius etiam Spiritus inspiratione Prophetae loquuti sunt 1.Pet.1.11.qui tandem vltimis temporibus ipsemet ore suo nobis omni Patris consilio ac voluntate patefacta, deinceps misit & quotidie mittit fidos suos pastores ac doctores ad suae domus spiritualis aedificationem.Ephes.4.11.& 12. Solus ille maledictio pro nobis factus est, Gal.3.13. vt fiat vicissim benedictio, id est sapientia, iustitia, sanctificatio & redemptio. 1. Corinth. 1.30. Porrò quum Iudæorum Rex nuncupatur, etsi proprie Iudæis factæ sunt promissiones, non ideo tamen hoc Regnum & Sacerdotium ad solos Iudæos pertinet ac restringitur, vt qui iam maxima ex parte quum hic titulus scriberetur huic Regi renuntiassent: sed ad Gentes etiam, quæ in eorum locum insitæ sunt. Idcirco voces illæ filiorum Abrahami, Israëlitarum & Iudæorum eo respectu, Gentes omnes & nationes orbis terrarum continent, ex quibus omnibus per Sacrosancti verbi prædicationem Deus suam Ecclesiam colligit, Matt.3.9. Rom. 4.12. Annon igitur tam eximia tamque pretiosa hæc arcana simul iuncta satis superque testantur non immerito dictum à me superius fuisse hoc titulo, veluti manu ipsa Patris scripto, & Cruci supra huius Crucifixi caput affixo, contineri summarium excellentissimum & omnino necessarium totius doctrinæ salutis nostræ, quam Prophetæ & Apostoli prædicarunt, vt eius expositio sit in Ecclesia Dei perpetua? Vtinam igitur Deus Opt.Max.hanc in nostris mentibus doctrinam magis ac magis infigat, ad nominis ipsius gloriam, & nostram salutem.
units.tr: Next he is declared King, and indeed that King promised to the Jews: King, I say, to whom all power in heaven and earth belongs (Matth. 21.15), on whose thigh is written "King of kings, and Lord of lords" (Apoc. 19.16); before whom all things above, between, and below must bow the knee (Rom. 14.11; Phil. 2.10); and especially the only spiritual King, head, preserver and lawgiver of his Church (Jas. 4.12). But it must be observed that this royal dignity, according to the pattern of the eternal priesthood, is inseparable from him whose figure was Melchizedek. Moreover, the priesthood under the Law was contained under three heads, namely the power of offering, of teaching, and of blessing, which belongs properly and peculiarly to this one and eternal Priest, whose figure was the high priest after the order of Aaron. He is the one who, by the offering of himself once for all on the cross, reconciled us all to the Father for ever and sanctified us (Rom. 3.24; Heb. 10.14). He is the one through whom the Father has always taught us the doctrine of salvation, and by whose Spirit the prophets spoke (1 Pet. 1.11). At the last times, having himself made known with his own mouth all the Father's counsel and will, he has since sent, and daily sends, his faithful ministers and teachers for the building up of his spiritual house (Eph. 4.11, 12). He alone was made a curse for us (Gal. 3.13), so that in turn there might be blessing, that is, wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption (1 Cor. 1.30). Moreover, although he is named King of the Jews, and although the promises were properly made to the Jews, this kingdom and priesthood does not on that account belong to, or get restricted to, the Jews alone, since they had for the most part already renounced this King when this title was written. It extends also to the Gentiles, who have been grafted into their place. Hence those expressions "sons of Abraham," "Israelites," and "Jews," in that respect, embrace all the Gentiles and nations of the earth, from all of whom God gathers his Church through the preaching of the holy Word (Matt. 3.9; Rom. 4.12). Do not these rare and precious mysteries, taken together, sufficiently and more than sufficiently testify that I was not wrong to say above that this title, as if written by the Father's own hand and fixed to the cross above the head of this Crucified One, contains the most excellent and wholly necessary summary of the whole doctrine of our salvation, which the prophets and apostles preached, so that its exposition in the Church of God may be perpetual? May God, the best and greatest, therefore fix this doctrine more and more in our minds, to the glory of his name and our salvation.

units.la: Historia deinceps narrat Christo dum Cruci affigitur oblatum vinum, vt ait Matth. felle mixtum & vt ait, Marcus vinum myrrhatum, qua in re videri possit quædam subesse repugnantia. Verum ex Marco Matthæus exponendus est, & Fellis voce intelligendum, non Fel proprie dictum, sed vinum conditum cum a Y. iiij.
units.tr: The history next tells that when Christ was being fastened to the cross, wine was offered to him, mixed with gall, as Matthew says, and wine mingled with myrrh, as Mark says. In this matter there may seem to be some contradiction. But Matthew must be explained by Mark, and the word "gall" understood not as gall properly speaking, but as wine seasoned with a certain bitterness, namely myrrh.

units.la: marore quodam,puta,myrrhæ. Est autem hæc potio diligenter distinguenda ab acero quod illi sitienti & potum petenti,iam iam animam exhalaturo, propinatū est. Decepti sunt etiam qui hanc potionem in Christi passionibus numerarunt,quasi tunc amara & iniucunda fuisset potatus.Nam contrà certis testimoniis constat myrrham qua vinum illud condiebatur, non eam fuisse quam hodie myrrham vocamus, ingrati admodum & cum amarore coniuncti saporis, quum vetus illa suauis fuerit & temperata: ad quam etiam alia fuisse adiecta pharmaca verisimile est,adeò vt potio gratissima fuerit & in deliciis habita. Constat etiam ex veterum quorundam Rabbinorum monumentis, solitas fuisse quasdam honestas matronas ludæas vinum illud condire, quod reis ad supplicium damnatis offerrent,ad hoc ipsum adferentes locum illum ex Prouerb.31.6. Non alienum igitur à vero est tunc à quibusdam ex iis mulieribus Christum sequentibus, plangentibus & lamentantibus oblatam illi hanc potionem. Luc.23. v.27. Quod igitur Christum illam recusasse conspicimus, non propter amarorem factum est, nec quòd metueret ne hac potione cruciatus quos tolerabat producerentur,quasi inuitus tantos dolores perferret,cuius erat tantum in eo posita voluntas vt Dei Patris voluntatem impleret & salutem hominum perficeret Luc.12.50.Contrà igitur recusauit,quòd suos cruciatus nollet leniri, cuius ante oculos Patris tantum obsequium,
units.tr: This drink must be carefully distinguished from the vinegar that was offered to him when he was thirsty and asked for drink, and was about to breathe out his soul at once. Those too are mistaken who count this drink among the sufferings of Christ, as if it had been bitter and unpleasant to drink. On the contrary, it is established by sure testimonies that the myrrh with which that wine was seasoned was not what we today call myrrh, which is very disagreeable and has a harsh, bitter taste; that ancient kind was pleasant and mild. To it other drugs were probably also added, so that the drink was very agreeable and held in delight. It is also established from the records of certain ancient rabbis that some respectable Jewish matrons were accustomed to season that wine, which they offered to criminals condemned to execution, citing for this very purpose the passage Prov. 31.6. It is therefore not far from the truth that this drink was offered to him then by some of those women who followed Christ, weeping and lamenting (Luke 23.27). Therefore, that we see Christ refusing it was not because of its bitterness, nor because he feared that the torments he endured would be lessened by this drink, as if he bore such great pains unwillingly. His will was set on this alone: that he should fulfil the will of God the Father and accomplish the salvation of men (Luke 12.50). On the contrary, he refused it because he did not wish his sufferings to be eased, since before his eyes were the Father's so great obedience and the salvation of men to be accomplished.

units.la: {a} ... quium, & salus hominum perficienda versabatur.
units.tr: ... and the salvation of men to be accomplished was at stake.

units.la: Absit autem vt proptera, quum maxima fit differentia in scopo & fine ad quem Iesu Christi passiones & nostræ referuntur, si forte contingat nos ad martyrium pro Christi nomine, aut etiam ad pœnas pro peccatis nostris luendas trahi, tolamen oblatum respuamus, modo tamen eiusmodi sit quo nec conscientia ipsa lædatur, nec zelus quo ad Dei gloriam promouendam nos ardere par est refrigescat, nec denique Christiana patientia superetur. Apage autem insanos illos à Satana fascinatos, qui sibi ipsis dum manus violentas adferunt, corpus & animam simul perdunt, & tamen se Paradisum sibi & aliis mereri misere sibi persuadent.
units.tr: Far be it from us, however, that, since there is the greatest difference in the aim and end to which the sufferings of Jesus Christ and our own are referred, if it should happen that we are drawn to martyrdom for the name of Christ, or even to undergo punishments for our sins, we should therefore spurn the cup offered to us. This holds provided, however, that it is of such a kind that conscience itself is not harmed, nor the zeal with which we ought to burn to promote God's glory grows cold, nor Christian patience is overcome. Away with those madmen bewitched by Satan, who, while they lay violent hands on themselves, destroy body and soul together, and yet wretchedly persuade themselves that they deserve Paradise for themselves and for others.

units.la: HOMILIA VICESIMANONA.
units.tr: HOMILY TWENTY-NINTH.

units.la: IOH. 19.
units.tr: JOHN 19.

units.la: 23. Milites ergo quum crucifixissent Iesum, acceperunt eius vestimenta, (& fecerunt quatuor partes, vnicuique militi partem) & tunicam. Erat autem tunica infutilis, à summo contexta tota.
units.tr: 23. Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments (and made four parts, to every soldier a part), and also the coat. Now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

units.la: 24. Dixerunt ergo inter se, Ne findamus eam, sed sortiamur de illa cuius futura sit: ut Scriptura impleretur, dicens, Partiti sunt vestimenta mea sibi, & super vestem meam iecerunt sortem. Milites igitur hæc fecerunt.
units.tr: 24. They said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it whose it shall be; that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which saith, They parted my garments among them, and for my vesture they did cast lots. These things therefore the soldiers did.

units.la: 25. Stabant autem iuxta Crucem Iesu, mater eius & soror matris eius, Maria Cleopæ uxor, & Maria Magdalene.
units.tr: 25. Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.

units.la: 26. Quum vidisset ergo Iesus matrem ac discipulum adstantem quem diligebat, dicit matri suæ, Mulier ecce filius tuus.
units.tr: 26. When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!

units.la: 27. Deinde dicit discipulo, Ecce mater tua. Et ex illa hora recepit eam discipulus ille domum suam.
units.tr: 27. Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.

units.la: HAC TENVS auditis iis quæ in executione sententiæ aduersus Dominum latæ contigerunt, sequuntur apud Euangelistas consideranda, quæ ab eius crucifixione facta dictaque sunt, primum ad sextam horam usque, deinde ad nonam qua Spiritum reddidit. Hic igitur primum occurrunt Christi vestimenta sorte inter quatuor à quibus cruci affixus fuerat carnifices diuisa: quæ quum sint vsitatissima, & in more apud omnes posita, subesse tamen hic occulta quædam arcana magni momenti statuendum est, de quibus alioqui Dauid Domini nostri figura non aliquid tam accurate prædixisset, Psalm.22.19. nec Euangelistæ tam distinctè factum istud recensuissent.
units.tr: Thus far we have heard what happened in the carrying out of the sentence pronounced against the Lord. Next, in the Evangelists, we must consider what was done and said from his crucifixion, first until the sixth hour, then until the ninth, when he gave up the Spirit. Here first occurs the division of Christ's garments by lot among the four executioners by whom he had been fastened to the cross. Although this is most customary and common among all, we must nevertheless hold that some hidden mysteries of great weight lie beneath it. Otherwise David, a figure of our Lord, would not have foretold it so exactly (Psalm 22:19), nor would the Evangelists have related the deed so distinctly.

units.la: Legimus igitur Genef.2.25.primos illos nostros à quibus ortum ducimus parentes, nudos creatos ante peccatum ita sine pudore vlo vixisse.Quod minimè quidem sic intelligendum quasi tunc infantibus similes vixerint, sine ratione,iudicio aut pudore,quos Deus tam excellentibus tum corporis tum animæ donibus perfectos crearat. Sed quòd in duabus istis tam insignibus rebus creatis ante peccatum nullum esset nec in anima vitium, nec in corpore labes vlla aut macula,cuius eos puderet. At post peccatum tam pura & honesta nuditas induit, tum eorum animam densissimis tenebris in intelligentia: & vitiorum omnium semine in voluntate & omnibus affectionibus: tum corpora non tantum ea deformitate quæ præcipuè in genitalibus & vicinis partibus apparet, sed necessitate etiam tegendi se, tum ad velanda pudenda,tum ad temporis iniurias propulsandas,quibus ad mortem quam inuexit peccatum gradibus peruenitur.
units.tr: We read in Genesis 2:25 that our first parents, from whom we derive our origin, were created naked and lived without any shame before the sin. This must not be understood as if they then lived like infants, without reason, judgment or shame, though God had created them perfect with such excellent gifts of body and soul. Rather, in these two so remarkable created things there was, before sin, no vice in the soul and no blemish or stain in the body of which they would be ashamed. But after the sin there came a nakedness no longer pure and honourable: their souls were plunged into the thickest darkness in understanding, and into the seed of all vices in will and all the affections; and their bodies were marked not only by the deformity which appears chiefly in the genitals and nearby parts, but also by the necessity of covering themselves, both to hide their shame and to ward off the injuries of the weather, by which steps they came to the death that sin had brought in.

units.la: Iesus Christus igitur secundus noster Adamus factus, secunda generatione spirituali, nudus in Cruce mori voluit,primùm ne quam ignominiam quam effemus meriti refugeret.
units.tr: Jesus Christ therefore, made our second Adam, by a second, spiritual birth, willed to die naked on the cross; first, so that he might not refuse any shame which we had deserved.

units.la: Deinde vt in Cruce nudus purissimam illam nuditatem in suo corpore, quod proprium est corpus Filij essentialis Dei, & integerrimam in anima ab omni labe & macula vacuam proponeret, vt in hac nuditate, qui veterem hominem in illo & cum illo crucifixerunt, non modò in pristinum illum statum ex quo excidimus restituätur,sed in illam gloriam & corruptionem incnarrabilem introducantur, in qua corpora ipsa nostra suscitabūtur,pretiosissima illa & ditissima IesuChristi nuditate superinduta 2.Cor.5 4. tantò quidem excellentiore & pretiouiore statu quantò vita spiritualis,cœlestis & æterna,infinitis modis est vita animali excellétior, licet ante peccatum, vt erant Adamus & Eua creati, esset immortalis.1.Cor.15.45.
units.tr: Then, so that naked on the cross he might set forth in his own body that most pure nakedness (his body being the proper body of the essential Son of God), and in his soul that most whole nakedness, free from every stain and blemish; so that, in this nakedness, those who crucified the old man in him and with him might be restored not only to that original state from which we fell, but be brought into that glory and incorruption beyond description, in which our own bodies will be raised, clothed over with the most precious and rich nakedness of Jesus Christ (2 Cor. 5:4). This will be a state far more excellent and precious, as far as spiritual, heavenly and eternal life is in infinite ways more excellent than animal life, even though, as Adam and Eve were created, before the sin they were immortal (1 Cor. 15:45).

units.la: Præter quæ omnia memoria repetendum est, æternum Dei filium, fratrem nostrum factum, assumpsisse in vnitatem naturæ totam naturam nostram,non quidé simpliciter quoad corporis & animæ essentiam nunquam exuendam, sed etiam quoad eius infirmitates, excepto peccato, quarum infirmitatum vestimenta (quibus indutus fuit vt cæteri homines) fuerunt ad tempus certissimum testimonium: donec nimirum in statu illo debitas peccatis nostris pœnas exsoluisset. Appropinquâte igitur tempore quo vitam animalem erat exuturus, vt in se vitam spiritualem,totius Ecclesiæ suæ vltimo die futuram inchoaret, voluit vestimentis suis terrenis in huius rei significationem spoliari.Nam quòd à resurrectione ad ascensionem vsque vestitus apparuit, vt quispiam alius apparuit, atque adeò bibit & edit cum quibus illi visum est, nec facta sunt illa per simplicem visionem, multóque minus per illusionem: nec tamen ex necessitate, cui se subiecerat antea, sed speciali dispensatione, vt plenè ac sensibiliter de sua resurrectione magis etiam incredulos facerct certiores.
units.tr: Besides all these things, it must be remembered that the eternal Son of God, made our brother, assumed into the unity of his nature our whole nature. Not simply as to the essence of body and soul, which is never to be laid aside, but also as to its infirmities, sin excepted. The garments of these infirmities (with which he was clothed as other men are) were a most certain testimony for a time, namely until in that state he had paid the penalties owed for our sins. So, as the time drew near when he was to lay aside animal life, in order to begin in himself the spiritual life which will be the lot of his whole Church on the last day, he willed to be stripped of his earthly garments as a sign of this matter. For that he appeared clothed from his resurrection until his ascension, as one might appear to anyone else, and ate and drank with whom it seemed good to him, these things were not done by mere vision, much less by illusion; nor yet were they from the necessity to which he had previously submitted, but by a special dispensation, so that he might make the unbelievers more fully and sensibly certain of his resurrection.

units.la: Denique Dominus noster Iesus Christus quum se veteribus exhibuisset, ritibus ac figuris, tanquam velo quodam, obtectum, per illas veluti per transennam conspiciendum: & tempus aduenisset quo se palàm patefaceret, & Ecclesiæ suæ clarissimè per suorum Apostolorum doctrinam & scripta depingeretur, Galat. 3. vers. 1. voluit in Crucem ascendens, veluti velamen istud exuere, spolio illo in manibus hostium relicto, quò se omnibus amicis in eximia illa sua pulchritudine nudum osten-taret.
units.tr: Finally, our Lord Jesus Christ, when he had shown himself to the men of old in rites and figures, as if covered with a veil, to be seen through them as through a lattice, and when the time had come in which he would reveal himself openly, and his Church would be most clearly portrayed through the teaching and writings of his apostles (Gal. 3:1), willed, ascending the cross, to strip off that veil, leaving the spoil in the hands of his enemies, so that he might show himself naked to all his friends in that outstanding beauty of his.

units.la: Iesus Christus igitur in opulenta illa nuditate seruauit nos, in qua nihil desideratur, hanc ob causam etiam Apostolo dicente nos in eo completos esse. Coloss. 2. 10. & Christum nobis esse omnia. Coloss. 3. ver. 11. præter quem & quidem crucifixum scire nihil voluerit. 1. Corinth. 2. vers. 2. At non in hac lignea Cruce iam quærendus est. Nec enim est amplius in ea, & nunquam fuit diutius quàm horarum sex spatio. Non in sepulchri rupe. Semel enim illud nunquam rediturus egressus est. Non in Hierusalem terrestri & homicida. Sed in cœlis quærendus, non quidem corporeo motu, in quos à resurrectione tantum attollenda sunt nostra corpora.
units.tr: Jesus Christ therefore saved us in that rich nakedness in which nothing is lacking, and for this reason also the Apostle says that we are complete in him (Col. 2:10), and that Christ is all things to us (Col. 3:11), and that he determined to know nothing except Jesus Christ, and him crucified (1 Cor. 2:2). But he is not to be sought now on this wooden cross: for he is no longer on it, and never remained on it longer than the space of six hours. Nor is he to be sought in the rock of the sepulchre, for he came out of it once and never to return. Nor is he to be sought in earthly and murderous Jerusalem. He is to be sought in heaven, not by any bodily motion, but to whom our bodies must be raised up only at the resurrection.

units.la: Verus Iesus Christus in nativa sua pulchritudine nudus ... se patefacit in Sanctorum verbo. 1.Thess.4.17.Non etiam sperandum vt realiter è coelo descendat, & secundum carnis essentiam.Nam coelo capi illum oportet ad tempora restitutionis omnium,diem nimirum vltimum.Act. 3. 21. quod etiam articuli fidei satis clarè declarant. At nobis in Sacrosancto verbo suo & Sacramentis ad viuum depingitur, in omnibus quae de ipso nobis ad salutem credenda sunt, seu quae personam ipsius, seu quae Mediatoris officiū spectat, vt nimirū oculis eū fidei intueamur, quatenus ad salutem in hac vita cognoscere possumus ac debemus, diem illum vltimum expectantes in quo sumus eum qualis est oculis ipsis conspecturi.1.Ioh.3.2.
units.tr: The true Jesus Christ, naked in his native beauty, reveals himself in the word of the saints (1 Thess. 4:17). Nor are we to hope that he will descend from heaven in reality, and according to the essence of his flesh. For he must be received in heaven until the times of the restoration of all things, namely the last day (Acts 3:21), as the articles of faith also declare sufficiently clearly. But to us he is depicted to the life in his most holy word and in the sacraments, in all that is to be believed about him for salvation, whether concerning his person or concerning the office of Mediator; so that we may look upon him with the eyes of faith, as far as we can and must know him unto salvation in this life, awaiting that last day on which we shall see him with our own eyes as he is (1 John 3:2).

units.la: Apage igitur pictorum Iesus Christos apage omnes Christos mille traditionibus humanis transformatos: apage nugas illas omnes & gesticulationes quibus imprudentes illi non magis venerandam religionem Christianam reddiderunt, vt sibi persuaserunt, sed contra Sacramentorum simplicitatem & pulchritudinem, totiusque adeo Diuini cultus miserè foedarunt, polluerunt ac funditus euerterunt. Illos igitur omnes Iesus Christos sciamus totidem esse mortua & muta idola, aut nihil nisi mendacij & vanitatis doctores, à quibus vtinam Deus pro sua immensa clementia Christianum orbem erutum magis ac magis protegat ac tueatur, nominatim verò ab eo Iesu Christo quem ambitiosi quidam homines, & hypocritae seipsos cum aliis miserè decipientes,& quidam alij quos Crucis Domini taedet det ac piget, sibi fingunt & inuehere conatur, triplici vt ita dicam, indutum veste, vna quidem veteribus scorti illius sordibus antiquitatis pallio & nomine ab illius lenonibus rectis: alia, vestibus quidem à Iesu Christi vera sposa mutuò acceptis,sed laceris & malè consutis: tertia denique suis inuentionibus mixtis & variis vt Ierusalem cœlestem cum terrestri Babylone,Mistam cum Euangelo, Lucem denique cum Tenebris concilient.Nec verò cœpit hoc tempore monstrum istud in Ecclesiâ irrepere & eam pertentare, non deficientibus falsis fratribus qui pro viribus illud introductum promoueant: qua de re vos fratres, admoneo, vósque hortor vt vobis ab hoc monstro diligenter caueatis. Spero verò Deum meliora suis cōcessurum, tantóque malo pro immensa sua misericordia remedium allaturum: sin minus,mementote vobis à me maturè hæc prædicta, antequam mihi Deus os occludat, quod vt faciat cum supplex oro priusquam imminentem desolationem meis oculis inspiciam. Et hæc quidem hactenus de falsis illis pseudochristis quos homines adornare voluerunt.
units.tr: Away then with the painters' Christs! Away with all the Christs transformed by a thousand human traditions! Away with all those trifles and gestures by which those foolish men, who persuaded themselves that they made the Christian religion more venerable, have in fact miserably disfigured, polluted and utterly overthrown the simplicity and beauty of the sacraments, and indeed of the whole divine worship. Let us therefore know that all these Christs are so many dead and dumb idols, or teachers of nothing but lies and vanity. May God, in his immense mercy, rescue and ever more protect the Christian world from them. Above all, may God protect it from that Jesus Christ whom certain ambitious men and hypocrites, miserably deceiving themselves and others, and certain other men whom the cross of the Lord wearies and displeases, invent and attempt to bring forward, clothed, as I may say, in three garments: one, indeed, in the old filthy rags of that harlot, a cloak of antiquity, and a name borrowed from her pimps; another, in garments indeed borrowed from the true bride of Jesus Christ, but torn and badly sewn; the third, finally, in their own mixed and varied inventions, so as to reconcile the heavenly Jerusalem with the earthly Babylon, the Mystery with the Gospel, and, in short, Light with Darkness. Nor did this monster begin to creep into the Church and to assault it only in this age, for false brethren have never been wanting who, as far as they can, promote what has been introduced. On this matter, brethren, I admonish you, and urge you to be diligently on your guard against this monster. I hope, however, that God will grant better things to his people, and in his immense mercy bring a remedy for so great an evil. But if not, remember that these things were foretold to you by me in good time, before God shuts my mouth; which I pray with suppliant voice he will do, before I see with my own eyes the impending desolation. And these things, so far, concerning those false pseudo-Christs whom men have wished to adorn.

units.la: Idem prorsus de reliquis Iesu Christis dicendum est, quos dum isti sartores vestire ex suo ingenio & arbitrio cupiunt, penitus spoliarunt,& quidem longè magis miseranda ratione quàm ij de quibus hæc historia mentionem facit. Milites enim isti solis eum vestimentis quibus tegebatur spoliarunt: at isti quos metiam lamoro,illum, vt ita dicam excoriarunt & eum fibiipfi surripuerunt. Eiusmodi sunt a quibus vera sua Humanitate spoliatur aut directe, vt Marcionitæ,aut obliquè & per cöfcquentiam, vt Vbiquitarij, Confubftantiatores & Transfubstantiatores:aut sua Diuinitate,vt Samosateniani, Arriani,Eunomiani,& similia hominum nostro seculo renascentia monstra: aut qui illum etiam in duas partes lacerant,vt Nestoriani: aut qui monstrum mixtum acconfusum faciunt, vt Eutychiani: aut in vniuersum a quibus Regia dignitate spoliatur,sibi vendicatibus regni eius spirituales leges & instituta pro arbitrio mutādi,detrahendi,aut ad eas adiiciendi potestatem: aut Sacerdotio suo æterno,datis ipsi sociis,seu a quibus iterum offeratur,seu qui pro nobis in Cœlis apud Deum intercedant: denique quicunque vel tantillum vero huic Iesu Christo detrahunt,qualis nobis nudè ac simpliciter, atque perfectissimè conspiciendus in sacris Scripturis, afflatu Spiritus Sancti à Prophetis & Apostolis conscriptis depingitur.
units.tr: The same must be said of the other Christs whom these tailors wish to clothe according to their own wit and judgment, and whom they have stripped utterly bare, and in a far more pitiable way than those of whom this history makes mention. Those soldiers stripped him only of the garments with which he was covered, but these men, as I may put it, have flayed him and robbed him of himself. Such are those who strip him of his true humanity, either directly, like the Marcionites, or indirectly and by consequence, like the Ubiquitarians, the Consubstantiators and the Transubstantiators; or of his divinity, like the Samosatenians, the Arians, the Eunomians and the similar monsters born again in our own age; or those who tear him into two parts, like the Nestorians; or those who make a mixed and confused monster of him, like the Eutychians; or those who strip him of his royal dignity, claiming for themselves the power to change, remove or add to the spiritual laws and institutions of his kingdom at their own pleasure; or of his eternal priesthood, by assigning him associates, whether they offer him again, or those who intercede for us in heaven before God alongside him. Finally, all who take away even the smallest part of the true Jesus Christ, such as we are to behold in the sacred Scriptures, where he is portrayed plainly and simply, and most perfectly, by the prophets and apostles who wrote under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Superest in textu nobis excutiendum quod de tunica infutili acu texta dicitur,quam inter fe milites sortiti sunt: per quam equidem cum fidelioribus interpretibus intelligo veras diuitias ab hoc Crucifixo terras deferente nobis relictas, non quidem omnibus, sed diuina & arcana Dei voluntate electis,qui nomine Sortis hoc loco significantur, ex iis quę de Sortibus scribuntur Prouerb.16.33.& quibus Ecclesiam fiam Apostolicam, quum sic tulit necessitas, vt fam esse legimus. Act. 1. 24. Quam ob causam saepissime videmus Ecclesiam sortem & portionem Domini vocari. Hinc etiam Cleri & Clericorum voces. Haec igitur tunica nobis sacrosanctam doctrinam repraesentat ex fundamentalibus articulis Religionis Christianae compositam, ita invicem, vt ita dicam, contextis & compactis, vt a se diuelli nequeant, & separati futuri sint inutiles: ita quidem vt haec etiam omnia ad vnius Ecclesiae ex quatuor terrarum angulis collectae structuram referantur, vt fiat in vnitate fidei & charitatis cor vnum & anima vna. Act. 4. 21. & sic compactum corpus ex sola vi intus agente capitis incrementum capiat pro mensura vniuscuiusque membri, Eph. 4. 16. Porro si quis aduersus hanc expositionem excipiat hanc tunicam apud profanos illos milites mansisse, quod non videatur cum sanctissima Dei Ecclesia congruere, aio Dominum etsi celeratissimis hominibus visus est in hoc salutis nostrae mysterio peragedo nihil impedire quominus per eos nostrae salutis arcana nos docuerit: nunquid enim Pilatus is est cuius manu Dominus visus est in scribendo & cruci affigendo titulo, quo huius historiae fructus continetur, & tanquam praecone cuius praeconio Dominus in regni sui possessionem in monte Sionis, vt erat a Dauide praedictum, Psal. 2. 6. mitteretur? Sed praeterea, quibus vnquam, obsecro, persomis oblata est haec tunica nisi per se peccatoribus & profanis, quando-
units.tr: What remains for us to examine in the text is what is said of the seamless tunic, woven from top to bottom, which the soldiers cast lots for among themselves. By this, indeed, I understand with the more faithful interpreters the true riches left to us by this Crucified One, who bore the earth, not for all, but for those chosen by the divine and hidden will of God, who are signified here by the name of lot, drawing on what is written of lots in Prov. 16.33, and by which the Apostolic Church was filled, since necessity so required, as we read was done in Acts 1.24. For this reason we very often see the Church called the lot and portion of the Lord. Hence also the words clergy and clerics. This tunic, therefore, represents to us the most sacred doctrine, composed of the fundamental articles of the Christian religion, so interwoven and joined together, as it were, that they cannot be torn from one another, and separated would be useless. And indeed all these things are referred to the building up of the one Church gathered from the four corners of the earth, so that in unity of faith and love there may be one heart and one soul (Acts 4.32), and so the body, thus joined together by the power working from within the head alone, may grow according to the measure of each member (Eph. 4.16). Moreover, if anyone objects to this interpretation that the tunic remained with those profane soldiers, which does not seem to fit with the most holy Church of God, I answer that the Lord, though he was seen to be among the most wicked men in carrying out this mystery of our salvation, did not hinder him from teaching us the secrets of our salvation through them. For is not Pilate the very man by whose hand the Lord was seen to write the title and fix it to the cross, in which the fruit of this history is contained, and as a herald by whose proclamation the Lord was sent into possession of his kingdom on Mount Zion, as David had foretold (Ps. 2.6)? But further, to whom, I beg you, has this tunic ever been offered, except to sinners and profane men by themselves, when we were all by nature children of wrath, and God has shut up all things under disobedience so that no one may be saved except by mercy (Rom. 11.32)? And what if we say, as is likely, that through him who drew this tunic were represented us Gentiles, such as we were before our calling (Eph. 2.12), just as those three other soldiers marked out the wretched Jews, scattered into the three parts of the world, who for embracing Jesus Christ crucified have held on hitherto, and still hold on as far as in them lies, to the whole of that outward Judaism, from which he willed to be stripped on the cross, as has been explained more fully above? There are many other interpretations of this passage that are by no means to be despised, but we must be content with those that have some analogy to Scripture and are more tolerable, and we must pray God that we may be counted among those who did not crucify Christ, but in whom he is crucified through his Holy Spirit; and may he grant us this grace, that in place of so many false Christs and counterfeits we may learn the true Jesus Christ, who is more and more impressed on our minds, whose open and unpainted beauty we may gaze upon, and whose sole true and unspeakable glory we may seek and find, to which he calls us daily through the sacred and pure preaching of his Gospel and the administration of his Sacraments.

units.la: Z. j. quidem omnes nascimur irae filij, & omnia Deus conclusit in contumacia, ut nemo seruetur nisi ex misericordia?Rom.11.32. Quid si vero dixerimus, ut est verisimile, per cu qui hanc tunicam sortitus est, nos Gentes fuisse repraesentatas, quales ante vocationem nostram eramus?Ephes.2.12. ut per tres illos alios milites miseri Iudaei notati sunt in tres orbis partes dispersi, qui pro Iesu Christo crucifixo amplexando retinuerunt hactenus & adhuc retinent quantum in ipsis est, totum illum Iudaismum exteriorem, a quo tamen in Cruce voluit spoliari, ut supra fusius explicatum est?Multae sunt aliae huius loci minime contemnendae expositiones, sed iis quae ad Scripturas quadam analogiam habent & sunt magis tolerandae contentos esse nos oportet, Deumque precari ut in eorum numero censeamur, non qui Cruci Christum affixerunt, sed in quibus est per Sanctum suum Spiritum crucifixus, nobisque hac largiatur gratiam, ut pro tot pseudochristis, & adulterinis, verum illum Iesum Christum discamus, qui mentibus nostris magis ac magis imprimatur, cuius apertam nobis & non fucatam pulchritudinem intueamur, & cuius solam veram & inenarrabilem gloriam illam quaeramus & inueniamus ad quam nos quotidie, per Sacrosanctam & puram Euangelij sui praedicationem, & Sacramentorum administrationem vocat.
units.tr: For indeed we are all by nature children of wrath, and God has shut up all things under unbelief, so that no one is saved except by mercy? Rom. 11.32. But what if we say, as is likely, that through the man who drew this tunic by lot, we Gentiles were represented, such as we were before our calling? Eph. 2.12. Just as those three other soldiers marked out the wretched Jews, scattered into the three parts of the world, who have held fast hitherto, and still hold fast as far as in them lies, to that whole outward Judaism, embracing the crucified Jesus Christ, from which nevertheless he wished to be stripped on the Cross, as was explained more fully above? There are many other interpretations of this place, by no means to be despised, but we ought to be content with those that have some analogy with Scripture and are more tolerable, and pray God that we may be counted among their number: not among those who fixed Christ to the Cross, but among those in whom he is crucified through his Holy Spirit. May he grant us this grace, that amid so many false christs and counterfeits we may learn the true Jesus Christ, who may be impressed more and more on our minds, whose open and unpainted beauty we may gaze upon, and whose sole true and inexpressible glory we may seek and find, to which he calls us daily through the holy and pure preaching of his Gospel and the administration of his sacraments.

units.la: Ecquid autem fratres amplius? Sane ut vno Iesu Christo mortuo in Cruce & nudato contentos tentos esse nos oportet, & ab illis pseudochri-stis cavere de quibus egimus, sic etiam tenen-dum est, si nudum eum in membris eius hic in terris reliquerimus, nunquam nos induedos eius diuitiis qui propter nos in Cruce sponte tam miser & abiectus factus est. Ecquando vero se maior occasio Christi in miseris membris induendi, quam nunc obtulit, quum passim tota urbe stipem quaerentes senes, viduas, & miseros orphanos vix reptantes, & mendicantes conspiciamus? Iesus Christus igitur pro foribus nostris vociferatur, Esurio, Sitio, Nudus sum, Nos vero non cum cibabimus? non alimenta praebebimus? non potum ministrabimus? non vestiemus? passim contra in vicis & plateis iacentes frigore sinemus enecari? At si tam immisericordibus, tam ingratis esse nobis contigerit, ecquem tandem non strum felicis ac beatae vocis illius, Venite benedicti Patris mei, possidete regnum paratum vobis ante iacta mundi fundamenta, participem fore speramus? Quis contra feret horrendum illud tonitru, Abite maledicti in ignem aeternum qui paratus est Diabolo & Angelis eius. Serio igitur ista cogitate & mente revoluite: excusatio procul omnis abesto. Dicta enim enim sententia est ab illo summo terrarum Iudice, olim venturo, & ex ea mundum iudicaturo, frustra iudicatis querentibus aut ab eius sententia pronocantibus.
units.tr: What more, then, brothers? Truly, just as we ought to be content with the one Jesus Christ dead and stripped on the Cross, and beware of those false christs of whom we have spoken, so too it must be held that if we leave him naked in his members here on earth, we shall never clothe ourselves with his riches, he who for our sake on the Cross became so wretched and abject of his own accord. And when has there ever been a greater opportunity of clothing Christ in his wretched members than now presents itself, when everywhere throughout the city we see old men, widows and poor orphans, scarcely crawling, begging for alms? Jesus Christ therefore cries out at our doors: "I am hungry, I thirst, I am naked." And we, shall we not feed him? Shall we not give him food? Shall we not give him drink? Shall we not clothe him? Shall we instead let them lie in the streets and alleys and allow them to perish of cold? But if it should happen that we are so merciless and so ungrateful, may we hope to be partakers of that happy and blessed voice, "Come, you blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you before the foundation of the world"? Who, on the other hand, will bear that dreadful thunderclap, "Depart, you cursed, into everlasting fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels"? Consider these things seriously then, and turn them over in your mind: let all excuse be far away. For the sentence has been pronounced by that supreme Judge of the earth, who will come one day and judge the world by it, and it is in vain for you who are judged to complain or appeal from his sentence.

units.la: Caeterum quum de Christo induto & spoliato hic agatur, cogit me materia ista de stupendo & intolerando abusu illo in tegedo se & nudando nonihil dicere, quem inter nos licet monitos tamen aboleri non posse mirum est. Nullum esse credo qui non miseros illos Americanos & similes populos suo calculo damnet, quos passim nudos incedere nemo ne-scit, non modo quod propter quaedam corporis partes minus honestas illud naturali pudori & verecundiae sit contrarium, sed etiam quod videatur aspectus ille cogitationes intuentium ad res inhonestas excitare: & tamen certissimum est infinitas esse vestimentorum species, & mille gestus molles & delicatos hodie inter multos visitatos, qui longe salaciores ac lasciuiores sunt, maioremque vim ad pravas cogitationes movendas quam miserorum Barborum nuditas habent. Et revera multae sunt a quarum aspectu, si quales sunt conspicerentur, ide abhorrerent qui tamen ita comptas admirantur: quod etiam de viris ipsis dictum volo. Non tantum igitur tegenda sunt quae tegenda, sed etiam tegenda ut decet: quum tamen siquod inter prophanos ac lasciuos homines novum vestimenti genus inhonestum & impudicum oriatur, seu in capite adornando, seu coma contorquenda, in collariis, in veltium humeris sublimioribus & velut ad fugam procul capessendam alatis, seu in tumidis instar tympanorum posterioribus partibus, aut in iliufmo di rebus pudendis statim illud ad nos usque perueniat. Quae si non ita frequenter atque alibi conspiciuntur, non tamen sane voluntas in multis abest: quum præsertim puellas, etiam à matribus tam maturè videamus sic erudiri vt in sc oculos omnium pelliciant, vt quum ad maiorem ætatem perucnerint, prius imbutam consuetudinem corrigere nec possint nec cupiant. Et hic quidem abusus in vestimentis committitur. Sin verò de nuditate agamus: fateor manus & faciem nundam & conspicuam sese præbere velut ex necessitate: verùm tamen mediocritatem hac in re castitas & honesta dictare debet, vt ita tum gestus tum oculi componantur, in coetibus præsertim, & sacris potissimum, vt nihil nisi ad ædificationem oculis intuentium obiiciatur. Romę velabantur mulieres, vt hodie Nonnæ, quæ se Iesu Christi sponsas dicunt: & hodie multis in locis, & nominatim apud Turcas, nunquam fœminæ in publico nisi velatæ conspiciuntur. Et sanè quę tam copiosè & diserte de istis præcipit Apostolus 1. Cor. 11. neminem esse puto qui ignoret. Quid verò? annon adhuc detecta guttura? annon ceruices se per byssina collaria conspicuas facientes adhuc aspicimus? annon pleræque mulieres adhuc magis nudare pectora gestiunt? Quot denique species sese nostris oculis offerunt vanitatum, ne graviore vocabulo res istas notem? Quid ego igitur ad hæc cum meis collegis ac symmiltis dicturus sum? Paucis accipite: quandoquidem non divini verbi auctoritas, non à Magistratibus positæ Leges, non ratio, non honestas quicquam apud vos possunt, ad Deum ipsum rebelles tum viros tum mulieres ablego : nominatim autem puellas & mulieres, tum iuniores tum ætate proiectiores ad 3. Esaiæ caput amando. Ibi sententiam & iudicium estis aduersum vos imminens audituræ, nisi mature prouideatis: Deum autem ipse supplex oro vt vobis hanc gratiam largiatur, vt serio de istis cogitetis & mentem meliorem induatis.
units.tr: Moreover, since here we are dealing with Christ clothed and stripped, this subject compels me to say something about that amazing and intolerable abuse, in covering and baring oneself, which is strange to see persist among us even though we have been warned. I believe there is no one who does not condemn those wretched Americans and similar peoples, whom everyone knows go about naked, not only because that nakedness, with regard to certain less decent parts of the body, is contrary to natural modesty and shame, but also because that sight seems to stir the thoughts of onlookers towards dishonourable things. And yet it is quite certain that there are endless kinds of clothing, and a thousand soft and delicate gestures among many people today, which are far more lascivious and wanton, and have a greater power to stir up wicked thoughts, than the nakedness of wretched barbarians. And indeed there are many women at whose appearance, if they were seen as they really are, those who now admire them so adorned would shudder; and I want the same said of men themselves. Therefore not only must what ought to be covered be covered, but it must also be covered as is fitting. Yet if among profane and wanton people some new, indecent and immodest style of dress arises, whether in adorning the head, in curling the hair, in collars, in sleeves raised high on the shoulders and, as it were, winged for flight, or in puffed-out shapes like drums at the back, or in such things as concern the private parts, that fashion immediately reaches us. If these things are not seen as often here as elsewhere, nevertheless the will is by no means absent in many, especially since we see girls trained by their mothers so early that they draw the eyes of all to themselves, so that when they reach a riper age they can neither correct the habit they have been steeped in from childhood nor wish to. And this abuse is committed in clothing. But if we speak of nakedness: I confess that the hands and face present themselves bare and visible, as if of necessity; yet modesty and honesty ought to dictate moderation in this matter, so that both gesture and eyes are composed, especially in assemblies and above all in sacred ones, so that nothing is offered to the eyes of onlookers except what builds up. At Rome women used to veil themselves, as nuns do today, who call themselves the brides of Jesus Christ; and today in many places, and notably among the Turks, women are never seen in public except veiled. And indeed I think there is no one who does not know what the Apostle prescribes so fully and clearly about these things, 1 Cor. 11. But what then? Do we not still see throats uncovered? Do we not still see necks made conspicuous by linen collars? Do not most women still eagerly bare their breasts even more? Finally, how many kinds of vanities present themselves to our eyes, not to name these things by a harsher word? What then am I going to say to these things, together with my colleagues and fellow ministers? Hear it briefly: since neither the authority of the divine Word, nor the laws set down by the magistrates, nor reason, nor decency can prevail with you, I send both men and women who are rebels against God himself, and especially the girls and women, both younger and more advanced in years, to the third chapter of Isaiah. There you will hear the sentence and judgment hanging over you, unless you take timely care. I myself pray God humbly that he may grant you this grace, that you think seriously about these things and put on a better mind.

units.la: Porrò, narratione executionis iniquissimæ aduersus Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum latæ sententiæ, cum omnibus ipsius circumstantiis sequitur iam eorum historia quæ illo in Cruce pendente contigerunt, quæ sex horarum spatium, vt suo loco diximus, continet, ita tamen vt in hoc spatio comprehendatur tempus elapsum in ipso crucifigendo & duobus illis cum ipso latronibus, ab hora diei tertia iam elapsa, quæ nobis hodie nona est, Matt. 15. 25. vsque ad horam circiter nonam Matth. 27. 46. & Marc. 15 34. quæ nobis tertia est pomeridiana. Diuus igitur Iohannes primum historiam quandam magnæ doctrinæ & consolationis plenam a tribus aliis Euangelistis omissam recesset, quibus sermo habitus a Iesu Christo ad Sanctam Virginem & dilectum eius discipulum continetur.
units.tr: Next, after the account of the most unjust execution of our Lord Jesus Christ and all its circumstances, comes the story of what happened while he hung on the Cross. As I said in its place, this covers a span of six hours, though the span includes the time spent in the actual crucifying and with the two thieves beside him. It runs from the third hour of the day, which for us is now the ninth (Matt. 15:25), until about the ninth hour (Matt. 27:46; Mark 15:34), which for us is three in the afternoon. Saint John first records a particular story, full of great teaching and comfort, which the other three Evangelists omit. It contains the words Jesus spoke to the holy Virgin and to his beloved disciple.

units.la: Hic autem est primo loco obseruandum Christum ad Crucem pro nobis properantem consolationem nullam a quoquam mortalium accepisse, quem vnus ex discipulis prodiderat, alter vero, sequutus quidem erat eminus, sed tandem ter abnegauerat: tertius vero maiore iore constantia & animo sequutus vsque ad Crucem, & ad mortem vsque comitatus, siluerat tamen: aliis nouem fuga sibi salute quaesita. Fœminæ verò illum à Galilæa sequutæ satis habuerant hæc eminus contemplari, vt scribunt expressè Matth. 27. verf. 55. Marc. 15. verf. 40. Luc. 23. verf. 49. cæteris turbis eum ad crucem abeuntem lugentibus & plangentibus, sed humana tantùm facilitate & misericordia, prorsus alioqui mutis. Quæ verò tres hic fœminæ nominantur, nempe sancta Virgo cum sorore, & Maria Magdalene ex qua septem dæmonia eiecerat, Luc.8. verf.2. (quam oportet etiam distingui tam à Maria Lazari & Marthæ sorore, quàm ab illa peccatrice, cuius meminit Luc.7. v.37. aduersus communem eorum errorem qui de tribus vnam tantùm fecerunt) propius quidem ad Crucem accesserunt, sed altum silentium egerunt. Horum autem omnium causa est, quòd ad diuinam prouidentiam attinet, quòd cum oporteret qui solus exsoluebat quæ mercueramus, nimirum à Dei facie rerumque omnium creaturarum reiici & depelli, in has etiam angustias coniici, vt nominatim erat à Dauide prædictum. Psal. 69 21.
units.tr: Here we must first observe that Christ, hastening to the Cross for us, received no consolation from any mortal. One disciple had betrayed him; another had followed at a distance but had three times denied him; a third, with greater courage and spirit, had followed as far as the Cross and had accompanied him even to death, yet he too had kept silent; the other eleven had fled to save themselves. The women who had followed him from Galilee were content to look on from a distance, as Matthew 27:55, Mark 15:40 and Luke 23:49 expressly write. The crowds that followed him to the Cross wept and lamented, but out of mere human pity, and were otherwise altogether silent. As for the three women named here, namely the holy Virgin with her sister, and Mary Magdalene, from whom Jesus had cast out seven demons (Luke 8:2), who must be distinguished both from Mary the sister of Lazarus and Martha, and from that sinful woman mentioned in Luke 7:37 (against the common error of those who make one of three), they drew closer to the Cross but kept a deep silence. The cause of all this, so far as divine providence is concerned, is that he who alone was to pay what we had earned had to be cast out and driven away from the face of God and of all creatures, and so be brought into this distress, as David had foretold by name (Ps. 69:21).

units.la: Fatendum tamen dilecti discipuli & sanctæ Virginis, duarumque aliarum mulierum fidei & constantiæ suam laudem merito deberi, quod non sint nimio metu imminentis sibi a leonibus illis periculi perterriti: quos eo deduxit diuina prouidetia & animum dedit, vt fidis illis Virginis, oculatis testibus, haec omnia fideliter nobis gesta recitarentur & monumentis coscripta traderentur: sic etiam bene consulente Domino eximmensa sua misericordia fidei infirmitati tum harum mulierum, quas primas suae resurrectionis praeconcs destinabat, tum reliquorum qui diffugerant discipulorum, ut pro fuga in Galilaeam aut longius, reditum in urbem & mutuam coniunctionem meditarentur.
units.tr: Yet we must admit that the faith and constancy of the beloved disciple, of the holy Virgin, and of the two other women deserve their due praise, in that they were not terrified by excessive fear of the danger threatening them from those lions. Divine providence led them there and gave them the courage that the faithful eyewitnesses, the Virgin among them, might faithfully relate to us all that was done and hand it down in written records. So too, with the Lord graciously providing, his immeasurable mercy addressed the weakness of faith both of these women, whom he was destining as the first heralds of his resurrection, and of the remaining disciples who had scattered, so that instead of fleeing into Galilee or farther away, they might think of returning to the city and of rejoining one another.

units.la: Quod si Crucis scandalum & tam imminens ab hostibus periculo tam infirmas adhuc personas iltas a sequendo Christo etiam ad Crucem vsque non deterruerunt, quantus erit pudor si Crucis ignominia resilire nos ab eo faciat, quem scimus supra coelos omnes cuectu, Maiestate & gloria inenarrabili plenum, coronam gloriae tandem iis redditurum qui Crucem suam ferentes ad metam vsque fuerint illum sequuti?
units.tr: If the scandal of the Cross and so imminent a danger from enemies did not deter those still weak persons from following Christ even to the Cross, how great will our shame be if the disgrace of the Cross makes us shrink back from him, whom we know to be above the heavens, full of unspeakable kindness, majesty and glory, and who will at last give the crown of glory to those who, bearing their own cross, have followed him to the goal?

units.la: Verum hoc loco nobis est accurate notanda impudentia summorum illorum idoli illiusveneratorum, quod Dominam Miseratio nis dicunt, quorum tanta caecitas est, ut occinentes cantiunculam illam no minus ineptam quam barbaram, Stabat mater dolorosa, pulchre se illam venerari putent, in qua tame eos non pudet Sanctam Virginem, verbis etiam consonante Musica, non tam dolentem ac gemen tem, quam veluti desperatam mulierem vlantem introducere. Absit autem dicam Sanctam Virginem ἀναίσθητον fuisse, & humanis afeaffectibus & laudabilibus caruisse,& in primis materna charitate, & sancta illa commiseratione, quae maxime Christianos decet: quum praesertim hoc vltimo actu fit adimpletum quod erat illi a Simeone praedictum: Luc.2.35. Verumtamen praeterquam quod tot sermonibus & factis aliis quae viuente Filio diligenter in corde seruauerat, Luc.2.19.& 51. edocta fe in hac probatione continuit,haec historia manifeste docet Sanctam Virginem Sancto Spiritu plenam ita vehementiorum passionum aestum temperaffe & fuperaffe, vt ipsam cum sociis in Ecclesia Dei perpetuum & singulare exemplum esse omnis sanctae constantiae & verae Christianae magnimitatis & fortitudinis oporteat.
units.tr: But here we must carefully note the shamelessness of those great idolaters and worshippers of the idol whom they call Our Lady of Mercy. Their blindness is so great that, singing that little hymn, as foolish as it is barbarous, "Stabat mater dolorosa," they think they honour her beautifully. In it, however, they are not ashamed to introduce the holy Virgin, with the music matching the words, not as grieving and sighing but as a woman screaming as if in despair. Far be it from me to say that the holy Virgin was insensible [ἀναίσθητον] and lacked human feelings and praiseworthy affections, above all maternal love and that holy compassion which most befits Christians, especially since in this final act was fulfilled what Simeon had foretold her (Luke 2:35). Yet, apart from the fact that, having kept in her heart with care so many words and deeds of her Son while he lived (Luke 2:19, 51), she showed in this trial the self-control of one taught by them, this story plainly teaches that the holy Virgin, full of the Holy Spirit, so tempered and overcame the heat of very violent passions that she, together with her companions, must be a lasting and singular example in the Church of God of all holy constancy, true Christian greatness of mind and fortitude.

units.la: Cuius sane memoriam & sanctorum omnium sic decet vsurpare,qui hanc viam fequuti sunt, vera imitatione virtutum quibus praediti fuerunt ex mera Dei gratia & fauore: non autem in idola transformare, & eius spoliis eos inducere quem dum viuerent tam sincere coluerunt, & cum quo spiritus eorum in coelis beatissima felicitate perfruuntur.
units.tr: Surely the memory of her and of all the saints who have followed this way should be honoured in this manner: by true imitation of the virtues with which they were endowed from the pure grace and favour of God. We should not turn them into idols, nor lead them to the spoils of him whom, while they lived, they worshipped so sincerely, and with whom their spirits now enjoy the most blessed happiness in heaven.

units.la: Hic igitur nobis cura quam de matre sua Iesus Christus in istis angustiis habuit ab Euangelista describitur. Porro magni illi Doctores contemplatiui, quibus non fuit religioni sacrosanctas has historias suis somniis & nugis impuriffimis polluere, quum existimarent absurdum esse Iesum Christum matris suae non meminisse, nisi in istis angustiis, mille fabulas
units.tr: Here, then, the care which Jesus Christ showed for his mother in these distresses is described by the Evangelist. Those great contemplative teachers, who did not think it wrong to pollute these most sacred histories with their dreams and most impure trifles, thought it absurd that Jesus Christ should remember his mother only in these distresses, and so they invented a thousand fables,

units.la: cotien-
units.tr: as many

units.la: prorsus ridiculas confinxerunt, quas praestat perpetuo silentio tegere quam recitare. Sed longe maior admirationis occasio sese videtur offerre considerantibus potius quomodo & cur in tota historia Euangelica, a Iesu Christi nativitate ad eius mortem, nulla fiat matris Iesu Christi nisi duobus aliis locis mentio, ex quibus tamen, si verba tantum considerentur, illa ipse non magni fecisse colligi posse videatur. In Actis autem Apostolorum sanctae Virginis mentio tantum uno loco, & quidem obiter fit, Act. 1.14. Itaque sciendum est ab Euangelistis, ut diserte nos Sanctus Iohannes Euangelista monet, Iohan. 20.31. & 21.25. non esse conscriptos libros ut sigillatim in iis annotarentur omnia Iesu Christi dicta vel facta, licet in iis superfluum, nihil futurum fuerit, sed hoc ipsis tantum fuisse propositum ut Prophetarum impletionem nos docerent: quaeque sunt ad salutem tum de Christi persona, tum de ipsius officio cognitu necessaria. Qua in re quu Spiritus Sanctus eos rexerit, atque adeo quae nobis erant ad salutem cognitu necessaria dictaverit, quantae obsecro & quam prophanae plenum est audaciae sanctae huic veritati commenta hominum admiscere? Et hoc tamen Satan statim ab ipsius Ecclesiae incunabulis est molitus, publicatis ab initio Ecclesiae multis historiis fabulosis, quae statim totius Ecclesiae calculo notatae sunt & condemnatae. Quantus igitur pudor est hominibus nostri seculi rursum illas nobis in Lucem revocatas obtrudere &c. re & memoriam refricare, quarum quæ supersunt veluti fragmenta potius oporteret reiicere & prorsus abolere?
units.tr: utterly ridiculous, which it is better to hide in perpetual silence than to recite. But a far greater cause for wonder seems to present itself to those who consider rather how and why, in the whole Gospel story from the birth of Jesus Christ to his death, mention is made of Jesus Christ's mother in only two other places, from which, if the words alone are considered, it might seem that he did not think much of her. In the Acts of the Apostles, mention of the holy Virgin is made in only one place, and that in passing (Acts 1:14). So we must know, as Saint John the Evangelist expressly reminds us (John 20:31; 21:25), that the Evangelists' books were not written so that every word or deed of Jesus Christ should be recorded one by one, although nothing superfluous would have been in them. Their purpose was only this: to teach us the fulfilment of the Prophets, and what is necessary for salvation to know, both about the person of Christ and about his office. Since the Holy Spirit guided them in this, and so dictated what was necessary for us to know for our salvation, how great, I beg you, and how profane a boldness it is to mix the inventions of men with this holy truth! Yet Satan attempted this at once, from the very cradle of the Church, when many fabulous stories were published from the beginning of the Church, which were immediately marked and condemned by the judgement of the whole Church. What shame, then, is it for men of our age to thrust upon us, and to revive and rub up, those stories that have been called back into the light, of which the surviving remnants ought rather to be rejected and utterly abolished?

units.la: Nihilominus tamen extra omne dubium est, eum qui semper omnem iustitiam implevit, adeò vt à iuuentute non tàtum matri subiiceretur, sed etiam Iosepho, licet minimè patri ipsius, vt etiam faber vocitaretur, Marc.6.3. perfectissimè toto vitæ suæ curriculo Legis quintum præceptum adimplesse vt reliqua omnia: sed quum aduenisset tempus mundo se patefaciendi, & sibi commissum à Patre munus exequendi, quæcunque vitam humanam spectant parui fecisse.
