Et hoc ipsum maturè pa- reutes anno ætatis duodecimo docuit, ne mirum ipsis videretur & insolens si quum muneris sui executionem aggrederetur perinde se gereret ac si sine matre & consanguineis foret: quod ipsum expressius etiam reipsa declarauit, quum occupato ipsi in docendo nuntiatum esset matrem & fratres eius colloquium eius quærere, respondit, Quæ est mater mea, & qui sunt fratres mei. Quisquis enim fecerit quod vult Pater meus qui est in cœlis, is est meus frater, & soror & mater. Quod à tribus Euangelistis summo consensu conscriptum est. Matth.12.48. Marc.3.32. & Luc.8.21. Eadem ratione quum sancta Virgo, quam ad hoc sola humana miseratio commouebat, minimè per se alioqui reprehendenda, vellet eum inducere vt vino in nuptiis illis deficiēti prouideret, quod non nisi extraordinario & inusitato aliquo modo posse ab ipso fieri satis iudicabat, ipse contra docturus eam a se non fieri miracula ad homines vino satiandos, & suae vocationis terminos ipsam egressam, humanā cogitationem cum divina & spirituali miscetem, ad cuius executione nullis hominum cōsiliis ac monitionibus opus haberet, nec a quo tem pore suam diuinitatem miraculis patefaceret, Mulier, inquit, Quid mihi tecum? Dura iane vox, sed in qua tamen nemo sine blasphemia dixerit illum modum excessisse.
units.tr: Nevertheless, it is beyond all doubt that he who always fulfilled all righteousness, so that from his youth he was subject not only to his mother but also to Joseph, though certainly not his father, so that he was even called a carpenter (Mark 6:3), kept the fifth commandment of the Law most perfectly throughout the whole course of his life, as he did all the rest. But when the time came for him to reveal himself to the world and to carry out the task committed to him by the Father, he set little store by all that pertains to human life. He taught his parents this early, in his twelfth year, so that it would not seem strange or unusual to them if, when he undertook the execution of his office, he conducted himself as if he were without mother and kinsfolk. He declared this even more plainly in fact when, while he was busy teaching, it was announced to him that his mother and brothers were seeking an interview with him, and he replied: "Who is my mother, and who are my brothers? For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother" (Matt. 12:48; Mark 3:32; Luke 8:21). All three Evangelists have written this with complete agreement. For the same reason, when the holy Virgin, moved by human pity alone, which in itself is not to be blamed, wished to bring him to provide wine at that wedding, which had run short, judging that this could be done by him only in some extraordinary and unusual way, he in turn was about to teach her that he would not perform miracles to satisfy men with wine, and that she had gone beyond the bounds of his calling, mixing human thought with the divine and spiritual, for the execution of which he needed no counsel or prompting of men, nor did he yet reveal his divinity by miracles. "Woman," he said, "what have I to do with you?" It is a harsh word, yet no one could say without blasphemy that he exceeded the proper measure in speaking it.

units.la: Contrà vero discimus ex hoc exemplo quis sit modus adhibendus in charitate & officiis quae ex Legis praescripto proximo debetur, ut nimirum quae Deo debemus ex nostra vocatione, publica vel privata, omnibus aliis rebus sine exceptione praeferantur, adeo quidem ut si proximis obsequia praestare nō possumus, quin ab officio nostro erga Deū tātillū recedamus, neminē mortaliū agnoscamus: multoq; magis quum praestari nequeunt officia proximis quin Dei voluntati, seu in solidū, seu quibusdā in cir cunstantiis, reluctemur, tunc tori mundo potius renūtiemus, vt Dominus ipse nobis exemplo ipse suo praeit & praecipit etiam Matth. 10.37. Marc. 10.29. & ipsi Apostoli. Act. 4.19. Et hanc ob eausam tribus Leui laudatur a Domino, & Sacerdotij honore decoratur, quum Domini praeceptum impleuissent nemini nec fratri nec amico parcerent. Exod. 32. v. 28. & 29. Deut. 33. verf. 8. & 9. Idcirco etiam Dominus rogatus à quodam vt liceret ad patrem abire cum sepelire, non permisit. Matth. 8. ver. 21. Ea cur Apostolus, iubeat nos sic mundo vti quasi non vtentes 1. Cor. 7. 31. Quae sane doctrina necessaria est omnibus, Christianis quos oportet ante omnia Dei regnum quaerere: sed nominatim iis quibus onus incumbit aliis verbi diuini & regni coelorum praedicandi, viamque ad illud suo exemplo commonstrandi.
units.tr: On the other hand, we learn from this example what measure ought to be observed in the love and duties owed to our neighbour under the Law's prescription. Obviously, whatever we owe God by reason of our calling, whether public or private, must be placed before all other matters without exception. So much so that if we cannot render services to our neighbours without departing from our duty to God even slightly, we should acknowledge no mortal at all. Much more so when duties cannot be performed for our neighbours without resisting the will of God, whether entirely or in certain circumstances. Then we should rather renounce the whole world, as the Lord himself goes before us with his own example and also commands it (Matt. 10:37; Mark 10:29), as did the Apostles themselves (Acts 4:19). For this reason the tribe of Levi is praised by the Lord and honoured with the dignity of the priesthood, because, having fulfilled the command of the Lord, they spared neither brother nor friend (Exod. 32:28–29; Deut. 33:8–9). Accordingly, too, when a certain man asked the Lord for permission to go away and bury his father, he did not allow it (Matt. 8:21). Why does the Apostle bid us use the world as not using it (1 Cor. 7:31)? This doctrine is certainly necessary for all Christians, who ought above all to seek the kingdom of God, but especially for those on whom the burden falls of preaching the divine Word and the kingdom of heaven to others, and of showing by their example the way to it.

units.la: Haec est igitur una ex causis quibus impulsus Dominus ita se erga matrem gesserit, ita tamen vt nullum officij genus filij erga matrem secundum carnem praetermiserit. Sed proterea certum est Dominum praevidentem magnos abusus, seu potius abominandam superstitionem in Ecclesiam olim excitandam, sub praetextu colendae memoriae sanctae Virginis, Dei filij matris secundum carne, & tanto malo cupientem aliam praecidere, voluisse illam in hac tota Euangelica historia veluti silentio quodam tegi, exceptis iis quae mysterium incarnationis & Filij Dei conceptionem spectant, de quibus nunquam satis eruditi possumus, quae sic nobis revelantur, vt de reliquis nihil amplius curiose sit inquirendum. Quam est igitur deplorandum istis homines non contentos: nihil Deo proprium reliquisse, nullumque honorem Christo debitum, qui non Mariae Virgini tribuatur: nullum titulum Iesu Christo proprie conuenientem, quo mater eius non sit exornata. Vocatur enim ille Dominus noster, haec vero Domina nostra. Rex Coeli dicitur: ipsa vero Regina Coeli. Magni illi Romani Catholici hodierni vocant eam spem suam, vitam, mundi salutem. Ecquid amplius? Iure matris natum vt iubeat orari: sunt enim ipsissima idololatrarum verba. Omitto in praesentia zonam eius, vestem, crepidam: tam fabulas et commentitias fabulas, quam illa de lacte ipsius, cuius tanta quantitas ostentatur et adoratur, si in vnum cogeretur, vt maioribus doliis implendis sufficiat. Omitto etiam fabulam mortis ipsius, et Assumptionis, de qua veteres, quum huius idololatriae fundamenta iacerentur dubitanter admodum loquuti sunt. Euaserunt tamen illa tandem articulus fidei, et quidem tantae dignitatis, vt nulla sit magis detestanda haeresis, si bonis iustis doctoribus fides adhibetur, quam aliquid eorum omnium negare. Deo vero maximas agamus gratias quod nos ex tantis istis erroribus extraxerit, licet agnoscimus sanctissimi huius vasis honorandam esse memoriam, et vitam tantae prophetiae, quantam ex ipsius cantico fuisse cognoscimus. At colendae eius memoriae ratio est in virtutum ipsius imitatione posita: quum certissimum sit eam si hodie in terris degeret, non tantum non approbaturam se Filij spoliis indui, sed etiam tam superstitiosis famulis dicturam quod olim illis dixerat nuptiarum famulis. Ioh. 2. 5. et quidem facturam quod ipsos Apostolos fecisse legimus Act. 14. 14.
units.tr: This, then, is one of the reasons why the Lord, moved by these considerations, behaved toward his mother as he did, yet in such a way that he omitted no kind of duty a son owes to his mother according to the flesh. But it is certain that the Lord, foreseeing great abuses, or rather the abominable superstition that would one day be raised up in the Church under the pretext of honouring the memory of the holy Virgin, the mother according to the flesh of the Son of God, and wishing to cut off so great an evil, wished that she be covered, as it were, with a kind of silence throughout this whole evangelical history. The exceptions are those things which concern the mystery of the incarnation and the conception of the Son of God, about which we can never be sufficiently instructed, since these are so revealed to us that nothing further about the rest need be inquisitively sought. How deplorable it is, then, that these men, not content with this, have left nothing proper to God and no honour due to Christ that is not transferred to the Virgin Mary, and no title properly belonging to Jesus Christ with which his mother is not adorned! For he is called our Lord, but she is called our Lady. He is called King of Heaven, but she is called Queen of Heaven. Those great modern Roman Catholics call her their hope, their life, the salvation of the world. What more? They bid her, as a mother, to command her Son to be prayed to. These are indeed the very words of idolaters. I set aside for the moment her girdle, her garment, her sandal, as fables and invented tales, as well as those stories about her milk, of which such a great quantity is displayed and adored that, if it were gathered into one place, it would suffice to fill larger casks. I also set aside the fable of her death and Assumption, about which the ancients, when the foundations of this idolatry were being laid, spoke very hesitantly. Yet these things have at last turned into articles of faith, and indeed of such dignity that no heresy is more to be detested, if credit is given to good and upright teachers, than to deny any of them. But to God let us give the greatest thanks that he has drawn us out of such great errors. We acknowledge that the memory of this most holy vessel is to be honoured, and her life of such prophecy as we know from her canticle. But the right way of honouring her memory lies in imitating her virtues, since it is most certain that if she were living on earth today, she would not only not approve of being clothed in the Son's spoils, but would also say to such superstitious servants what she once said to the servants at the wedding (John 2:5). And indeed she would do what we read the Apostles themselves did (Acts 14:14).

units.la: Igitur vt ad historiam reuertamur, Dominus eam hoc loco nec proprio, nec Matris nomine compellat, sed tantum Mulierem vocat, non eam
units.tr: So then, to return to the history: the Lord here addresses her neither by the name of proper name nor of Mother, but only calls her Woman, not her

units.la: Cur Iesus Christus Sanctam cam sane dedignatus, vt testis est idoneus cura quam de illa in his angustiis gerit: sed vt iam tunc palam faceret, se quum gloriae suae proximus esset, non amplius secundum carnem cognoscendum, vt loquitur Apostolus, id est eorum respectu quae hanc terrenam & animalem vitam spectant, vt de vita nostra in coelis futura Christus loquitur, Matth.22.30. Ex quo satis aperte condemnantur qui somniant gradus illos Matris & Filij in coelis permanere inter Iesum Christum & matrem eius non aliter quam quum in terris versarentur.
units.tr: Not that Jesus Christ scorned her indeed, as the care he shows for her in these straits is a sufficient witness. Rather, he wished to show then and there that, being now close to his glory, he was no longer to be known according to the flesh, as the Apostle says (2 Cor. 5:16), that is, with respect to those things which pertain to this earthly and natural life, just as Christ speaks of our life to come in heaven (Matt. 22:30). From this it is quite clearly condemned those who dream that the degrees of mother and son remain in heaven between Jesus Christ and his mother, just as they did while they lived on earth.

units.la: Caeterum Iesus Christus hic nobis perfectissimum exemplum praebet quod imitemur in obseruatione quinti praecepti, quum in tantis & inauditis angustiis & agone mortis matris tamen sollicitudinem non abiecit, sed etiam in posterum illi cauit, substituto velut in locum suum dilecto discipulo, qui curam eius haberet: quod ipsum sane homines ipsa natura doceret, nisi tantopere corrupta & depravata esset in maxima terrarum orbis parte, quae detestanda monstra fouet, indigna tamen quae hac Luce fruantur, aut quae terra ferat amplius. Atque vtinam ne in medio nostrum quidam reperiantur quibus Parentum vita longior est. Neque vero tantum hic ago de horrendo illo contra naturam contemptu liberorum erga Parentes: sed de dissidiis inter familias quarum paucissimas inter se cohaerere conspicimus: mutuis contra odiis & inimicitiis grassantibus etiam inter proximos consanguineos, quasi omnes à Caino, non autem à Setho aut Noacho traheremus originem: horrendum profecto testimonium iræ Dei in vniuersum genus humanum, vt id declarat Apostolus, Rom. 11.18. An verò frustrà distinctas cognationes & familias arbitramur? & cognationum gradus constitutos? Immò verò si qui hominem videt, carnem & ossa sua videt, vt voluit ipse Dominus omnes ab vno Parente originem trahere, quid fiet quum ad hæc vinculum etiam consanguinitatis accessit? Quid vetere illo trito proverbio, Verum sanguinem mentiri non posse? Fateor spiritualem cognationem, cuius Christus est vinculum inter domesticos fidei, esse omnium inter homines obligationum arctissimam, Gal. 6. 10. sed quæ tamen naturalem dilectionem non aboleat, quam contrà regit & stabilit vti superius diximus, & cuius vsum nobis hoc loco Christus ostendit. At si naturalis huius affectionis priuatio reddit homines Hominum nomine indignos, quo iure se Christianos venditabunt quos esse tam ἀ-στόργους non pudet? Et quinam in Dei filiorum numero censerentur, qui ne in rebus quidem creatis numerari merentur? Et tamen quàm multi sunt, horret animus, sed cogor tamen non sine ingenti dolore dicere, quàm multi sunt, inquam, istiusmodi homines pauperum proximorum consanguineorum contemptores, quos etiam agnoscere dedignantur, quum tamen quintum Legis præceptum non tantùm de ascendentium ac descendentium, sed etiam
units.tr: Moreover, Jesus Christ here gives us a most perfect example to imitate in keeping the fifth commandment. In such great and unheard-of distress, and in the agony of death, he did not cast off his care for his mother, but also provided for her in the future, having put in his place, as it were, his beloved disciple to take charge of her. Nature itself would teach men this, were it not so greatly corrupted and depraved in the largest part of the world, which cherishes detestable monsters, unworthy indeed to enjoy this light, or which the earth bears any longer. And would that there were not some among us to whom their parents' life is too long! Nor am I speaking here only of that horrible contempt of children toward their parents, which is against nature, but of the quarrels between families, of which we see very few living in harmony with one another. Instead, mutual hatreds and enmities rage even among close relatives, as though we all derived our origin from Cain and not from Seth or Noah. This is surely a dreadful testimony of the wrath of God upon the whole human race, as the Apostle declares (Rom. 11:18). Do we suppose that the distinct kindreds and families and the degrees of kinship were established in vain? Indeed, if one looks upon a man, he sees his own flesh and bones, since the Lord himself willed that all should trace their origin from one parent. What, then, will happen when the bond of blood relationship is added to this? What of that old and worn proverb, that blood cannot lie? I grant that spiritual kinship, of which Christ is the bond among the household of faith, is the closest of all obligations among men (Gal. 6:10). Yet it does not abolish natural affection, which rather it governs and establishes, as we said above, and whose use Christ shows us in this place. But if the lack of this natural affection makes men unworthy of the name of men, by what right will those who are not ashamed to be so without natural affection [ἀ-στόργους] pass themselves off as Christians? And who would be counted among the number of God's children, when they do not deserve to be counted even among created things? Yet how many there are, my mind shudders to say, but I am compelled to say with great grief, how many there are, I say, of such men who despise their poor kinsfolk, whom they even refuse to acknowledge, though the fifth commandment speaks not only of ascendants and descendants but also of

units.la: de Collateralium gradibus loquatur? Quid autem amplius? Parum est dum vita fuit superstes cos neglexisse, sed quum Dominus coram tribunali suo rationem vitae reddituros evocat, quis ignorat quae Testamenta fiant, quibusque artibus multi alienas hereditates involent, quae deveniunt ad proximos agnatos, iure naturae, quo nullum melius, quodque violare sine magnis & necessariis de causis religioni ducere debemus: abominandum sane facinus, abominandum, inquam, quod coram Deo nullae Leges, nulla consuetudo, nulla Iudicum sententia sit unquam excusatura. Et revera Dominus ipse suo exemplo contrarium nos docet, qui licet in terris adeo miser ut non haberet ubi caput reclinaret, Matri tamen tunc ut potuit consuluerit, ac velut in manus dilecti discipuli illam depositerit. Praeterea docuit Honoris nomen quod Parentibus debetur non in externo tantum verborum aut gestuum honore positum, (quod tamen etiam honoris pars est aliqua) sed in cura & sollicitudine qua inveniuntur Parentes & facultatibus & personis etiam suorum liberorum immo vita ipsa, si necessitas postulauerit: quod si praestitum erit, minime tamen adhuc gloriari possint se Parentibus par pari retulisse. Sin aliquis excipiat non defuisse Christo alias rationes longe maiores & honoratiores quascunque nimirum vellet quibus matri prouideret, aio sciuisse ipsum eam non quaesituram huius mundi terrena magis a Filij morte: quam dum in terris viveret: & hac in re pulchrè sanè inter eos conuenie-bat. Denique Dominus hac in re, vt in cæteris omnibus vitæ Christianæ perfectionem nobis ostensurus, nec naturæ iura soluit, vt Monachalis vita, in qua tamen summa vitæ perfectio salsissimo nixa fundamento ponitur, nec imitatus est perditos illos non sanè ἐκκλησίας Ecclesiæ sed potius λῃστὰς, & nominatim sedis Romanæ monstra illa, partim pauperum bona abligurientes, partim illis ad summos gradus suis consanguineis quærendos abutentes, conscìis & spectantibus illud ipsis scorti istius procis, tali Domina dignissimis mancipiis.
units.tr: of the degrees of collateral kin? And what more? It is too little that they neglected them while life remained, but when the Lord calls men before his tribunal to render an account of their lives, who does not know what wills are made, and by what arts many seize other people's inheritances, which by the law of nature pass to the nearest agnates, a law than which none is better, and which we ought to regard as sacred to violate except for grave and necessary reasons? It is truly an abominable crime, abominable, I say, which no laws, no custom, no sentence of judges will ever excuse before God. And indeed the Lord himself teaches us the opposite by his own example. Although on earth he was so wretched that he had nowhere to lay his head, yet he provided for his mother as well as he could then, and committed her, as it were, into the hands of his beloved disciple. Moreover, he taught that the honour owed to parents does not lie only in outward honour of words or gestures, though that too is a part of honour, but in the care and concern by which parents are supported, both with goods and with personal service, and even with the lives of their children themselves, if necessity should demand it. Even if this is rendered, they still can by no means boast that they have repaid parents in equal measure. But if someone objects that Christ lacked other, far greater and more honourable means by which he might have provided for his mother, whatever means he might wish, I answer that he knew she would not seek the earthly things of this world from her Son's death more than while she lived on earth, and in this matter they agreed very well together. Finally, the Lord, in this as in all other matters, wishing to show us the perfection of the Christian life, neither dissolved the rights of nature, as monastic life does, in which nevertheless the highest perfection of life is placed on a most unsavoury foundation, nor did he imitate those lost men, not indeed churchmen [ἐκκλησίας] but rather robbers [λῃστὰς], and especially those monsters of the Roman see, who partly devour the goods of the poor, partly abuse them to seek high offices for their relatives, with the knowledge and approval of those courtiers of that harlot, most worthy servants of such a mistress.

units.la: In dilecto autem discipulo, pulcherrimum nobis proponitur verae amicitiae exemplum, iis longè dissimili qui nostro seculo non recusant hæreditates aut legata adire lucrosa, sed onerosa officia, vt tutelam aut tale aliquod officium refugiunt, mortua cum defuncto amicitia quorum exempla quotidie plurima conspiciuntur, ex quibus satis apparet quales maxima ex parte sint amici mundani. At norint istiusmodi homines magnopere suos liberos periclitari ne in similé aut etiam maius periculum incidant quàm miseri amicorum pupilli quos ita sprecerint: & sanè non procul horum exempla quærenda sunt. Non sic Booz erga Rutham Moabitidem se gessit, suam tantum affinem: quem hoc etiam honore Deus dignatus est vt in maioribus Domini nostri censeatur. D. igitur Iohannes hoc legatum minimè neglexit, sed ex eo tempore matrem Domini apud se, non tantùm hospitio recepit, sed etiam vt matrem coluit & honorauit: nec dubium est quin se fidelissimè ad extremum erga eam gesserit, licet historia non huc vsque progrediatur.
units.tr: In the beloved disciple we are set before a most beautiful example of true friendship, very unlike those in our own age who do not refuse inheritances or profitable legacies, but who flee burdensome duties such as guardianship or some similar office, when friendship dies along with the deceased. Such examples can be seen every day in great number, from which it is sufficiently clear what sort of friends worldly people are for the most part. But such people should know that their own children are greatly in danger of falling into a similar or even greater peril, as the wretched orphans of friends whom they have thus neglected; and indeed such examples are not far to seek. Booz did not behave like this towards Ruth the Moabitess, his own kinswoman; and God honoured him with this distinction, that he is counted among the ancestors of our Lord. John, therefore, by no means neglected this bequest, but from that time took the mother of the Lord into his own home, not only receiving her as a guest but also cherishing and honouring her as his mother; and there is no doubt that he behaved most faithfully towards her to the end, although the history does not proceed so far.

units.la: Sed præter superiora omnia, locus hic docet quod alibi dicuntur discipuli omnia reliquisse vt Christum sequerentur, non sic intelligendum quasi familias prorsus deseruerint, quod tum ex hoc loco manifestum est, tum ex eo vbi post resurrectionem in Galilæam iussi, dicuntur apud se rediisse, etiam ad piscationem. Ioh. 21. 2. Ex verbis igitur illis intelliguntur omnia domestica negotia Domini nostri vocationi postpositusse, sic tamen vt qui familias habebant non prorsus nec simpliciter officio renuntiarint. Fateor tamen deinceps quum in vniversum orbe Euangelium prædicaturi mitterentur, oportuisse illos rebus domesticis aliter prouidere, & semel omnia priuata sua negotia publico muneri postponere. Sed quid habet istud commune cum egregio illo cœlibatus & paupertatis voto, idest voto comedendi viduarum domos longarum precum prætextu, & alienis sumptibus in vniversum orbem terrarum idololatriam & superstitionem serendi? Quinam verò dicentur Apostoli se voto cœlibatus astrinxisse, quum secum vxores suas circumducerent, vt manifestum est ex prioris ad Corinth. cap. 9. v. 5. At tamen si mendicis istis Monachis, flagris potiùs quàm cibis dignissimis fides adhibetur, ipsi soli vitam perfectam & Apostolicam degunt: Sed bene est quòd ipsi Papæ mendacium illis impingunt: & vix agitur quinquagesimus annus ex quo si creditum fuisset doctioribus & insignioribus tunc temporis Cardinalibus, non amplius Christianorum prata tales locustæ tonderent. Sit verò Deus benedictus in omne seculum qui nobis tales Serlatanos ac locustas detexit, quos vtinam, iis exceptis quos sua misericordia dignabitur, vt nostra memoria plurimos, dignatus est ex suo beneplacito, Deus in abyssi puteum cum sui similibus recondat, ex quo prius exiuerant, teste D. Ioanne Apocalyp. 9. 3. & nobis hanc gratiam concedat vt pro talibus nugis sanam doctrinam in hac historia comprehensam amplectamur & ad vsum referamus ad Nominis sui gloriam & nostram salutem.
units.tr: But beyond all that has been said, this passage teaches that when the disciples are said elsewhere to have left everything to follow Christ, this must not be understood as though they utterly abandoned their families. This is clear both from this passage and from that place where, after the resurrection, they were ordered into Galilee and are said to have returned to their own homes, even to fishing (John 21:2). From those words it is understood that they set all their domestic affairs after the calling of our Lord, yet in such a way that those who had families did not altogether or simply renounce their duty. I admit, however, that when they were sent to preach the Gospel throughout the whole world, they had to provide for their domestic affairs in another way, and once for all to place all their private concerns after the public office. But what has that in common with the splendid vow of celibacy and poverty, that is, the vow of eating up widows' houses under the pretext of long prayers, and of spreading idolatry and superstition throughout the whole world at other people's expense? Indeed, how can the Apostles be said to have bound themselves by a vow of celibacy, when they led about their wives with them, as is plain from 1 Corinthians 9:5? Yet if those beggarly monks, deserving of whips rather than food, are believed, they alone live the perfect and apostolic life. But it is well that the Popes themselves impose these lies upon them; and scarcely fifty years have passed since, had the more learned and distinguished cardinals of that time been believed, such locusts would no longer shear the meadows of Christians. Blessed be God for ever, who has disclosed to us such charlatans and locusts; and would that God, with the exception of those whom in his mercy he deigns to save, would shut up in the pit of the abyss with their like, from which they had come forth, as the most of them, as our memory serves, he by his good pleasure has been pleased to do, as the beloved John witnesses in Revelation 9:3; and may he grant us this grace, that for such trifles we may embrace the sound doctrine contained in this history, and apply it to the glory of his name and to our salvation.

units.la: Amen.
units.tr: Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA TRICESIMA.
units.tr: HOMILY THIRTIETH.

units.la: MATTH. 27.
units.tr: MATT. 27.

units.la: 39. Qui vero præteribant conuitiabantur ei, mo-uentes capita sua,
units.tr: 39. But those who passed by reviled him, wagging their heads,

units.la: 40. Et dicentes, Tu qui dissoluis templum, & triduò ædificas, serua temetipsum: si Filius Dei es, descendito è cruce.
units.tr: 40. And saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself: if thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.

units.la: 41. Similiter autem etiam primarij Sacerdotes illudentes cum Scribis & Senioribus, dicebant,
units.tr: 41. Likewise also the chief priests, mocking him with the scribes and elders, said,

units.la: 42. Alios seruauit, seipsum non potest seruare. Si Rex Israel est, descendat nunc è Cruce, & cre-demus ei.
units.tr: 42. He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he is the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.

units.la: 43. Confidit in Deo, eruat ipsum nunc, si placet ei, Dixit enim, Filius Dei sum.
units.tr: 43. He trusted in God; let God deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God.

units.la: 44. Idipsum etiam latrones qui crucifixi erant cum eo exprobrabant ei.
units.tr: 44. The thieves also who were crucified with him reproached him in the same way.

units.la: MARC. 15.
units.tr: MARK 15.

units.la: 29. Qui vero præteribant conuitiabantur, mo-uentes capita sua & dicentes, Vah qui destruis templum & triduo ædificas:
units.tr: 29. And those who passed by reviled him, wagging their heads and saying, Ha! Thou that destroyest the temple and buildest it in three days:

units.la: 30. Serva teipsum, & descende de Cruce.
units.tr: 30. Save thyself, and come down from the cross.

units.la: 31. Similiter autem & principes sacerdotum illudentes ad alios cum Scribis, Aliós seruare non potest.
units.tr: 31. Likewise also the chief priests, mocking him with the scribes, said to one another, He saved others; himself he cannot save.

units.la: 32. Christus ille Rex Israel, descendat nunc à Cruce, ut videamus & credamus. Et qui crucifixi erant cum eo, probris afficiebant eum.
units.tr: 32. Let Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe. And those who were crucified with him also reviled him.

units.la: LVC. 23.
units.tr: LUKE 23.

units.la: 25. Et stabat populus spectans. Sanniis autem excipiebant eum etiam primores cum eis, dicentes, Alios seruauit, seruet seipsum, si hic est ille Christus, ille Dei electus.
units.tr: 25. And the people stood beholding. But the chief men with them scoffed at him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he is that Christ, the chosen of God.

units.la: 36. Illudebant autem etiam ei milites, accedentes, & acetum ei offerentes,
units.tr: 36. The soldiers also mocked him, coming up and offering him vinegar,

units.la: 37. Dicentésque, Si tu es Rex ille Iudæorum, serua temetipsum.
units.tr: 37. And saying, If thou art the King of the Jews, save thyself.

units.la: 39. Vnus autem ex maleficis qui erant suspensi, conuitiabatur ei, dicens, Si tu es Christus ille, serua teipsum & nos.
units.tr: 39. One of the malefactors who were hanged there reviled him, saying, If thou art that Christ, save thyself and us.

units.la: 40. Respondens autem alter obiurgauit eum, dicens, Ne tu quidem Deum times, quum in eadem sis damnatione?
units.tr: 40. But the other, answering, rebuked him, saying, Do you not even fear God, seeing you are under the same condemnation?

units.la: 41. Et nos quidem iustè: (nam digna factis recipimus) iste verò nihil indecens fecit.
units.tr: 41. And we indeed justly, for we receive what our deeds deserve; but this man has done nothing amiss.

units.la: 42. Dixitque Iesu, Domine, memento mei quum veneris in regnum tuum.
units.tr: 42. And he said, Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.

units.la: ACTENVS sese Iesus Christus in passionibus verè plus quàm admirandum præbuit, seu præstitam Patri pro nobis obedientiam, seu immensam & multis effectis tenarrabilem charitatem tam illi donauerat confio- erga eos quos Pater tientiam, & inenarrabi-. seu inuictam patientiam, & in maximis suis angoribus studium indefessum mulieres eas docendi quæ ipsum sequebantur, & lugebant, & pro crucifigentibus precandi, miserum illum latronem seruandi, matri de necessariis prouidendi, quæ singula perfectissima sunt exempla ad quæ vitam nostram singuli componamus. Sed quæ supersunt in hac historia nobis explicanda longe adhuc euidentius eadem illa cófirmant: quum minimè dubium sit quin tot in eum âvenenatis illis linguis contorta conuicia, tot dicteria tot denique contumeliæ: tot taurorum pinguium Basanis mugitus:tot rabidorum canum latratus : tot ferocium leonum rugitus (veluti nobis illa depinguntur speciatim psal.22.vt etiam ipsorum verborum quę vomuerunt quedam exprimantur) longè grauiùs eum quàm alij omnes licet grauissimi cruciatus lancinarint, & ad ossium vsque medullas transfodcrint:quod idem Propheta nobis tanquam Iesu Christi figura testatur, psal. 42. quæ singula Christianos omnes oportet distinctè vt sunt in sacris historiis tradita,considerare. Sed quò melius huius facti horror appareat, hanc circunstantiam diligenter oportet expendi,nempe esse nefas reum licet capitalissimum in Magistratus potestate positum, vel facto vel sermone etiam offendere præter Iudicis sententiam, multóque minus supplicij pœnam aggrauare, quum contrà necessario dicendus sit omnem humanitatis sensum exuisse, qui vel inimicum suum, merito supplicio affectum,
units.tr: Hitherto Jesus Christ has shown himself in his sufferings truly more than admirable: whether in the obedience he rendered to the Father on our behalf, or in his immense charity, which cannot be fully told, towards those whom the Father had given him, or in his unconquered patience. In his greatest anguish he showed a tireless zeal in teaching the women who followed him and mourned, in praying for those who crucified him, in saving that wretched thief, and in providing for his mother's needs. Each of these is a most perfect example to which each of us should conform our life. But what remains of this history for us to explain confirms these same things far more clearly still. For there is no doubt that so many reproaches twisted from those poisonous tongues, so many taunts and finally so many insults, the bellowing of the fat bulls of Bashan, the barking of the rabid dogs, and the roaring of the fierce lions (as these are depicted for us in Psalm 22, so that some of the very words they vomited forth are expressed), wounded him far more grievously than all the other most severe torments, though these pierced him to the marrow of his bones. The same Prophet testifies to this as a figure of Jesus Christ in Psalm 42. All Christians ought to consider each of these things distinctly, as they are handed down in the sacred histories. But so that the horror of this deed may appear more clearly, this circumstance must be carefully weighed: it is wrong, even when the guilty party is the most capital criminal and is placed in the power of the magistrate, to offend him by deed or word beyond the judge's sentence, and much less to aggravate the punishment. On the contrary, one must say that those who would take vengeance, even privately, upon an enemy who has justly been subjected to punishment have cast off all human feeling.

units.la: A a. iiij. etiam priuatim vlciscatur. Hic igitur fuit fce-leratorum istorum furoris cumulus, ex quo magis ac magis innocentia Domini nostri Iesu Chrilti aduersus Crucis scandalum patefit: docemúrque vicissim peccatorum noftrorū magnitudinem intueri, quum nulla fuerit alia nos Deo reconciliandi ratio quàm fuso Filij Dei sanguine: ac proinde immensam & infinitam Patris clementiam, & sponsoris ac vadis nostri charitatem erga suos inimicos suspicere.
units.tr: Here, then, was the culmination of the fury of these wicked men, and from it the innocence of our Lord Jesus Christ is revealed more and more against the scandal of the Cross. We are taught in turn to look upon the greatness of our sins, since there was no other way of reconciling us to God than by the shed blood of the Son of God; and therefore to look up to the immense and infinite clemency of the Father, and to the charity of our surety and pledge towards his enemies.

units.la: Primùm igitur hic fit mentio prætereuntium, qui tum verbis tum gestibus indignißimis quæ ne David quidem ipse Pfal. 22. reti cuit, Duo potissimùm exprobrabant, quorum primum est, vt quum fe iactaffet templum destructorum, triduóque illud instauraturum, seipsum saltem seruaret, & Cruci eriperet: alterum, vt qui fe Dei Filium dixerat, reipfa tc- staretur illud, è Cruce virtute sua diuina de- fcendens: quorum prius illud erat falsitate inexcusabili contortum: alterum vero horrendum huius Nationis cæcitatis argumentum. Primùm enim, minimè dixerat Iesus Christus, Ego destruam hoc templum, sed destruite hoc templum: nec de templo materiali loquutus erat, sed de suo corpore, in quo non figurate, sed corporaliter, idest perfonaliter tota Deitas habitat. Ioh.2. 19. & 21. Sin excipiat aliquis, ad istos irrisores excusandos, non fuisse à Iesu Christo Templi vocem hanc expositam, quum vsus est ea loquendi phrafi, saltem in eo fuisse prorsus inexcusabiles aio, quòd non fit verisimile. simile latuisse ipsos,sic contortum ab ipsis fer-monem & coram Caiapha aduersus Christum agitatum testibus tamen probari non potuif. fc.Mar.14.58.&59 Sed ita solent improbi pu-dore omni abiecto millies etiam refutata sub-inde regerere. Immo & maximum quoduis mendacium semel avulgo receptum semper admittitur, & quasi non adulterina moneta recepitur. Et hoc ipsum in aduersariis nostris quotidie nimium experimur, calumniarum plena volumina inontium instar aduersum nos cum insigni impudentia & fronte perfri-cta scribentibus, quorum infinita possem, fi res ita postularet, exempla in medium adferre. Aduersus haec omnia remedia vnicu est no mi rari fi Spiritus medax cafdem aduersum seruos quas aduersus Magistratu artes versat:nec pro-pterea tame ab incoepto desistere, sed alacriter in opere Domini per gloria & ignominia, per conuitia & laudes pergere. 2. Cor. 6.8. certò scientes calumniam tandem suo loco & tem-pore in fumos abire,veritatem autem in æter-num permanere. Et hoc ipsum profecto hac in parte duplici ratione contigit. Nam isti in-ter calumniandum Icfum Christum, ea ipsa reapse Icfu Christi verba adimplebant,corpus Iesu Christi ab anima separantes, & ita quan-tum in ipsis erat verum Deitatis vti diximus templum destruebant: nec procul aberat ter-tius ille dies quo suscitandum erat illud tem-plum per resurrectionem in sempiterno dura-turum.Preterea pro eo quod his vocibus vtentes significabant nunquam suum templum de-struētum iri, magnæ impietati contrarium dicere tribuentes, ipsimet tamen veluti propriis manibus illud euertebant. Nam contrà suam intentionem ea tamen admittebant quibus Deus prouocatus non longo post tempore merito templum & Sacerdotium aboleuit, vt de scelératis istis meritas poenas sumeret, tum, vt exhibita veritate figuras aboleret. Quæ si non eodem momento quo tantum facinus admissum est contigerunt, immensæ Dei patientiæ scelératos istos adhuc triginta quatuor annos expectanti acceptum ferendum est.
units.tr: First, then, mention is made here of the passers-by, who, with words and gestures most unworthy, which not even David himself passed over (Ps. 22), chiefly cast two reproaches at him. The first was that, since he had boasted that he would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, he should save himself at least and come down from the Cross. The second was that, since he had called himself the Son of God, he should prove it in fact by coming down from the Cross by his divine power. Of these, the first was twisted by an inexcusable falsehood, while the second was a dreadful proof of the blindness of this nation. For Jesus Christ did not say, "I will destroy this temple," but "Destroy this temple"; nor did he speak of a material temple, but of his own body, in which dwells not figuratively but bodily, that is, personally, the whole Deity (John 2:19, 21). If anyone should object, to excuse these mockers, that this word of Jesus Christ about the temple was not explained to them, since he used that manner of speaking, I say that they were utterly inexcusable in this, and it is not likely that they were unaware of it. Their distortion of his words, brought forward before Caiaphas against Christ, could nevertheless not be proved by witnesses (Mark 14:58-59). But such shameless men, with all modesty cast aside, are accustomed to repeat things again and again even after they have been refuted a thousand times. Indeed, the greatest lie, once received among the common people, is always admitted and taken as if it were genuine coin. We experience this every day too much among our adversaries, who, with remarkable impudence and hardened brows, write volumes full of calumnies against us as if they were truths. I could bring forward countless examples of this, if the matter required it. The one remedy against all of these is not to be surprised if the lying spirit employs the same arts against the servants as it does against the Master; yet we should not on that account desist from what we have begun, but cheerfully press on in the work of the Lord through glory and dishonour, through reproach and praise (2 Cor. 6:8), knowing with certainty that calumny in its own place and time vanishes into smoke, while truth remains for ever. And indeed, in this part, this has happened in a twofold way. For while these men were slandering Jesus Christ, they were in fact fulfilling those very words of Jesus Christ, separating the body of Jesus from the soul, and so, as far as lay in them, they were destroying the temple of the Deity, as we have said. Nor was the third day far off, on which that temple was to be raised again through the resurrection and was to last for ever. Moreover, although by these words they signified that his temple would never be destroyed, which was contrary to their great impiety, they themselves, as if with their own hands, were overthrowing it. For, contrary to their intention, they were admitting the very things by which God, provoked, not long afterwards rightly abolished the temple and the priesthood, to take merited punishment on those wicked men, and also to abolish the figures once the truth was revealed. If these did not come about at the very moment when so great a crime was committed, this must be credited to the immense patience of God, who waited for those wicked men for thirty-four years more.

units.la: Quòd ad secundum probrum attinet, quantæ & quàm admiranda cæcitatis huius Nationis testimoniū fuit petere à Iesu Christo vt si verus erat Messias, de Cruce descenderet, quandoquidem sine Cruce verus esse Messias non poterat, nisi nimirum impleret quæ de ipso per Prophetas erant olim prædicta? Quid verò aliud prædixerat Esaias, nisi quod oculis suis intuebantur? Nam ait Es.capite 53. Non est forma neque decor: & quando intuemur eum, non inest aspectus cur desideremus eum contemptus & abiectissimus virorum doloribus affectus: Caligatio pacis nostræ imponitur ei, & liuore eius fit curatio nobis. Ad occisionem vt agnus ductus est. Et Psalm. 22.17. Foderunt manus meas & pedes meos praeter alia quàm plurima ex eodem Psalm. & 69. testimonia diligenter & accurate ab Euangelistis annotata, & singulis pene singularibus huius historiæ. storiæ factis adaptata.
units.tr: As for the second reproach, how great and how admirable a testimony to the blindness of this nation it was to ask Jesus Christ that, if he was the true Messiah, he should come down from the Cross. For without the Cross he could not be the true Messiah, unless he fulfilled what had been foretold of him long before by the Prophets. For what else had Isaiah predicted, except what they were looking at with their own eyes? For he says (Isa. 53, Es. capite 53.): "He has no form nor comeliness; and when we look upon him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. He is despised and the most abject of men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with infirmity. The chastisement of our peace is laid upon him, and by his bruises we are healed. He was led like a sheep to the slaughter." And Psalm 22:17: "They pierced my hands and my feet." Besides these, very many other testimonies from the same Psalm and from Psalm 69 were carefully and accurately noted by the Evangelists, and were applied to almost every single fact of this history.

units.la: Sic plerumque vsu venire conspicimus vt nulli sint iis imperitiores qui libros scientiæ volunt: Dei quidem iusto iudicio, sua Luce ea abutentes priuantis.Quînam igitur dixerimus personarum Successionem in muneribus Ecclesiasticis esse veram & essentialem veræ Ecclesiæ notam, quum ne Sacrarum quidem Scripturarum volumina sint illius absolutè & simpliciter nota, sed hac addita conditione vt legantur Scripturæ & secundùm verum illarum sensum prædicentur? Quomodo igitur stabit eorum opinio, qui vt Scripturarum veram interpretationem à falsa distinguant, personis inhærent, & opinionum antiquitati, id est Solem à tenebris cum lucerna discernere volunt? Sed de his pluribus superius in huius historiæ quibusdam locis egimus.
units.tr: Thus we commonly see that nobody is more unskilled than those who want to read books of learning. Justly, by God's judgment, they abuse his light and are deprived of it. Who, then, would we say that the succession of persons in ecclesiastical offices is the true and essential mark of the true Church, when not even the volumes of the holy Scriptures are known to it absolutely and simply, but only on the added condition that the Scriptures be read and preached according to their true sense? How, then, will the opinion of those stand who, in order to distinguish the true interpretation of Scripture from the false, cling to persons and to the antiquity of opinions, that is, who wish to discern the sun from darkness with a lamp? But we have discussed these matters more fully earlier, in some places of this history.

units.la: Hoc vnicum addam Iesum Christum sequutus Iudæos alloquentem, & monentem oportere ipsum cognituros non tantum oculis corporeis intueri, sed etiam scripturas scrutari. Ioh.5 39. idem nobis faciendum vt vnicus verus Iesus Christus discernatur ex Prophetarum & Apostolorum descriptione ab omnibus pseudoChristis, quos inuentiones & traditiones finxerunt, aut meræ putæ humanæ aut mixtæ cum hoc verbo Dei, quocunque tâdem fuco colorentur. Cæterùm ex hominum istorum tam profana audacia duo nobis doctrinæ capita sunt edisce nda.
units.tr: I will add only this: Jesus Christ, addressing and warning the Jews, said that they ought to search the Scriptures and not merely look with their bodily eyes (John 5:39). We must do the same, so that the one true Jesus Christ may be distinguished, from the descriptions of the Prophets and Apostles, from all the pseudo-Christs whom inventions and traditions have fashioned, whether purely human or mixed with the Word of God, however they may be coloured with whatever disguise. Meanwhile, from the so profane audacity of these men, we must learn two points of doctrine.

units.la: Primùm non oportere homines Deo præscribere vt hoc vel illud faciat vt hominibus innotescat, sed eius vnius esse eligere quodcunque libuerit quibuscunque mediis id efficiat, temporibus aut momentis. Alterum est vehementer esse cauendum ne in dubium reuocetur Dei vel Sapientia, vel Bonitas, vel etiam potentia, si non se nobis ad nostram voluntatem exhibet, quod tamen isti flagitiosi postulabant. Nam patienter exspectandae sunt nobis ipsius reuelationes quas suo semper loco & tempore patefacit, vt hic quoque factum est. Nam quum Iesus Christus vere ante mortuus, virtute propria ex sepulchro surrexit viceturus in seculum, satis ostendit quis esset, & quidem longe excellentiore & magis admiranda manifestatione, quam si ad perditos illos irrisores confundedos de Cruce viuus descendisset, seque morti praesenti subduxisset. Ac sane quis dubitet quin is qui potuit ex mortuis seipsum virtute propria suscitare, potuerit etiam eadem virtute de Cruce descendere saluus & incolumis si sic ei visum esset. Verum id si fecisset, nec in Cruce mortuus esset, in qua tantum ad momentum affixus pependisset, quid nobis miseris hodie fieret, atque adeo omnibus ex sola eius morte vitam trahentibus?
units.tr: First, men ought not to prescribe to God that he should do this or that in order to make himself known to men. It belongs to him alone to choose whatever pleases him, by whatever means, times or moments he brings it about. The other point is that we must take great care lest the wisdom, goodness or even the power of God be called into doubt if he does not show himself to us according to our will, which those wicked men nonetheless demanded. For his revelations must be patiently awaited; he always discloses them in their own place and time, as happened here too. For since Jesus Christ, truly dead beforehand, rose from the sepulchre by his own power, to conquer for ever, he showed sufficiently who he was, and that by a far more excellent and admirable manifestation than if he had come down alive from the Cross to confound those lost mockers and withdrawn himself from present death. Indeed, who would doubt that he who could raise himself from the dead by his own power could also, by the same power, have come down from the Cross safe and sound, if that had seemed good to him? But if he had done so, he would not have died on the Cross, on which he hung only for a moment. What would become of us wretches today, and of all who draw their life solely from his death?

units.la: Quàm multa vero sese offerunt exempla rerum quae nostro seculo contigerunt, & quidem paucis ab hinc annis, ex quibus manifeste conspicimus optimum & necessarium fuisse vt faceret, quod fecit, quando & quomodo voluit, quum tamen praeclarius actum iri nobiscum
units.tr: How many examples present themselves of things that happened in our own age, and indeed in the last few years, from which we clearly see that it was best and necessary for him to do what he did, when and how he willed, although it would have turned out more splendidly for us

units.la: dum est Deo prae scribere vt hoc vel illud faciat: aut tempus & modu illud faciendi quod pollicitus est: quum ab eius sola voluntate pendere nos oporteat. cum cogitaremus & etiam optaremus si aliter fecisset? Discamus igitur, fratres, discamus inquam, in talibus negotiis seu totam Ecclesiam, seu priuatos spectantibus, sic ad Deum preces nostras dirigere, & optare vt regnum eius adueniat, aut in hac aut illa re, vt abeius sola prouidentia & sapientia sanctâqu[?]luntate toti pendeamus: solus enim ipse novit quid tum ad suam gloriam tum ad suorum vtilitatem ac salutem expediat.
units.tr: if we were to prescribe to God that he do this or that, or the time and manner of doing what he has promised, since we ought to depend on his will alone, when we had thought and even wished that he had acted otherwise? Let us learn, therefore, brethren, let us learn, I say, that in such affairs, whether they concern the whole Church or private persons, we must so direct our prayers to God, and so wish that his kingdom may come, whether in this or that matter, that we may wholly depend on his providence, his wisdom and his holy will alone. For he alone knows what is expedient both for his own glory and for the good and salvation of his people.

units.la: Accedamus ad Seniores populi, Sacerdotes &Scribas quorum Euangelistæ speciatim meminerunt, vt doceant grauius adhuc eos reliquis omnibus in Christum peccasse suis conuitiis, quæ tamen in ipsorum capita reciderùt: exprobrabant autem ei non posse quum alios seruasset seipsum seruare, quod quid aliud erat quàm inficiari quemquam ab eo seruatum, id est ab aliquo malo liberatum. Nec enim hic illi de æterna salute loquuntur: & tamen an fuit oblecto genus vllum miraculorum quod non à Christo præstitum aut oculis essent intuiti, aut auribus percepissent? Annon enim leprosos sanauerat, cæcis visum reddiderat, surdis auditum, claudos ambulare fecerat, mutis vsum vocis dederat, omnis generis morbos & languores sanauerat, Diabolos expulerat, mari & ventis imperarat, hominum myriadas panibus & piscículis paucis multiplicatis nutriuerat: mortuos authoritate sua & plane diuina virtute suscitarat? Quoties autem ad hæc obstupuerant? Non igitur hic de simplici quadam ignorantia, sed de horrendo illo Dei furore, homines in reprobum sensum dantis agitur. Hoc scilicet impulsi furore dixerunt eum Daemonia eiicere per virtutem Beelzebub principis Daemoniorum: unde Iesus Christus ultimam aduersus eos futurae condemnationis irrevocabilis sententiam dixerat, tanquam generali apostasia & malitia immedicabili in Spiritum Sanctum peccantes.
units.tr: Let us come to the elders of the people, the priests and scribes, whom the Evangelists mention by name, so that we may see how they sinned against Christ even more grievously than all the rest, with their reproaches, which nevertheless fell back upon their own heads. They taunted him that, having saved others, he could not save himself. What was this but denying that anyone had been saved by him, that is, freed from some evil? For here they are not speaking of eternal salvation. And yet was there any kind of miracle that Christ had not performed, which they had not seen with their eyes or heard with their ears? Had he not cleansed lepers, restored sight to the blind, hearing to the deaf, made the lame walk, given the dumb the use of speech, healed every kind of disease and infirmity, cast out devils, commanded the sea and the winds, fed thousands of men with a few loaves and small fishes multiplied, and raised the dead by his own authority and plainly divine power? And how often had they been astonished at these things? So this is not a matter of simple ignorance, but of that dreadful wrath of God by which men are given over to a reprobate mind. Driven by this very fury, they said that he cast out demons by the power of Beelzebub, prince of the demons. For this Jesus Christ pronounced against them the final and irrevocable sentence of future condemnation, as sinning against the Holy Spirit in a general apostasy and an incurable malice.

units.la: Quàm multos autem hodie terrarum orbis habet eandem viam insistentes, & pertinaci malitia cognitam veritatem oppugnantes? Deum vero supplex oro ut miseros in viam revocet ne ad finem usque in malitia perseverent. Sed nostrum est ex tam horrendorum iudiciorum consideratione aduersus conscientiae bene edoctae monita non reluctari, nec passionibus nostris laxas habenas dare: ad Deum unicum in omnibus tentationibus confugere: longa ipsius patientia non abuti: sic de nostra salute eius bonitatis & clementiae respectu certos esse, ut nos ipsos intuentes & infirmitates nostras apprehendentes Deo cum omni modestia serviamus. Act.20.19. & cum timore & tremore nostram salutem concinciamus. Philipp. 2. 12. ut qui stare videtur non cadat. 1. Cor. 10. 12. & qui lapsus est, relevetur.
units.tr: How many people throughout the world today follow the same path and, with obstinate malice, assail the truth once known! I pray to God earnestly that he may call these wretched people back to the way, so that they do not persevere in malice to the end. But it is our part, from the consideration of such dreadful judgments, not to resist the admonitions of a well-instructed conscience, nor to give free rein to our passions. We must flee to the one God in all temptations, not abuse his long patience, and so be certain of our salvation out of regard for his goodness and clemency that, looking upon ourselves and grasping our infirmities, we may serve God with all modesty (Acts 20:19), and work out our salvation with fear and trembling (Phil. 2:12), so that he who seems to stand may not fall (1 Cor. 10:12), and he who has fallen may be raised up.

units.la: Sed praeterea perditorum istorum impudentiam cum summa caecitate coiunctam audiamus, dicentium, Si Rex est Israelis, descendat nunc ex Cruce ut videamus eum & credamus in eum. Nam ut superius diximus nisi Rex iste mortuus esset in Cruce, non fuisset pro- missus ille Messias, non inficiantibus Rabbi- nis Iudæorum licet excæcatis, vt vidimus, E- saiam loco citato de Messia loquutum esse,ad- eò vt propterea pro vnico Messia promisso duos faciant,vni tribuentes quæ de miseriis & perpessionibus eius dicuntur, alteri verò quæ de regni ipsius excellentia prædicantur, quod semper terrenum arbitrantur,id est fœdus salutis penitus abolent. Et sanè hic eorum est exitus qui Dei sapientiam ex suæ rationis excæcatæ modulo metiuntur: quam tamè nec caro nec sanguis revelant, vt Dominus Petro respondit, qui nihilominus nō ita multò post in eundem errorem lapsus est.Matth.16.17.& 23.
units.tr: But further, let us hear the impudence of these lost men, joined with the greatest blindness, as they say: "If he is King of Israel, let him now come down from the Cross, that we may see him and believe in him." For, as we said above, unless this King had died on the Cross, that promised Messiah would not have come, and the rabbis of the Jews, though blinded, as we have seen, do not deny that Isaiah spoke of the Messiah in the place cited. Indeed, so far are they from doing so that, on this account, they make two out of the one promised Messiah, attributing to one the things said of his miseries and sufferings, and to the other the things proclaimed of the excellence of his kingdom, which they always think of as earthly. That is, they utterly abolish the covenant of salvation. And indeed this is the outcome for those who measure God's wisdom by the measure of their own blinded reason, which flesh and blood, however, do not reveal, as the Lord answered Peter, who nevertheless not long afterwards fell into the same error (Matt. 16:17; 23).

units.la: Et hæc quidem de crassa ipsorum cæcitate: sed quæ sequuntur eorum hypocrisin cum eadem cæcitate mixtam oltendunt. Ecquis enim sibi persuaserit si Christus ex Cruce descendis- set fuisse ipsos in illù potiùs credituros quàm quum tot miracula & quidem isto quod po- stulabant maiora facientem conspexissent? Itaque sic loquentes insigniter mentiebantur. Nam contrà si Christus ex Cruce saluus & incolumis descendisset (quod sine difficultate poterat, vt qui maiora præstitisset etiam in ipsa Cruce licuti paulò post audituri sumus) nec eorum malitiam compescuisset (vt fecit quum voluit donec ipsius hora aduenirer, Luc. 4. verf. 30.) certissimum est eandem ipsis paratam calumniam quam superius audiuimus, nimirum pulchrè illi cum Diabolo conuenire, & Incantatorem vocaturos fuisse, sicut eum à morte nominant, Matth. 27. 63. rursúsque correptum iterum Cruci fuiff affixuros. En eorum hypocrifin eandem cum ea qua vsi erant prius, miraculum è cœlo lagitantes. Matth. 12. 38.
units.tr: So much for their crass blindness. What follows shows their hypocrisy mixed with the same blindness. For who would persuade himself that, had Christ come down from the Cross, they would have believed in him, rather than when they had seen so many miracles, and indeed greater ones than the one they demanded? So in speaking thus they were lying shamelessly. For on the contrary, had Christ come down from the Cross safe and sound (which he could have done without difficulty, as one who had performed greater things even on the Cross, as we shall shortly hear), and had he not restrained their malice (as he did when he willed, until his hour came: Luc. 4.30), it is quite certain that the same calumny we heard above would have been ready for them: namely, that he agreed splendidly with the devil, and they would have called him a sorcerer, as they name him from his death (Matt. 27:63), and, having seized him again, would have crucified him once more. Behold their hypocrisy, the same as that with which they were previously afflicted, demanding a sign from heaven (Matt. 12:38).

units.la: Sed animaduertite quæso crassissimum in rebus sanctis & diuinis inscitiam: in eo quòd sibi pollicentur fe posse in eum credere, i què postulant ab ipso fieri viderint: quum tamen vera fides fine qua Iesus Christus nihil prodest nisi ad condemnationem, nō fit à nobisipsis, sed à sola Dei gratia, quando & cui Deo placuerit cor aperire & eam largiri. Act. 16. 14. Ephes. 2. 8. Philipp. 1. 29. Idem de Poenitentia dictum volo, quam sibi nonnulli quotiescunque libebit pollicentur, quum tamen Dominum vocantem & inuitantem oporteat nunquam procrastinantes sequi. Psal. 95. 7. Ac si fidei necessarium & proprium obiectum est Iesus Christus crucifixus, mortuus sepultus, suscitatus, quomodo isti vera illa fide credidissent, sine qua Iesus Christus nullius mortalis Seruator est, si Iesus Christus de Cruce descendisset? Non sine causa igitur Dominus eos caecos, caecorum duces vocauerat. Matth. 15. 14. & quidem hæc est plus quàm horrenda punitio qua Deus sacrosancti verbi sui contemptum vlciscitur.
units.tr: But please notice the very gross ignorance in holy and divine matters: they promise that they can believe in him, if they see him do what they demand. Yet true faith, without which Jesus Christ profits nothing except to condemnation, does not come from ourselves but from the grace of God alone, when and to whom God is pleased to open the heart and bestow it (Acts 16:14; Eph. 2:8; Phil. 1:29). I want the same said of repentance, which some promise themselves whenever they like, though we ought to follow the Lord when He calls and invites us, without ever putting it off (Ps. 95:7). If the necessary and proper object of faith is Jesus Christ crucified, dead, buried and raised, how could these men have believed with that true faith, without which Jesus Christ is the Saviour of no mortal, if Jesus Christ had come down from the Cross? Not without reason, then, did the Lord call them blind leaders of the blind (Matt. 15:14). Indeed, this is more than a horrible punishment, by which God avenges the contempt of His holy Word.

units.la: Tales hodie sunt nostri seculi Pharifæi & Scribæ, qui rationibus conuicti & ad metam non loqui redacti, subinde recurrunt ad miracula: cula: quorum egomet cuidam hoc à me in il- lustri quodam consessu postulanti regessi ver- ba Iesu Christi, Matth. 16 4. Natio mala & a- dulterina signum requirit: & quidem addita duplici ratione: quarum vna est eandem do- ctrinam cum Christo & Apostolis profitentes, nullis aliis indigere miraculis quàm quæ ab Euangelistis monumentis ad nos transmissa sunt de quibus nullo modo possit dubitari: al- tera, probè nosse ipsum (nam erat mihi res cum quodam ex Sorbonæ non vlt imis doctoribus) donum miraculorum in Ecclesia desiisse, nec abs re, quum Euangelica doctrina satis sufficienter obsignata sit. Sed Ionæ miraculum, de quo Iesus Christus loquutus erat sui temporis Pharisæos alloquutus, nostro seculo renouatum esse, quo veluti de nouo Christus erat inter nos suscitatus, post non quidem tridui, sepulturam, sed multorum seculorum, quibus in scholis ipsorum veluti mortuus iacuerat. Absit igitur à nobis, fratres, vt inter illos miraculorum flagitatores censeamur, sed doctrinæ tot miraculis obsignatæ fidem adhibeamus, Deúmque supplices oremus, vt infausta illa incredulitas, quam nascentes nobiscum attu-limus, in veram & firmam fide commutetur, fructusque bonæ & sanctæ vitæ feramus. Denique pro Christo què illi ex Cruce descéde-re voluerunt, credamus in eum qui mansit in ea donec Spiritum emisisset mortem ipsam sua morte interfecturus: & qui nouissime frustra renitentibus aduersariis, & obsignato sepulchri lapide,& ipso sepulchro militibus armatis septo,virtute sua suscitatus victoreuafit vt nobis vitam ęternam & in ętcrnum p:rmanentem acquireret.
units.tr: Such are the Pharisees and scribes of our own age, who, when they are convicted by arguments and driven to silence, keep running back to miracles. I once answered one of them, who demanded this of me in a certain distinguished gathering, with the words of Jesus Christ: "An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign" (Matt. 16:4). And I added two reasons. The first is that we profess the same doctrine as Christ and the apostles, and need no other miracles than those handed down to us in the Gospel records, about which there can be no doubt. The second is that I know well (for I had to do with a man who was one of the teachers of the Sorbonne, and no mean one) that the gift of miracles has ceased in the Church, and rightly so, since the evangelical doctrine has been sealed sufficiently. But the sign of Jonah, of which Jesus Christ spoke when addressing the Pharisees of His own time, has been renewed in our age, when Christ, as it were, has been raised anew among us, not after a burial of three days but after many centuries, during which He lay as though dead in their schools. Far be it from us, brethren, that we should be counted among those who demand miracles. Let us rather give credence to a doctrine sealed by so many miracles, and pray humbly to God that that unhappy unbelief, which we bring with us from birth, may be changed into a true and firm faith, and that we may bear the fruits of a good and holy life. Finally, let us believe in Him in place of those who wished Christ to come down from the Cross, who remained on it until He had yielded up the Spirit, destined to destroy death itself by His own death; and who, rising at last, when His adversaries resisted in vain, with the stone of the sepulchre sealed and the tomb itself surrounded by armed soldiers, by His own power was raised up and became victor, so that He might win for us eternal life, abiding for ever.

units.la: Tertium sequitur perditorum istorum hominum in peius ruentium aduersus Iesum Christum conuitium, Confidit, inquiunt, in Deo,liberet eum nunc si vult eum,dixit enim, Filius Dei sum. Quorum quidem sermonum hic videtur esse sensus. Quod sperct ab homi-nibus hic amplius non habet: quoniam autem religiosus semper haberi voluit, solum illi super est auxilium à Deo. Age igitur, Deus iam ostendat,num qui iam Crucifixus est tam sit ei acceptus. Nam id aut hoc ipso momento faciat aut nunquam oportet, quum præsertim non contentus hominum conditione:se ipsum dixerit Filium illum Dei nobis promissum.
units.tr: There follows a third insult against Jesus Christ from these lost men, who are rushing towards worse things: "He trusts in God; let Him deliver him now, if He will have him, for he said, I am the Son of God" (Matt. 27:43). The sense of these words seems to be this: since he can expect no more help from men, and since he has always wished to be thought religious, only help from God remains to him. Come, then, let God now show whether He who is already crucified is so acceptable to Him. For He ought to do this at this very moment, or never, especially since he, not content with the condition of men, has said that he is the Son of God promised to us.

units.la: Ecce vero non tantum conuitia & iniurias aduersus Iesum Christum, sed impia & blasphema verba in Deum ipsum:& falsitatis malignè aduersus Iesum Christum vt cætera omnia effictæ plena. Nam vt de blasphemia primùm dicam, quæ tanta audacia est Deo mortales hoc vel illud faciedum præscribere,& quidem intra certum & præfixum tempus, seu iudicia ipsius seu misericordiam considereS? Si Deus qui solem suum oriri facit super bonos & improbos, sceleratum quempiam extremo aliquo periculo eripit, vt quotidie facit,an propterea dicendus est Dominus aut impium approbare, aut impium illum talem non esse qui habehabebatur? Etsi Dominus non exaudito eo à quo vere colitur & inuocatur, liberationem eius differt, atque adeò vel explorationem vel castigationem duplicat, an merito d ci potest Dominus suos non exaudire, aut talis vir pro hypocrita habendus, qualem Satan & amici Iobi de ipso quondam sententiam tulerunt? Sane infinita Scripturarum sacrarum exempla, & quotidiana Ecclesiæ experientia (quæ tam raro est à Cruce vacua, licet aliquas suis inducias aliquando Dominus concedat) tales conclusiones satis aperte falsi coarguit & condemnat: non frustrà monente nos Sapiente non esse de Dei amore aut odio ex rerum prosperarum aut aduersarum euentu in hoc mundo iudicandum Ecclesiastes 9. 1. Siquis autem ex magnis illis doctoribus quæsiuisset utrum exististaret Deo fuisse gratum, Abelem an Cainum Iacobum an Esauum, annon satis conuicti fuissent? Annon vero Patres suos condemnantes tanquam Prophetarum homicidas, quorum ipsi ædificabant sepulchra, Matth. 23. 29. sibi ipsis mendacium impingebant? Nec enim inficiari poterant ita cælos Prophetas vera in Deum fide fuisse præditos, & ipsi charos & acceptos, qui tamen erepti morti non fuissent ea ratione quâ isti poltulabant: longè sanè crudeliores & ferociores in Filium & hæredem quàm fuerant illi ipsorum maiores in seruos ingrati: quod tam perspicuè Dominus ipsis in vineæ similitudine declararat: & satis bene perceperant, licet parùm aut nihil omnino profecerant. Matth. 21,37. & 45.
units.tr: Here we see not only insults and injuries against Jesus Christ but impious and blasphemous words against God Himself, and, as in everything else, malicious falsehood against Jesus Christ. To begin with the blasphemy: what great audacity it is for mortals to prescribe to God that He should do this or that, and indeed within a fixed and set time, whatever His judgments or His mercy may be! If God, who makes His sun rise on the good and the evil, rescues some wicked man from some extreme danger, as He does every day, is the Lord therefore to be said to approve the wicked, or that the man is not the wicked person he was thought to be? And if the Lord, though he is not heard by one who truly worships and calls upon Him, delays his deliverance, and thereby doubles either his trial or his chastisement, can it rightly be said that the Lord does not hear His own, or that such a man must be held a hypocrite, as Satan and the friends of Job once pronounced judgment upon him? Certainly the countless examples of the sacred Scriptures and the daily experience of the Church (which is so seldom free of the Cross, although the Lord sometimes grants it a truce) plainly refute and condemn such conclusions as false, the Wise Man warning us not without reason that we ought not to judge of God's love or hatred from the outcome of prosperous or adverse things in this world (Eccl. 9:1). But if one of those great teachers had been asked whether Abel or Cain, Jacob or Esau, was pleasing to God, would they not have been sufficiently refuted? And did not they, in condemning their fathers as murderers of the prophets, whose sepulchres they built (Matt. 23:29), fall into a lie of their own making? For they could not deny that the prophets of old were endowed with true faith in God, and were dear and acceptable to Him, yet were not rescued from death in the way these men demanded; and that they themselves were far more cruel and fiercer against the Son and heir than their ancestors had been against the ungrateful servants. The Lord had made this plain to them in the parable of the vineyard, and they understood it well enough, though they profited little or nothing at all (Matt. 21:37, 45).

units.la: En igitur iterum aliud maxime horrendæ fiqua fuit vnquam, cæcitatis testimonium. Sed præterea consideranda nobis in hoc factomaxima in Dei decreto & voluntate, & in isto-rum hominum sensu naturali, repugnantia. Tantum enim abfuit vt fiducia illa quam Ie-sus Christus secundum humanitatem habuit in Patre, cruce ipsum eripere debuerit: vt contra eadem illum in hoc agone à principio ad finem confirmarit & erexerit: nec de morte victoriam erat reportaturus, nisi prius ipse mortuus fuisset: Morte etiam contrà illi exprobratura, si, vt isti volebat, ex Cruce descendisset, non expectatam mortem illum fugere. Sed præterea maximum Dei opus in eo positum est, quod vnico Filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis eum ad mortem dedit. Et revera Dominus in hoc mysterio sese qualis est conspiciendum exhibuit, summe nimirum iustum & summe Misericordem. Et tamen egregii isti Scribæ & Sacerdotes concludunt atque ita plebem docent, nisi Pater Filium Cruci eximat, non fore amplius Patrem: & hunc qui se Filium vocat, non Filium fore sed blasphematorem. Ecce in quam abyssum præcipites tandem ferantur, qui suis passionibus locum dantes in Dei maximorum quæ acceperant donorum abusu & prophanatione perseuerant.
units.tr: Here, then, is yet another testimony to the most dreadful blindness that ever was. But besides this, we must consider in this matter the greatest contradiction between God's decree and will and the natural sense of these men. For that confidence which Jesus Christ, according to His humanity, had in the Father was so far from obliging Him to be snatched from the Cross, that on the contrary it strengthened and sustained Him in this contest from beginning to end. Nor was He to win the victory over death unless He first died; and to come down from the Cross, as these men wished, would have been to flee from a death that was expected, a death which would rightly have been thrown up to Him. But further, the greatest work of God lies in this, that He did not spare His only Son but gave Him up to death for us. And indeed in this mystery the Lord showed Himself to be seen as He truly is, namely supremely just and supremely merciful. Yet these distinguished scribes and priests draw their conclusions and so teach the people: unless the Father takes the Son down from the Cross, He will no longer be Father, and he who calls himself the Son will not be the Son but a blasphemer. See into what abyss they are at last hurled headlong, who, giving place to their passions, persist in abusing and profaning the greatest gifts of God that they have received.

units.la: Nihilominus tamen quicquid isti dixerint aut fecerint, Deus in suis promissis verus constans repertus est:& lapis quem ædificantes reprobrarunt, positus est in fundamentum ædificij: ad quem quum isti alliserint, contriti sunt: qualis est etiam futurus omnium eorum exitus qui vestigiis istorum inhærentes non aliter se aduersus membra gerunt quàm olim isti aduersus ipsum caput.
units.tr: Nevertheless, whatever these men said or did, God has been found true and constant in His promises, and the stone which the builders rejected has been set as the foundation of the building; and those who have dashed against it have been broken (Matt. 21:42). Such also will be the end of all those who, clinging to the footsteps of these men, deal with the members of Christ no differently than these men once dealt with the Head Himself.

units.la: Quòd si merito nobis isti sunt abominationi, quid futurum putamus hodiernis Dei contemptoribus & Atheis hominibus? Quid fiet monstris illis, ac potius Diabolis incarnatis, eum blasphemantibus quem ipsi Diaboli metuunt, nec corpori, nec sanguini, nec carni, nec vulneribus tuis, æterne Fili Dei, qui peccata nostra supra lignum tulisti, parcentibus? O infaustum seculum! O immensam Dei patientiam! Quid autem ad hæc aliud dicturus sum, nisi ut supplex Dominu orem ut aut cito suos ad se recipiat, aut talibus hominum monstris os in æternum occludat: quod ipsa tellus quæ ipsos sustinet gemens efflagitat, aër quem spirant, & cœlum quo teguntur expostulat?
units.tr: But if these men are rightly an abomination to us, what do we think will become of the despisers of God and the atheists of our own day? What will happen to those monsters, or rather incarnate devils, who blaspheme him whom the devils themselves fear, and who spare neither your body, nor your blood, nor your flesh, nor your wounds, eternal Son of God, who bore our sins upon the wood? O unhappy age! O immense patience of God! What else can I say to this, except that I pray to the Lord as a suppliant, that either he will soon take his own to himself or shut the mouths of such monsters of men for ever? The earth itself, which bears them, groans and demands this, and the air they breathe and the heaven that covers them cry out for it.

units.la: Sic igitur præcipui inter Iudæos Gubernatores Iesu Christo conuicia facientes propriam condemnationem obsignarunt. Contrà verò vicissim miseri illius latronis conuersi historia nobis ostendit quomodo Iesus Christus, qui ad ea conuicia prorsus obmutuerat, dignis istis conuiciantibus, non sane respondit, sed pœna & supplicio, tertium quendam abipsis non expectatum admiranda ratione propulerit, à quo palàm coarguerentur. Ac sanè, tanta erat
units.tr: So the chief governors among the Jews, by heaping insults upon Jesus Christ, sealed their own condemnation. On the other hand, the story of that wretched thief who was converted shows us how Jesus Christ, who had utterly kept silent under those insults, did not indeed answer those who deserved such insults, but by punishment and suffering, in a wonderful manner, drove off a third party, one not expected from among them, by whom they would be plainly convicted. And indeed, his self-emptying was so great

units.la: ipsius exinanitio, vt necesse fuerit aduersus ea radium aliquę suae Maiestatis in mediis istis tenebris effulgere. Haec igitur historia inter omnes sacrosanctas historias insignis est, ex qua discimus Iesum Christum, minime quidem simplicibus verbis, quibus erant isti indignissimi, sed admirandis factis palam esse testatum aduersus irrisores istos hanc exinanitionem & tam abiectum statum minime coactum esse aut inuoluntarium, neque ex aliqua necessitate aduersus quam nihil poterat, sed spontaneum ad salutem, non sane incredulorum & contemptorum ac conuitiantium, sed eorum qui a peccatorum sordibus conuersi, ad agnitam eius misericordiam confugerent. Quoniam autem fiduciam suam illi obiecerunt & in se seruando impotentiam: eadem etiam illos ratione coarguit, tantum abesse vt vana esset fiducia, & non poterat, si vellet, omnibus sese passionibus subducere, vt se contra vere Filium Dei nuncuparit, in quo solo fiduciam oporteat collocari, quique alios etiam seruaret, morte ipsorum in aeternae vitae introitu commutata. Esi igitur adhuc Cruci affixus, & omnium cruciatuum, adhuc maximum, ipsum nimirum vitae exitum passurus, tamen hic tanquam victor & de omnibus suis hostibus, tam visibilibus quam invisibilibus triumphans loquitur: Cruce, non amplius vt patibulo, sed vt Maiestatis diuinae folio vtens, & tituli capiti suo impositi veritatem asserens, se nimirum, etsi Crucifixum, Seruatorem tamen esse, verumque rúmque Nazaræum, verum illum Iudæis Regem promissum, & credentibus omnibus ad vltimos vsque terrarum fines exhibitum, aduersus Diaboli, peccati & mortis potentiam: denique perinde fuit ac si è cœlis ipsis in suorum inimicorum capita sententiam illam detonasset. Vos me inter latrones, tanquam sceleratorum omnium sceleratissimum huic Cruci affixistis: at reipsa vobis ostendam a vobis ipsis erectum mihi solium ex quo feram horrendam aduersum vos sententiam. Et pro eo quod me ex Cruce descendente, per vos minime starct quominus ij quos mihi Pater dedit sicuti vos & vobiscum perirent, egomet vobis quantumuis frendentibus in ipsa Cruce fixus, meos seruabo, vosque mihi seuerissimas poenas dabitis.
units.tr: Such was his self-emptying that it was necessary for some ray of his majesty to shine out against those enemies in the midst of that darkness. This history therefore stands out among all the holy histories, for from it we learn that Jesus Christ made plain, not with simple words, which were all these most unworthy men deserved, but by admirable deeds, against these mockers, that this self-emptying and so abject a state was not forced upon him or involuntary, nor due to some necessity against which he could do nothing.
