Primum igitur hic occurrit correlatio in his vocibus, sum Mei, qua vsus erat supplex, & Tu, qua vsus Christus in respondendo: Ex quo discimus fidem quae suum effectum in nobis producit ad salutem, habere quidem obiectum suum veritatem verbo Dei comprehensam, & quendam nominatim Iesum Christum, & quid pro nobis praestitit. Sed tenendum est fidem si impliciter apprehendit illa tanquam in se vera, non aliam esse fidem quam Diabolorum quum nihil amplius credamus quam quod ipsi Diaboli nobis melius norunt & credunt, & quorum improbos non arguat ipsa conscientia. Aliam igitur praeterea formam essentialem oportet esse fidei eius quae Dei filiorum propria est, & qua electi olim seruandi, & a reprobis olim damnandis distinguuntur. Eximium Dei donum illud est, quo singulis electis datur sibi ipsis priuatim salutis in Domino nostro Iesu Christo promissione applicare. Nam alioqui quomodo pace in conscientiis haberent Dei Filij, si dubia fluctuaret, vt solet infidelium fides? Rom.5. 1.& quomodo cum fiducia clamaremus ad Deum, Abba, Pater? Rom.8.15. & quomodo nostris hostibus insultaremus? Rom.8.33. Quaenam esset illa fides? ducia qua fretos Apostolus nos ad thronum gratię iubet accedere?Heb.4.16.Quomodo Iacobus iuberet nos orare cum fide nihil diffidentes?Iac.1.6.
units.tr: Let us now weigh the individual words of the Lord one by one. "You will be," he says, "where?" In Paradise. "When?" Today. "In what state?" With me. First, then, a correspondence arises in these words: "I" (the suppliant used "Remember me") and "you" (Christ, in replying, used "you will be with me"). From this we learn that the faith which produces its effect in us unto salvation indeed has its object: the truth comprehended in the Word of God, and in particular Jesus Christ and what he has done for us. But it must be held that if faith apprehends these things only implicitly, as true in themselves, it is no other than the faith of the devils, since we then believe nothing more than what the devils themselves know and believe, and better than we do, and whose wickedness their own conscience does not refute. There must therefore be another, essential form of faith, which is proper to the sons of God, and by which the elect, who are to be saved, are distinguished from the reprobate, who are to be condemned. That is the outstanding gift of God, by which each of the elect is given to apply to himself, privately, the promise of salvation in our Lord Jesus Christ. For otherwise how would the sons of God have peace in their consciences, if it wavered in doubt, as the faith of unbelievers usually does (Rom. 5:1)? And how would we cry to God with confidence, "Abba, Father" (Rom. 8:15)? And how would we insult our enemies (Rom. 8:33)? What kind of faith would that be without the confidence by which, relying on it, the Apostle bids us approach the throne of grace (Heb. 4:16)? How would James bid us pray in faith, doubting nothing (Jas. 1:6)?

units.la: Fateor quidem etiam aduersus constantissimi cuiusque & fortissimi fidem in hoc mundo reliquias incredulitatis & diffidentiæ pugnare: at tamen vincat fides oportet, vt cum illius Lunatici Patre dicamus, Credo, Domine, succurre incredulitati meæ,Marc.9.24.
units.tr: I admit indeed that even in the most steadfast and bravest believer in this world, remnants of unbelief and distrust fight against faith. Yet faith must conquer, so that with the father of that lunatic boy we may say, "I believe, Lord; help my unbelief" (Mark 9:24).

units.la: Aduersarios verò nostros hanc veritatem oppugnantes, sine qua tamen nullus est Deo acceptus, dicentes arrogantiā & præsumptionem esse de Dei gratia certo persuasum esse: pudeat oportet huius erroris. Nam quum is cui data hæc fides est salutem omnem suam in sola Dei gratia in Iesu Christo reponat,& suarum virium imbecillitatem agnoscens magis magisque coram Domino abiiciatur, quinam, obsecro, arrogans ac superbus diceretur? At contrà nostrorum aduersariorum propria est hæc superbia, quos fiduciam in Dei promissionibus collocatam damnare non pudet, & tamen Sanctorum merita iactare, in bonis operibus & satisfactionibus fiduciam ponere:& in ipsorum Indulgentiis spem collocare. At quis hic est qui audit, Tu eris mecum in paradiso, etiam Hodie? Annon ille miser latro merito ad supplicium damnatus & affectus, quòd perpetuò latrociniis indulsisset?
units.tr: But as for our adversaries, who attack this truth, without which no one is acceptable to God, and who say that to be persuaded with certainty of God's grace is arrogance and presumption, they ought to be ashamed of this error. For when the one to whom this faith has been given places all his salvation in the grace of God alone in Jesus Christ, and, recognising the weakness of his own powers, humbles himself more and more before the Lord, who, I beg you, could be called arrogant and proud? On the contrary, this pride is characteristic of our adversaries, who are not ashamed to condemn trust placed in God's promises, and yet boast of the merits of the saints, place their confidence in good works and satisfactions, and set their hope in their indulgences. But who here hears, "You will be with me in Paradise, even today"? Was not that wretched thief rightly condemned and afflicted with punishment, since he had given himself up to robbery all his life?

units.la: Vox illa quam addit Dominus HODIE, testatur animam istius viri in ipso Crucis exitu,
units.tr: The word that the Lord adds, TODAY, bears witness that the soul of this man,

units.la: qui fuit post Christi sub vesperam exitum, in eundem locum sublatam fuisse in quem Iesus Christus prius iuerat. Quo nam? In Paradisum, inquit ipse Dominus: Est autem extra omne dubium hac voce hoc loco, vt & illo Apostoli 2.Cor.2.4. & Diui Iohannis Apocal.2.7. intelligendum locum illū quem antea Iesus Christus domum Patris sui dixerat. Ioh.14.2. extra hunc mundum & supra omnes coelos. Eph.4.10. locum throno gloriæ Dei, & æternæ quieti Ecclesiæ dicatum. 1. Thessal. 1.4.17. de quo nihil sit amplius inquirendum: Hac autem voce Spiritus Sanctus vsus est, alludens ad hortum illum plenum amoenitatis, in quo fuerat Adamus à Domino ante peccatum collocatus, & figuram illius æternæ quietis, in quam introducimur à secundo Adamo. Nec vero dubitandū est quin omnes omnium vere credentium & poenitentiam agentiu animę ex hac vita excedentes in eundem illum locum etiam recipiantur in quem huius viri anima recepta est, modo ad eundem scopum colliment, & eandem viam insistant prout Iesus Christus Patrem rogauit, Ioh.17.20. & 24. & orauit Diuus Stephanus. Act.7.55. & 59. & Paulus Apostolus exoptauit, Phil.1.23. rantisper dum plenam illius gloriæ fruitionem corpore & anima vltimo die consequantur. Plena sane consolationis sententia est, qua quum Spiritus erroris penitus delere nunquam potuerit, multis tamen iam diduum inuolucris involuere conatus est.
units.tr: who was taken up into the same place, after Christ's departure at the evening, into which Jesus Christ had gone before. Where then? "In Paradise," says the Lord himself. It is beyond all doubt that by this word, in this place, as also in that passage of the Apostle (2 Corinthians 12:4) and of the divine John (Revelation 2:7), is to be understood that place which Jesus Christ had earlier called his Father's house (John 14:2), outside this world and above all the heavens (Ephesians 4:10), a place dedicated to the throne of the glory of God and to the eternal rest of the Church (1 Thessalonians 4:17), concerning which nothing more need be inquired. The Holy Spirit used this word, alluding to that garden full of delight in which Adam had been placed by the Lord before the fall, and to the figure of that eternal rest into which we are introduced by the second Adam. Nor indeed should we doubt that the souls of all who truly believe and repent, when they depart from this life, are received into that very place into which the soul of this man was received, provided they aim at the same goal and keep to the same way, as Jesus Christ asked the Father (John 17:20, 24), as the blessed Stephen prayed (Acts 7:55, 59), and as the Apostle Paul desired (Philippians 1:23), until on the last day they attain the full enjoyment of that glory in body and soul. Indeed this is a sentence full of consolation, which, since the spirit of error could never utterly destroy it, has for a long time now been struggling to wrap it in many coverings.

units.la: Dd. iij.
units.tr: Dd. iij.

units.la: Non contentus enim impurus ille Spiritus duobus illis locis quæ nobis in Scriptura declarantur, Paradisus nempe, beatis locus destinatus: & Inferi, locus ad mortem æternam damnatis præparatus, duos errores in Ecclesiam paulatim inuexit. Prior est eorum qui finxerunt Spiritus veterum fidelium, qui adventum Christi in carnem præcesserunt, receptos fuisse, non in cœlis quos Christus nondum aperuisset, sed quodam alio in loco, quem alij nomine Sinus Abrahami designatum putauerunt, Luc. 16. 22. alij nomine Custodiæ aut Carceris, 1. Pet. 3. 19. alij nomine Inferorum, Psal. 16. 10. hanc etiam interpretationem ad articulum descensus Christi ad Inferos transferentes. Hi igitur sentiunt & docent animam Iesu Christi, quandiu corpus eius in sepulchro mansit, loca illa penetrasse in quibus animas Patrum inuiseret ex eo liberandas, & in cœlum tandem secum deducendas, quum in cœlum evectus est. Doctores autem Sorbonici sese huic quæstioni immiscentes longius progressi sunt, disputantes etiam de situ loci & statu eorum qui in eo detinebantur, in quiete quidem, aiunt, sed non in fruitione gloriæ Filij Dei, nondum nati, nec in cœlos secundum humanitatem recepti. Conciliaturi autem nomen Inferorum cum hac quiete, duas contignationes commenti sunt, inferiore nimirum Inferorum parte damnatis propriam sedem, in quam si anima Christi descendit, non sane in iis locis passura descedit, nec damnatos inde liberatura, sed poenam eorum potius adauctura. Superiorem vero contignatione, quam dixerunt Limbum, quasi dicas, Inferorum fimbriā, afsignarunt, primo fideliū veterū animis, quibus inde Christi ad ea loca descensu liberatis, in eorū locum animas reposuerunt infantiū abortiuorum qui Luce nunquā aspexerunt, nec baptizari potuerunt: quibus locis eas in perpetuum addicunt.
units.tr: For that unclean spirit was not content with the two places that are declared to us in Scripture, Paradise, namely, the place destined for the blessed, and Hell, the place prepared for those condemned to eternal death. Gradually he introduced two errors into the Church. The first is of those who imagined that the spirits of the faithful of old, who went before the coming of Christ in the flesh, were received not in heaven, which Christ had not yet opened, but in some other place, which some have designated by the name of Abraham's bosom (Luke 16:22), others by the name of Custody or Prison (1 Peter 3:19), others by the name of Hell (Psalm 16:10), transferring also this interpretation to the article about Christ's descent into Hell. These men therefore hold and teach that the soul of Jesus Christ, while his body remained in the tomb, penetrated those regions in which he was to visit the souls of the Fathers, to free them from there, and to lead them with him into heaven when he was carried up into heaven. But the Sorbonne doctors, meddling in this question, went further, disputing also about the location of the place and the state of those who were held there: in rest, they say, but not in the enjoyment of the glory of the Son of God, who was not yet born, nor received into heaven according to his humanity. Wishing to reconcile the name of Hell with this rest, they devised two storeys: in the lower part of Hell, which is the proper seat of the damned, into which, if the soul of Christ descended, it would not indeed suffer there, nor would it deliver the damned from there, but would rather increase their punishment. But the upper storey, which they called Limbo, as if you should say, the fringe of Hell, they assigned first to the souls of the faithful of old, who were thence freed by Christ's descent to those regions; and in their place they put the souls of infants who were born dead, who never saw the light and could not be baptized, and whom they condemn to these regions forever.

units.la: Siquis autē obiiciat hæc verba, Hodie mecum eris in Paradiso, respondent intelligenda de fruitione gloriæ diuinitatis Iesu Christi, qua frui coeperunt veterū Patrū & huius miseri latronis conuersi Spiritus descensu animæ Iesu Christi in Limbum, in quo tam diu remansit quamdiu corpus in sepulchro iacuit: ac proinde Paradisus hic de quo hæc historia loquitur, erit superior Inferorū contignatio, ex quibus nec Veterū Patrū Spiritus nec huius latronis prius exiuerint, nec in cælum recepti fuerint quàm Christus in cælum ascenderit, ex iis, inquiunt, quę Eph.4.8. scribitur. En vero quomodo pedetentim spiritus erroris, ex ineptis quorundā Scripturæ locorū expositionibus, idé in cœlesti sapientia molitus est quam Deus per suū Spiritū Ecclesiæ suę dedit, quo din cognitione Dei quā natura dictat vanis & curiosis hominū ratiocinationibus effecerat, Rom. 1.21. At istis omnibus occurritur, si dicamus non restringendū fructū mortis & passionis Domini, qui positus est in cœlorū apertura, & ascensu, vitaq; æterna, nec ad tépus incarnationis eius, nec mortis, nec resurrectionis, nec in cœlū Ascensionis. Nā Iesus Christus venturus nō minus Patres qui aduentū eius præcesserunt, seruauit, quàm qui deinceps in eū crediderunt, & quotidie credūt & crediturī sunt, donec completus sit electorum numerus: vt hac ratione nunquam plures sed vnus tantùm Seruator fuerit, vna Ecclesia, vna fides, vna spes, vnus Paradisus, vt fusiùs hæc declarantur, Heb. 11. licet fides, spes & salus eorum qui ante Iesu Christi in terras aduentum vixerunt ea respexerit quæ realiter Christus suo tempore pro ipsis & nobis impleuit: & hoc quidem respectu dispensatio scientiæ salutis minor tunc fuerit, idest obscurior sub vetere fœdere vt, quæ in spe posita fuerit & sub figuris Legalibus exhibita, quàm noui fœderis tempore, quo realiter & actualiter exhibita est à Dei Filio: primùm quidem quum ipsemet carne assumpta se videndum præbuit, deinde per ministerium Euangelicum ad consummationem vsque seculorum duraturum. Quòd ad locos autem illos Scripturæ male iam pridem intellectæ & adaptatæ, vt Spiritus erroris mature cœpit tenebras offundere, in loco illo ex Psal. 16.10. vox Hebrea satis aperte sepulchrum notat, vt pulchrè docuit Petrus Apostolus, Act. 2. 29. opponens sepulchrum Iesu Christi vacuum, & ex quo Iesu Christi corpus exierat antequam vllam corruptionem pateretur, sepulchro in quo Dauidis corpus in corruptione iacebat. Quòd ad vocem attinet Animæ, non tantùm eo loco, sed etiam pluribus aliis vox qua Prophcta vtitur Hebræa sæpe accipitur non quidem pro altera hominis parte, sed sæpe pro toto homine viuo, vt quum in Ægyptum Iacobus descendisse dicitur cum Animabus septuaginta quinque: & nonnunquam pro mortui cadauere vt Num. 19. 13. vt etiam est hoc loco necessario ea significatione accipienda, quum non possit nisi de Christi corpore dici fuisse illud à corruptione immune. Sinus autem Abrahæ figuratè dicitur, propterea quòd Abrahamus Pater credetium vocatur, vt ita ostendatur vnio & consensus mutuus Patris Abrahami & filiorum eius eodem fundamento fœderis innixorum, & in eandem cum ipso vitam æternā collectorum. Quoniam autem Iesus Christus in quem Abrahamus & veri omnes ipsius filij crediderunt & sperarunt, nunc vltimis iltis temporibus realiter exhibitus est, & actualiter nostræ salutis mysterium impleuit, atque adeo in regni sui possessionem ingressus est, idcirco nó iam dicimus nostras animas in sinum Abrahæ colligi, sed cum Iesu Christo, cum quo Abrahamus ipse & filij eius vnà collecti sunt, vt ita nulla quidem varietas locorum designetur, sed tamen quædam gloriæ & honoris amplificatio. Nam hoc merito præsupponendum nobis videtur, reali aduentu capitis gaudium & gloriam membrorum ipsius & Angelorum ipsorum vehementer auctam & amplificatam: ita tamen vt de istis rebus nihil curiosius inquirendum sit, quàrū ampliorem in hoc mundo nobis cognitionem negatam videmus. Sin autem vlterius aliquid de huius Abrahami sinus situ liceret inuestigare, quanta fuit tamen Scolasticorum audacia vt illum facerent fecundam Inferorum contignationem, idest locorum ipsa etiâ terra inferiorum, quum D.Lucas 16.26. tam sublimem faciat? Ad locum autem Petri 1.Pet.3.19. mirum est tantos viros & iam pridem sic impegisse: quum fatis manifestum fit Apostolum eo loco de veteribus Patribus fidelibus non agere, sed contrà de infidelibus: ex quorum numero in exemplum adfert eos qui diluuio illo perierunt, quòd Iesu Christo illos per Noachum spiritualiter docente noluissent attentas aures præbere. Denique quòd ad locum Apostoli Ephef. 4.8. ibi etiam non agitur de fidelibus Patribus qui improprie captiui dicerentur: sed contrà de Iesu Christi inimicis, Diabolo, Peccato & Mundo, quos alibi dicitur fpoliaffe & victor in triumphum traduxisse. Coloff. 2.15.
units.tr: If anyone objects these words, "Today you will be with me in Paradise," they reply that they must be understood of the enjoyment of the glory of the divinity of Jesus Christ, which the spirits of the ancient Fathers and of this wretched thief began to enjoy when the soul of Jesus Christ descended into Limbo, where it remained as long as his body lay in the tomb. So this Paradise of which the history speaks will be the upper storey of the Underworld, out of which neither the spirits of the ancient Fathers nor that of the thief came forth earlier, nor were they received into heaven until Christ ascended into heaven, on the basis of what is written in Eph. 4.8. See, however, how by degrees the spirit of error, from the unskilled explanations of some passages of Scripture, has undertaken to set aside the heavenly wisdom which God gave to his Church through his Spirit, and by which the knowledge of God that nature teaches had been obscured by the vain and curious reasonings of men, Rom. 1.21. But all these claims are met if we say that the fruit of the death and passion of the Lord, which was laid up in the opening of the heavens, in the ascension and in eternal life, is not to be restricted either to the time of his incarnation, or to his death, or to his resurrection, or to his Ascension into heaven. For Jesus Christ, who was to come, saved the Fathers who preceded his coming no less than those who afterwards believed in him, who believe daily and who will believe until the number of the elect is complete. In this way there have never been many saviours but only one, one Church, one faith, one hope, one Paradise, as is explained more fully in Heb. 11. Although the faith, hope and salvation of those who lived before the coming of Jesus Christ on earth looked to what Christ in reality fulfilled in his own time for them and for us, in this respect the dispensation of the knowledge of salvation was then smaller, that is, more obscure under the Old Covenant, since it was placed in hope and shown under legal figures, than in the time of the New Covenant, in which it was actually and really exhibited by the Son of God: first when he himself, having assumed flesh, showed himself to be seen, and then through the evangelical ministry, which will last until the consummation of the ages. As for those passages of Scripture long since badly understood and misapplied, since the spirit of error soon began to cast its shadows, in that place from Ps. 16.10 the Hebrew word quite plainly denotes the sepulchre, as the Apostle Peter taught well, Acts 2.29, setting the empty sepulchre of Jesus Christ, from which his body had come out before it suffered any corruption, against the sepulchre in which David's body lay in corruption. As for the word "soul," the Hebrew word the prophet uses is often taken not in that place only but in many others, not for the other part of man but often for the whole living man, as when Jacob is said to have gone down into Egypt with seventy-five souls; and sometimes for the body of the dead, as in Num. 19.13. In this place too it must necessarily be taken in that sense, since it can only be said of Christ's body that it was free from corruption. The bosom of Abraham is spoken of figuratively, because Abraham is called the father of believers, so that the union and mutual agreement of Father Abraham and his sons, who rest on the same foundation of the covenant and are gathered into the same eternal life with him, might be shown. Now since Jesus Christ, in whom Abraham and all his true sons believed and hoped, has in these last times been really exhibited, has actually fulfilled the mystery of our salvation, and so has entered into possession of his kingdom, we no longer say that our souls are gathered into the bosom of Abraham, but with Jesus Christ, with whom Abraham himself and his sons were gathered together. So no difference of places is indicated, but a certain enlargement of glory and honour. For this seems rightly to be presupposed: by the real coming of the Head, the joy and glory of his members and of the Angels themselves have been greatly increased and enlarged. Yet in these matters nothing more curious is to be inquired into, since we see that a fuller knowledge of them is denied us in this world. But if one were allowed to investigate further anything about the position of this bosom of Abraham, how great was the audacity of the Schoolmen in making it the second storey of the Underworld, that is, of places lower even than the earth itself, when St Luke 16.26 makes it so lofty! As for the passage in 1 Pet. 3.19, it is strange that such great men have long stumbled over it in this way, since it is quite clear that the Apostle in that place is not speaking of the ancient faithful Fathers but on the contrary of unbelievers, from whose number he brings forward as an example those who perished in that flood, because they would not give attentive ears to Jesus Christ teaching them spiritually through Noah. Finally, as for the Apostle's passage in Eph. 4.8, there too it is not about the faithful Fathers, who would be called captives only improperly, but on the contrary about the enemies of Jesus Christ: the Devil, Sin and the World, whom he is said elsewhere to have despoiled and, as victor, to have led in triumph, Col. 2.15.

units.la: Et de Limbi quidem fabula hactenus. Superest alia machina paulatim etiam in Ecclesiam inuecta quam Purgatorium dicunt, aut Thermas animarum fidelium, quæ vt ipsi dicunt, non plene in hoc mundo pro pœnis peccatorum à Baptismo suo commissurum satisfecerunt. Dogma, quod non dicam errorem aut vanam opinionem, vt fuit illa prior, quæ cum fæno & stramine comparari potest, vt docet Paulus 1.Cor.3.12. sed doctrinam inquam diabolicam, meritum mortis & passionis Domini abolen-
units.tr: And so much for the fable of Limbo. There remains another contrivance, gradually introduced into the Church, which they call Purgatory, or the baths of the souls of the faithful, which, as they themselves say, have not fully made satisfaction in this world for the punishments of the sins committed after their Baptism. This is a dogma which I will not call an error or a vain opinion, as the former was, which can be compared to hay and straw, as Paul teaches, 1 Cor. 3.12. I call it a diabolical doctrine, one that is abolishing

units.la: abolentem, qui non essεt alioqui pax nostra & reconciliatio nostra, nec agnus qui tollit peccata mundi, nec lauacrum nostrum, nec is qui peccata nostra tulit super lignū, nisi quantum ad culpam, & aliquam pœnæ imminutionem, vt loquuntur harum thermarum architecti. Nam cum perfricta impudentia persuadent mortē Domini pœnam alioquin æterna in temporariam esse commutatam, nempe decem millium annorum in singula maiora peccata, pro quorum deinde satisfactione, quum fateri cogantur animas nec posse Mereri nec Demereri, miseras conscientias præsertim ad Sanctorum merita, quos hac ratione dicendū erit à Purgatorio fuisse immunes: deinde ad suas peccatorum Remissiones & Indulgentias quas numerata pecunia vendunt: tum ad aquā lustralem, & præsertim ad Missas suas & Vigilias: tandémque ad eleemosynas & oblationes amandant, quas ipsi pro defunctis deuorant. En inquam egregij istius Purgatorij Theologiam, quo non solum Iesu Christi beneficium maxima ex parte exinanitur: Dei verbo mendacium impingitur: Deus iniustissimus dicitur satisfactionem petens ab iis quorum culpam aboleuit: & quæ vnius Iesu Christi pro nobis fusi sanguinis propria sunt, rebus creatis, mortuis & sine sensu tribuuntur: & præterea homines (quos autem oro maxima ex parte homines) non pudet se Sacrificos illius facere qui solus habens iusistud Sacerdotis, vnica oblatione sui ipsius semel facta Ecclesiam suam in perpetuum sanctificauit. Quas blasphemas voces satis est semel detestari, ne in refutandis diutius haereamus.
units.tr: abolishing the merit of the death and passion of the Lord, which otherwise would not be our peace and reconciliation, nor the Lamb who takes away the sins of the world, nor our laver, nor he who bore our sins upon the tree, except as far as guilt goes and some lessening of punishment, as the architects of these baths put it. For with brazen impudence they persuade us that the death of the Lord has changed an otherwise eternal punishment into a temporary one, namely ten thousand years for each greater sin; and for the satisfaction of these, since they are forced to admit that souls can neither merit nor demerit, they send wretched consciences to the merits of the Saints, from whom, on this reasoning, they must be said to have been exempt from Purgatory; then to their remissions of sins and Indulgences, which they sell for counted money; then to lustral water, and especially to their Masses and Vigils; and at last they refer them to alms and offerings, which they themselves devour on behalf of the dead. See, I say, the theology of that splendid Purgatory, by which not only is the benefit of Jesus Christ for the most part emptied out, but a lie is thrust upon the word of God; God is called most unjust for demanding satisfaction from those whose guilt he has abolished; and things which belong only to the blood of Jesus Christ shed for us are attributed to created things, dead and without sense. Moreover, men (who, alas, are for the most part men) are not ashamed to make themselves priests of him who alone, having this priesthood, by one offering of himself made once for all, has sanctified his Church forever. It is enough to detest these blasphemous words once, lest we linger longer in refuting them.

units.la: Denique vox illa: Mecum, dignissima est quam attente consideremus, qua non tantum docemur non esse locu capiti seorsim a membris destinatum, sed eandem esse gloriae & felicitatis aeternae in regno coelesti capiti & membris communionem, secundum declarationem quam ipsemet Dei Filius expresse nobis in suo Testamento factam reliquit. Luc.22. 29. quam ob causam etiam eius coheredes dicimur. Rom.8.17. etsi dignitas & praeeminentia in totum corpus debetur Capiti ad dextram Patris sedenti: ita ut quod in capite perfectissimum est, membris secundum vniuscuiusque mensuram distribuatur.
units.tr: Finally, that word With me is most worthy of our careful consideration, for it teaches us not only that no place is assigned to the Head apart from the members, but that there is one and the same communion of glory and eternal happiness in the heavenly kingdom for the Head and the members, according to the declaration which the Son of God himself expressly left us in his Testament, Luke 22.29; for which reason we are also called his co-heirs, Rom. 8.17. Although dignity and pre-eminence are owed to the Head seated at the Father's right hand over the whole body, so that what is most perfect in the Head is distributed to the members according to each one's measure.

units.la: Apagesis igitur detestandum eorum errorem qui docent animas ex corpore exceden- tes, sine vllo sensu sopitas esse: quo posito, sane multo melior esset hoc respectu animarum in hoc mundo, quam cum Iesu Christo collecta- rum conditio: falsum dogma, quo maxima & incomprehensibili consolatione priuamur, ut omittam multa Scripturae contraria ex diametro testimonia: & hoc dogmate mortales animas cum suis corporibus fieri: duasque post hanc vitam resurrectiones constitui: Igitur pro tam prohano commento toto vitae nostrae curriculo respondum istud tam foelix Domini nostri Iesu Christi quo miserum latronem est dignatus, omnibus respicientibus & in eadem fide & inuocatione morientibus meditemur. Quomodo igitur & cur mortem metueremus? aut quomodo non potius eam singulis horis quantum expeti potest & debet expeteremus? cur non eam accedentem ambabus vlnis ampleƈteremur, quum tam felicis mutationis nostræ conditionis & habitationis nuntium adferat, & nobis fit veræ æternæ felicitatis principium & introitus?
units.tr: We must therefore reject and detest the error of those who teach that souls, when they depart from the body, sleep without any sensation. If that were so, the condition of souls in this world would in this respect be far better than that of souls gathered together with Jesus Christ. It is a false doctrine that deprives us of a very great and incomprehensible consolation, not to mention the many testimonies of Scripture that directly contradict it. By this doctrine mortal souls are also made to be with their bodies, and two resurrections are set up after this life. Therefore, against so profane an invention, let us meditate throughout the whole course of our life on that most happy word of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which he deigned to answer the wretched thief, for all who look to him and die in the same faith and invocation. How then, and why, should we fear death? Or how should we not rather long for it as much as it can and ought to be longed for, every hour? Why should we not embrace it with both arms when it brings us the news of so happy a change of our condition and dwelling, and becomes for us the beginning and entrance of true and eternal happiness?

units.la: En igitur in summa vt Iesus Christus, sicuti dixi quum huius textus explicationem aggressus sum, contemptoribus & irrisoribus illis mendacium impegerit, ipso suæ exinanitionis angustissimo & afflictissimo tempore, Cruci se affixum esse & in ea manere testatus, quòd hæc esset sua voluntas: Crucem ipsam esse iam sibi instar solij ad suos hostes iudicandos: denique se per illatam ab ipsis ignominiam, in possessionem sibi perpetui promissi regni iam ingredi, vt illud etiam quibuscunque videbitur communicet, frustra frendere Satana, peccato, & morte, & irritis omnibus eorum futuris conatibus in suum ipsorum caput recisuris. Sed quòd abiltis cæcis non animaduerterentur hæc spiritualia & inuisibilia testimonia, & viderentur ipsis potius ridicula somnia, testimoniis etiam aliis & signis sensibiliter obstupendis voluit quis quantúsque esset demonstrare: quæ idcirco fusè & distinctè nobis ab Euangelistis proponuntur: vnû quidem in cœlo factum ante excessum è vita: alia in terris in ipso mortis ipsius articulo: postrem mum autem in ipsis terrae penetralibus, in se-pulchris nimirum, & in ipsa mortis spelunca post suam resurrectionem, licet Matth. huic historiae illud cap.27.52.propter suae narrationis seriem inferat:ut iam tunc ipsi hostes Christi vel inuiti nollent, ipsum per Crucem in illius Regni fruitionem ingredi de quo verba facit Esa. cap. 45.23. cuius fidus interpres Paulus Philip.2.11. oportet, ait, ut ad nomen Iesu omne genu se flectat coelestium, terrestrium ac subterraneorum:tantum abest ut hostes Iesu Christi sua consilia ad optatum finem perduxerint:aut spontanea ipsius submissione nequidem vnquam nos oporteat,ab eius adoratione quam animo & corpore debemus deterreri.
units.tr: In sum, then, as I said when I began the explanation of this text, Jesus Christ has refuted those scorners and mockers by a lie of theirs. In the most narrow and afflicted time of his humiliation, he testified that he was fixed to the cross and remained on it because this was his will; that the cross itself was now to him like a throne for judging his enemies; and finally that, by the shame inflicted on him by them, he was entering into possession of the everlasting kingdom promised to him, so that he might share it with whomever he pleases. Satan, sin and death may rage in vain, and all their future attempts will be fruitless and will recoil on their own head. But because these spiritual and invisible testimonies were not noticed by the blind, and seemed to them rather ridiculous dreams, he wished to show by other testimonies, and by signs that astound the senses, how great and what kind they were. These are set out for us fully and distinctly by the Evangelists: one in heaven, made before his departure from life; another on earth, at the very moment of his death; and the last in the very depths of the earth, namely in the tombs and in the cave of death itself after his resurrection. Matthew, indeed, adds this event in chapter 27 verse 52 because of the sequence of his narrative, so that even then Christ's enemies, whether they wished it or not, saw him enter through the cross into the enjoyment of that kingdom of which Isaiah speaks in chapter 45 verse 23. Its faithful interpreter Paul says in Philippians 2:11: "that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, on earth and under the earth." So far were Christ's enemies from bringing their plans to the desired end. Nor ought we, by his voluntary submission, ever to be deterred from adoring him with mind and body, as we owe.

units.la: Narrat igitur haec historia, Dominum nostrum Iesu Christum post dictam a Pilato sententiam mortis circa tertiam horam ab ortu Solis, quo ad locum supplicij cum mille cotumeliis & couitiis ductus,esset crucique affixus, tandem circa sextam horam qui nobis est Meridies, tenebras ortas super totam regionem, vsque ad horam nonam,quae tertiae pomeridianae respondet.
units.tr: This history therefore relates that our Lord Jesus Christ, after the sentence of death pronounced by Pilate, was led to the place of punishment with a thousand insults and reproaches, and was fixed to the cross about the third hour after sunrise. Then, about the sixth hour, which for us is noon, darkness arose over the whole region and lasted until the ninth hour, which corresponds to three in the afternoon.

units.la: Minime vero Matth.aut Marcus. vnde sint aut quomodo coortae, memorant:quum saepe contingat ipso Meridie coelum ex causis naturalibus & satis ordinariis obtenebrari.Sed Tenebrarum voce aliquid amplius declaratur, & quae Lucas addit,Solem ipsum obscuratum ofstendunt nocte non minus obscuram & densam ea quae olim Aegyptum texit, cuius fit metio, Exod.10.21. Præterea non est per Tenebras vlla Solis eclipsis naturalis intelligenda, nimirum interpositu corporis Lunæ, inter Solem & terram. Nam in Solis eclipsi, verum est propter interpositionē Lunæ inter Solem & terram, non posse durante illa interpositione Solis radiis terras illustrari. At non propterea corpus eius obscuratur, præterquam quòd Lunæ corpus nunquam potest Solis totū corpus tegere, vt nunquam contigerit, nec futurū sit vt contingat integer seu totalis Solis defectus, ne siquidem centrum corporis Lunæ ex diametro opponatur centro corporis Solis inter Solem & terras. Hæc verò quum contigerint festo Iudæorum Paschatis, nempe Plenilunio Martio, Luna proinde ex diametro Soli oppositā : quum contrà Solis eclipsis nunquam nisi in ipsa Solis & Lunæ coniunctione contingat, ac proinde Nouilunio, necessario hic nō agi de vlla Solis eclipsi, sed de vera in corpore ipsius obscuratione fatendū est.
units.tr: Matthew and Mark, however, do not say whence or how the darkness arose, although it often happens that the sky is darkened at midday from natural and quite ordinary causes. But by the word "darkness" something more is declared, and what Luke adds shows that the sun itself was obscured, by a darkness no less thick and dense than that which once covered Egypt, of which mention is made in Exodus 10:21. Moreover, this darkness must not be understood as any natural eclipse of the sun, namely by the interposition of the body of the moon between the sun and the earth. For in a solar eclipse it is true that, because of the interposition of the moon between the sun and the earth, the earth cannot be lit by the sun's rays while that interposition lasts. But the body of the sun is not thereby obscured. Besides, the body of the moon can never cover the whole body of the sun, so that a total or complete eclipse of the sun has never occurred and never will occur, unless the centre of the moon's body lies exactly opposite the centre of the sun's body, between the sun and the earth. Now these events happened at the Passover feast of the Jews, namely at the full moon of March, when the moon was therefore diametrically opposite the sun. Whereas a solar eclipse happens only at the conjunction of sun and moon, and therefore at new moon, it must be admitted that no solar eclipse is meant here, but a true obscuring of the sun's body itself.

units.la: Ecquis autem præstare istud potuit nisi idem hoc Verbum Patris coæternum & coessentiale per quod Pater ab initio Lucem & Luminaria creauit? Is nempe cui nihil camro ademit, & in quo nihil Crux immutauit, aut de Deitate quidquam imminuit. Hic est igitur ille Crucifixus, cuius veram & coëssentialem Deitatem Solus iste prædicat adversus Arrianos, & quosdam alios hæreticos. Nequis verò nobis hic obiiciat Iosue illius exemplum, qui licet non Deus, tamen cum aliqua iubentis speciè, Solem & Lunam tare fecit.Iof.10.13.Nec enim Iofue vt homini Sol & Luna obtemperarunt, sed suo Creatori,per os Iosue loquenti: quum hic tamen etiam sine voce vel mandato vllo creatori suo obsequatur.
units.tr: Who, however, could bring this about except that same Word of the Father, co-eternal and co-essential, through whom the Father created light and the lights from the beginning? He is the one from whom nothing was taken away by the flesh, and in whom the cross changed nothing or diminished anything of his Deity. This, then, is the one who was crucified, whose true and co-essential Deity this very passage proclaims against the Arians and certain other heretics. And lest anyone object here the example of Joshua, who, though not God, nevertheless made the sun and moon stand still with some appearance of command (Joshua 10:13), let us note this: the sun and moon did not obey Joshua as a man, but their Creator speaking through Joshua's mouth. Yet here the sun obeys its Creator without any voice or command at all.

units.la: Verùm hic se quędam offert difficultas quòd plerique etiam ex veteribus pro eo quod legimus in textu,Supra totam regionem, legant, Supra totam terram:quam etiam expositionem ferunt voces quibus vsi sunt Euangelistæ, quasi hę tenebrę in vniuersum terrarum orbem diffusæ sint,ad hanc tuendam lectionem testimonia adferentes partim manifestè fabulosa,partim non satis firmis nixa probationibus. Sed duæ sunt manifestissimæ meo iudicio rationes,ex quibus facilè dignoscatur has tenebras ad regionem quam tunc Iudæi obtinerent, restringendas,Iudæam puta,Galilæam,& finitimas regiones. Primum enim extra omne dubium est si tantum prodigium in vniuerso terrarum orbe contigisset, omnes historicos Græcos & Latinos, immo & ipsos barbaros illud monumentis suis fuisse tradituros. Secundo loco series & scopus huius historiæ videntur satis dilucidè ostendere miraculosas illas tenebras à Deo in Iudæa immissas fuisse,sensibiliter & palpabiliter annuntiaturas huic misero populo, tū imminente sibi horrendam destructionem & excidium,tum etiam excisione à Dei fœdere, in qua adhuc hoc tempore permanent, obscuratis oculis mentis ipsorum co velaminvelamine quod notat Paulus 2.Cor.3.14.adeò vt hę tenebrę ex diametro opponantur iis quæ in tota Ægypto contigerunt, excepta terra Gozen quæ ad habitandum erat assignata Israëlitis. Exod.10.23. Quemadmodum enim illæ tenebræ minabantur Ægyptiis cæcitatem, qua sese in exitium præcipites iederunt, & contrà Dei gratiam erga suum populum indicabant: sic vice versa hæ tenebræ Iudæis imminens exitium portendentes, Gentibus etiam Solis veritatis apud eas exortum prædicebant, & temporum illorum aduentum quibus quę sub nominibus Lo-Ruhama, & Lohammi prædicta fuerant. Ose.1.6.& 9. implerentur. En quis fuerit miserorum istorum exitus, qui tam pertinaciter abusi singulari Dei gratia fuerant quos Deus à reliquis omnibus terræ populis sibi viniendos & coniungendos speciali fœdere distinxerat: adeò vt hæ tenebræ non tam aërem ipsum quàm corda perditorum istorum obscurauerint, non tantùm ad trium horarum spatium, sed etiam in perpetuum tâ in hoc quàm in futuro seculo: hodie adhuc in hanc miseram gentem incumbentibus, cui Lux illa crucifixi vertitur in velamen tanto densius & obscurius, quanto magis in Euangelij prædicatione splen-det.2. Corinth.3.15.iis quidem quibus Deus oculos aperuit. Ephes.1.18.
units.tr: But here a certain difficulty presents itself, because many even of the ancients, instead of what we read in the text, Over the whole region, read Over the whole earth. They also bring forward the interpretation of the words the Evangelists used, as if this darkness had spread over the whole orb of the earth, and to defend this reading they cite testimonies, some plainly fabulous and some resting on not very firm proofs. But in my judgment there are two very clear reasons by which it is easily recognised that this darkness must be restricted to the region which the Jews then held: namely Judea, Galilee and the neighbouring regions. First, it is beyond all doubt that if so great a prodigy had occurred throughout the whole orb of the earth, all the Greek and Latin historians, and even the barbarians themselves, would have handed it down in their records. Second, the sequence and purpose of this history seem to show quite clearly that those miraculous darkness were sent by God upon Judea, to announce sensibly and palpably to this wretched people both the horrible destruction and overthrow impending over them, and also their excision from God's covenant, in which they still remain at this time, their eyes of mind obscured by the veil that Paul mentions in 2 Corinthians 3:14. So these darkness are directly opposed to what happened in all Egypt, except the land of Goshen, which had been assigned to the Israelites for dwelling (Exodus 10:23). For just as those darkness threatened the Egyptians with blindness, by which they threw themselves headlong into destruction, and at the same time showed God's favour towards his own people, so conversely these darkness, portending the destruction hanging over the Jews, also proclaimed to the Gentiles the rising of the Sun of truth among them, and foretold the coming of those times when what had been foretold under the names Lo-Ruhamah and Lo-Ammi (Hosea 1:6, 9) would be fulfilled. Behold the outcome for these wretched people, who abused so obstinately the singular grace of God, and whom God had set apart from all the other peoples of the earth to be joined and united to himself by a special covenant. So these darkness obscured not merely the air but the hearts of these lost people, not only for the space of three hours but also for ever, in this age and in the age to come. Today still they lie heavy upon this wretched nation, for whom that light of the crucified One turns into a veil all the thicker and darker, the more it shines in the preaching of the Gospel (2 Corinthians 3:15), except for those to whom God has opened the eyes (Ephesians 1:18).

units.la: Quid verò, aliquem ex hac historia fructum percipiamus, nos iuuabit ingratam prorsus nationem nostro calculo notare & detestari, si peiores illa fumus? Nóf-ne verò adeò
units.tr: But what fruit shall we take from this history? It will help us to mark and detest that utterly ungrateful nation by our own reckoning, if we are no better than they. Surely we are not so

units.la: E. j. fore stupidos & amentes vt nobis perfuadea- mus cum qui non pepercit ramis naturalibus, Iudæis ab Abrahamo oriundis,parcitum o-leaftris,nobis nimirum Gentibus in eorum locū infititiis,fi nos in maiore culpa quàm ipsos deprehenderit? Non ita sentit Paulus Rom. 11. 21. 2.Cor.3.18. prædicens fore vt quum plenitu-do Gentiū introierit, reliqui etiam excindan-tur: & contrà Israel renocetur, quod etiam ipsum Prophetæ plurimis locis testantur. Sed esto,ne sint illa prædicta,nonne Deum iustum esse iudicem oportet? & seruum qui Domini voluntatem sciuit,nec ex eius voluntate fecit pluribus plagis cædi:Luc.12.47. Dicitur igitur hoc loco Sol obscuratus ab hora sexta ad no-nam,ita notatis horrendis illis tenebris adhuc hanc nationem obtenebranibus,quæ verum ad ipsam cœlitus missum Solem neglexit.Quid verò nos?Quales obsecro, quantæque tenebræ per multa seculā Christianismum obruerunt, donec verus ille Sol particulam Occidentis limpidissimo suo splendore cœpit illustrare, interea reliqua mundi parte,in densissimis illis suis tenebris magis ac magis in dies augescen-tibus immersa? Et,quæso,ab hinc paucis annis quot & quales Soles, vel saltem qualia sydera, vt vocantur à Daniele cap.8.& 10:& qualia luminaria,Philipp. 2.15. occiderunt?Immo quot iam candelabra partim extincta sunt, partim iam iam in medio nostrūm extinguenda videtur? Iudæi igitur quibus nominatim Messias erat promissus, non tantùm non agnouerunt cum, sed quod peius est crudelissime & ignominiosissime Cruci affixerunt. Quid vero nos qui Christianum nomen iactamus, inter quos remanserunt notae fœderis, nempe Baptismus, & Sacrae Scripturae, vt olim erat apud Iudæos reliqua circumcisio, & Sacerdotij exterioris forma, annon adhuc peius istis facimus? Nec enim vnquam apud veterem populum tanta Lux veritatis Euangelica resplenduit quanta per Apostolorum prædicationem Patribus nostris illuxit, & ab ipsis est credita. Fateor Christum præsentem manibus nostris non adesse, supra cœlos omnes euectum, (adeo vt excipi tractarique amplius non possit vt est à Iudæis exceptus & tractatus) & titulis etiam ipsi conuenientibus à nobis ornari. At si de recipienda eius doctrina agitur, quis dubitat Christum si eo quo in terras olim habitu venit, eodem ad nos rediret, etiam eodem modo à persecutoribus tractandum quo misera eius membra ab ipsis tractantur? Quod ad Græcas Ecclesias in Oriente reliquas in mediis sordibus Mahumetanorum, aut versus Meridiem Abyssinas, quatus horror est veritatem tantopere deformatam intueri variis erroribus, qui pedetentim in eas irrepserunt, quæ partim fama ad nos delata partim etiam ex scriptis ipsorum cognoscimus? Sed vt de iis dicamus quæ ipsi noltris oculis intuemur & auribus percipimus, qualem hodie dixeris reliquum in Occidente Christiamismum? An vnquam orbis terrarum genuit Atheorum & Epicureorum tantam multitudinem,non tantum in moribus,sed etiam in ipsa fide & religione? Annon testes istius impietatis in omnibus linguis tot prophani libri passim in hoc Christianismo sparsi conspiciuntur? Et quum Deus nostro seculo linguarum cognitionem velut antea sepultam suscitarit,bonarumque literarum studia in quibus erat proficiendum, nonne contra videmus alios quidem amisso gustu sapientiae veri Dei, nihil minus quàm de salutis doctrina cogitare? alios parum memores moniti Apostolici Col. 2. 18. & 1.Tim.6.20.sed veteris cuiusdam dictum ratum facientes, Philosophos putà patriarchas esse haereticorum, vix vllum fidei nostrae articulum intactum relinquere quod suis imaginationibus miserè non inficiant? Annò Arriani sua Deitate illum spoliantes rediuiu i sunt? Annon Marcionitae,eius humanitatem in spectrum transformantes,in Vbiquitariis,Transubstantiatoribus & Consubstantiatoribus resurrexerunt? Annon est revocatus Pelagianismus in Libero arbitrio & meritis praeparatoriis? Annon instauratus Pharisaismus im falsa bonorum operum doctrina? Annò tamè Caiaphas & Scribae noltri temporis, (quum ij de quibus haec historia loquitur, non potuerint à Pilato impetrare, vt crucifixi capiti superimpositus titulus, quo continebantur in summa quae ad Christi officium spectant, mutaretur) ipsimet cum plus quàm Diabolica audacia renuulse-runt,lesum Christum,quantum in ipsis est Regia spirituali ipsius dignitate, auctoritate praedicadicanti Euangelicam doctrinā, & suo perpetuo Sacerdotio spoliantes? Immo, annon eum ex Cruce, vt ita dicam, auellunt, quotidie suis manibus Deo Patri offerendum? Sane omnino, dum ore quidem eum Seruatorem & Redemptorem dicunt, sed Crucem nō Crucifixum adorant, iis non admodum dissimiles, à quibus per contemptum spinis coronatus est & Rex Iudæorum salutatus.
units.tr: stupid and foolish as to persuade ourselves that he who did not spare the natural branches, the Jews descended from Abraham, will spare the wild olive branches, that is, us Gentiles grafted in their place, if he finds us guilty of greater fault than they. Paul does not think so, Rom. 11:21; 2 Cor. 3:18, foretelling that when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, the rest will also be cut off, and on the contrary Israel will be called back, as the Prophets also attest in very many places. But grant that these things were not foretold: must not God be a just judge, and must not the servant who knew his master's will and did not act according to it be beaten with many stripes? Luke 12:47. So the sun is said in this place to have been darkened from the sixth hour to the ninth, marking those dreadful shadows that still darken this nation, which neglected the true Sun sent to it from heaven. But what of us? What, I ask you, and how great, were the shadows that overwhelmed Christianity through many ages, until that true Sun began to illuminate a part of the West with its most clear splendour, while the rest of the world remained immersed in those very dense shadows, growing thicker day by day? And, I ask, how many and what suns, or at least what stars (as they are called by Daniel, ch. 8 and 10), and what lights (Phil. 2:15), have gone down within these few years? Indeed, how many candlesticks have already been partly extinguished, and now seem about to be extinguished in the midst of us? The Jews, therefore, to whom the Messiah had been promised by name, not only did not recognise him, but, worse, most cruelly and most shamefully nailed him to the Cross. But what of us, who boast of the Christian name, and among whom the marks of the covenant remain, namely Baptism and the Holy Scriptures, just as among the Jews of old remained circumcision and the outward form of the priesthood? Do we not still do worse to them? For never among the ancient people did so great a light of Gospel truth shine as shone upon our fathers through the preaching of the Apostles, and was believed by them. I confess that Christ is not present in our hands, having been carried above all the heavens (so that he can no longer be received and handled as he was by the Jews), and that we adorn him with titles that befit him. But if the question is of receiving his doctrine, who doubts that if Christ returned to us in the same form in which he once came upon earth, he would be treated by persecutors in the same way that his wretched members are now treated by them? As for the Greek Churches remaining in the East amid the filth of the Mahometans, or the Abyssinians to the south, what a horror it is to behold the truth so deformed by the various errors that crept into them little by little, which we know partly by report and partly from their own writings! But to speak of those things which we see with our own eyes and perceive with our own ears, what would you say of the Christianity that remains today in the West? Has the world ever produced such a multitude of atheists and Epicureans, not only in morals but even in faith and religion? Are not witnesses of this impiety seen everywhere in this Christianity, so many profane books scattered abroad in every language? And since God in our age has, as it were, raised up the knowledge of languages that had been buried before, and the study of good letters in which we ought to make progress, do we not on the contrary see some who, having lost the taste for the wisdom of the true God, think nothing less than about the doctrine of salvation; and others, little mindful of the Apostle's warning (Col. 2:18; 1 Tim. 6:20), who make valid the saying of an old man that the philosophers are the patriarchs of heretics, and leave hardly any article of our faith untouched that they do not wretchedly taint with their own fancies? Have the Arians returned, stripping him of his Deity? Have the Marcionites, transforming his humanity into a phantom, risen again among the Ubiquitarians, Transubstantiators and Consubstantiators? Has Pelagianism been revived in free will and preparatory merits? Has Pharisaism been restored in the false doctrine of good works? And yet, since those of whom this history speaks could not obtain from Pilate that the title placed over the crucified head, in which was summed up what pertains to Christ's office, should be changed, do Caiaphas and the scribes of our time themselves, with more than diabolical audacity, refuse to acknowledge Jesus Christ as King in his spiritual dignity and authority, while he preaches the Gospel doctrine, and strip him of his perpetual priesthood? Indeed, do they not tear him, so to speak, from the Cross, to be offered daily to God the Father by their own hands? Certainly, while with their mouths they call him Saviour and Redeemer, but adore the Cross and not the Crucified, they are not very unlike those by whom he was crowned with thorns in mockery and saluted as King of the Jews.

units.la: Nos verò quibus Deus quòd ad scientiam oculos dedit, quid aliud vt plurimum facimus, prauum conscientiam habentes & inordinatè vitam agentes quàm quod eum & doctrinam eius infidelium vocibus blasphemis & ludibrio exponimus? Rom. 2 14.1. Tim. 6.1. Et vt verbo dicam, annon illud est eum aperte, cuius nomine gloriamur, contemnere & irridere? Denique, quum vel apud ipsos Turcas capitale sit blasphemas voces in Iesum Christum proferre, nonne in solis iis regionibus quæ hodie tam falsò Christi nomine gloriantur, blasphemis vocibus totus aër personat? Et ita quidem Iesus Christus proscinditur ac lacerarur, vt non eius capiti, non sanguini, non carni, non corpori parcatur? O vtinam verò tam procul hęc à nobis fierent, quàm prope tamē accesserunt! Quid nobis igitur miseris futurum putamus? Agite, agite, inquā, vos tāti sceleris, auctores, plorate, & gemite, Deiqz irā in nos & vos amplius prouocare definite. Vos verò, Domini, qui à Domino sceptrum quod gestatis, accepistis, vt si tempus adhuc est, tanto malo medeamini, recipsa testamini quantopere vobis illa disputiceant. Nos vero, fratres, saltem ploremus & gemamus, Loti inter Sodomitas exemplum imitati, de quo Apostolus 2.Pet.2.8. & cum Dauide dicamus, Psal.26.9. Ne colligas cum peccatoribus animam nostram, & cum viris sanguinolentis vitam nostram. Abstit autem vt vel ad punctum temporis segnescamus: nam comminationibus nullus amplius locus est, quandoquidem tantopere iusti diuini furoris ignis exarsit, testibus tota Asia, totaque Aphrica, sub horrenda illa apostasia Mahumetana, vt vnicus superstit in Europa angulus hoc igne penitus consumendus: Et quidem, inquā, Penitus, quū pauci superstint siue respicias (spiritualem administratione, adeo quidē obscurata vt iam a multis seculis perditus ille sedeat in medio templi Dei: siue temporale) qui non scortū illud adoret, vino scortationis ipsius inebriati: quū huc accedat praeterea, parum abesse quin diuina patientia tandiu Gentes ad poenitentiam exspectarit, a prima ipsarum conuersione per Apostolorum praedicationem ad hoc vsque tempus, quandiu genus humanum tolerauit a creatione mundi vsque ad diluuium: & Israelitas ab ingressu in terram Chanaan, ad hanc vsque hiltoriam ipsis lamentabilem. Abstit autem haec proferam, quasi tempora suppu tatu- rus, vt plerique fanatici, quos etiam sua somnia non pudet in vulgus emittere. Sed quum animadvertam Gentium plenitudinem de qua loquitur Apostolus. Rom. 11.25. impleri, quatenus nus in dies Lucis diuinæ beneficium minuitur: & passim omnem iniquitatem abundare, vt ad cumulū venisse videatur: &spirituales tenebras in vniuersum orbē magis ac magis incumbere, longè densiores & periculosiores iis de quibus hic agitur, aio nunquam nobis maiorem necessitatem incubuisse accensas lampades, virginum illarum sapientum instar, præparandi: quum sit verisimile sponsum hunc media nocte venturum, diu amplius tardare non posse, Matth.25.6.&10. Tunc verò quanta felicitate nuptias illas ingressi perfruentur. Faxit Deus Opt.Max. vt in hoc numero censeamur, déque istis tam sedulò cogitemus, vt nos nunquā incautos deprehendi contingat.
units.tr: But we, to whom God has given eyes for knowledge, what else do we for the most part do, having a corrupt conscience and living disorderly lives, than expose him and his doctrine to the blasphemous voices of unbelievers and to ridicule? Rom. 2:14; 1 Tim. 6:1. And, to put it in a word, is it not to despise and mock openly the very one in whose name we glory? Finally, since even among the Turks themselves it is a capital offence to utter blasphemous words against Jesus Christ, do not blasphemous voices resound through the whole air in those regions alone which today so falsely boast of the name of Christ? And so Jesus Christ is torn and mangled, and nothing of him is spared: not his head, not his blood, not his flesh, not his body! O that these things were as far from us as they have come near! What then do we suppose will become of us wretched people? Come, come, I say, you authors of so great a crime: weep and groan, and cease to provoke God's wrath further against yourselves and us. And you, lords, who have received from the Lord the sceptre you bear, if there is still time to heal so great an evil, show by your deeds how greatly those things displease you. But we, brothers, at least let us weep and groan, imitating Lot among the Sodomites, of whom the Apostle speaks (2 Pet. 2:8), and let us say with David (Ps. 26:9): Do not gather my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men. Far be it from us to grow lukewarm even for a moment; for there is no longer any room for threats, since the fire of just divine wrath has been kindled so fiercely, all Asia and all Africa witnessing it under that horrible Mahometan apostasy, so that the one corner of Europe that remains is to be wholly consumed by this fire. And indeed I say wholly, since few remain, whether you look at the spiritual administration, so obscured that for many ages that perdition has sat in the midst of God's temple, or at the temporal, which no one adores except that harlot, drunk with the wine of her fornication. Moreover, it is added that divine patience has waited so long for the Gentiles to repent, from their first conversion through the preaching of the Apostles down to this time, nearly as long as the human race endured from the creation of the world to the flood, and as long as the Israelites from their entry into the land of Canaan down to this history, so lamentable for them. Far be it from me to set forth these things as if I were computing times, like many fanatics, who are not ashamed to publish their dreams to the common people. But since I perceive that the fullness of the Gentiles of which the Apostle speaks (Rom. 11:25) is being completed, insofar as the benefit of divine Light is daily diminished, and iniquity everywhere abounds as if it had come to its height, and spiritual darkness settles more and more upon the whole world, far denser and more perilous than those of which we are speaking, I say that never before has greater necessity pressed upon us to prepare our lamps lit, like those wise virgins; since it is likely that this Bridegroom will come at midnight and cannot delay much longer (Matt. 25:6, 10). Then indeed, with what happiness will they enter those nuptials and enjoy them! May God, best and greatest, grant that we be counted in this number, and think on these things so diligently that we never happen to be found unwary.

units.tr: HOMILY THIRTY-SECOND.

units.tr: MATTHEW 27.

units.la: 46. Circiter verò horam nonam exclamauit Iesus voce magna, dicens, Eli, Eli, Lama-sabachtani? Hoc est, Deus mi, Deus mi, cur deseruisti me?
units.tr: 46. About the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?" That is, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"

units.la: 47. Quidam autem ex iis qui illic stabant, quum audissent, dicebant: Eliam vocat iste.
units.tr: 47. Some of those standing there, when they heard it, said, "This man is calling Elijah."

units.la: Ec. iiij. hoc audissent, dicebant, Eliam vocat iste.
units.tr: Ec. iiij. When they heard this, they said, "This man is calling Elijah."

units.la: 48. Et statim currens quidam ex eis quum acceptam spongiam impleuisset aceto & circumposuisset calamo, dedit ei vt biberet.
units.tr: 48. And at once one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink.

units.la: 49. Reliqui vero dicebant, Sine, videamus an veni at Elias seruaturus eum.
units.tr: 49. But the rest said, "Leave him alone; let us see whether Elijah will come to save him."

units.la: MARC. 15.
units.tr: MARK 15.

units.la: 34. Et hora nona clamauit Iesus voce magna, dicens, Eloi, Eloi, Lamma sabacthani? quod est, siquis interpretetur, Deus mi, Deus mi, cur me deseruisti?
units.tr: 34. And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?" which, if anyone translates it, means, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"

units.la: 35. Et quidam asstantium quum audissent, dicebant, Ecce, Eliam vocat.
units.tr: 35. And some of those standing by, when they heard it, said, "Look, he is calling Elijah."

units.la: 36. Cucurrit autem quidam, & impleta spongia, aceto, & arundini circumposita dedit ei potum, dicens, Sinite: videamus an veniat Elias ad eum detrahendum.
units.tr: 36. And someone ran and, filling a sponge with vinegar and putting it on a reed, gave him a drink, saying, "Leave him alone; let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down."

units.la: LVC. 23.
units.tr: LUKE 23.

units.la: 46. Quúmque clamasset voce magna, Iesus ait, Pater in manus tuas depono spiritum meum. Et quum hæc dixisset, exspirauit.
units.tr: 46. And when he had cried out with a loud voice, Jesus said, "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit." And when he had said this, he breathed his last.

units.la: IOH. 19.
units.tr: JOHN 19.

units.la: 28. Postea quũ sciret Iesus reliqua omnia iâ perfecta esse, vt perficeretur Scriptura, dixit, Sitio.
units.tr: 28. Afterwards, since Jesus knew that all things were now finished, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, he said, "I thirst."

units.la: 29. Vas igitur illic erat positum aceto plenum. Illi vero impleuerunt spongiam aceto, & hyssopo circumpositam admouerunt ori eius.
units.tr: 29. A vessel full of vinegar was standing there. So they filled a sponge with vinegar, put it on a hyssop stalk, and held it to his mouth.

units.la: I peccatis nostris grauis tantum aliquis cruciatus deberetur, quæ hactenus de Iesu Christi perpessionibus accepimus nobis liberandis suffecissent: sed quum peccato-
units.tr: Our sins deserved some torment so great that the sufferings of Jesus Christ we have heard of so far would have been enough to free us. But since the wages of our sins is death,

units.la: Vadem ac sponsorem nostrum oportuit tu corpore tuo
units.tr: our surety and sponsor had to suffer both in his body and in his soul,

units.la: catorum nostrorum stipédium sit mors, Chri- stum etiam oportuit veré pro nobis mori, vt nos peccatis nostris exsoluerët. Et hoc ipsum veterafacrificia repræsentabant,in quibus pe- cudes non tantùm ad altare trahebantur, sed earum etiam fundebatur sanguis,sine cuius ef- fusione non fiebat remissio.Heb. 9.22. An igi- tur Iesum Christum sese pro nobis ad mortem vsque,quæ separatio est corporis ab anima de- misisse, scire & credere satis est? Minimè pro- culdubio, nisi hæc mors speciali quadam con- ditione notetursine cuius consideratione non esset nobis Christi mors vita. Vehemen- ter igitur illi falsi sunt & falluntur adhuc, qui in his Christi perpessionibus, & in hac ipsius morte nominatim,nihil aliud quàm dolores corporeos, sensuales & naturales intuentur. Nam(vt copiosè disseruimus, in precationis à Iesu Christo in horro factæ explicatione)si hoc esset, profectò Iesus Christus perfectissimum omnis veræ & sanctæ magnanimitatis & fortitudinis exemplar, & per cuius vnius Spiritu Dei filij in omnibus suis miseriis corroborantur,Philip.4 13.dicendus esset longè magis abiecto & fracto animo fuisse quàm multæ Martyrum myriades, cuiusuis sexus, ætatis & conditionis,in quos sæuitum est omni genere crudelitatis & horrendorum cruciatuum quos Satanæ & subiectorum ipsius Ecclesiam persequentium rabies suggessit. Iesu Christi igitur mors talis est qualem peccata nostra merentur, ac proinde vadem & sponsorem nostrum oportuit pati non tantum dolores & cruciatus animæ & corpori communes, vsque ad animæ exhalationem: sed istis etiam accedere quod summum est, sensum nimirum in ipsa anima horrendi furoris quem peccata omnium electorum qui sunt, fuerunt & futuri sunt ad seculorum vsque consummationem, merebantur.
units.tr: since the wages of our sins is death, Christ also had truly to die for us, so that he might release us from our sins. The old sacrifices also represented this very thing: animals were not only led to the altar, but their blood was poured out, and without that shedding there was no forgiveness (Heb. 9.22). Is it therefore enough to know and believe that Jesus Christ gave himself up for us even to death, which is the separation of the body from the soul? Certainly not, unless this death is marked by a special condition, and without considering that condition Christ's death would not be life for us. Those men are therefore greatly mistaken, and still deceived, who in these sufferings of Christ, and in this death of his in particular, look at nothing but bodily, sensual and natural pains. For (as we discussed at length in our explanation of the prayer Jesus made in the garden) if that were so, Jesus Christ, the most perfect pattern of all true and holy magnanimity and courage, through whose Spirit alone the sons of God are strengthened in all their miseries (Phil. 4:13), would have to be said to have been far more cast down and broken in spirit than the many myriads of martyrs of every sex, age and condition, against whom every kind of cruelty and horrible torment was inflicted, which the rage of Satan and of his subjects who persecute the Church suggested. Christ's death was therefore such as our sins deserved. Accordingly, our surety and sponsor had to suffer not only the pains and torments common to soul and body, up to the breathing out of the soul, but to these there had to be added, which is the greatest of all, the sense of the horrible wrath in the soul itself, which the sins of all the elect, who are, have been, and will be until the end of the ages, deserved.

units.la: Quoniam autem peccatis nostris reddimur debitores, non tantum morti primæ, quæ separatio est corporis ab anima, quam sequitur corruptio corporis: sed etiam morti secundæ, quæ est corporis & animæ repetita copulatio, cum perpetua Dei maledictione coniuncta, & poenis inenarrabilibus & in æternum duraturis iusti ipsius furoris, quæri non immerito potest quomodo igitur apud Deum penitus liberati simus eo quod debebamus, nisi Mediator & Redemptor noster mortem utramque pro nobis passus sit. Aio primùm, quandoquidem reconciliator noster, qui idem pro nobis spopondit, non potuit nos à maledictione Dei defendere qua ipse obrutus fuisset, sequi necessario sic oportuit ipsum cum morte prima luctari, ut victor tandem eluctaretur: secundam autem aliter deglutare quàm qui ea opprimuntur.
units.tr: Since we are made debtors to God by our sins, not only to the first death, which is the separation of the body from the soul and is followed by the corruption of the body, but also to the second death, which is the reunion of body and soul, joined with a perpetual curse of God and with unspeakable punishments of his just wrath that will last for ever, it can rightly be asked how we could ever be fully freed before God from what we owed, unless our Mediator and Redeemer had suffered both deaths for us. I answer first: since our reconciler, who also made the promise for us, could not defend us from the curse of God by which he himself would have been crushed, it was necessary that he should wrestle with the first death in such a way as to come forth at last as victor, but that he should swallow the second in a different way from those who are overwhelmed by it.

units.la: Deinde facile ad hanc quæstionem responderi posse, si consideremus cur primam mortem excipiat secunda, quod nimirum in priore non inueniant remedium aduersus secundam qui ad utramque damnati sunt. Primus igitur Adamus seque suosque posteros ad mortem primam & secundam obstrinxit, ad primam quidem,
units.tr: Next, this question can easily be answered if we consider why the second death follows the first, namely because those condemned to both find no remedy against the second in the first. The first Adam, therefore, bound himself and his posterity to the first death and the second: to the first indeed,

units.la: Quomodo Christus persolutis omnibus quæ debebamus mortem primam in vitæ in troitu per mutatur seque & suos à secunda mortè vindicauit. dem, quod se vsu vitæ præsentis indignum reddiderit: ad secundam verò quod sua rebellione felicem illam immortalitatem, (quam tamen acceperat hac conditione vt Creatorem perpetuò agnosceret) in horrendam immortalitatem commutarit, mortis potius æternæ quàm vitæ dignam nomine. At Creator optimus ac summè misericors ex hoc lapsu arrepta occasione admirandam suam bonitatem maioribus adhuc argumentis quàm vnquam hactenus patefaciendi erga eos quos eligeret ex mera gratia, voluit Filium suum assumpta integra nostra natura tum corpore tum animo ex posteris Adami, sed eadem purissima & sanctissima per Sanctum eius Spiritum, vadem ac spontaneum hominum fieri, in quo sic suorum electorum peccata puniret, vt morte priore sterneretur via non ad mortem secundam, & æternam, sed ad veram & æternam vitam, longè felictiorem infinitis partibus ea quam in Adamo perdiderant. Iesus Christus igitur sponsor noster primam hanc mortem subiit, coniunctam cum omnibus apprehensionibus & pauoribus iræ ac furoris Dei, quibus infideles mortui à prima morte ad secundam transeunt. Sed quoniam sponte mortis prioris dolores subiit cum ea quam dixi conditione, & coniunctam cum apprehensione & terrore secundæ, & quidem eam ingressus est cum spontanea perfectissima & sanctissima obedientia, primorum parentum nostrorum oppositā rebellioni, idcirco etiam exēptus est à corporis corruptione, mortis prioris effecto : multóque magis exemptus poenis æternis mortis secundæ : facta sibi contra per priorem mortem via in gloriam veræ vitæ, tum sibi, tum iis quos Pater ipsi dedit, & pro quibus naturam nostram assumpsit & glorificauit, etsi hæc inter caput & membra differentia est, quòd caput se à corruptione corporis etiam vendicauit, quamtamen eius membra pati necesse est, tanquam mediam viam inter hanc vitam & illam æternam. In aliis autem mors prima vires suas naturales retinet: & quoniam extra Christum ex hac vita excedunt in eadem rebellione & peruersitate in qua vixerunt, & iunctis iterum corporibus & animabus, accepta condemnatione iustissima cum Diabolis, perseueraturi sunt in odio iudicis, magis etiam ac magis augendo : necessario etiam iustus Dei furor in eos exarsurus est & augedus in perpetuum, vt hac tota passim historia docemur. Certissima sane & indubitata doctrina, siue de illa cogitemus, siue non, tantum adferens Dei filiis consolationis, quantum misericordiæ Dei contemptoribus confusionis. Iesus Christus igitur morte sua potentissimè & fortissimè tam mortem priorem quàm secundæ terrores & apprehensiones superauit, & Dei furorem erga suos omnes electos & credentes, ex quibus eius Ecclesia colligitur, placauit: defluente hac virtute à capite in membra, non tamen sine maxima luêta humanitatis, ex qua ipsemet licet esset iustissimus, & Spiritum accepisset sine mensura, nunquam emerfiflet, nisi ipsius Deitas naturam nostram in ipso ne succumberet, sustinuisset.
units.tr: How Christ, having paid all that we owed, passes through the first death into life and vindicates himself and his from the second death. The first man, by his use of the present life, made himself unworthy of it, and to the second death, because by his rebellion he changed that happy immortality, which he had received on the condition that he should always acknowledge his Creator, into a dreadful immortality, worthy of the name of eternal death rather than life. But the best and most merciful Creator, seizing the occasion of this fall, willed to show his wonderful goodness, with greater proofs than ever before, toward those whom he would choose out of pure grace. He willed that his Son, taking our whole nature, both body and soul, from the posterity of Adam, but that same nature in its most pure and holy state, through his Holy Spirit, should become the surety and voluntary substitute of men. In him he would so punish the sins of his elect that by the first death a way would be laid open, not to the second and eternal death, but to true and eternal life, infinitely happier than that which they had lost in Adam. Jesus Christ, therefore, our sponsor, underwent this first death, joined with all the apprehensions and terrors of the wrath and fury of God by which unbelieving dead pass from the first death to the second. But since he undertook the pains of the first death voluntarily, under the condition I have named, and joined with the apprehension and terror of the second, and entered it with a voluntary, most perfect and most holy obedience, set against the rebellion of our first parents, for this reason he was also freed from the corruption of the body, which is the effect of the first death, and much more freed from the eternal punishments of the second death, the way to the glory of true life having been made for himself through the first death, both for himself and for those whom the Father gave him, and for whom he assumed and glorified our nature. Although there is this difference between the head and the members: the head has also claimed for itself exemption from the corruption of the body, while its members must nonetheless suffer it, as a middle way between this life and that eternal one. In others, however, the first death keeps its natural force; and since those who depart from this life outside Christ do so in the same rebellion and perversity in which they lived, and when their bodies and souls are joined again, having received the most just condemnation together with the devils, they will persist in hatred of the Judge, increasing it more and more. Therefore the just wrath of God will necessarily blaze up against them and be increased for ever, as this whole history teaches us in many places. This is a most certain and undoubted doctrine, whether we think about it or not, bringing as much consolation to the sons of God as confusion to the despisers of God's mercy. Jesus Christ, therefore, by his death, most powerfully and most bravely overcame both the first death and the terrors and apprehensions of the second, and appeased the wrath of God toward all his elect and believers, out of whom his Church is gathered. This power flowed from the head into the members, yet not without the greatest struggle of his humanity; and that humanity, though he was most just and had received the Spirit without measure, would never have come through, unless his Deity had sustained his human nature in him so that it should not succumb.

units.la: En causam etiam cur Iesus Christus quum ad tempus nihil aliud videret nec apprehen- deret in suis illis summis angoribus, & quos humanitate patiebatur cruciatibus, nisi Patris vultum iratum, & horrendi furoris plenum advertisse, tanquam vadem & sponsorem nostrum, tantopere fit perterritus, vt etiam grumos sanguinis in terram defluentes sudarit. Contrà filij Dei videntes & apprehendentes in morte vera fide Patrem sibi reconciliatum, & Seruatorem vlnas tendentem, quorum ad se sursum attractas animas excipiat, tatisper dum corpora quiescunt, vltimo die tandem incorruptione vestienda, magnopere laetantur vt qui stadium suae peregrinationis decurrerint. Ecquis vero non obstupescat admiratus Dei nostri sapientiam, bonitatem & immensam misericordiam in tantis istis tamque sublimibus & incomprehensibilibus mysteriis, quibus in libertatem asserimur ab eo qui pro nobis ligatus & vinctus est: cuius condemnatione, absoluimur: morte, vitam adipiscimur: sepultura, incorruptione induimur: & cuius tandem cruce veluti per scalas in gloriam caelestem ascendimus: si modo tamen ex tanto iudicij Dei in nostrum sponsorem effusi furore discamus quantum sit Deum offendere, & peccatum detestemur renuntiantes nobis ipsis, & tanquam filij Lucis ambulemus in mensura Spiritus: & miseri huius latronis conuersi monstrata vestigia legentes, singuli nostrum ex hac vita excedentes, in illam beatam Paradisi sedem & quietem peruenïamus, in quam receptum fuisse superius audiuimus.
units.tr: Here too is the reason why Jesus Christ, when for a time he saw and perceived nothing in his extreme anguish and the torments he suffered in his humanity but the angry face of the Father, full of dreadful wrath, was so terrified, as our surety and sponsor, that he even sweated drops of blood falling to the ground. On the contrary, the Sons of God, seeing and grasping by true faith in death the Father reconciled to them, and the Saviour stretching out his arms to receive their souls drawn up to him, rejoice greatly while their bodies rest, until on the last day they are finally clothed with incorruption, as men who have run the course of their pilgrimage. Who indeed would not be astonished, marvelling at the wisdom, goodness and immense mercy of our God in such lofty and incomprehensible mysteries, by which we are set free by him who was bound and fettered for us; by whose condemnation we are absolved, by whose death we obtain life, by whose burial we are clothed with incorruption, and by whose cross we ascend as if by a ladder into heavenly glory. This holds provided that, from the outpouring of God's judicial wrath against our surety, we learn how great a thing it is to offend God, detest sin, deny ourselves, and walk as children of the light in the measure of the Spirit; and that, reading the footsteps of that wretched thief who was converted, each of us, departing this life, may come to that blessed seat and rest of Paradise into which we heard above that he was received.

units.la: Quibus ita positis facilior fit nobis expositio miserandae & stupendae illius Domini nostri Iesu Christi quereláe paulo ante quàm Spiritum emitteret: stupendae, inquam, vt quę primo intuitu videtur directè & ex diametro repugnare iis omnibus quae de Christo nobis credenda sunt & in eo quaerenda. Nam, dicat aliquis his non bene intellectis, hac querelam, non aliunde quàm ab animo indignante profectam. At si indignatus est, quinam eius obedientia voluntaria dicetur? At ni voluntaria fuisset, quomodo rebellionem nostram suscitasset? Praeterea quinã à Patre fuisset derelictus, quin & à seipso & à S. Spiritu derelictus fuisset, siquidem eadem Deitate cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto Deus est? Id vero si ita est, quinam Seruator noster erit, quum vere & propriè nostra salus ab vnico Deo procedat viuificam mortem nostri Redemptoris nobis efficiente?
