What, then, should we do, looking upon him with the eyes of faith and calling upon him as he now sits victorious at the right hand of God the Father? Such was the desire of the Apostle, Phil. 1.23; Rom. 7.24. Yet this too must be pursued toward that same goal which the same Apostle teaches, Phil. 3.12, 14.

units.la: Notanda praeterea vox qua vtitur Dominus ad nostram consolationem, quae non quidem simpliciter aliquid in alterius manu ponere significat, sed tanquam depositum committere depositario, de cuius conscientia & bona fide minimè dubitetur. Ac siquis est inter homines bonę fidei contractus, id est depositum: adeò vt depositarius fidem fallens, aut aequo negligentior, eiusdem rei ablatæ compensatione non liberetur, Exod. 22. 7. Quis verò patre nostro cœlesti, fidelior est depositarius? de quo loquitur Apostolus 2. Tim. 4.8. Custos, inquam, ille Israëlis, qui nunquam dormitat? Psal. 121. 4. adeò vt nulla vnquam ex eius ouibus per ignauiam aut imprudentiam sit peritura? Et cuius etiam tanta vis est vt Leoni comparetur, cui prœda quam non deuorandam sed seruandam cepit, nunquam possit eripi? Esa. 31. 4. Quid amplius? Qui in Patris manus animam suam & nostras commendauit, vt in fortissimi, fidelissimi, & amantissimi depositoris, suæ exinanitionis respectu, ad corporis resurrectionem vsque tantùm duraturæ, paulò post ipse noster depositarius factus est, adeò vt D. Stephanus suum illi Spiritum moriens commendarit, Act. 7. 59. quemadmodum etiam Apostolus confidit se cum illo hinc migrantem esse colligendum, Philipp. 1. 23. En igitur animas nostras in Patris cui nullus est par, manibus, de cuius potestate, fidelitate & beneuolentia nemo est qui dubitet, quum Filium vnicum nobis sibi vindicandis in mundum miserit. En earum custodem à Patre Dei vnicum Filium, retinentem se nunquam passurum sibi vllam ex suis ouibus quas dedit ei Pater eripi. Iohan. 10. 28. & adeò fidelem earum pastorem vt etiam aberrantes ipsemet requirat, nec vnquam nisi reductis illis in suum ouile conquiescat, Matt. 18. 13. & promittentem se nullam vnquam foras eiecturum. Iohan. 6. 37. En prætereà Sanctum SpiriSpiritum à quo in omnem huius salutis spem introducimur, & conseruamur. Ecquid erit igitur quod viui vel mortui metuamus, si modò ad nostri Capitis exemplum, & eiusdem virtute ad asylum istud & perfugium vnicum confugiamus?Psal.125.
units.tr: Note also the word the Lord uses for our consolation. It does not simply mean to place something in another's hand, but to commit something as a deposit to a depositary, whose conscience and good faith are not in doubt. And if there is any contract among men of good faith, it is a deposit: so that a depositary who betrays the trust, or is more careless than is fair, is not released by making compensation for the thing taken, Exod. 22.7. But who is a more faithful depositary than our heavenly Father, of whom the Apostle speaks, 2 Tim. 4.8? That guardian of Israel, I say, who never sleeps, Ps. 121.4, so that none of his sheep will ever perish through sloth or carelessness? And whose strength is such that he is compared to a lion, from whom no prey that he has seized, not to devour but to keep, can ever be snatched, Isa. 31.4? What more? He who committed his soul and ours into the hands of the Father, so that, with respect to his self-emptying, he might become, as the most strong, faithful and loving depositary, the depositary of ours a little later, for it would last only until the resurrection of the body. So it was that St. Stephen, dying, committed his spirit to him, Acts 7.59, just as the Apostle also trusted that when he departed hence he would be gathered to him, Phil. 1.23. Behold, then, our souls are in the hands of the Father, to whom there is no equal, and of whose power, faithfulness and goodwill no one can doubt, since he sent his only Son into the world to claim us for himself. Behold, the only Son of God is the guardian of them from the Father, who declares that he will never allow any of his sheep, whom the Father gave him, to be snatched from him, John 10.28; and he is so faithful a shepherd that he himself seeks out even those who have strayed, and never rests until he has brought them back into his fold, Matt. 18.13; and he promises that he will never cast out anyone. John 6.37. Behold, moreover, the Holy Spirit, by whom we are led into and kept in all hope of this salvation. What then will there be for us, living or dead, to fear, if only, following the example of our Head and by his power, we flee to that one sanctuary and refuge? Ps. 125.

units.la: Obseruanda præter illa superiora phrasis hæc, In manus tuas, qua nobis quiddam expressius significatur quàm si de Deo in genere aut eius protectione verba fierent. Nam perinde est ac si diceretur Pater non agere cum hoc deposito vt solent homines depositarij, qui sibi commissum depositum certo quodam loco custodiût, non sine metu furum, quòd nô semper vbique adsint: sed Deum veluti suis manibus continere semper sibi præsentes suorum animas, quum ex hoc mundo excedentes, suis spoliatæ corporibus maximè instar miserarum ouium errabundæ, & luporum faucibus prœda parata, videri possent. Agite igitur bono animo & alacri simus, animum adhæc aduerten- tes, & nobis in necessitatem tam certas támque eximias consolationes, præsertim in vltimam illam luctam reponamus: ante oculos nobis eum proponentes in cuius custodiam à Patre dati sumus: cuius non amplius manus Cruci affixæ tenentur quales à pictoribus nobis effinguntur, (quod si esset nequaquam nos amplecteretur) sed qui contrà liberas vlnas expandit, supernè morientium in ipso animas amplexaturus, quas sinu suo foueat, rantisper dum illæ suis corporibus reddantur in vitam æternam & spiritualem, & ipse veniat in nubibus coeli in occursum nostri, & nos vicissim in occursum Domini in aëra rapiamur, vna cum ipso parata nobis felicitate in sempiternum fruiturI. Theff.4.17.
units.tr: Besides those points mentioned above, observe this phrase, Into your hands, by which something is signified to us more expressly than if words were spoken about God in general or about his protection. For it is just as if it were said that the Father does not deal with this deposit as human depositaries usually do, who guard the deposit committed to them in some fixed place, not without fear of thieves, because they are not always and everywhere present; but that God, as it were with his own hands, always keeps the souls of his people present to himself, which, when they depart from this world, stripped of their bodies, might seem most like miserable sheep wandering, and prey laid out for the jaws of wolves. Come, then, let us be of good courage and cheerful, attending to this, and let us lay up in our need, especially in that final struggle, such certain and remarkable consolations: setting before our eyes him into whose keeping we have been given by the Father; whose hands are no longer held fixed to the Cross, as painters depict them for us (for if they were, they could by no means embrace us), but who on the contrary spreads out his free arms, from above, ready to embrace the souls of the dying in himself, to foster them in his bosom until they are restored to their bodies for eternal and spiritual life, and until he himself comes in the clouds of heaven to meet us, and we in turn are caught up to meet the Lord in the air, with him, to enjoy forever the happiness prepared for us. 1 Thess. 4.17.

units.la: Accedamus ad vltimas Domini ex hoc mundo excedentis voces, Consummatum est, admodum sane breues, sed quæ tamen sint totius Veteris Fœderis commentarius & summa totius Noui, attenta proinde consideratione dignifi-mę, & ad totius vitę nostræ consolationem applicadæ. Hic igitur agit de munere quod acceperat à Patre, quo realis & actualis executio cotinetur eorum quæ ad nos à morte liberandos & in vitam æternam alferedos requirebantur, quod ipsis Patribus statim à peccato fuerat promissum, & deinceps toto illo cultu diuino ceremoniali figuratum & adumbratum.
units.tr: Let us come to the last words of the Lord as he departed from this world, It is finished. They are very short, yet they are both the commentary on the whole Old Covenant and the summary of the whole New. They therefore deserve the most careful consideration and are to be applied to the comfort of our whole life. Here he speaks of the office he had received from the Father, which contains the real and actual execution of all that was required to free us from death and bring us to eternal life. This had been promised to the Fathers themselves immediately after the fall, and afterwards prefigured and foreshadowed in the whole ceremonial worship of God.

units.la: Hic vero duæ difficultates occurrunt, ad quas sigillatim est respondendum. Prior, quomodo Iesus Christus dixerit salutis nostræ mysterium sua morte esse completum, quum adhuc eius sepultura, Ascensio, Resurrectio & plena glorificatio superessent, etiam articuli fidei ad salutem necessarij. Aio igitur longè differre, id quo a morte liberamur, & ius ad vitam æternam acquirimus, ab eo quod adhuc supererat ad nos in possessionem istius liberationis & ius vitæ æternæ mittendos. Prius illud igitur impletum est obedientia Iesu Christi in carne sua, cuius clausula fuit mors in Cruce, iam tum eius infirmitate quam nostra causa subierat finem. nem accipiente. Merito igitur pronuntiauit impletum à se quicquid ad nos persoluto redemptionis pretio morte liberandos & ad ius vitæ æternæ nobis acquirendum integra Legis tum moralis tum Ceremonalis impletione requirebatur. Hoc igitur solum supererat, vt nos in eorum possessionem & fruitionem, quæ supra diximus, immitteret: quod suo tempore patefiet, quum nostrorum tandem corporum corruptione superata virtute eadem qua corpus eius in sepulchro à corruptione fuit immune, suscitabimur, in cœlum ascensuri, & tandem cum ipso in locis cœlestibus sessuri.
units.tr: Two difficulties arise here, and each must be answered in turn. The first is how Jesus Christ could say that the mystery of our salvation was completed by his death, when his burial, ascension, resurrection and full glorification still remained, along with the articles of faith necessary to salvation. I say, then, that what frees us from death and gives us the right to eternal life is far different from what still remained, namely, that we should be sent into possession of that liberation and of the right to eternal life. The former was therefore accomplished by the obedience of Jesus Christ in his flesh, whose end was death on the Cross, his weakness, which he had undertaken for our sake, now reaching its goal. Rightly, then, he declared finished whatever was required for us to be freed from death by the payment of the redemption price, and for the right to eternal life to be acquired for us, through the full fulfilment of both the moral and the ceremonial law. Only this remained: that he should put us into the possession and enjoyment of the things we have mentioned. This will be made plain in its time, when, the corruption of our bodies overcome, we are raised by the same power by which his body in the tomb was kept free from corruption, and ascend into heaven, to sit at last with him in the heavenly places.

units.la: Altera difficultas in eo posita est, quòd si salus hominum hac vnica Implctione nititur, Patres omnes qui Iesu Christi in carnem adventum præcesserunt, & passiones ipsius vsque ad mortem Crucis, sine spe salutis vixisse videri possint. Ad quod sic respondum esto, Iesum Christum venturum, & Iesum Christum qui venit: Iesum Christum passurū, & Iesum Christum passum, vnum & eundem esse Iesum ac Seruatorem, cuius non minor vis fuerit in sercredentibus in venturum ac passurum, quàm credentibus in passum. Idcirco testabatur Christus olim Abrahamum suum diem vidisse & lætatum esse, Ioh. 8.16. & dicitur etiam Agnus inde à mundi initio mactatus. Apocal. 13. 8. putà, quòd ad oblationis eius efficaciam: quû tâta sicut dei vis vt fit ... & ... Fides igitur verorum Pa-
units.tr: The second difficulty lies here: if the salvation of men rests on this one fulfilment, then all the Fathers who went before the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh, and his sufferings even to the death of the Cross, might seem to have lived without hope of salvation. To this it should be answered thus: Jesus Christ who is to come and Jesus Christ who came, Jesus Christ who is to suffer and Jesus Christ who has suffered, are one and the same Jesus and Saviour, whose power was no less effective for those who believed in him as coming and about to suffer than for those who believed in him as having suffered. For this reason Christ once testified that Abraham saw his day and rejoiced, John 8.16., and he is also called the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world, Rev. 13.8., namely because of the efficacy of his oblation, since so great is the power of God that ... and ... The faith, therefore, of the true Fathers...

units.la: Iesus Christus Filius Venturus in se credentes Patres re demit, non minus quàm credentes in eū qui venit & de se tradita implenis. trum sub Vetere fœdere, & nostra sub Nouo, fides vna & eadem est, in vnum Seruatorem incumbens, & ad eandem salutem aspiras, & eadem quòd ad res significatas habens Sacramenta : dicente nimirum Apostolo eos in mari fuisse in nube baptisatos: & eandem escam Spiritualem edisse, & omnes eundem potum spiritualem bibisse, qui fuit Iesus Christus. 1. Cor. 10. 2. vt vicissim nos cum ipsis Circuncifi fuisse dicimur. Coloss. 2. 11. circuncifione manu non facta : & admonemur vt festum agitemus non fermentatis panibus sinceritatis & veritatis. 1. Corinth. 5. 8. Et de illis difficultatibus hactenus.
units.tr: Jesus Christ the Son redeemed the Fathers who believed in him as the one who was to come, no less than those who believe in him as the one who has come and has fulfilled what was handed down concerning himself. The faith of the Fathers under the Old Covenant and ours under the New is one and the same, resting on one Saviour and aiming at the same salvation, and the sacraments have the same things signified. For the Apostle says that they were baptized in the cloud and in the sea, and ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink, which was Jesus Christ, 1 Cor. 10.2. In the same way we are said to have been circumcised together with them, Col. 2.11, with a circumcision not made by hands; and we are urged to keep the feast with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, 1 Cor. 5.8. And so much for those difficulties.

units.la: Ex hac praeterea Iesu Christi voce summatim colligendum nobis est quid commune inter se habeant in ipso fundamento Vetus & Nouum Fœdus, & rursus quibus in rebus differant. Hoc igitur habent inter se commune quòd vtrumque est tractatus fœderis cum Deo patre placato erga suam Ecclesiam ad salutem hominum per vnicum Mediatore Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, vt vitam æternam per eundem vnicum Seruatorem & veteres illi & nos seruati consequantur. Sed in eo discrimen est quòd Patres contentos esse oportuerit ea reuelationis mensura quam diuersis gradibus sub Leuitico ministerio variis vmbris & figuris ceremoniarum adiunctis acceperunt. Sed vbi plenitudo temporum aduenit Dei Filius in carnem visibiliter venit, tú personaliter nobis omne Dei Patris sui consilium de nonostra salute clarissimè & plenissimè declara-turus. Act.20. 27. Ioh. 15. 15. tū reipsa implctis quæ tá de ipsius persona quàm officio Mediatoris promissa fuerant & prædicta, Rom.1. 2. vmbris cæremoniarum sinem allaturus.Col.2. 17. Denique sicut Leuitico ministerio sub vetere fœdere commissa fuit in terris domus Dei administratio : ita Dei filius Sacerdos æternus assumpta in propria persona paternæ domus cura, nonsæpiùs sacrificaturus, sed annunciaturus & applicaturus fructum oblationis suæ semel factæ & suis omnibus numeris absolutæ reliquit in his terris (in cœlum nimirum quòd ad sui corporis præsentiam abiens) primùm architectos & fundatores Ecclesiæ suæ, Apostolos, Prophetas & Euangelistas Sancto Spiritu extraordinaria mensura donatos: & deinceps per & post eos misit & missurus est ad finem vsque seculorum ex ordine in Ecclesia sua instituto Pastores & doctores, Ephef.4.11.ad ædificandam quocunque terrarum loco singuli missi sint, & quibuscunque gregibus commissi sint, 1.Pet. 5. 2. cœlestem illam Ierusalem super fundamento scriptorum Propheticorum & sacrarum tabularum quas in hunc finem illi ad nostransmiserunt. Ephef. 2.20. tantisper dum Deo Patri reddito regno pacato tam salus omnium electorum & credentium per eius misericordiam, quàm iudicium reprobis & incredulis iustissimo eius furore præparatum perficiatur.1.Cor.15.25.& 28.
units.tr: From this word of Jesus Christ we must gather in summary what the Old and New Covenants hold in common at their very foundation, and again in what respects they differ. What they have in common is this: each is a covenant arrangement with God the Father, reconciled towards his Church, for the salvation of men through the one Mediator, our Lord Jesus Christ, so that both the ancients and we who are saved obtain eternal life through the same one Saviour. The difference, however, is that the Fathers had to be content with the measure of revelation they received in various degrees under the Levitical ministry, with various shadows and figures of ceremonies attached. But when the fullness of time came, the Son of God came visibly in the flesh, to declare to us personally all the counsel of God his Father concerning our salvation, most clearly and most fully, Acts 20.27; John 15.15; and in fact fulfilling what had been promised and foretold both concerning his own person and the office of Mediator, Rom. 1.2, and bringing an end to the shadows of the ceremonies, Col. 2.17. Finally, just as under the Old Covenant the administration of God's house on earth was committed to the Levitical ministry, so the Son of God, the eternal Priest, took upon himself in his own person the care of his Father's house. He was no longer going to sacrifice, but to proclaim and apply the fruit of his oblation, made once and complete in all its parts. He left in this world (when he went up to heaven, that is, to be present with his body) first the architects and founders of his Church, the Apostles, Prophets and Evangelists, endowed with the Holy Spirit in an extraordinary measure. Afterwards, through and after them, he has sent, and will send to the end of the ages, ministers and teachers, appointed in his Church in an order, Eph. 4.11, to build up that heavenly Jerusalem in whatever place on earth each one is sent, and over whatever flocks they are committed, 1 Pet. 5.2. This is built upon the foundation of the writings of the Prophets and the sacred tablets which they handed down to us for this purpose, Eph. 2.20. This will continue until the kingdom is handed back to God the Father and pacified, and both the salvation of all the elect and believers through his mercy, and the judgment prepared for the reprobate and unbelieving in his most just wrath, are brought to completion, 1 Cor. 15.25 and 28.

units.la: En, inquam, præcipuum discrimen inter Cur pra-
units.tr: Here, I say, is the chief difference between the Why pre-

units.la: Vetus & Nouum fœdus, ex quo apparet quàm sit potior Ecclesiæ præsentis conditio quàm Patrum qui sub Lege fuerunt, quod discipulos suos Christus docebat, Matth.13.17. vt non abs re Petrus testetur Prophetas diligenter inquisiuisse & scrutatos esse temporis articulum quo implerentur magna illa mysteria quæ nobis prædixerunt. 1. Pet.1.12. Sed quemadmodum Iudæis tenebras potius diligentibus quàm Lucem, veram illam & infinitā Lucem præsentiæ ipsius Dei Filij nihil profuisse videmus, Ioh.1.11. Sed contrà versam in densissimas & exitiosissimas tenebras: idem etiā maximæ parti Ecclesiarum ex nobis miseris Gentibus coactarum contigisse conspicimus, adeò vt reliquiæ sint admodum exiguæ ac pene nullæ. Faxit verò Deus vt deinde serio cogitemus, nos, inquam, ad quos ab hinc annis septuaginta hæc Lux veluti cælitus iterum demissa resplenduit ad fugandas ac dissipandas tenebras quibus maxima pars Christianismi obruebatur, longè, inquam, crassioribus & densioribus quàm illæ Iudaicæ quum ad ipsos promissus ille Messias missus est.
units.tr: Old and New Covenant. From this it appears how much better the present condition of the Church is than that of the Fathers who lived under the Law, since Christ taught this to his disciples, Matt. 13.17. So it is not without reason that Peter testifies that the Prophets diligently inquired and searched into the time at which those great mysteries would be fulfilled which they foretold to us, 1 Pet. 1.12. But just as we see that the Jews, loving the shadows rather than the Light, gained nothing from the true and infinite Light of the presence of the Son of God himself, John 1.11, but on the contrary it was turned into the thickest and most destructive darkness, we see that the same has happened to most of the Churches gathered from us wretched Gentiles, so that the remnants are very small and almost none. May God grant that we then consider seriously, we, I say, to whom this Light has shone forth again these seventy years, as if sent down anew from heaven, to put to flight and scatter the darkness by which the greater part of Christianity was overwhelmed, a darkness far thicker and denser, I say, than that Jewish darkness when the promised Messiah was sent to them.

units.la: Exempli gratia, quandoquidem Iesus Christus verè loquutus est, & quæ facta sunt, infecta esse non possunt, quanta docentium est impudentia, & quanta credentium cæcitas ad Iesu Christi meritum alia etiam accedere oportere, & ad eius mortem & passionem esse aliquam pro peccatis satisfactionem apud Deum adiciendam? Unde verò de Purgatorij doctrina, de perpetua iteratione oblationis Iesu Christi apud Deum Patrem pro viuis & mortuis tan- dem emersit? Quo verò fundamento nituntur indulgentiæ, & peccatorum remissiones pœnæ vel Culpæ? aqua lustralis venialia peccata delens, & animas in Purgatorio refrigerans, & aliæ istiusmodi voces quàm plurimæ blasphemæ & impietatis plenæ, quas in præsentia omitto, quibus,rebus etiá inanimatis, quæ Dei vnius & vnici nostri Seruatoris propria sunt tribuuntur? An verò Dominus ideò veteres ceremonias aboleuerit, & earum iugo Christianam Ecclesiam exemerit, vt nouas figuras & Sacramenta pro veteribus illis Ecclesia sibi fingeret, quarum aliæ iterum à Iudaismo manifestè manarunt, aliæ ab Ethnicismo, aliæ denique nihil nisi merę nugæ sunt, quarum author ipse Satan hominibus illudens esse videtur? Agite igitur,gratias ingentes agamus Domino,qui nobis oculos aperuit, & illis omnibus opponamus hęc pretiosissima Domini nostri nouissima verba, clarè & apertè dum Spiritum emitteret pronuntiata, quibus aduersus quaslibet tentationes conscientiæ nostræ confirmentur, vera & viua fide amplexantes integram illam, vnicam & numeris omnibus absolutissimam oblationem Iesu Christi semel à seipso factam, qua nostræ conscientiæ in perpetuum tranquillentur. En quæ consolatio ex verbis illis, breuibus quidem si sonum eorum attendas,sed tam amplis,si sensum inspicias,vt quæ in illis continentur opes exhauriri non possint.
units.tr: For example, since Jesus Christ has truly spoken, and what has been done cannot be undone, how great is the impudence of teachers, and how great the blindness of believers, who hold that something must be added to the merit of Jesus Christ, and that some satisfaction for sins must be added before God to his death and passion? From what source, indeed, did the doctrine of Purgatory, and the perpetual reiteration of the oblation of Jesus Christ before God the Father for the living and the dead, at last emerge? On what foundation do indulgences rest, and remissions of penalty or of guilt? Lustral water, which blots out venial sins and cools souls in Purgatory, and very many other such phrases, blasphemous and full of impiety, which I now pass over, by which even inanimate things are given what belongs to the one and only God and our Saviour? Or has the Lord abolished the old ceremonies and freed the Christian Church from their yoke, only so that the Church might devise for herself new figures and sacraments in place of those old ones? Some of these have clearly flowed again from Judaism, others from heathenism, and others finally are nothing but mere trifles, whose author seems to be Satan himself, mocking men. Come, then, let us give great thanks to the Lord, who has opened our eyes, and let us set against all these things these most precious last words of our Lord, spoken clearly and openly as he gave up the Spirit. By them our conscience is confirmed against any temptations, as we embrace with true and living faith that whole, unique and in every respect most complete oblation of Jesus Christ, made once by himself, by which our consciences are calmed for ever. See what consolation there is in those words: brief indeed if you attend to their sound, but so ample if you look at their meaning, that the riches contained in them cannot be exhausted.

units.la: Sequitur apud Euangelistam Dominum e- misisse Spiritum, vt loquitur Matth.aut expirasse, vt scripserunt Marcus & Lucas, aut tradidisse, Spiritum, vt Ioannes loquitur, putà in manus Patris, cui commendauerat. Et hoc à quatuor Euangelistis expressum est, vt sciamus non tantum animi deliquium passum fuisse, sed reuera Iesu Christi animam à corpore ipsius separa- tam, capite post hæc verba inclinato, sine viri- bus ad se sustentandum: quod Iohannes, testis horum omnium oculatus, expressit.
units.tr: Next, in the Evangelist, the Lord is said to have sent forth the Spirit, as Matthew puts it, or to have expired, as Mark and Luke wrote, or to have delivered up the Spirit, as John says, namely into the hands of the Father, to whom he had committed it. The four Evangelists expressed this so that we may know that he did not merely suffer a swooning of the spirit, but that the soul of Jesus Christ was truly separated from his body, his head bowed after these words, with no strength left to hold himself up. John, an eyewitness of all these things, expressed this.

units.la: Etsi vero loquendi variæ illæ phrases rem vnam eandémque notant, tamen ex ea qua D. Matthæus, & D. Iohannes vsi sunt, tria quædam magni momenti capita nobis proponuntur: ac primum quidem animas hominum non esse simpliciter, sicut reliquarum animantium hac litum, sed substantiam spiritualem quæ morte non euanescat. Deinde easdem corporibus ex- cedentes ad creatorem ipsarum à quo suis cor- poribus sunt assignatæ reuerti, vt ipse sapiens loquitur, Eccles. 12. 9. alias quidem in gloriam recipiédas, Act. 7. 59. alias in locum suum mit- tendas, Luc. 6. 23. Act. 1 25. Ac proinde tertio animas non esse ex traduce vt corpora (qua in re multi tum veteres tum recentiores hallucinati sunt) sed vt factum legimus in prima hominis creatione, Genes. 2. 7. Deum etiam eas creare & & infundere quotidie immediatè in nascen- tium corpora, vt expressè dicitur apud Zach. 12. 1. quo etiam maximè respectu Deus Pater SpiriSpirit119 dicitur, & Patribus nostrorum corporum opponitur, Heb. 12.9.
units.tr: Although these various ways of speaking note one and the same thing, the expressions used by Saint Matthew and Saint John set before us three points of great importance. First, that the souls of men are not simply like those of the other living creatures, but are a spiritual substance that does not vanish at death. Second, that these souls, when they leave their bodies, return to their Creator, by whom they were assigned to their bodies, as the wise man himself says (Eccles. 12.9). Some are received into glory (Acts 7.59), others are sent to their own place (Luke 16.23; Acts 1.25). Third, therefore, souls are not derived by propagation from the parents as bodies are (a point in which many writers, both ancient and recent, have gone astray), but, as we read was done at the first creation of man (Gen. 2.7), God creates them and infuses them immediately, every day, into the bodies of those being born, as is expressly said in Zechariah 12.1. It is for this reason especially that God is called the Father of spirits, and is set against the fathers of our bodies (Heb. 12.9).

units.la: Cæterum, quùin tanta sua exinatione Dominus tamen diuinæ suę Maiestatis radios clarissimos iaculatus esset, potuerunt adhuc aliquot ipsius studiosi homines ac mulieres circumstantes spem aliquâ fouere, fore nimirũ vt in suorũ hostium cõsusionem à morte se vindicaret. Sed quum vitam cum morte commutasset, abiiciendi ac despondendi prorsus animum oblata videri poterat occasio, & ab hoc spectaculo cum summa confusione reuerten-di, quinam hæc nimirum ipsi contingere potuissent. Et quidem hanc illos subiisse cogitationem apparet ex sermonibus de quibus inter se duo illi viatores colloquebantur, apud Lucam. 24.19. Dominus igitur morte ad tempus clauso sacro ore suo, huic scandalo mature medeti voluit testimoniis diuinæ suæ Maiestatis, clarissimis & apertissimis: palàm etiam suis inimicis ostensurus rcipsa, non defore sibi, licet inuitis ipsis ac ringentibus, præcones quibus coarguerentur, quod erat etiam ipsis Luc. 19. 40. interminatus, Si siluerint isti (vt revera nemo tum ei patrocinatus est) mox lapides ipsi clamabunt. Qui igitur asinæ Balaami ad eius confusionem os aperuit, hic aliquid longè maius ac magis stupendum fecit, quinque admirandis & stupendis excitatis sine lingua tamen & ore concionatoribus, nempe Sole cœlorum omnium interprete, velo templi (Ecquis verò tanta vi præditus illud possit, nisi qui templo maior erat, & in Patris domo verus Dominus? Heb.3.6.) Et terra, & ipsis rupibus:(Ecquis vero potuit nisi à quo fundata est & coram cuius facie montes ipsi sudant?)Ecquid amplius? etiam, mortem, licet mutam & surdam, loqui voluit, apertis faucibus quibus mortuos suos euomeret. Quis igitur in hoc Crucifixo spem & fiduciam reponet qui non aducrsus quasuis tentationes tutus sit: quis illi contrà futurus inimicus, qui non pereat?
units.tr: Moreover, although the Lord, in so great an agony, nonetheless shot forth the most brilliant rays of his divine Majesty, some of his devoted men and women standing around could still cherish some hope, namely that he would avenge himself on his enemies and bring them to confusion, even from death. But since he had exchanged life for death, the occasion seemed to offer a reason to give up hope altogether and to turn away from this spectacle in utter confusion, asking what could possibly have happened to them. And indeed it appears that these thoughts had come to those two travellers, from the words they were discussing with each other, in Luke 24.19. The Lord, therefore, having closed his sacred mouth in death for a time, wished to deal promptly with this scandal by testimonies of his divine Majesty, most clear and manifest; and he was going to show openly to his enemies, by the facts themselves, that he would not be lacking heralds to convict them, even though they were unwilling and gnashing their teeth. He had threatened this to them as well (Luke 19.40): "If these men keep silent (as in truth no one then took his part), the stones will immediately cry out." He who opened the mouth of Balaam's ass to his confusion did something far greater and more astonishing, when he roused, without tongue or mouth, heralds of wonders and marvels: the Sun, interpreter of all the heavens; the veil of the temple (and who could have rent it with such force, except he who was greater than the temple, and the true Lord in his Father's house? Heb. 3.6); the earth, and the very rocks. (And who could have done this, except he from whom it was founded, and before whose face the mountains themselves sweat?) What more? He even willed that death, though mute and deaf, should speak, opening its jaws to vomit forth its dead. Who, then, would place his hope and trust in this Crucified One, and not be safe against any temptations? Who would be his enemy and not perish?

units.la: Age vero istorum praeconum quemque sigillatim audiamus fructum necessarium colligere, quod non vsque adeo difficile est in hac historia, licet eorum conciones ad verbum Euangelistae non retulerint. Primo igitur loco Velum quo arcebatur populus, immo ipsi Sacerdotes, excepto summo Sacerdote à conspectu Sanctuarij, videtur ipsi Domino AMEN respondisse quum ab imo ad summum vsque finderetur, ratâque fecisse nouissima Christi verba, CONSVMMATVM EST, quasi hoc velo iam tum Ecclesiam vniuersam Christianam his verbis inuitante, Adeste electi, & ipsa Dei de veltra salute penetralia scrutamini. Nam ecce magnus hic aeternus Sacerdos semel in verum caeleste Sanctuarium ingressus est, vt illum ingressum sequamini, cognitionem adepti, vmbris & figuris omnibus finem allaturam: Agite igitur audacter ingredimini thronum huius Maiestatis, legentes illius vestigia, cui iam cedo, siquidem ministerij mei tempora iam praeterierunt.
units.tr: Come now, let us hear each of these heralds in turn, and gather the fruit that is needed. This is not so hard to do in this history, although they have not reported their sermons word for word, as the Evangelist did. In the first place, the veil by which the people were kept back, or rather the priests themselves, except the high priest, from the sight of the Sanctuary, seems to have answered AMEN to the Lord when it was torn from top to bottom, and to have confirmed the last words of Christ, IT IS FINISHED. It was as if the veil, even then, were inviting the whole Christian Church with these words: "Come, you elect, and search out the innermost secrets of God concerning your salvation. For behold, this great eternal High Priest has entered once for all into the true heavenly Sanctuary, so that you may follow his entrance, having obtained knowledge which will bring an end to all shadows and figures. Go on, then, and boldly enter the throne of this Majesty, following the footsteps of him to whom I now yield, since the times of my ministry have now passed away."

units.la: Habetis veli istius concionem fine ore & fine lingua clarè & perspicuè ex hoc populo ele &tos alloquentis, & nos adhuc hodie, vt fufiùs hæc explicantur,Heb.9. & 10. capitibus. Quid igitur de miseris illis dicturi fumus velum istud Apostolorum temporibus iterum erigentibus, Circumcisionem cum Baptismo coniungenti- bus,vt expressa fit eorum mentio,Act.15.1. qui præ cæteris tantum Apostolis negotij exhi- buerunt? Et eos quidem fi iure vocat Apo- ftolus hostes Crucis Domini nostri Iesu Chri- fti,Philip.3.18.vt etiam dicat,Si circundamini, Christus vobis nihil prodest,Gal. 5.2. quid su- turum iis putamus qui pro Mofaico velo quod ex parte restituerunt, non desierunt hactenus nec adhuc desinunt nouis inuolucris totum Christianum velare?& quidem eò vsque deue-nerunt impudentiæ vt palàm etiam plebecu-lam arceant à Sanctuarij via, quæ lectio & intelligentia Scripturarum Sacrarum est?Nam in cantilenas infinitis impofturis ac medaciis re-fperfas Scripturas transformarunt, quas etiam peregrino idiomate populis vana fidei implicitæ larua deceptis obtrudunt.
units.tr: You have the sermon of this veil, addressing this chosen people clearly and plainly, without mouth and without tongue; and we still explain it more fully today in Hebrews, chapters 9 and 10. What, then, shall we say of those wretched men who, in the times of the Apostles, set up that veil again, joining circumcision with baptism, as their mention is expressly made in Acts 15.1, men who gave more trouble than all the other Apostles together? If the Apostle rightly calls them enemies of the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ (Phil. 3.18), and even says, "If you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing" (Gal. 5.2), what do we think will become of those who, in place of the Mosaic veil, which they have partly restored, have not ceased until now, and do not cease even now, to cover the whole Christian faith with new wrappings? Indeed they have reached such a pitch of shamelessness that they openly keep the common people from the road into the Sanctuary, which is the reading and understanding of the Holy Scriptures. For they have turned the Scriptures into songs, steeped in endless impostures and lies, and they thrust these, in a foreign tongue, upon peoples deceived by the empty mask of implicit faith.

units.la: Ecce verò aliam ciufdem præconis concionem, ad huius crucifixi inimicos & percussores, sic eos compellantis, Væ vobis maledicti, quid facitis?Aperitis viam in cœlos ei quem in terris ferre non potestis, quæ hactenus clausa fuerat, quod hic affixum ego velum repræsentabam. Me quidem viam illi pandere ab imo ad summum oportet.Verùm ego simul vosadmonco, vos, inquam, hypocritas abusos velo deuotionis ac pietatis ad occidendum authorem & principem vitæ, vobis ipsis esse exitij vestri & huius templi quo estis abusi tantopere, abolitionis instrumenta. Viam enim illi aperio qui hactenus figurate in hoc templo habitarat, egressuro nunquam exeo & nunquam in illud reddituro, vacuam ac desertam hanc domū vobis relicturo, vt prædixit vobis, quum bis ex ipso vos cum vestris mercibus flagris eiecit. Ioh. 2. 15. Matth. 21.12. & 25.28. Et hæc quidem fuit huius veli ad populum ingratum cocio, apud quem hodie nullum est Sacerdotium, nullus Sacerdos, nullum altare, nullum templum, nullus denique populi status (quæ sanè vsui nulli essent ipsis hodie) sed, quod longè pe ius est, cuius cordi tantum velamen est impositum, vt in Veteris & Noui Fœderis intelligentia prorsus cæcutiant 2. Cor. 3. 15. Eheu verò quanto maius est nostrum miserarum Gentiū ingrati animi vitiū, tanto maior est cæcitas nostra quàm fuerit vnqu alludæorū, quòd Pastores (neglecto duce Spiritu Sancto a quo tanta cum Luce ducebamur in omnem veritatem Sacris Scriptis verè Apostolicis cum insigni fulgore comprehēsam,) alij ex nimia negligentia, alij ex nimia scientiæ persuasione, alij ex ignorantia & superstitione passi sint, non tantum iterum confui & affigi velum Iudaicum, quod ex Iudaicis ceremoniis in Christianismū inuectis perspicuum est, (quarum testes sunto aqua lustralis, Chrisma, vnctio istius olei, lampades pades & cerei, Sacerdotales vestes & istiusmodi nugæ non paucæ) sed etiam crassius adhuc & densius velamen quàm apud Ethnicos fuerit, pietatis ac religionis prætextu retineri, testibus eadem illa aqua lustrali, altaribus, idolis, quarum tantùm nomina mutata sunt, coronis, & vestibus insignibus, quibus adoratis etiam thura adolent, & Missæ denique gesticulationibus: cum infinitis aliis velis nouis & Sacramentis ab ipsis confictis: ob quæ Dominus merito succensens infinitas Ecclesias, in Oriente, Meridie, Septentrione, & maxima parte Orientis etiam funditus euertit ac subruit. Quòd ad reliquias autem attinet, in Occidente merito Deus Spiritui erroris dedit efficaciam, adeò vt à Iudæis Christus nihil passus fit quod exiguus adhuc superstes Dei filiorum numerus, quibus Deus oculos aperuit, ab istius seculi Caiaphis, Sacerdotibus ac Pilatis non patiatur. Et, quod longè magis deflendum est, etiam conspicimus tenebras, paulatim offusas in iis ipsis locis quæ verus ille Sol radiis suis adeò micantibus & splendidis coeperat illustrare. Nam proculdubiò nimium multi sunt in iis etiam à quibus nostro seculo Iesu Christi spirituale templum coeptum est instaurari, qui (non animaduertentes diserte dici à quatuor Euangelistis, velum istud fissum esse nō ex parte tantùm dimidia, aut tertia, quartaue, sed ab imo ad summum) grauiter errarunt, relictis, vt reipsa experimur, fermenti reliquiis, quò, nisi maturè occurratur, totum fermentum magis quàm hactenus accescat. Gratias autem, fratres, agamus immortales Deo Opt. Max. secus huic loco contigisse, & aliis non paucis: scrib tamen cogitantes nisi maiore studio tanquam filij Lucis incedamus, splendorem Euangelij sequuti, dum adhuc splendet, quod olim populo Iudaico dicebat Dominus, Ioh. 12.35. fore vt tantum istud beneficium in maius iudicium convertatur, sicut minatur Dominus, Luc. 11.26. cuius rei quàm multi, proh dolor! hodie sunt testes improbi Apostatae, qui ex superstitiosis ab initio, tandem in Atheos, Libertinos & Epicuros, immo Ecclesiae Dei persecutores euaserunt, à quo merito sunt eius domo foras expulsi, principique tenebrarum traditi.
units.tr: Look again at another sermon of the same herald, addressed to the enemies and killers of this Crucified One, speaking to them thus: "Woe to you, accursed ones, what are you doing? You open a way into heaven for him whom you cannot bear on earth, a way that until now had been closed, since I, the veil fixed here, have represented it. I must open the way to him from top to bottom. But at the same time I warn you, you hypocrites who abused the veil of devotion and piety to kill the author and prince of life: I am the instrument of your ruin and of the abolition of this temple, which you have so greatly abused. For I open the way for him who until now had dwelt figuratively in this temple, who is going to depart and never leave, and who will never return to it; and I leave you this house empty and deserted, as he foretold you when he twice drove you out of it with your merchandise, with a whip (John 2.15; Matt. 21.12; 23.38)." This was the sermon of the veil to the ungrateful people, among whom today there is no priesthood, no priest, no altar, no temple, and finally no state of the people (which indeed would be of no use to them today). But, far worse, they have a veil laid upon their hearts, so that they are utterly blind in the understanding of the Old and New Covenants (2 Cor. 3.15). Alas, how much greater is the vice of ungrateful mind in us wretched Gentiles, and how much greater is our blindness than ever was that of the Jews! For our ministers, neglecting the Holy Spirit as leader, by whom we were led into all truth with such light, and by whom the truly Apostolic Scriptures were grasped with remarkable brilliance, some through excessive negligence, others through excessive confidence in their learning, and others through ignorance and superstition, have allowed not only the Jewish veil to be stitched up and fixed again (as is clear from the Jewish ceremonies brought into Christianity, of which the witnesses are the lustral water, the chrism, the anointing with that oil, the lamps and candles, the priestly vestments and not a few other trifles of this kind), but also a veil thicker and denser than any among the heathen to be retained under the pretext of piety and religion, witnessed by that same lustral water, by altars, by idols (whose names alone have been changed), by crowns and distinctive vestments, to which they burn incense while worshipping, and finally by the gestures of the Mass; along with countless other new veils and sacraments invented by themselves. Because of these things the Lord, rightly kindled to anger, has utterly overthrown and razed to the ground countless churches in the East, the South, the North, and in the greater part of the Orient. As for the remnants, in the West, God has justly given efficacy to the spirit of error, so that the small surviving number of God's children, to whom God has opened their eyes, do not suffer from the Caiaphases, priests and Pilates of this age what Christ suffered from the Jews. And, what is far more lamentable, we also see darkness gradually spreading over those very places which that true Sun had begun to illuminate with his most dazzling and splendid rays. For there are certainly too many, even among those by whom, in our century, the spiritual temple of Jesus Christ was begun to be restored, who (not noticing that the four Evangelists plainly say the veil was torn not only in part, a half, a third, or a quarter, but from top to bottom) have gone seriously astray, leaving behind, as we experience in fact, remnants of leaven, by which, unless it is promptly met, the whole mass will be more soured than hitherto. Let us, brothers, give thanks to God Most Good and Most Great that it has gone otherwise in this place and in many others. Yet let us consider that unless we walk with greater zeal, as children of the Light, following the splendour of the Gospel while it still shines (as the Lord once said to the Jewish people, John 12.35), this great benefit will be turned into a greater judgment, as the Lord threatens (Luke 11.26). How many, alas! are today wicked witnesses of this, apostates who, from being superstitious at the start, have at last become atheists, libertines and Epicureans, and even persecutors of the Church of God; and for this reason they have justly been cast out of his house and handed over to the prince of darkness.

units.la: Et haec quidem olim velum praedicabat, & eadem adhuc hodie nos docet. Iam audiamus quid terra significarit, quae quum vnius Dei fortissimo brachio subsistat, nunquam moveatur quin illud etiam brachium moueatur, magnum & extraordinarium Dei furorem nuntians: quasi homines amplius à terra sustineri aegre ferentis: vt non sit in causis naturalibus fecundis haerendum, quibus Dominus vtitur quando & quomodo ipsi libet. Sed hoc loco satis perspicue nos historia docet terram nominatim infandissimū omnium quae vnquam contigerunt scelerum in ipsam Creatoris personam patratum, detestatam & abominatam testari voluisse, se, licet abiectum & exinanitum Crucifixum illum agnoscere, & aduersus eius persecutores fidem & obsequium hoc illi motu exhibere, tanquam suo Creatori sine quo nihil factum est eorum quae facta sunt. Ioh. 1.3 Hoc praeterea motu veluti gemitu apud Deum conquesta est se ad tam nefandum & sceleratu populum sustinendum & alendum cogi, & veluti veniam eos sicut olim Coracum & Datanum, in abyssum suam absorbendi petiit, Num. 16. 31. siquidem hic agebatur de Mose longe maiore, & alio omnino a Mose, atque adeo de crimine longe magis detestando quam quod in Mosen erat admissum: & revera non ita multo post istos homines terra euomuit, & Romanorum gladius absumpsit. Praeterea terra haec tantis a Deo beneficiis extraordinaria vbertate praesertim cumulata, motu suo testata est horrendam in quam incidebat mutationem, paulatim in desertum transformata, quasi sulphure & sale conspersa, quod futurum ipse Moses tot ante saeculis tam exprese praedixerat, Deut. 16. 21. & ipse Propheta loquutus erat. Psal. 107. 34. En terrae tunc apud surdissimum quemque concionem.
units.tr: And indeed this veil once proclaimed these things, and it still teaches us the same today. Now let us hear what the earth signified. Though it stands firm by the mighty arm of the one God, it never moves without that same arm moving too, announcing the great and extraordinary wrath of God, as if it were grievous to the earth to bear up men. So we should not dwell on the fruitful natural causes that the Lord uses when and how he pleases. But here history teaches us quite plainly that the earth, by its own motion, wished to testify by name that it detested and abhorred the most unspeakable of all the crimes ever committed, the crime committed against the very person of the Creator. It wished to acknowledge that this crucified man, though abject and emptied of his glory, was its Creator, without whom nothing was made that was made (John 1:3), and by that motion to show faith and obedience to him against his persecutors. Moreover, by that motion, as if with a groan, it complained before God that it was forced to bear and feed so wicked and accursed a people, and it asked, as once with Korah and Dathan, to swallow them up into its abyss (Num. 16:31). For here the matter concerned a Moses far greater and wholly different from Moses, and therefore a crime far more detestable than the one committed against Moses. And in truth, not long after, the earth vomited those men out, and the sword of the Romans consumed them. Besides, this earth, especially heaped with such great benefits from God and extraordinary fertility, by its motion bore witness to the dreadful change into which it was falling, being gradually turned into a wilderness, as if sprinkled with sulphur and salt, which Moses himself had so expressly foretold many centuries before (Deut. 29:23), and which the Prophet also spoke of (Ps. 107:34). Behold, the earth then preaches a sermon to every most deaf person.

units.la: Sed ab eo tempore, vbi gentium non idem, & quidem asperius praedicauit. Nam quot vrbes subuersae? immo quot regiones eiusmodi terrae motibus in qualibet terrarum orbis parte absorptae sunt etiam nostra memoria? Et ne procul abeam, an non istud in quod conuenimus templum, est cum vrbe tota concussum, & tota vicina regio ad miliaria in circuitu quinquaginta sub tam magnorum & altorum montium iam inde a mundi iactis fundamentis existentium pondere,ab hinc an- nis paucis tremuit? At fi Deus nobis pepercit, non ita tamen cum omnibus egit nec tá mā- fuerè:Nā ecce non ita pridem Vienna in Au- stria,propugnaculû orbis Christiani aduersus Turcas dimidia subuersa est.Quis verò com- mouetur?quis tremit?quis denique alieno do- ctus exemplo sapit?
units.tr: But from that time on, wherever the nations... (the same warning, and indeed more harshly, is proclaimed). For how many cities have been overthrown? Indeed, how many regions have been swallowed up by such earthquakes in every part of the globe, even within our own memory? And, not to go far afield, did not this very temple where we are gathered, together with the whole city, shake a few years ago, and the whole neighbouring region for fifty miles around, under the weight of such great and lofty mountains, which have stood since the foundations of the world were laid? But if God has spared us, he has not dealt in the same way with all, nor has he been so merciful to everyone. For behold, not long ago Vienna in Austria, the bulwark of the Christian world against the Turks, was half overthrown. Yet who is moved? Who trembles? Who, finally, taught by another's example, becomes wise?

units.la: Nec verò speciales quædam circunstantia leuiter hic est præterecunda, nempe rupes ip- sas fissas esse, non sane copiam aquarum vt olim in deserto ex ingenti Dei fauore pro- ducturas, Exod. 17.6. sed litem contrà impro- bis iliis ferrei & indomiti cordi intentatu- ras. Quid porro? Nonne ante decennium ru- pes quæ immotæ videbantur ante nostros ocu- los fissæ sunt? annon plus quàm miliare totum rotatæ volutatæque sunt, obuia quæque incre- dibili impetu confringentes, & tandem, hor- rendum visu! domos,prata,vineas,agros,viros, mulieres, infantes, greges denique & armenta obrucrunt? Et quidem eorum, si vera sunt quæ de ipsis, referuntur, de quibus verè dici potest quod Dominus sui temporis hominibus dice- bat,de iis quos turris Siloam decidens opprei- ferat,Luc.13.4.
units.tr: Nor should a certain special circumstance be passed over lightly here: namely, that the very rocks were split, not indeed to produce a supply of waters, as once in the wilderness by the great favour of God (Exod. 17:6), but to bring strife upon those wicked, iron-hearted and untameable people. And what then? Did not rocks that seemed immovable before our eyes split a decade ago? Were not more than a whole mile of them rolled and tumbled down, shattering everything in their path with incredible force, and at last, horrible to see, overwhelm houses, meadows, vineyards, fields, men, women, infants, and finally flocks and herds? And indeed these were of such a kind, if what is reported of them is true, that of them it can truly be said what the Lord said to the people of his time about those whom the tower of Siloam fell upon and crushed (Luke 13:4).

units.la: Non desunt igitur nobis præcones ex rebus etiam natura sua sensu carentibus, præter ea quæ ex Dei verbo quotidie nobis inculcantur, & ipsa conscientia noctes diesque dictat. Sed neque oculos ad videndum nec aures ad au- diendum habemus, vt sola superfit horrenda minaminarum Dei tam diu à nobis spretarum exe-cutio, gemente sub pedibus nostris terra, & ad-uersus hominum iniquitates iudicium ac vin-dictam diuinam expetente, diémque illum vl-timum cum suspiriis expectante, Rom. 8. 20. quo die cuncta restituentur. Act. 3. 21. quum e-runt cœli noui & terra noua, 2. Petr. 3. 13. Apoc. 21. 5. Agite igitur, fratres maturè immutemur, quum alioqui futurum sit vt nos Deus immu-tet. Cum tremore & timore cor illud contri-tum & abiectum sacrosancti verbi sui prædi-catione, & tam longa patientia nobis oblatum recipiamus: vt veré & sine fuco semel cū Pro-pheta sic cum compellemus, Æterne, me insu-rore tuo ne arguas: neque in ira tua corripias me. Vtinam verò Deus nobis mentem hanc largiatur. Superest quintus horum extraordi-nariorum præconum, natura sua superioribus furdior & magis mutus, mors ipsa, cuius præ reliquis longè fuit clarius & illustrius præco-nium, quod quoniam breui temporis spatio absolui nō poterit, in aliud tempus differemus.
units.tr: Therefore we are not lacking heralds, even from things which by their nature lack sense, besides those things which are daily impressed upon us from the Word of God, and which conscience itself dictates night and day. But we have neither eyes to see nor ears to hear, so that only the dreadful execution of the threats of God, so long despised by us, remains: the earth groaning beneath our feet, and seeking divine judgment and vengeance against human iniquities, and awaiting with sighs that last day, on which all things will be restored (Rom. 8:20; Acts 3:21), when there will be new heavens and a new earth (2 Pet. 3:13; Rev. 21:5). Come, then, brothers, let us be changed in good time, since otherwise God will change us. Let us receive that heart, broken and cast down by the preaching of his holy Word and offered to us by so long a patience, with trembling and fear; so that truly and without pretence, once with the Prophet, we may speak thus: "O Eternal, rebuke me not in your anger, nor chastise me in your wrath" (Ps. 6:1). Would that God would grant us this mind. There remains the fifth of these extraordinary heralds, by nature more deaf and more mute than the others: death itself, whose proclamation, beyond all the rest, has been far clearer and more illustrious. Since this cannot be finished in a short space of time, we will defer it to another occasion.

units.la: HOMILIA TRICESIMA quarta.
units.tr: HOMILY THIRTY-FOURTH.

units.la: MATTH. 27.
units.tr: MATTHEW 27.

units.la: 52. Et monumenta aperta sunt: & multa corpora sanctorum qui dormierant, surrexerunt.
units.tr: 52. And the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had slept arose.

units.la: 53. Qui egressi e monumentis post resurrectionem eius, introierunt in sanctam urbem, & apparuerunt multis.
units.tr: 53. And coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they went into the holy city and appeared to many.

units.la: 54. Centurio vero & qui cum eo erant servantes Iesum, viso terraemotu & iis quae facta fuerant, timuerunt vehementer, dicentes vere Filius Dei erat iste.
units.tr: 54. But the centurion and those who were with him, guarding Jesus, when they saw the earthquake and the things that had happened, feared greatly, saying, "Truly this was the Son of God."

units.la: 55. Erant autem illic mulieres multae e longinquo spectantes, quae secutae fuerant Iesum a Galilaea ministrantes ei.
units.tr: 55. Many women were also there, watching from afar, who had followed Jesus from Galilee and served him.

units.la: 56. Inter quas erat Maria Magdalene, & Maria mater Iacobi & Iose, & mater filiorum Zebedaei.
units.tr: 56. Among them were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

units.la: MARC. 15.
units.tr: MARK 15.

units.la: 39. Quum vidisset autem Centurio qui adstabat ipsi ex adverso, eum ita emisso clamore, expirasse, dixit, Vere homo iste Filius erat Dei.
units.tr: 39. When the centurion who stood facing him saw that he had breathed out his last with such a cry, he said, "Truly this man was the Son of God."

units.la: 40. Erant autem etiam & mulieres e longinquo spectantes: inter quas erat Maria Magdalene, & Maria Iacobi parvi & Iose mater, & Salome. lome.
units.tr: 40. There were also women watching from afar, among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.

units.la: 41. Quæ etiam quum esset in Galilæa sequutæ fuerant eum, & ministrauerant ei: aliaque multa quæ simul cum eo ascenderant Hierosolyma.
units.tr: 41. These had followed him and served him when he was in Galilee, and there were many others who had come up with him to Jerusalem.

units.la: LVC. 23.
units.tr: LUKE 23.

units.la: 47. Quum vidisset autem Centurio quod factum fuerat, glorificauit Deum, dicens, Vere hic homo iustus erat.
units.tr: 47. When the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God, saying, "Truly this man was righteous."

units.la: 48. Et omnis turba quæ simul ad hoc spectaculum accesserat, spectans quæ facta fuerant, verberans pectora sua reuertebatur.
units.tr: 48. And all the crowd that had gathered together to this spectacle, seeing what had happened, returned beating their breasts.

units.la: 49. Stabant autem omnes noti eius procul, & mulieres quæ erant vnà sequutæ à Galilæa, videntes ista.
units.tr: 49. But all his acquaintances stood at a distance, and the women who had followed him from Galilee, watching these things.

units.la: INTER eos omnes testes quos habemus, tenus sine ore & lingua loquentes, Solem nimirum & totum cælum horrendis tenebris obductu tres horas continuas, velut tepli à summo ad imum fissum, terrâ tremente, & rupes fissas audiuimus, qui superesset vltimus mors ipsa nimirum qua omnia animantia muta & surda fiunt præcipuum locum obtinet: Hic est etenim veluti clara voce vociferata Crucifixum illum quem sui inimici protraxisse sibi videbantur, ipsi morti morte intulisse per seipsam: adeo vt vncis illis & tenacibus vinculis quibus mortuos constringebat laxatis, ipsa cogeretur etiam prædâ demittere, sepulchris veluti faucibus ipsius apertis, quasi diceret, Exite captiui quum vobis videbitur. Ac si accuratius Matthaei Euangelistae verba excutiamus, hic sepulchrorum hiatus primum tres vltimas horas primi huius historiae diei durauerit, deinde noctem & diem Sabbathi, tum denique noctem a qua tertius dies initium capiebat, dum vero Lux resurgeret, & hi etiam cum illo sub auroram dici Dominici, quae vocamus. Quare sane stupidissimos etiam quosque & maxime lethargicos oportuerat commoueri, & discipulos ad Magistri sui resurrectionem credendam praeparari. Nihilominus deinceps visuri sumus quam tardi fuerint in iis credendis quae tam expresse praedicta fuerant, quaeque ne ipsi quidem hostes ignorabant, vt Matthaeus testatur. 27.63.
units.tr: Among all the witnesses we have, who speak without mouth or tongue, we may surely note the sun and the whole sky, covered with terrible darkness for three continuous hours, and the earth trembling, and the rocks split as if a veil had been torn from top to bottom. The last witness, which holds the chief place, is death itself, which renders all living things dumb and deaf. For death, as if crying out with a clear voice, announced that the Crucified One, whom his enemies seemed to have dragged to his death, had himself inflicted death on death through his own person; so that, the hooked and tenacious bonds with which death held the dead being loosed, death was compelled to give up its prey, its tombs opened like its jaws, as if to say, "Go out, captives, when it seems good to you." If we examine more closely the words of the evangelist Matthew, this opening of the tombs lasted first for the last three hours of that first day of the story, then through the night and the day of the Sabbath, and finally through the night with which the third day began, until the light rose, and these also came out with him at the dawn of the Lord's day, as we call it. Therefore even the most stupid and especially the most lethargic should have been stirred, and the disciples prepared to believe in their Master's resurrection. Nevertheless we shall see presently how slow they were to believe things that had been so plainly foretold, and which even his enemies did not ignore, as Matthew testifies (27:63).

units.la: Nihilominus tamen apud Dei populum doctrina resurrectionis Carnis passim erat recepta, exceptis Sadducaeis illis caecis, cuius rei testes sunt tam multa passim Scripturae loca, & nominatim illa Marthae sororis Lazari insignis restificatio. Ioh. 11.24. At ea resurrectio die vltimum respiciebat, quod etiam in nostro Symbolo confitemur. Quicquid sit, licet de nulla alia resurrectione cogitassent quam de qua tam multa ante oculos exempla viderant, & quidem, paulo antequam haec contingeret, in Lazaro iam quatriduano mortuo, sepulchrorum illa parefactio debuit eos ad tale quid exspectandum incitare: Quid vero? Nae si ordinaria Dei opera quae per causas secundas operatur in nostros sensus incurrentia tantopere maxima pars hominum contemnunt, aut ad natunaturam, quam vocant, ea referunt, qui causas penitius quàm ipsum vulgus scrutatur, & in ea subsistunt altius non intuentes, longè grauius in operum Dei extraordinariorum consideratione peccant. Alij enim ea non credunt, quòd mentis suæ captum superent, testibus ipsis Philosophis Paulum irridentibus Athenis de resurrectione mortuorum disputantem, Act. 17. 32. & ridiculo Faulti Iudeæ Gubernatoris dicto, Act. 26.24. Alij verò licet conuicti, rationes tamen quærunt Deum sua debita laude spoliandi: quemadmodum Iesu Christi inimici opera ipsius calumniabantur, & ex suacacitate metiebantur: nisi forte quum falsa miracula confinguntur, aut ipse Satan imitatur, vt olim Magi tempore Pharaonis in Ægypto Dei opera imitabantur. Nam tunc imitatores illi peruersæ credulitati explendæ non sufficiunt, vt ipse Christus prædixit, Ioh. 5. 43. & quotidiana experientia testatur.
units.tr: Nevertheless, the doctrine of the resurrection of the flesh was everywhere received among the people of God, except by those blind Sadducees. Many passages of Scripture everywhere bear witness to this, and especially the remarkable raising of Lazarus's sister Martha (John 11:24). But that resurrection looked to the last day, as we also confess in our Creed. Whatever the case, although they had thought of no other resurrection than the one whose many examples they had seen before their eyes, and indeed shortly before this happened, when Lazarus had already been dead four days, the opening of the tombs ought to have stirred them to expect something of this kind. But what then? Indeed, if most men despise the ordinary works of God, which he performs through secondary causes and which fall under our senses, and refer them to what they call nature, those who investigate causes more deeply than the common people, and rest in these without looking higher, sin far more gravely in considering the extraordinary works of God. For some do not believe these, because they exceed the grasp of their minds, as the Philosophers at Athens, mocking Paul when he disputed about the resurrection of the dead (Acts 17:32), and the ridicule of Festus, the governor of Judea (Acts 26:24), show. Others, though convinced, nevertheless seek reasons for stripping God of his due praise, just as the enemies of Jesus Christ slandered his works and measured them by their own blindness, unless perhaps when false miracles are invented, or Satan himself imitates them, as the Magi once imitated God's works in the time of Pharaoh in Egypt. For those imitators do not suffice to satisfy a perverse credulity, as Christ himself foretold (John 5:43), and daily experience bears witness.

units.la: En quanta passim homines in mundo tum ignorantia tum malitia præcipites in iuitum exitium agat quod ipsis Propheta minatur, Psal. 28. 5. Nos verò contrà probè scientes vel in minimis Dei operibus tanquam in speculo infinitam sapientiam, potentiam ac bonitatem erga suos elucere, in omnibus eum vt par est debitis laudibus extollamus. Sed in hoc potissimum nostræ salutis ineffabili mysterio, tam fideliter ab Euangelistis monumentis tradito, quo aduersus quanuis incredulitatem vtamur in hac vita, nec, quum ita feret naturæ cursus, sepulchrum horreamus, satis gnari eum à quo sunt aperta, quum ipse tamen illud ingtedere-tur, longè potiore ratione nobis eadem aper-turum die illo vltimo, quandoquidem ipse primus sepulchrum victor egressus est.
units.tr: See how widely men in the world, driven headlong by ignorance and malice, rush into the destruction the Prophet threatens them with (Ps. 28:5). But we, on the contrary, knowing well that even in the smallest works of God his infinite wisdom, power and goodness shine forth toward his own as in a mirror, should exalt him in all things with the praise due to him. But above all in this ineffable mystery of our salvation, handed down so faithfully by the Evangelists in these monuments, let us use it against all unbelief in this life, and not fear the grave when the course of nature so requires, knowing well that he by whom the tombs were opened, who himself stepped into them, will open them for us on that last day with far better reason, since he himself first came forth from the tomb as victor.

units.la: Porrò, ne sepulchrorum istam patefactionem vanam & illusoriam putaremus, sed illi suum adiunctum effectum, historia deinceps narrat, multorum sanctorum corpora post Domini resurrectionem suscitata fuisse, multisque in urbe Ierusalem conspicienda praebuisse. En igitur primum in Iesu Christi membris certissimum & prorsus indubitatum testimonium mortuorum quā exspectamus futurae resurrectionis. Deinde, cuius id virtute futurum sit, discimus, eius nimirum qui primus resurrexit, ut hic nominatim dicitur, quam etiam ob causam factus dicitur primitiae eorum qui obdormierunt, 1.Cor.15.20. & vita. Ioh.14.6. ad viuificandos quos vult. Ioh. 5.21. Denique Philosophorum omnium, aut potius huius mundi stultorum ac insanorum hominum inanibus speculationibus & deliris haec placitis opponuntor. Primus igitur inter homines in vitam aeternam resurrexit. Nam qui ante ipsum & per ipsum ex miraculo suscitati sunt, iterum morituri suscitati sunt, quum tamen huius miraculi finis sit, ut sciamus hos fuisse suscitatos testes virtutis resurrectionis Iesu Christi in aeternam felicitatem futuros.
units.tr: Moreover, lest we think this opening of the tombs vain and illusory, the history goes on to tell that the bodies of many saints were raised after the Lord's resurrection and made visible to many in the city of Jerusalem. Here, then, we have first, in the members of Jesus Christ, the most certain and wholly indubitable testimony of the dead whom we expect at the future resurrection. Next, we learn by whose power this will come about: namely, of him who rose first, as is named here, and for this reason is said to have become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep (1 Cor. 15:20), and the life (John 14:6), to quicken whom he wills (John 5:21). Finally, these things are set against the empty speculations and dreams of all philosophers, or rather of the foolish and insane men of this world. Therefore he first among men rose to eternal life. For those who were raised by miracle before him and through him were raised to die again, whereas the purpose of this miracle is that we may know these were raised as witnesses of the power of the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who were to enter into eternal happiness.

units.la: Tertio ex hoc loco animarum à corpore ad tempus separatarum immortalitas & subsistentia stentia asseritur. Nec enim hic Deus nouas a- nimas creasse dicitur,nec animæ suscitatæ, sed corpora, quæ quum sola morte occiderint,e- tiam sola sunt, animarum coniunctione re- staurata.
units.tr: Thirdly, from this passage the immortality and subsistence of souls, separated from the body for a time, is affirmed. For here it is not said that God created new souls, nor that souls were raised, but bodies, which, having perished by death alone, are restored by reunion with their souls.

units.la: Sin quæratiquis quonam igitur loco sic asseruarentur,absit curiosius inista inquira- mus, quorum non minus periculosæ sunt & inanes solutiones, cuiusmodi sunt eæ quibus singulis sua conclauia quædam assignantur:
units.tr: But if anyone asks where, then, these were kept, let us not inquire too curiously into this, since the solutions to it are no less dangerous and empty, such as those which assign to each soul its own particular chamber.

units.la: sed in primis eæ quibus in inferorum subur-biis collocantur,quæ nouo etiam & inusitato, Limbi vocabulo designarunt,quasi dicas Infe-rorum marginem,in quæ loca volunt animam Iesu Christi deuenisse, custoditas illic animaş quæsituram:quç sane nullo Scripturarum fun-damento nituntur, vt superius in historia la-tronis conuersi, pluribus docui, & hic iterum repeto, nisi Petri malè intellecto loco : quum tamen Abrahami sinus in locis superioribus non inferioribus collocetur, Matth. 16. 22. Fa-teor igitur, quod ex Christi responso ad latro-nem conuersum liquet, animam Iesu Christi ex corpore migrantem in eum locum receptâ, in quo veteres Patres erant,sed eum locum Pa-radisum vocari dico,nisi forte,quod absurdissi-mũ foret,huic cõuersi latronis animæ specialis locus assignetur. Igitur concludamus ꞓcuri fi-des vna eadémque fuit Patrum in Christum venturum sperantium cum nostra in Christum iam exhibitum, sic in eandem illos quietem quæ Paradisus vocatur, esse ingressos, quum non fit minor vis & efficacia mortis & resurrectionis Iesu Christi ante eius aduentu quàm post earundem impletionem, quandoquidem sola fides est rerum nondum existentium subsistentia. Nihil tamen vetat quominus credamus reali impletione passionum Iesu Christi & victoriæ quam adeptus est, Patrum spiritibus magnum & inenarrabile gloriæ & felicitatis incrementum accessisse: quo fortasse respectu locus ille per metaphoram, dictus Abrahami sinus, vt patris credentium, veteris populi habita ratione, melius vocatur Paradisus (allusione tamen facta ad eximium illum paradisum & hortum in Edem) post Iesu Christi mortem, Luc. 22. 43. & post ascensionem in tertio cælo collocatur, 2. Cor. 12. 2. & 4. supra alios omnes cælos. Ephes. 4. 10. vbi D. Stephanus cum oculis suis est contemplatus, & Spiritus eius est receptus, Act. 7. 55. Idipsum Paulus optabat, nobis quod imitemur exemplum in se ipso exhibens. Phil. 1. 23. At iis quæ sacrarum Scripturarum fundamento nituntur contentos esse nos oportet, ab omnibus curiosis speculationibus abstinentes, & viam potius quæ ad hanc felicitatem ducit quærere & insistere, quàm de eius situ aut aliis occultis nobis circumstantiis anxius inquirere, quarum etiam cognitione nostræ mentes longè sunt inferiores.
units.tr: But above all are those which place them in the suburbs of Hell, which by the new and unusual word Limbo they have designated, as if you should say the border of Hell, into which places they wish the soul of Jesus Christ to have come, to seek out the souls kept there. These indeed rest on no foundation of Scripture, as I have shown at length above in the history of the converted thief, and repeat here, unless a passage of Peter is badly understood; whereas the bosom of Abraham is placed in higher places, not lower (Matt. 16:22). I admit, therefore, what is clear from Christ's answer to the converted thief: the soul of Jesus Christ, departing from the body, was received into that place where the ancient Fathers were; but I say that this place is called Paradise, unless perhaps, which would be most absurd, a special place is assigned to the soul of the converted thief. Let us conclude, then, that the faith of the Fathers who hoped for Christ to come was one and the same as ours in Christ already revealed, and so they entered into that rest which is called Paradise; since the power and efficacy of the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ are no less before his coming than after its fulfilment, for faith alone is the substance of things not yet existing. Nevertheless, nothing prevents us from believing that by the real fulfilment of Jesus Christ's sufferings and the victory he obtained, a great and inexpressible increment of glory and happiness came to the spirits of the Fathers. With this in view, perhaps, that place is by metaphor called the bosom of Abraham, as the father of believers, and, considering the ancient people, is better called Paradise (with an allusion, however, to that excellent paradise and garden in Eden), after the death of Jesus Christ (Luke 23:43), and after the ascension it is placed in the third heaven (2 Cor. 12:2), and above all the other heavens (Eph. 4:10), where Saint Stephen gazed with his eyes and his spirit was received (Acts 7:55). Paul desired the same thing, presenting in himself an example for us to imitate (Phil. 1:23). But we ought to be content with what rests on the foundation of the sacred Scriptures, refraining from all curious speculations, and rather to seek and keep to the way that leads to this happiness, than to inquire anxiously about its location or other hidden circumstances, the knowledge of which is far beyond our minds.

units.la: Cœterum, multorum tantum hic fit mentio, quod generalis resurrectio reseruetur in vltimum diem. Præterea sanctorum tantum meminit Euangelista, quòd tantum ad fideles de Do-
units.tr: Moreover, only a few are mentioned here, because the general resurrection is reserved for the last day. The Evangelist also mentions only the saints, because it was only to the faithful that he meant to make the Lord's resurrection more certain, and this was done by the Lord, so this should not be stretched any further.

units.la: Domini resurrectiones certiores faciedos hoc à Domino factum sit, nec longius istud trahi oporteat. Nam alioquin hic est certissimus articulus fidei ipso ore Domini & suorum Apostolorum saepius pronuntiatus, omnes ultimo die resurrecturos, fideles quidem ad salutem, ex foederis formula, virtute resurrectionis Iesu Christi capitis ipsorum: alios autem ad mortem secundam & aeternam, etiam per Iesum Christum, sed tanquam Iudice & executorem decretae poenae, nempe secundae mortis post priorem. Idcirco licet mors omnibus sit communis, atque adeo corporis ipsa corruptio, proprie tamen Mori dicuntur qui extra Christum moriuntur, quod prior illa mors sit veluti suburbium inferorum, quae secunda mors est, quodque in ipsis suis sepulchris non minus maledicti sint quam corrupti: quum contra qui in Domino moriuntur Quieturi dicantur abire, felicem illam ultimo die resurrectionem expectantes.
units.tr: For otherwise this is the most certain article of faith, often proclaimed by the Lord's own mouth and by his Apostles: that all will rise on the last day. The faithful will rise to salvation, according to the form of the covenant, by the power of the resurrection of Jesus Christ, their head. The others will rise to the second and eternal death, also through Jesus Christ, but as Judge and as executor of the penalty decreed, namely the second death after the first. Therefore, although death is common to all, and so too is the corruption of the body, those are properly said to die who die outside Christ, because that first death is like the suburb of hell, which is the second death. And in their very sepulchres they are no less accursed than they are corrupt. On the other hand, those who die in the Lord are said to depart to rest, awaiting that blessed resurrection on the last day.

units.la: Denique quod dicuntur hi Sancti suscitati multis apparuisse, nequaquam est de intelle- ctuali visione quapiam intelligendum, aut de quapiam actuali forma sine substantia, quarum in Scripturis formarum multa passim occurrunt exempla: sed sciendum eos vere & sensibiliter sese suis corporibus suscitatos videndos praebuisse. Annon enim alioqui vani tantum testes futurae quam speramus resurrectionis fuissent, in qua tamen eorum haec est praerogatiua ut in ea nos praecedant, qui praecipuus est Ij. ij.
units.tr: Finally, when these saints are said to have risen and appeared to many, this must not be understood of some intellectual vision, or of some actual form without substance, of which many examples occur here and there in the Scriptures. Rather, we must understand that they truly and sensibly showed themselves to be seen in their own bodies, risen again. For otherwise they would have been mere empty witnesses of the resurrection we hope for, in which resurrection this is their special prerogative: that they go before us in it, as the firstfruits, who is the chief one (Ij. ij.).

units.la: Hi suscitati vere in suis corporibus apparuerunt. à nobis in hac historia fructus colligendus.
units.tr: These risen ones truly appeared in their bodies. From this history we are to gather fruit.

units.la: Hæc igitur sufficiunto, quandoquidem nihil amplius nobis Dominus exposuit: & hinc profanam illam curiositatem, vt ab omnibus rebus, arceamus inquirendi in nomina horum suscitatorum, & eorum quibus apparuerunt, qui sermones eorum inter ipsos fuerint, quandiu in terris remanserint, & similes nugas quas Doctoribus illis Contemplatiuis relicturi fumus, ea scrutantibus quorū cognitionem nunquam sunt adepturi, quos potius oportuerat ad Dei gloriam & suum vsum revocare quæ nobis hic explicantur: quæque ad salutem sufficiunt.
units.tr: Let these things therefore suffice, since the Lord has set forth nothing more to us. From this we should keep away that profane curiosity which pries into all things: inquiring into the names of these risen ones and of those to whom they appeared, what their conversations were among themselves, how long they remained on earth, and similar trifles. We would leave such things to those contemplative teachers, who pry into matters whose knowledge they will never attain. They ought rather to have turned their minds to the glory of God and their own use the things explained to us here, which are sufficient for salvation.

units.la: Qui verò ex hoc loco Spirituum & mortuorum inter viuos & apparitiones deducere conantur, lógè sanè fallùtur quum hæc doctrina nihil ad hunc locū faciat, nulloque Scripturarum fundamento nitatur, sed meræ potius sint illusiones arte Satanæ & Magorum fabricatę tam ad veteres idololatras confirmandos, quàm ad myriades superstitionum in Ecclesiam Christianam inuehendas: quales putà reliquiarum venerationem, pœnas Purgatorij, & preces pro mortuis: quorum omnium falsitas fatis superque in qua officina sint fabricatæ restatur. Itaque vt paucis absolua, aio tales omnes ineptias esse responso indignas, licet in eas quidam ex veteribus Patribus nimiùm facilè consenserint.
units.tr: But those who try to derive from this passage the apparitions of spirits and of the dead among the living are greatly mistaken. This doctrine has nothing to do with this place and rests on no foundation of Scripture. Rather, these are mere illusions, devised by the art of Satan and of magicians, both to confirm the ancient idolaters and to bring myriads of superstitions into the Christian Church: such as, for example, the veneration of relics, the pains of Purgatory, and prayers for the dead. The falsehood of all these things sufficiently and more than sufficiently refutes the workshop in which they were fabricated. So, to finish briefly, I say that all such absurdities are unworthy of an answer, although some of the ancient Fathers too readily agreed to them.

units.la: Vrbi verò illi quòd tribuitur Sanctæ Ciuitatis nomen, interfectrici Prophetarum, Matt.
units.tr: As for the city to which the name of Holy City is given, the murderess of the Prophets (Matt.

units.la: 23.32.& principis etiam vitæ.Act. 3. 15. fit pro-pter visibiles & conspicuas in ea notas Fœde-ris Domini, puta templum ipsum, & totum ritualem cultum ab ipso Deo præscriptum, qui quidem tunc temporis purius quàm multis retrolapsis seculis ante & post captiuitatem Babylonicam administrabatur.
