Etsi verò totius illius cultus vera intelligentia & rectus vsus, atque adeò doctrina per Mosen & Prophetas tradita miserrimè pollueretur, & fermento Scribarum & Pharisæorum depravaretur, lectio tamen Mosis & Prophetarum in Synagogis integra retinebatur, cuius etiam fidos auditores tam in intelligentia quàm illius vsu Dominus habebat, Zachariam, Elizabetham, Iosephum, Mariam sanctam Virginem, Simeonem, Annam prophetissam, Iosephum Arimathæensè, Nicodemū & alios istis similes, veræ Ecclesiæ membra. Præterea locus erat designatus à Domino colligendæ per Apostolorum prædicationem primæ illius purissimæ & excellentissimæ Christianæ Ecclesiæ si quæ fuit vllis vnquam seculis, quàm deinde paulatim in vniuersum terrarum orbem longè lateque spargeret ac disseminaret. Quo sane respectu merito Sanctæ ciuitatis hactenus nomen retinuit. At post abolitū Leuiticum Sacerdotium, & totius nationis excisionem, omne decus illud etiam intercidit. Etsi verò Dominus in ea Christianam Ecclesiam quàdiu voluit & quomodo conseruauit, tamen iam ante multa seculâ grauem illi nota inussit: qua in re magna fuit Satanæ fraus in inuehenda paulatim stupenda superstitione Domini sepulchrum inuisendi, & loca sanƈta, quæ vocant, crebris peregrinationibus frequentandi, quæ paulatim ex ridicula superstitione in derestandam idololatriam cuascrunt: quibus Episcopi Romani plurimum ad loculos suos implendos Indulgentiarum illarum prætextu sunt abusi: & hodie iure optimo dici potest vrbs illa pollutissima, in eam duobus Antichristis concurrentibus, Orientali & Occidentali, pollutionum omni genere fœdatis.
units.tr: 23.32), and of the Prince of life (Acts 3.15), this is because of the visible and conspicuous marks of the Lord's covenant in it, namely the temple itself and the whole ritual worship prescribed by God himself. This worship was administered more purely at that time than in the many centuries that had slipped away before and after the Babylonian captivity. Yet although the true understanding and right use of that whole worship, and the doctrine delivered through Moses and the Prophets, were most wretchedly polluted and corrupted by the leaven of the Scribes and Pharisees, nevertheless the reading of Moses and the Prophets was kept whole in the synagogues. The Lord had faithful hearers of it, both in understanding and in its use: Zechariah, Elizabeth, Joseph, the holy Virgin Mary, Simeon, Anna the prophetess, Joseph of Arimathea, Nicodemus, and others like them, true members of the Church. Moreover, a place was designated by the Lord for the gathering, through the preaching of the Apostles, of that first most pure and most excellent Christian Church, if there ever was one in any age, which would then gradually spread and scatter itself far and wide over the whole orb of the earth. In this respect the city has rightly retained the name of Holy City up to now. But after the Levitical priesthood was abolished, and the whole nation cut off, all that glory also perished. Although the Lord has preserved the Christian Church in it for as long as he willed, and in the manner he willed, yet many centuries ago he stamped upon it a grave mark. In this matter lay Satan's great fraud: he gradually introduced the amazing superstition of visiting the Lord's sepulchre and of frequenting the so-called holy places with constant pilgrimages. These gradually grew from ridiculous superstition into a damnable idolatry. The Roman bishops abused these very much, under the pretext of those Indulgences, to fill their own coffers. And today it can rightly be said, with the best reason, that this city is most polluted, since two Antichrists, the Eastern and the Western, have come together there, defiled with every kind of pollution.

units.la: At quæ conuenientia Hierosolymæ à Deo electæ vt sedes esset temporaria & spiritualis sui populi: Templi Hierosolymitani Dei ipsius mandato extructi: Sacerdotij Leuitici, ac cæremoniarum rituumque qui erant eorum figura quorum Iesus Christus erat veritas & corpus, quæ, inquam, conuenientia cum vrbe Roma monstrōque illo, cuius tam expressa fit in Apocalypsi mentio, nostrōque tempore tam clare patefacto, vt nemo nisi volēs falli possit? Itaque nostri temporis Mediatores ad illa Prophetæ verba relegare non verebor, Esa. 5.20. & 21. Væ vobis qui malum dicitis bonum, & bonum malū: qui facitis tenebras Lucem, & Lucem tenebras, & statuitis amarum pro dulci, & dulce pro amaro. Væ sapientibus iudicio suo, & coram facie sua intelligentibus. En verò cur sic nostros Mediatores compellem. Primùm enim ex ipsis quæro cur particulari cuidam Ecclesiæ, Romanæ putà, nomen Ecclesiæ Catholicæ licæ tribuant, quum pars Totius non sit totum ipsum, etsi pars illa veræ Ecclesiæ nomine digna censeretur. Hoc inquam ex illis Mediatoribus quæro qui nobiscum sentire in ea auctoritate quam sibi Papa in omnes Ecclesias tribuit condemnanda videri volunt, quum tamen hæc proferre non possint quin sibi ipsis repugnantia loquantur.
units.tr: But what correspondence is there between Jerusalem, chosen by God to be the temporary and spiritual seat of his people, the Temple of Jerusalem built by God's own command, the Levitical priesthood, and the ceremonies and rites which were figures of those things of which Jesus Christ is the truth and the body; what correspondence, I say, is there between these and the city of Rome and that monster, of which such an express mention is made in the Apocalypse, and which in our time has been revealed so clearly that no one can be deceived by it unless he wishes to be? Therefore I will not hesitate to refer our present-day Mediators to those words of the Prophet: "Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter. Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight" (Isa. 5.20, 21). Indeed, here is why I address our Mediators in this way. First, I ask them why they attribute the name of Catholic Church to one particular church, the Roman one for example, since a part is not the whole itself, even if that part were judged worthy of the name of true Church. I ask this of those Mediators who, though they agree with us, want to seem to condemn the authority which the Pope claims for himself over all churches; yet they cannot say these things without speaking things that contradict themselves.

units.la: Præterea, quum etiam hæc vox Ecclesiæ Catholicæ, aliam significationem habeat, ex communi loquendi usu, nempe ut pro Ecclesia & coetu veram & Orthodoxam doctrinam & religionem profitentem & omnibus hereticis conuentibus opposita capiatur, quæro, qua conscientia nomen istud Ecclesiæ Romanæ hodiernæ tribuant, in qua nobiscum tot deresta-ndos errores agnoscere coguntur.
units.tr: Moreover, although this expression "Catholic Church" has another meaning in common usage, namely that it is taken for the Church and the assembly professing true and orthodox doctrine and religion, and set against all heretical assemblies, I ask with what conscience they give that name to the present Roman Church, in which they are forced to acknowledge with us so many errors to be condemned.

units.la: Quid ad hæc respondere sint equidem nescio, sed quantum ex eorum scriptis potui cognoscere, respondent se hoc nomé illi tribuere, veluti corpori ægro & admodum cacochymo, idest vitiosis humoribus pleno, quod nihilominus corpus est humanum, & adhuc subsistens: nec enim, aiunt, æquum esse, Romanam hodiernam Ecclesiam, licet impurissimam, cum synagoga Iudæorum, ex fœdere excisorum & Christi hostium, aut Turcarum, nullam Christianismi notam habentium, comparare.
units.tr: I indeed do not know what they would answer to this. But as far as I have been able to learn from their writings, they reply that they give this name to it as to a sick body, very cacochymic, that is, full of corrupt humours. Nevertheless it is a human body and still subsists. For, they say, it is not fair to compare the present Roman Church, however impure, with the synagogue of the Jews, who have been cut off from the covenant and are enemies of Christ, or with the Turks, who have no mark of Christianity at all.

units.la: Quibus vt respondeam, hoc prius positum velim, me hac voce Ecclesiæ Catholicæ Romanæ intelligere cœtum eorum omnium qui Romanum Episcopum, quem Papam dicūt, se profitentur agnoscere, & habere pro Christi hic in terris vicario, & suo capite: & simul etiam eius doctrinam cuius nuper summam Concilium Tridentinum collegit. Quæstio igitur est an Ecclesiæ Christianæ nomen illi cœtui conueniat vlla ratione. Quibus cum mihi res est, aiunt, ego vero inficior. Quum vero fateantur Ecclesiam illam talem non esse qualem oportuerat, & qualis ab initio fuit: sed esse instar anhelantis adhuc ægroti, cuius vitæ indicia sint, primum Episcopalis Successio personalis inde vsque ab Apostolis repetita, secundum quod dicitur homo peccccati sefurus in templo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia: Deinde verus Baptismus cuius substantiam retinet, quæ vera est Ecclesiæ Christianæ nota, licet illum fateantur ipsimet multis pollutionibus fœdatum: tertio denique Sacræ Scripturæ, quas integras conseruat cum symbolo Apostolico, Athanasij & Niceno, in tribus aliis Conciliis quæ cum ipsis admittimus approbato & exposito.
units.tr: To answer them, I would first wish this to be laid down: by this expression "Roman Catholic Church" I understand the assembly of all those who profess that they acknowledge the Roman bishop, whom they call the Pope, and hold him to be Christ's vicar here on earth and their head; and at the same time also the doctrine whose summary the Council of Trent lately gathered. The question, therefore, is whether the name of Christian Church can in any way belong to that assembly. With such people, they say, I have a quarrel; but I deny it. Yet since they confess that this Church is not such as it ought to have been, and such as it was from the beginning, but is like a still gasping sick man, whose signs of life are: first, the personal succession of bishops, traced back from the Apostles onward, according to what is said, "the man of sin will sit in the temple of God, which is the Church"; second, the true Baptism, whose substance it retains, which is a true mark of the Christian Church, although they themselves confess that it has been defiled by many pollutions; third and finally, the Holy Scriptures, which it keeps whole, together with the Apostles' Creed, the Athanasian and the Nicene, approved and expounded in the three other Councils which we also admit.

units.la: De successione primum respondeo, quum & rationibus & omnium seculorum experientia manifestum sit hæreticos Pastores posse & potuisse veris pastoribus succedere, sequi necessario nullam esse huius argumenti vim, quæcunque tandem antiquitas aut quæcunque successorum longa series prætexatur, nisi probetur istos successores eandem cum Apostolis doctrinam profiteri: quod si nostri Catholici testimoniis ex Sacris Apostolorum tabulis depromant.
units.tr: On the question of succession, I reply first that it is clear both from reason and from the experience of every age that heretical ministers can succeed, and have been able to succeed, the true ministers. It follows necessarily that this argument has no force, however much antiquity or however long a series of successors is put forward, unless it is proved that those successors profess the same doctrine as the Apostles. Our Catholics should bring forward testimonies for this from the sacred records of the Apostles.

units.la: Responsio ad obiectionem de Successione Episcopali Romana. promptis probauerint, næ victoribus herbam dabo : sed parûm hoc metuo.Idcirco in Ecclesia Christiana quum agitur de fidei articulis, nunquam est admittenda vox ista Successionis, quod veteris Fœderis temporibus factum est, cui Nouum oportebat succedere. Doctrinam enim quam Iesus Christus primùm prædicauit, deinde Apostoli & Euangelistæ in universo terrarum orbe promulgarunt oportet ad mundi consummationem vsque sine mutatione aut alteratione vlla perdurare. Qua propter Successioni doctrinæ Christianæ nullus locus est, cuius tamen esse perpetuam continuationem oportet, licet Satan eam his vel illis locis, Pastorum negligentia, iustóque Dei iudicio sæpius interrumpat, quod paulatim contigisse videmus, præsertim in hodierna Romana Ecclesia, & quidem iam à multis seculis, sicut D. Petrus & Paulus tam disertis verbis iam olim prædixerant.
units.tr: Reply to the objection about the Roman episcopal succession. They will readily prove it; indeed, I will yield the palm to the victors, but I have little fear of this. Therefore, in the Christian Church, when the articles of faith are under discussion, this word "succession" must never be admitted. That was the case in the times of the Old Covenant, to which the New ought to succeed. For the doctrine which Jesus Christ first preached, and which the Apostles and Evangelists afterwards published throughout the whole world, must remain without change or alteration until the consummation of the world. For this reason there is no place for succession in Christian doctrine, though its perpetual continuity must be maintained. Satan often interrupts that continuity in this or that place, through the negligence of ministers and by the just judgment of God. We see that this has happened gradually, especially in the present Roman Church, and indeed for many centuries now, just as Saints Peter and Paul had foretold long ago in such plain words.

units.la: Deinde vera omnis Successio in muneribus verè Ecclesiasticis & spiritualibus, initiû ducat oportet à Filij Dei mandato,quod ipse per se,vel per suos Apostolos instituerit. Quo fundamento quum Ecclesia Romana careat, & Papatus Oecumenicus, & quicunque ab his ordines dependent, frustrà nobis Successionis obtrudi nomen afferimus,seu Prælaturæ ipsorum aliiuæ Ordines solum nomen retinentes, mera alioqui spectra,seu inuentiones humanæ, quæ tandem in meram tyrannidem euaserunt, considerentur.
units.tr: Further, every true succession in truly ecclesiastical and spiritual offices must take its beginning from the command of the Son of God, which he himself instituted either in person or through his Apostles. Since the Roman Church lacks this foundation, and the Ecumenical Papacy, together with whatever orders depend upon it, lacks it too, we declare that it is in vain that the name of succession is forced upon us. Their prelacies and other orders, which retain only the name, are otherwise mere specters, or human inventions, which have at last turned into sheer tyranny.

units.la: Accedo ad eos qui veri Baptismi in nomine Patris, Filij, & Spiritus Sancti administrationem obiiciunt, quem adhuc quod ad substantiam Ecclesia Romana retinet, unde nostri Mediatores audacter inferunt non posse nomen Ecclesiae Christianae Romanensibus negari, cuius nota & sigillum sit Baptismus. Aio vero contrà non minùs falsam & ineptam esse conclusionem, quàm si quis diceret latronibus vi maiore in sanctam familiā ingressis: potè quā cuersam, depopulatam, sus deque versam domum in eadem electo sibi domicilio, Deo volente, tamen staret adhuc atrium tectique pars quaedam, ex qua totam familiam eiicere non potuissent, sed tamen eorum vsum nonnisi durissimis & iniquissimis conditionibus concederent, quas tamen vera familia, ne prorsus tecto & atrio eiiceretur gemens admisset, illis inquam sic gestis, & huius familiae liberatore veniente si latrones illi, propterea quod domū sic inuaserint, ius in eam sibi tribuerent, quid, inquam, de tam impendentibus malae fidei vsurpatoribus aut tam malae causae patronis fieret? Et quidem asseuero eos de quibus hic ago esse istis simillimos: nempe in magna illa Apostasia quam praedixit Apostolus, Episcopum Romanum, huius in Occidente turbae principem & caput, pro viribus omnia in Dei domo pederentim subuertisse, ipsis illud historiis testantibus: miseramque hanc familiam modis indignissimis tractauisse, quam tamen funditus euertere, nec huius Dominationis tabulas & insiinsignia penitus conuellere nequiuerit. Quis verò propterea dicat turbam illam sibi posse Dominationis nomen vendicare, licet illius instrumenta & insignia palàm ostentet,quibus potiùs iniquæ suæ vsurpationis coarguantur? Talis olim fuit decem tribuum in genere conditio, quæ Circuncisionem quidem retinuerunt,sed à Dauidis domosceparatæ,expulsis Leuitis, & adoratione vitulorum Bethelitocorum inuecta, iam tunc populi Dei nomine fuerint indignæ,Osee.1.9. quo tamen merito gloriabantur Prophetarum cœtus, & alij aliquot electi Dei, quos in medio tribuum illarum sibi Dominus reseruarat. Denique vt hoc caput absoluam,si Mediatores nostri coguntur fateri vocem hanc Ecclesiæ nec hypocritis,nec contrariam veræ Religioni doctrinam profitentibus, qui tamen priuati sunt huc & illuc sparsi reuera dari posse, quomodo nomen Ecclesiæ tribuemus baptizatis quidem in nomen Patris Filij & Spiritus Sancti,sed tamen non modo non admittentibus quod præ se fert Baptismus,immo etiam Baptismo contrariam Religionem profitentibus, ipsámque adeo veritatem persequentibus?
units.tr: I come to those who object the administration of true baptism in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, which the Roman Church still retains as to its substance. From this our mediators boldly infer that the name of Christian Church cannot be denied to the Romanists, of whom Baptism is the mark and seal. I say, on the contrary, that this conclusion is no less false and absurd than if someone said this to robbers who by greater force had entered a holy household: though they had overturned, plundered and turned upside down the house, and though, by God's will, they had chosen it as their dwelling, there still remained some courtyard and part of the roof from which they could not expel the whole family. Yet they granted the family the use of these only on the harshest and most unjust conditions, which the true family, groaning, admitted so that it would not be driven entirely from the roof and courtyard. Suppose, I say, that those robbers, because they had invaded the house in this way, claimed a right over it for themselves, and suppose that the liberator of this household then came: what, I ask, would become of such usurpers of bad faith, or such patrons of a bad cause? And indeed I assert that those of whom I am speaking here are very like these robbers. In that great Apostasy which the Apostle foretold, the Roman Bishop, the prince and head of this tumult in the West, has, as far as he could, gradually overturned everything in the house of God, as the histories testify, and he has treated this poor family in the most shameful ways. Yet he has not been able to overthrow it utterly, nor to tear out completely the tablets and insignia of this dominion. Who, then, would say that this tumult can claim for itself the name of dominion, although it openly displays the instruments and insignia of that dominion, by which it is rather convicted of its unjust usurpation? Such was once the condition of the ten tribes in general. They did retain circumcision, but, separated from the house of David, with the Levites expelled and the worship of the calves of Bethel introduced, they were already then unworthy of the name of the people of God (Hos. 1.9). Yet the assembly of the prophets and the other chosen servants of God, whom the Lord had reserved for himself in the midst of those tribes, rightly gloried in that. Finally, to complete this chapter: if our mediators are compelled to admit that this name of Church can be given to those who profess a doctrine that is neither hypocritical nor contrary to true religion, yet who are scattered here and there in private, and if such a Church really can exist, how shall we give the name of Church to those who are indeed baptized in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, but who not only do not accept what Baptism carries with it, but even profess a religion contrary to Baptism, and persecute that very truth?

units.la: Quòd ad sacra volumina Veteris & Noui foederis,quæ Romana de qua loquimur Ecclesia admittit & conseruat, idem aio quod de Baptismo: Deum nempe hanc veritatem conseruasse, minimè quidem vt eam adulterantes & persequentes ad fucum faciendum abutantur ea, sed vt contrà tanto clarius & apertius eorum falsitas appareat, & ad eorum salutem promouendam inseruiat quos ab omni seculo sibi ex media ista Babylone Occidentali tandem eruendos reseruauit. Ac reuera semper hac ratione nonnullos in mediis eius penetralibus excitauit, qui se huic secreto iniquitatis opponerent, fide & doctrina secessionem a falsa ista Ecclesia facientes, licet corporibus in eadem impliciti: testibus omnium seculorum historiis, & praesertim iis quae a Constantiensi Concilio tam aperte in omnium hominum conspectu gesta sunt. Denique, asseuerantes Ecclesiam Romanam vlla ratione mereri nomen verae Ecclesiae & Sponsae Domini, quod tam diu suo sinu verae Ecclesiae, cuius nomen mentitur, tabulas & insignia fouerit, aio tam pulchre tamque bene argumentari ac siquis furem dicat virum bonum, & aliquatenus saltem bonae conscientiae possessorem, quod furtum pera sua probe tegat & conseruet.
units.tr: As to the sacred books of the Old and New Covenants, which the Roman Church of which we are speaking admits and keeps, I say the same as about Baptism. God has indeed preserved this truth, not so that those who corrupt and persecute it may use it to put on a show, but on the contrary so that their falsehood may appear all the more clearly and openly, and may serve to promote the salvation of those whom he has reserved for himself in every age, to be at last rescued from this Western Babylon. And indeed, in this way he has always raised up some in the very heart of that Church, who set themselves against this secret of iniquity, separating themselves in faith and doctrine from that false Church, though still bodily involved in it. The histories of all ages bear witness to this, and especially those things which were done so openly before the eyes of all men at the Council of Constance. Finally, when they insist that the Roman Church in no way deserves the name of the true Church and Bride of the Lord, because for so long it has cherished within its bosom the tablets and insignia of the true Church, whose name it falsely claims, I say that this argument is as absurd as if someone called a thief a good man, and at least a possessor of a good conscience, because he carefully hides and keeps the theft in his bag.

units.la: Verum amplius aliquid dicam, nempe Sacras Scripturas super quarum vera intelligentia & professione, vt eas Prophetae & Apostoli docuerunt, vera Ecclesia superstructa est, Eph. 2.20. & sunt semen illud incorruptum quo homines, ex quibus vera Ecclesia constat, Domino generantur, 1.Pet. 1.23. & cibus qui solus in vitam aeterna nutrit. Ioh.6.27. non modo illos de quibus loquor, ouibus subtraxisse a prohibentes adhuc hodie quantum in ipsis est eas tractari manibus, & legi noto omnibus idiomate: sed praeterea quum probe scirent hoc vnum velandis ipsorum mendaciis asylum sibi superesse, si Dei nomen sacrosanctum & sacras eius Scripturas in medium adferat, multis modis eas suis sophismatibus depravasse, mutasse, adulterasse, detraxisse, addidisse ut tulit ipsorum voluntas, ut nullus hoc cibo sic ab eis condito vescatur quin etiam eiusdem veneno inficiatur. Hoc ipsum nostro tempore magni illi Dei servi suscitati & ipsi docuerunt, & parati sumus adhuc in omnibus vere liberis & Christianis Conciliis demonstrare, in quibus nec adversae partes nostrae sedeant iudices, nec nos ipsi, sed sacrosanctum Dei verbum, adeo clarum & apertum ut nemo sit, modo ne passionibus & praeiudiciis locus detur, qui, Deo favente, non percipiat huius doctrinae veritatem & splendorem, quo falsitas omnis patefiat & euanescat.
units.tr: But I will say something more: the Holy Scriptures, upon the true understanding and profession of which, as the Prophets and Apostles taught them, the true Church is built (Eph. 2.20), are that incorruptible seed by which men, out of whom the true Church consists, are begotten to the Lord (1 Pet. 1.23), and the food which alone nourishes to eternal life (John 6.27). Those of whom I speak have not only taken these from their sheep, and still today forbid them to be handled by hand or read in a language known to all, as far as they can; but moreover, since they knew well that the only refuge left for covering their lies was if the sacred name of God and his holy Scriptures were brought into the open, they have in many ways depraved, changed, corrupted, subtracted from and added to these by their sophistries, as their will has prompted, so that no one feeds on this food as they have prepared it without being infected with its poison. The great servants of God raised up in our own time have themselves taught this very thing, and we are still prepared to demonstrate it in all truly free and Christian councils, in which neither our opposing side should sit as judges, nor we ourselves, but the most holy Word of God, so clear and plain that there is no one, provided passions and prejudices are not allowed a place, who, by God's favour, would fail to perceive the truth and splendour of this doctrine, by which all falsehood is laid bare and vanishes.

units.la: Quid iuuat igitur vel Trinitatis articulum in medium adferre, vel personalem vnionem duarum in Domino nostro Iesu Christo persona-rum, & Sp.S. personam, vel alios sacrorum Symbolorum articulos, fideliter e sacris Scripturis erutos ab authenticis & Orthodoxis Conciliis, & ab utraque parte legitime approbatis & admissis, si, decantatis illis omnibus lingua peregrina, Deus fingitur nec summe iustus, nec summe misericors? Si differentia Legis & Evangelij tollitur? si quod vnius Deitatis proprium est & incommunicabile, rebus tamen creatis etiam quae ex mundo excesserunt, communicatur? Si Dei filius officio suo spoliatur, ex hominum arbitrio datis illi seu æqualibus seu inferioribus sociis? si denique vix vlus superesset in symbolo Christianorum fidei articulus quæ Ecclesia ista Romana hodierna directè vel obliquè non adulterarit? Si restituuntur idola, si mortui colluntur & invocantur? Si duorum Ecclesiæ Christianæ Sacramentorum alterum mille modis polluitur, quod tamen Deus aboleri funditus non permisit: alterum vero non tantum ex parte sublatum est, sed etiam in intolerandam idolomaniam transformatum? Si verus Christianismus in monstrum transmutatum, ex duobus cadaueribus Iudaismo & Ethnicismo, & tandem mimica gesticulatione non minus ridicula quàm superstitiosa componitur?
units.tr: What use, then, is it to bring forward the article of the Trinity, or the personal union of the two natures in our Lord Jesus Christ, or the person of the Holy Spirit, or the other articles of the sacred creeds, faithfully drawn from the Holy Scriptures by authentic and orthodox councils and lawfully approved and accepted by both sides, if, all these things having been sung in a foreign tongue, God is pretended to be neither supremely just nor supremely merciful? If the difference between Law and Gospel is removed? If what belongs to the one Deity alone and cannot be shared is nevertheless communicated to created things, even to those which have departed from this world? If the Son of God is stripped of his office, and companions, whether equal or inferior, are given to him at human pleasure? If finally there is hardly a single article of the faith in the creed of Christians which this present Roman Church has not corrupted, directly or indirectly? If idols are restored, if the dead are worshipped and invoked? If one of the two sacraments of the Christian Church is polluted in a thousand ways, though God has not permitted it to be utterly abolished, while the other has not only been partly taken away but has also been transformed into an intolerable idolatry? If true Christianity has been changed into a monster, and put together out of the two corpses of Judaism and heathenism, and at last out of a mimic performance no less ridiculous than superstitious?

units.la: Denique admitto Deum ad tempus permisisse vineam suam, Ecclesiam Catholicam ex Gentibus collectam in manus pessimorum vinitorum Romanorum, ut olim sub veteri fœdere vineam suam Iudaicam in eorum manus de quibus agitur, Matt. 20. Sed etiam alio Dei electos semper ab illis fide sua discessionem fecisse, prout ad cognitionem Domini vocabatur ab ipso, sicuti nostris temporibus potenter operatus est. Fateor etiam non inuitus multas miseras conscientias, instar egrotorum, in media Babylone Romana, gemetes & languidas esse, licet tamen in hoc numero non sit illa Babylon censenda. Concedo & illud cum Apostolo, homine peccati cum sua turma tandem in Dei templum irrepsisse & sedere, quæ vera est Ecclesia: sed eos esse huius templi spiritualis, ex viuis lapidibus constructi partem audacter nego:stolidámq; & ridiculâ illâ dico cóclufionem quæ ex eo inferat Babylonē Ecclesiā esse, quòd in Ecclesia sedeat,quū longè sit aliud esse in Ecclesia, quàm Ecclesiā esse:quū nimium multos esse in Ecclesia constet,minimè tamē de Ecclesia. Agnosco etiā adhuc in hac Babylone,Scripturas,Symbola, SacrofanctùBaptismū repe-riri: sed tanquā veram lucē in laterna quæ ipsa cæca est,licet hac luce laterna illustrata,lumen aliquibus præbeat.Quapropter Babylon semper est Babylon,idest cœtus hominū quos Dominus ipse latrones per fenestram ingressos,sui temporis homines alloquēs, vocat. Ioh. 10. 1. quos Spiritus erroris agit,& repugnant ex diametro verae & vnicae Iesu Christi Domini nostri sui capitis Ecclesiae & Sponsae, ac proinde nó posse nec debere hunc cœtū comparari cor pori κακοχύμῳ, reliquam tamen adhuc in se vitam aliquam habenti & respiranti, sed contrà cadaueri quòd ad vitam spiritualem.Ac proinde procul ab ea tū animis tū corporibus disiū-gi, non est vt loquūtur isti Mediatores Ecclesiam transformare,pro ea reformanda, nec altare aduersus altare erigere. Contrà vero sansta congregatio & coitio est ad exeunduū Babylone, iuxta Ieremiæ Prophetæ exhortationem, Ierem. 51. 6. & idola fugienda, vt monemur,1.Iohan.5.21.vt omnes in sanctam Ciuitatem colligamur. Hoc ipsum est sese cognoscere vt inuicem sub vno capite strictiùs coarctemur. Et Altare Damasci abiicere, minimè
units.tr: Finally, I grant that God for a time allowed his vineyard, the Catholic Church gathered from the Gentiles, to be handed over to the wicked vinedressers of Rome, just as under the old covenant he handed his Jewish vineyard over to those of whom Matthew 20 speaks. But I also grant that God's elect have always withdrawn their faith from them, as they were called by the Lord to the knowledge of him, as he has powerfully worked in our own times. I also freely admit that many wretched consciences, like the sick, groan and languish in the middle of Roman Babylon, although Babylon itself is not to be counted among them. I concede with the Apostle that the man of sin, with his crowd, has at last crept into God's temple and sits there, which is the true Church; but I boldly deny that they are part of this spiritual temple, built of living stones. And I say that the foolish and ridiculous conclusion drawn from this, that Babylon is the Church because it sits in the Church, does not follow: it is one thing to be in the Church and another to be the Church, since it is evident that there are far too many in the Church, yet by no means are they the Church. I also acknowledge that the Scriptures, the creeds and holy Baptism are still found in this Babylon, but they are like a true light in a lantern that is itself blind; though the lantern is lit by this light, it gives light to some. Therefore Babylon is always Babylon, that is, the assembly of men whom the Lord himself calls thieves who have entered through the window, addressing the men of his time (John 10.1). They are driven by the spirit of error and are directly opposed to the true and only Church of Jesus Christ our Lord, its head, and its Bride; and therefore this assembly cannot and should not be compared to a body full of bad humours [κακοχύμῳ], which still has some life left in itself and breathes, but rather to a corpse as far as spiritual life is concerned. Accordingly, it is not, as those Mediators say, to transform the Church, in order to reform it, nor to set altar against altar, that we must separate ourselves far from it, in soul and body. On the contrary, a holy gathering and coming together is needed to leave Babylon, according to the exhortation of the prophet Jeremiah (Jer. 51.6), and to flee idols, as we are warned (1 John 5.21), so that we are all gathered into the holy city. This itself is to know ourselves, so that we may be drawn together more closely under one head. And to cast off the altar of Damascus, not, I say, so that we may set up some other altar, old or new, but so that we may cling to the one offering, made once for all and destined to last for ever, upon the altar of the cross.

units.la: {te} nec expa-te vt aliud quodpiam vetus aut Nouum erigamus, sed vt in vnica semel facta & in aeternum duratura oblatione super altari crucis facta hæreamus.
units.tr: Nor should we fear, but cling to the one offering, made once for all and to endure for ever, upon the altar of the cross.

units.la: Etsi vero, vt ad historiam reuertamur, tot testimonia tot-que testes tam luculenti tamque clare loquuti, & in superioribus orbis partibus & in infimis, plus satis redarguendis improbis, & confirmandis bonis sufficerent: infinitamque vim & potentiam Iesu Christi, licet adhuc in Cruce pendentis ac mortui testarentur, nihilominus tamen ad illa Dominus etiam voluit accedere testimonium tam eorum à quibus erat Crucifixus, quàm turbarum quæ coram Pilato tam instanter & alte fuerant vociferatæ Crucifigendum: quibus nulli magis authentici & omni exceptione maiores esse potuerunt.En igitur hinc quidem miserum Ethnicum, cui fuerat iktius executionis cum suis militibus cura demandata, clarè & apertè testantem, Iesum Christum fuisse Dei Filium, ac proinde tum iudicibus tum accusatoribus medacium impingentem, & quod ipsemet iussus impleuerat condemnantem. Inde vero ecce miseram plebeculam cum testimonio maximi doloris & ægritudinis, Magistratuum suorum improbitatem, & suum etiam consensum detestantem, quæ age sigillatim expendamus.
units.tr: Although, to return to the history, so many and such clear testimonies, and so many witnesses speaking so plainly, in the upper and lower parts of the world alike, would be more than enough to refute the wicked and confirm the good, and although they bore witness to the infinite power and might of Jesus Christ, even while he hung on the cross and was dead, nevertheless the Lord also wished to have the testimony of those by whom he was crucified, and of the crowds who had shouted so urgently and loudly before Pilate that he should be crucified. No witnesses could be more trustworthy or beyond all objection than these. Here, then, is a wretched Gentile, to whom the care of the execution, with his soldiers, had been entrusted, clearly and openly testifying that Jesus Christ was the Son of God, and so charging both judges and accusers with lying, and condemning them for what he himself had been ordered to carry out. Then, behold, the wretched common people, with a testimony of great grief and distress, detesting the wickedness of their magistrates and their own consent to it. Let us now weigh these one by one.

units.la: Duo igitur hûc Centurione cum suis militibus in hanc sententiam impulerunt, vt hic nominatim exprimuntur: vnum quod Iesus Christus Spiritum emittens tam vehementer & tam alte altè fuerat locutus, quod penitus est in tali prę- fertim supplicio, póstquc tot cruciatus, inusi- tatum & insolens: alterum quòd tam miranda, tam repentè alia aliis excipientibus contigil- sent. Igitur conclusio quam inferunt optima est ex communi sensu. Nam si Deus homines ad sui cognitionem vocat per opera sua ordinaria, nonne multò maiorem vim extraordinaria in hominibus commouendis habet? Qui fit igitur vt ij ad quos magis ista pertinebant, Caiaphas putà cum suis sociis, minùs istis commouentur, quæ Centurio tamè Ethnicus admiratur? Nempe qui conscientiæ pertinaciter vim faciunt, etiam amissa, iusto Dei iudicio, in ipsis adhuc reliqua Luce naturali qualicunque, nó habent unde collapsi resurgant: ac licet suâ præ aliis hominibus acumen prædicent (testibus ipsis Epicuris, Atheis, & egregiis illis quibus hodie scatet mundus politicis) tamen ipsis tandè animatibus crassiores & stupidiores hebetioresque comperiuntur, cuiusmodi fuisse videmus eos de quibus hic agimus, quos cœlum & terra, cum rupibus ipsis flagitij coarguebant. Hoc ipsum docet Apostolus, Rom. 1. 28. Idcirco Dominus ipse populum suum olim ad infideles ipsos per Prophetam ablegabat, Ier. 2. 11. ex quibus quæ scire debuerant edisce-rent. Nostro verò seculo nulla gens est tá malè in Religione & rebus ad conscientiá spectantibus edocta, quæ nó per se sufficiat ad errores condemnandos quos tuentur tam impudenter ac pertinaciter, qui Spiritum Sanctu suis cam-
units.tr: Two things moved this centurion and his soldiers to this opinion, as they are named here: first, that Jesus Christ, giving up his spirit, cried out so loudly and so clearly, which was entirely unusual and strange, especially in such a punishment and after so many tortures; and second, that such wonderful events, one after another, had happened in quick succession. So the conclusion they draw is entirely sound by common sense. For if God calls men to know him through his ordinary works, does he not have much greater force to move men through extraordinary works? How is it, then, that those to whom these things pertained more, such as Caiaphas and his companions, were less moved by them, while the Gentile centurion marvelled at them? Clearly, those who stubbornly do violence to their consciences, even when they have lost, by God's just judgment, the natural light of some kind that remains in them, have nothing by which to rise again once they have fallen. And although they boast of their own sharpness over other men (as the Epicureans, the atheists, and those outstanding political men with whom the world now teems bear witness), yet at last they are found to be cruder, more stupid and duller in their minds, as we see was true of those of whom we are speaking, whom heaven and earth, and even the rocks, accused of their crime. The Apostle teaches this very thing (Rom. 1.28). For this reason the Lord himself once sent his people through the prophet to the unbelievers, that they might learn from them what they ought to have known (Jer. 2.11). But in our age there is no people so badly taught in religion and in matters pertaining to conscience that it would not be enough in itself to condemn the errors which they defend so shamelessly and stubbornly, those who bind the Holy Spirit to their own

units.la: Kk. j. panilibus alligant.
units.tr: Kk. j. stocks.

units.la: Quis vero credat tam amentes homines inueniri posse qui fidem adhibeant multorum hæreticorum quotidie renascentium somniis ac deliriis? Exempli gratia, quis vnquam cogitasset Alcoranum Mahumeti fabulis maxime omnium ridiculis, quæ in mentem hominis veniant, plenum, à maxima terrarum orbis parte approbatum & admissum iri? En quo deueniat qui sibi ipsis oculos eruunt, addente præsertim Domino ad ordinaria testimonia etiam extraordinaria, quod nostra tempestate, si alias vnquam, factum esse videmus. At hic cauendæ tanquam icopuli Satanæ præstigiæ. Summus enim est in operibus Domini confingendis artifex, & quidem maxime extraordinariis, siue per illusionem, siue per causas naturales nobis incognitas agat. Testes sunt Magi Pharaonis, Simon Magus. Act.8 Elymas incantator, Act. 13. torquè huiusmodi apud historicos profanos & sacros exempla passim occurrētia. Quid igitur hic agas? Primùm aio considerantibus attentè quæ sic obtrudūtur miracula, tam apertas & manifestas impostu-ras fore, vt illis nemo nisi volens fallatur. Deinde, de istiusmodi operibus ex operatoribus facienti iudicium, vt Dominus ipse nos admonet, facile fore non decipi. Sed in primis ipso Domino dante iusto suo iudicio efficaciam erroris Spiritui, vt loquitur Apostolus 2. Thess.2.11. facile fraudes ipsius inimici detectum iri, si quam ipse Dominus cautionem populo Deut.13.1.&2.&3. præscribit scribit adhibeamus, doctrinam nimirum miraculis istis obsignandam, an à Deo sit, necne, discutiamus. Nam ab eodem Spiritu tam doctrina quàm miracula proficiscatur necesse est.
units.tr: But who would believe that men so mad could be found who give faith to the dreams and delusions of many heretics who are reborn every day? For example, who would ever have thought that the Koran of Mahomet, full of the most ridiculous fables that can enter a man's mind, would be approved and admitted by the greatest part of the world? See where those end up who tear out their own eyes, especially when the Lord adds extraordinary testimonies to ordinary ones, as we see has happened in our own time, if ever at any time. But here we must beware of Satan's illusions as of rocks. For he is the greatest artificer in counterfeiting the works of the Lord, and especially the extraordinary ones, whether he acts through deception or through natural causes unknown to us. Witnesses are the magicians of Pharaoh, Simon Magus (Acts 8), and Elymas the sorcerer (Acts 13), and examples of this kind occur everywhere in profane and sacred historians. What, then, should you do here? First, I say that to those who attentively consider the miracles thrust upon them in this way, the deceptions will be so plain and manifest that no one is deceived by them unless he wills to be. Second, as the Lord himself warns us, it will be easy not to be deceived in judging such works by their workers. But above all, since by his just judgment the Lord gives the power of error to the spirit, as the Apostle says (2 Thess. 2.11), the deceits of the enemy himself will easily be detected if we observe the caution which the Lord himself prescribes to the people (Deut. 13.1, 2, 3), namely, that we examine the doctrine which is to be confirmed by these miracles, whether it is from God or not. For both doctrine and miracles must necessarily come from the same Spirit.

units.la: Cæterum non sic iste Centurio, nec eius milites dicunt Iesum Christum esse Dei Filium, vt Caiaphas ex eo an esset Dei Filius quæsierat. Matth. 26.63. sed simpliciter dicunt, fuisse Dei Filium. Miser enim iste Ethnicus hunc Dei Filium Iudæis declaratum & promissum ignorabat: multíque adeò in ipso Dei populo tantum istud arcanum non capiebant. Deinde si de quopiam verè Dei Filio per generationem loquutus esset, quales poëtæ multos in fabulis confinxerunt, nec suam socordiam patefecisset.
units.tr: But this centurion and his soldiers do not speak in the same way, nor do they say that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, as Caiaphas asked him whether he was the Son of God (Matt. 26.63); they simply say that he was the Son of God. For this Gentile wretch did not know that the Son of God had been declared and promised to the Jews, and indeed many in God's own people did not grasp this secret. Moreover, if he had spoken of someone truly the Son of God by generation, in the manner in which the poets invented many such figures in their fables, he would not have revealed his own dullness.

units.la: Nam à Deo quopiam verè progenitus, Deus etiam fuisset, ac proinde immortalis: ideoque minimè dicendum, Hic erat Dei Filius, quasi non amplius esset, siquidem erat mortuus. At non est ista miser hic Ethnicus penitius scrutatus: sed quoniam in Iudæorum accusatione adversus Christum, audiuerat inter reliqua illi obiicivoce & titulum Filij Dei, hac etiâ vsus est voce, Iudæis exprobrans, verè talem fuisse Iesum Christum qualem se dicebat, magnum nempe & eximium virum, iustum ac innocentem, qualem eum Pilatus prædicauerat: licet aduersus eum sententiam coactus dixisset, prout etiam Lucas hanc Filij Dei vocem exponit, Luc. 23. 43. Sed reuera Centurio hic quæ tam insolentia & admiranda contigerant cum stupore intuitus, aliquid etiam amplius dicere voluit fuisse in Christo aliquâ vim & potentiam plus quàm humanam: & sanè verum istud erat, sed longè aliter quàm hic sibi Centurio persuaderet. Verumenimuerò quum longè fit illustrior nostra cognitio, qua Iesus Christus nobis patefit, quàm istius Ethnici, non eum tantùm vt hominem ab ipsa conceptione, longè ipsis etiam Angelis excellentior em, sed etiam vt verû Dei Filiû coëffentialem & coæternum agnoscemus: nam hæc est vera cognitio cui vita æterna promittitur. Ioh.17.3. quod suo loco pluribus persecuti fumus: ad quem etiam scopum oportuit edita tum à Domino tum abipfius discipulis miracula referri.
units.tr: For someone truly begotten of God would also have been God, and therefore immortal; so it should by no means be said, "This was the Son of God," as if he were no longer so, since he had died. But this wretched heathen did not examine the matter more deeply. Having heard, among the other charges in the Jews' accusation against Christ, the title of Son of God, he used this expression too, reproaching the Jews that Jesus Christ was truly what he claimed to be: a great and outstanding man, just and innocent, as Pilate had declared him, although he had been compelled to pronounce sentence against him. Luke also explains this expression "Son of God," Luke 23:43. But in truth this centurion, gazing in astonishment at what had happened so strangely and wonderfully, wanted to say something more, namely that there was in Christ some power and might beyond the human. And indeed that was true, but very differently from what the centurion persuaded himself. However, since our knowledge, by which Jesus Christ is revealed to us, is far clearer than that of this heathen, we acknowledge him not only as a man far more excellent than the angels from his very conception, but also as the true Son of God, co-essential and co-eternal. For this is the true knowledge to which eternal life is promised, John 17:3, which we have pursued at length in its place. To this same end it was necessary that the miracles performed both by the Lord and by his disciples be recounted.

units.la: Turbæ verò reuertentes prorsus aliæ quàm venerant, pectora sua tundentes, quarum pars ad hoc spectaculum ex curiositate venerant: pars ex eorum erant numero qui Crucifigendum erant ex Sacerdotum perfuafione vociferati, quod diserte dicit Matt.27.20. docent nos quanta fit innocentiæ & veritatis vis, quæ licet obruta tamè emergit. Quicquid enim molian-tur homines, Deum cum sua veritate regnare necesse est: & peccatorem à conscientia sua quando minimè velit, excitari. Beatus ille verò qui loquentem maturè audit, vt ab eius offensione recedat: quod sanè serius quàm nuquam fieri satius est. Factorum autem præteritorû illam detestationem minimè fuisse simulatam, sicut illa Caiaphi fuerat simulatio & hypocrisis detestanda, veltimenta sua lacerantis, Matt. 26.65. ex pectorum illa verberatione conspicuum cuum est: quod fieri non potuit sine eorum offensione & detestatione manifesta in publico qui populo tam misere impositerant: in quorum aspectu haec fiebant: & quidem vt sit mihi verisimile, non sine durioribus verbis & contumeliis in ipsos Sacerdotes, licet ab Euangelistis perscripta non sint.
units.tr: The crowds, however, returned quite different from how they had come, beating their breasts. Some of them had come to this spectacle out of curiosity; others were among those who, at the persuasion of the priests, had shouted for him to be crucified, as Matthew 27:20 plainly states. They teach us how great is the power of innocence and truth, which, though overwhelmed, rises again. For whatever men may plot, God's truth must reign, and a sinner, even when he does not wish it, is roused by his conscience. Blessed is he who hears the one speaking in time, so as to withdraw from giving offence to him; and indeed it is better that this be done late than never. That their detestation of the things done in the past was not feigned, as the pretence and hypocrisy of Caiaphas was, who tore his garments (Matthew 26:65), is clear from this beating of their breasts. It could not have happened without manifest offence and detestation, openly shown, toward those who had so wretchedly deceived the people, in whose sight these things were done. And indeed, as seems likely to me, not without harsher words and insults against the priests themselves, although the Evangelists have not recorded them.

units.la: Discamus igitur ex iis non sufficere si peccatores admissorum facinorum interiore poenitentia tangantur, sed, vt res postulabit, etiam requiri, saltem iis quibus aedificandis inseruire potest, fieri manifesta. Qua in re duo nobis extrema fugienda sunt. Nam sicut non pauci sunt in quibus ille conscientiae morsus statim evanescit, vel illis testibus qui sufficere iactitant, siquis haec demurmuret, aut Peccavi, aut Mea Culpa, aut Confiteor: aut aquae lustralis aliquam aspersionem ad peccata delenda: sic plerumque contingit vt qui extrinsecus in multorum gestuum excessu peccare videntur, minus tamen intrinsecus afficiantur. Hic igitur a Deo sana rectaque conscientia postulanda est, quam Spiritus ipse Sanctus regat, ex quo discamus quousque gemitus illos ineffabiles oporteat progredi. Rom. 8. 26. & quid expediat: cuius rei plurima nobis ante oculos propositia sunt excellentissima exempla nominatim in Dauide & Petro, & in misero Publicano, multo maiora apud se premente quam extrinsecus proferente, de quo Lucas 18.13.
units.tr: Let us therefore learn from these people that it is not enough for sinners to be touched by inward repentance for the crimes they have committed; where the matter requires it, and at least for those whose edification it can serve, it must also be made manifest. In this matter two extremes must be avoided. For just as there are not a few in whom that gnawing of conscience quickly vanishes, relying on those witnesses who boast that it is enough, if someone mutters this formula, "I have sinned," or "my fault," or "I confess," or sprinkles himself with some lustral water to wipe away sins, so it commonly happens that those who seem to sin outwardly, in the excess of many gestures, are nonetheless less affected inwardly. Here, therefore, a sound and upright conscience must be sought from God, ruled by the Holy Spirit himself, from which we learn how far those ineffable groanings ought to go (Romans 8:26), and what is expedient. Of this there are very many most excellent examples set before our eyes, especially in David and Peter, and in the wretched publican, who held much more within himself than he expressed outwardly (Luke 18:13).

units.la: Historia deinceps narrat Iesu Christi familiares, & nominatim quasdam foeminas quae Ie suim Christum à Galilæa sequutæ fuerât ei subministrantes procul ista spectasse: quæ sunt nobis etiam consideranda. Nec enim abs re momentis tradita sunt, & quidem Spiritus S. quasdam ex illis mulieribus est honore tanto dignatus, ut nomen etiam earum edi voluerit.
units.tr: The history next tells of Jesus Christ's familiar acquaintances, and especially of certain women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and ministered to him, who watched these things from afar. These too must be considered by us. For they were not recorded without purpose, and indeed the Holy Spirit thought some of those women worthy of such honour that he wished their names to be published as well.

units.la: Nobis igitur hic exemplum proponitur specialis gratiæ quam iis Deus largitur, qui se huius sæculi potentum iudicio facilè non permittunt, quales eo tempore fuerunt Sacerdotes Pharisæi & Scribæ: nec etiam imperitæ plebeculæ multitudini: sed rationem qua perveniat ad veritatis cognitionem quærunt, ex qua ipsorum conscientiæ tranquillentur, quam etiam inuentam quæcunque tandem ingruant pericula persequuntur, ad eorum de quibus hic agimus exemplum. Vbi tamen obseruandum maiores iis fuisse faciendos progressus, quod in historia resurrectionis sumus pluribus audituri. Quod vero procul sterisse dicuntur, de omnibus singillatim intelligendum non est: Mater enim ipsa Iesu Christi tam forti fuerat animo & verè admiranda constantia, ut propè Iesum Christum Crucifixum staret, & quædam aliæ cum ipsa mulieres. Ioh. 19. 25. quas tamen quum hic iterum recenseri videamus cum iis quæ procul hæc intuebantur, ex eo docemur omnes illas (excepto dilecto discipulo, qui ibidem quousque latus Iesu Christi lancea perfossum esset permansit Ioh.19.35.) postquam animam exhalasset Christus cœpisse domum recipere, sed sæpius conuersas procul spectasse. stasse, minimè quidem ex metu aut infirmitate, sed quòd non sine summo mœrore possent à Christo auelli, quandiu pendentem in Cruce conspicerent: quæ confirmantur ex eo quod de iisdem mulieribus narratur apud Matth. 27. 61. & Luc. 33. 55. non deseruisse ipsas Christi corpus priusquam quid eo fieret, & vbi locaretur conspicerent. En igitur singularis amicitiæ exemplum, sanè non tantùm humanæ, sed à Spiritu Sancto proficiscentis, etsi nondum tamen perfectæ, quod sumus ex historia sepulturę cognituri.
units.tr: Here, then, is set before us an example of the special grace that God bestows on those who do not readily allow themselves to be judged by the powerful of this age, such as the priests, Pharisees and scribes of that time, nor by the untutored mass of the common people; but who seek the way to the knowledge of the truth, by which their consciences may be quieted, and who, once they have found it, pursue it whatever dangers threaten. This is the example of those of whom we are speaking. Yet we must observe that they were to make greater progress later, which we shall hear about at length in the history of the resurrection. But that they are said to have stood afar off must not be understood of all of them individually. For the mother of Jesus Christ herself was of such strong spirit and truly admirable constancy that she stood near Jesus crucified, and some other women with her (John 19:25). Yet since we see them listed again here among those who watched from afar, we are taught that all of those women (except the beloved disciple, who remained there until the side of Jesus was pierced with a lance, John 19:35) began, after Christ had breathed out his spirit, to withdraw home, but often turned back and watched from a distance, and stood still. They did this not from fear or weakness, but because they could not be torn away from Christ without the greatest sorrow while they saw him hanging on the cross. This is confirmed by what is related of the same women in Matthew 27:61 and Luke 23:55: they did not leave Christ's body before they had seen what was done with it and where it was laid. Behold, then, an example of singular friendship, certainly not merely human but proceeding from the Holy Spirit, though not yet perfect, as we shall learn from the history of the burial.

units.la: Porrò si mulierum istarum tantus fuit erga Christum adeò exinanitum & abiectum animus & tantus amor, quam tandem excusatio- nem hodie sunt allaturi, qui quum vere suscitatum ipsum sciant, & in gloriæ possessionem venïsse, omnémque potestatem habere in cœlo & terra, tam facilè tamen terrentur, adeò vt ad minimas etiam Satanæ minas eius professionem abiicere parati sint, quum prorsus etiam ij sint inexcusabiles, qui semel inceptum ex Dei gratia cursum ad metam vsque non decurrunt? Serió itaque, fratres, de istis cogitemus, ne à mulierculis istis arguamur ignauiæ: & contrà assiduè fidei incrementa petamus vt ad metam vsque perueнiamus, in qua vna non in principio, nec in medio cursu nobis est corona reposita.
units.tr: Furthermore, if those women had such great devotion and such great love toward Christ when he was so emptied and abased, what excuse will those today offer who, though they know that he has truly been raised and has entered into possession of glory, and has all power in heaven and on earth, are nevertheless so easily terrified that they are ready to cast away their profession at even the slightest threats of Satan? Those too are wholly inexcusable who do not run to the goal the course begun by the grace of God. Let us therefore think seriously on these matters, brethren, lest we be convicted of cowardice by these poor women; and on the contrary let us constantly seek increase of faith, so that we may reach the goal, in which alone the crown is laid up for us, not at the beginning nor in the middle of the course.

units.la: Cæterum, licet Christus humanitatis suę re- spectu longè remotior à nobis, qui in terris sumus, sit, supra cœlos omnes eneċtus, quàm
units.tr: Moreover, although Christ, with respect to his humanity, is far removed from us who are on earth, and is raised above all the heavens, nevertheless

units.la: Vsus humanitatis exemplis.
units.tr: The use of the examples of his humanity.

units.la: quo tempore haec contigerunt, non habemus tamen quod de locorum intervallo conquera- mur(quo sane ab eius conspectu corporei no- stri oculi arcentur) aut inde capiamus excusa- tionem cum non intuendi. Nam praeterquam quod est cum Ecclesia sua, & futurus est ad se- culorum usque consummationem Deitatis suae vi & salutari potentia (cuius praesentiae respe- ctu dicitur ipse & Pater in nobis ipsis habita- re, Ioh. 14. 23. Matth. 28.20.) oculis etiam fidei non corporeis Christus ad salutem proprie vi- detur, quorum tanta vis est & acies ut illis Abrahamus diem Domini procul aspexerit, etiā ante quam eius humanitas extaret, Ioh. 8. 56. Hos igitur oculos si Deus dederit, vere etiam eum intuendi contemplandique facultas dabitur, ut nullus sit nobis alius visus necessarius, quod ipse Iesus Christus Thomam alloquutus, nos docet, Ioh. 20. 29. Nec vero fides tantum oculos quibus cum in superioribus locis intucamur suppeditat, sed etiam manus, quibus ad salutem ipsum amplectamur, quandoquidem instrumentum est quo illi tanquam membra capiti copulamur & utimur. Praeterea, quū ipse Christus in verbo suo, sicuti loquitur Apostolus, ob oculos mentis nostrae depingatur, & Sacramenta non sint inania signa, sed fidei nostrae tanquam oculis inspicienda praebeant, tam Iesum Christum quam quaecunque possumus ac debemus ab ipso beneficia exspectare, ne amplius de eius absentia conquera- mur, sed propius ad eum accedamus, ut quotidie prior ad nos per verbi prædicationem, Sacramentorum administrationem, internámque in conscientiis Sancti Spiritus solicitationem accedit: quibus contentos esse nos oportet tamen perdum eum qualis est videamus. 1. Ioh. 3. 2. quando nimirum quod in nobis tantum est inchoatum, ex parte perficietur. 1. Cor. 13. 10. Cauendum autem summopere nobis ab eorum stupiditate qui ipsum adhuc in terris quærunt, & tantopere delirantes somniant vt oculis corporeis illum videre se arbitrentur, & manibus ipsis & ore suo continere quem in supernis quærere debuerunt, vbi est ipse quòd ad humanitatem, & futurus est ad seculorum vsque consummationem, testibus ipsis Angelis, Act. 1. 11. & D. Petro Act. 3. 21. sicuti nos etiam in Articulo fidei diserte, Venturum ipsum ad viuos & mortuos iudicandum profitemur.
units.tr: at the time when these things happened, we nevertheless have no reason to complain of the distance of places (which indeed keeps our bodily eyes from his bodily sight), nor to take from this an excuse for not seeing him. For, besides the fact that he is with his Church and will be, until the consummation of the ages, by the power and saving might of his Deity (in whose presence it is said that he and the Father dwell in us, John 14:23; Matthew 28:20), Christ is also seen properly for salvation by the eyes of faith, which are not bodily. Their power and keenness are such that Abraham saw the day of the Lord from afar, even before his humanity appeared (John 8:56). If God gives us these eyes, the faculty of truly seeing and contemplating him will also be given, so that we need no other sight; as Jesus Christ himself, addressing Thomas, teaches us (John 20:29). Nor does faith supply only the eyes with which we look upon him in the higher places, but also the hands with which we embrace him for salvation, since it is the instrument by which we are joined to him, as members to the head, and by which we make use of him. Moreover, since Christ is depicted before the eyes of our mind in his Word, as the Apostle says, and the sacraments are not empty signs but offer themselves to be looked upon by our faith as if by the eyes, we should expect from Jesus Christ both himself and whatever benefits we can and ought to expect from him. Let us therefore no longer complain of his absence, but draw nearer to him, as he daily comes nearer to us through the preaching of the Word, the administration of the sacraments, and the inward stirring of the Holy Spirit in our consciences. We ought to be content with these things, until we see him as he is (1 John 3:2), when what is only begun in us will be brought to completion in part (1 Corinthians 13:10). We must, however, take the greatest care to avoid the stupidity of those who still seek him on earth, and who, so raving, dream that they think they see him with bodily eyes and hold with their hands and mouths him whom they ought to seek above, where he is as to his humanity, and where he will remain until the consummation of the ages, as the angels themselves bear witness (Acts 1:11), and Peter too (Acts 3:21). So also we openly profess in the article of faith that he will come to judge the living and the dead.

units.la: Superest quod de mulieribus istis dicitur, Iesu Christo nimirum illas subministrasse, ventibus Euangelistis voce quæ in genere vel ministerium vel subsidium significat, quod alijs præstare possumus ac debemus amico-rum necessitatem nostris etiam facultatibus subleuantes. Quacunque igitur significatione accipiamus, veræ charitatis exemplum nobis hic proponitur, quæ non in verbis nudis sed in effectu posita est, Iac. 2. 16.
units.tr: It remains to speak of these women, that they ministered to Jesus Christ, the evangelists using a word which in general signifies either ministry or support, which we too can and ought to give to others, relieving the needs of friends even from our own resources. Whatever meaning we take, an example of true charity is set before us here, which lies not in bare words but in deeds (Jas. 2.16).

units.la: Deinde videndum hic nobis vt & in tota Iesu Christi vita quousque se ipse po nobis abiecerit, & pauper factus sit quippe qui vo-
units.tr: Next we should see here, as in the whole life of Jesus Christ, how far he humbled himself for us and became poor, he who

units.la: lucerit in stabulo nasci, Luc. 2.7. & in fabri domo educari. Marc. 6.3. locum non habere in quo caput reclinaret. Matth. 8.20. quae in se omnia sane recepit, tum vt peccatis nostris debitas poenas exsoluteret, tum nostram conditionem nobis ob oculos poneret: & exemplo praeiret, ex quo nominatim vera bona & non caduca sequi & ampletti discamus.2. Cor. 8.9. Aures ergo praebete, vos quibus terrenae opes denegatae sunt, attendite, inquam, ac scitote vos paupertate magnis impedimentis & oneribus subleuari: vobisque hanc praerogatiuam dari vt Filij Dei insignibus vestiamini, & veterum Patrum sub tabernaculis vitam agitantium, atque adeo Iohannis & Petri non habentium vnde stipem illi pauperi claudo erogaret, Act. 3.6. & D. Paulo qui labore manuu sibi in diem saepe victum quaesiuit. Act. 18.3. & 20.34. Vos vero, diuites, ne cogitate vos ex diuitiis coram Deo pluris quam alios fieri. Nam contra, non ij estis, maxima saltem ex parte, quos in suam familiam Deus adscisit, vt ipse testatus est, Luc. 18.25. & omnium seculorum experientia comprobauit, 1. Cor. 1.16. Quid ergo? nempe diuitem Abrahamum imitamini, & cum pulchre vobiscum agi sentietis. Nec vero Paupertas ipsa per se, nec eius votum coelos aperit. At Dei timor, via est qua tum diuites tum pauperes in vitam ingrediuntur. Licet vere illud dicatur, huius seculi facultatibus onustos, ad cursum esse aliis segniores, & ad superanda huius vitae multa incommoda longe ineptiores.
units.tr: willed to be born in a stable (Luke 2.7) and to be brought up in a carpenter's house (Mark 6.3), and had no place where he might lay his head (Matt. 8.20). He indeed took all these things upon himself, partly so that he might pay the penalties owed for our sins, and partly so that he might set our condition before our eyes and go before us as an example, from which we learn to seek and embrace true goods, which do not perish (2 Cor. 8.9). So give ear, you to whom earthly riches have been denied; attend, I say, and know that poverty relieves you of great hindrances and burdens, and that this privilege is given to you, that you may be clothed with the marks of the sons of God, like the fathers of old who lived in tents, and like John and Peter, who had nothing to give that lame beggar (Acts 3.6), and like the apostle Paul, who often sought his daily bread by the labour of his own hands (Acts 18.3; 20.34). But you rich, do not think that you are counted more highly before God than others because of your riches. For on the contrary, you are not, at least for the most part, those whom God has taken into his household, as he himself testified (Luke 18.25), and as the experience of all ages has proved (1 Cor. 1.26). What then? Imitate indeed the rich Abraham, and you will feel that you are dealt with handsomely. Yet poverty in itself does not open heaven, nor does its vow. But the fear of God is the way by which both rich and poor enter into life. Though it is truly said that those laden with the wealth of this age are slower in the race than others, and far less fit to overcome the many troubles of this life.

units.la: Tertio,
units.tr: Thirdly,

units.la: Tertiò, licet Christus, quoties ita voluit sa-tis testatus esset non deesse rationes sibi vitæ necessitates suas & suorum sine hominum ministerio subleuandi: quandoquidem tam pau-cis panibus & piscciculis tantam hominum multitudinem pauerat: teste quoque statere in ore piscis inuento.Matt.17.27.verè tamen aliorum opus habuit subsidio & ministerio : & ipse accepta subuentione, cuius exemplum habemus in domo Lazari,Ioh.11.ad exemplum Prophetæ, docuit suo exemplo, spiritualia serentes,carnalia posse metere, vt loquitur Apostolus.1.Cor.9.11.dignumque mercede sua operarium, vti sub Lege Deus Leuitis suam portionem assignarat. Ac si merito culpantur qui in rebus terrenis suorum mercenariorum mercedem retinent,Leuit.19.13.quanto magis non tantum fures dicendi sunt, sed sacrilegi suis Pastoribus victum denegantes, quibus iustum stipendium persoluentes, de suo nihil largiun-tur,sed quæ merito debent exsoluunt?
units.tr: Thirdly, although Christ, whenever he chose, sufficiently showed that he had means of relieving his own and his followers' needs without the ministry of men (since he fed so great a crowd of men with so few loaves and little fishes; and also the stater found in the mouth of the fish bears witness, Matt. 17.27), nevertheless he truly had need of the help and ministry of others. And, having received support, of which we have an example in the house of Lazarus (John 11), he taught by his own example, after the pattern of the prophet, that those who sow spiritual things may reap carnal things, as the Apostle says (1 Cor. 9.11), and that the labourer is worthy of his wage, just as under the Law God assigned their portion to the Levites. If those are rightly blamed who keep back the wages of their hired servants in earthly matters (Lev. 19.13), how much more are they to be called not merely thieves but sacrilegious, who deny food to their pastors, not paying them a just stipend, and giving nothing from their own means, but paying only what they rightly owe?

units.la: Porrò duo scopuli veris Pastoribus hic sunt cauendi. Prior ne mercenarij sint,ideò merce-dis causa seruiant, quū res sanctæ non vedan-tur,sed à Deo gratis per seruorum suorum ministerium dentur,Matth.10.8.contra quàm Simo ille Magus imaginaretur, Act.8.20. Alter scopulus, cupiditas habendi & auaritia à qua procul alienos esse oportet,multóque magis à rapacitate nimium Pharisæis familiari, de qua fit mentio,Matth.23.14. & Sacerdotibus ipsis olim tanquam panem populum vorantibus, vt eis Prophetę exprobrant: quos victu & vestitu 1.Tim.6. 8. & quidem nonnunquam ut e-runt tempora tenuiore conditione contentos esse oportet.
units.tr: Moreover, there are two rocks which true ministers must avoid here. The first is that they not be mercenaries, serving for the sake of wages, when holy things are not to be sold but are given freely by God through the ministry of his servants (Matt. 10.8), unlike what that Simon the Magician imagined (Acts 8.20). The other rock is the desire of having and avarice, from which they ought to stay far away, and much more from the rapacity too familiar among the Pharisees, which is mentioned (Matt. 23.14), and among the priests themselves, who of old devoured the people as bread, as the prophets reproach them. They ought to be content with food and clothing (1 Tim. 6.8), and indeed, as the times are, sometimes with a meagre condition.

units.la: Denique hinc facessant procul, falsi Pastores,Sacrilegi, solum nomen pastorum præ se ferentes,Mendici illi fratres,quos alieno viure ex voto non pudet, cantillationibus mundo imponentes, & quidem adeo perfrictæ frontis homines,vt huius subuentionis prætextu, non vereantur se Iesu Christi exemplo tueri: qua in re non immerito Papa quidam illos grauiter increpuit. Nec enim Iesus Christus mendicauit, prohibita nempe Lege mendicitas erat, Deut.15.11.& in omnibus bene constitutis Rebuspublicis : qua propter nisi fascinarentur homines, istos etiam publicis affici pœnis oporteret.Contra vero,licet Christus quū ita tulit necessitas oblatam subuentionem accepit, tamesuum ipse dispensatorem habuit, & pauperibus etiam aliquid largitus est. Præterea, tantum abest vt a quibus subuentionem accepit,aliquid eo nomine debuerit, vt contra ea accepta ab ipsis non paruo sit eos honore dignatus. Ac sane, qui charitatem sic exercent, potius accipiunt quam largiuntur, nisi ipsam hac de re Domini sententiam,Matth. 10.42.& quæ se vltimo die pronuntiaturum & executurum præmonuit Matth.25.34.& 40.in dubium reuocemus.
units.tr: Finally, let the false pastors, the sacrilegious, who bear only the name of pastors, depart far from here: those mendicant brothers who are not ashamed to live on another's means by vow, imposing on the world with their chants, and indeed men of such brazen forehead that under the pretext of this support they do not hesitate to defend themselves by the example of Jesus Christ. In this matter a certain Pope rightly rebuked them severely. For Jesus Christ did not beg, since begging was forbidden by the Law (Deut. 15.11), and in all well-ordered commonwealths. Therefore, unless men were bewitched, such persons ought also to be punished by public penalties. On the contrary, although Christ, when necessity so required, accepted the support offered, yet he had his own steward, and he also gave something to the poor. Moreover, so far is it from being the case that he owed anything on that account to those from whom he received support, that on the contrary he thought them worthy of no small honour for what he had received from them. Indeed, those who exercise charity in this way rather receive than give, unless we call into doubt the Lord's own sentence (Matt. 10.42), and his promise, which he forewarned he would pronounce and execute on the last day (Matt. 25.34, 40).

units.la: {*} Hæc Mendicos illos Monachos aut alios ipsis similes non sunt.
units.tr: {*} These things do not apply to those mendicant monks or others like them.

units.la: HOMILIA TRIcesima quinta.
units.tr: Homily thirty-fifth.

units.la: Historia sepultura Iesu Christi.
units.tr: The history of the burial of Jesus Christ.

units.la: IOH. 19.
units.tr: John 19.

units.la: Iudæi autem vt non manerent in cruce corpora Sabbatho, quoniā erat Parasceue, (erat enim magnus dies illius Sabbathi) rogarunt Pilatum vt confringerentur eorum crura, ac tollerentur. 31.
units.tr: The Jews then, so that the bodies might not remain on the cross on the Sabbath, since it was the Preparation (for that Sabbath was a great day), asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and they might be taken away. 31.

units.la: 32. Venerunt ergo milites, & prioris quidem [latronis] confregerunt crura, & alterius qui crucifixus erat cum eo.
units.tr: 32. So the soldiers came, and broke the legs of the first [thief] and of the other who was crucified with him.

units.la: 33. Ad Iesum autem quum venissent, vt viderūt eum iam mortuum, non confregerunt eius crura.
units.tr: 33. But when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs.

units.la: 34. Sed quidam ex militibus lancea latus eius fodit, & statim exiuit sanguis & aqua.
units.tr: 34. But one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once there came out blood and water.

units.la: 35. Et qui vidit testatur, & verum est testimonium eius: ille [inquam] scit se verum dicere, vt & vos credatis.
units.tr: 35. And he who saw it bears witness, and his testimony is true; he, I say, knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe.

units.la: 36. Facta sunt enim hæc vt Scriptura impleretur [dicens] Non confringetur [vllum] os ipsius.
units.tr: 36. For these things happened so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: "Not one of his bones shall be broken."

units.la: 37. Et rursus alia Scriptura dicit, Videbunt quem transfixerunt.
units.tr: 37. And again another Scripture says: "They shall look on him whom they pierced."

units.la: VVM Dominicae resurrectionis articulus tanti sit momenti
units.tr: When the article of the Lord's resurrection is of such moment

units.la: ut sine illo mortis ac passionis Domini fructus nullus sit (nec enim a morte nos ille liberaret, qui semetipsum eius tyrannide non exemisset) ac proinde sit inanis omnis de ipso praedicatio, & fides etiam de ipso nostra, 1. Corinth. 15.14. hunc etiam articulum oportet necessario credi a nobis & admitti. At sensui communi & humanae rationi ex diametro repugnat, adeo quidem ut magni illi Athenis Philosophi de ea disputare volentem Apostolum irriserint. Act. 17.32. Ideo nos Spiritus Sanctus variis testimoniis de huius articuli veritate facere certiores voluit, ut in historiae explicatione visuri sumus. At ut mille calumniis obviam iretur, oportuit primum de morte Iesu Christi certo constare, ne forte posset obiici quod Christus inclinato capite, etiam obmutuisset, factum ex animi deliquio, reipsa vero mortuum non esse. Ad hoc igitur doctrinae caput, ut & ad alia quam plurima excellentissimae doctrinae capita, referenda est haec ab aliis Euangeliistis omissa historia, sed a Iohanne teste oculato fidelissimoque conscripta.
units.tr: that without it there is no fruit of the Lord's death (for he who did not free himself from the tyranny of death would not free us from it), and therefore all preaching about him, and our faith in him as well, is empty (1 Cor. 15.14), this article too must necessarily be believed and accepted by us. Yet it runs directly against common sense and human reason, so much so that those famous philosophers at Athens mocked the Apostle when he wished to discuss it (Acts 17.32). Therefore the Holy Spirit wished to make us more certain of the truth of this article by various testimonies, as we shall see in the explanation of the history. But to meet a thousand calumnies, it was first necessary to be certain about the death of Jesus Christ, lest it be objected that Christ, having bowed his head, had only swooned, a faint of the spirit, and was not in fact dead. To this head of doctrine, as to very many other most excellent heads of doctrine, this history, omitted by the other Evangelists but written down by John, an eyewitness and most faithful, is to be referred.

units.la: Singularem igitur hic Dei providentiam observemus, eligentis testes harum rerum non simpliciter suum discipulum suspectum futurum & reiectaneum, sed ipsos Iudaeos, quorum precibus & instantia facta sunt haec omnia: deinde militem Ethnicum & prophanum, sine du-
units.tr: Let us observe, then, the singular providence of God, who chose as witnesses of these things not simply his own disciple, who would be open to suspicion and rejection, but the Jews themselves, at whose prayers and insistence all these things were done; and then a heathen and profane soldier, who

units.la: bio Christum,nisi prius eflet mortuus, inflicto lethali vulnere interfecturum. Quum Dominus igitur tantus sit & tam insignis opifex, vt quotiescunque velit hostibus etiam suis vtatur iudicioru m suorum executoribus, vt quae decreuit ad minimum etiam vsque apicem tam ad suam gloriam, quàm ad hostium suorum pudorem & suorum salutem exequantur, precemur cum vt nobis hanc gratiam largiatur, vt in omnibus angustiis & difficultatibus ad sacrosanctam eius & tutissimam prouidetiam vt ad sacram anchoram confugiamus, patienter exitum illius exspectantes, vt pulchre monet, Psal.27. quo tandem cum eodem Propheta, verè in has laudes erumpamus, Exspectando exspectaui Iehouam, & inclinauit sese ad me, & audiuit clamorem meum. Psal.40.1.
units.tr: without doubt would have killed Christ by inflicting a deadly wound, had he not already been dead. Since the Lord is therefore so great and so remarkable a craftsman that whenever he wishes he uses even his enemies as executors of his judgments, carrying out what he has decreed, down to the smallest point, both for his own glory and for the shame of his enemies and the salvation of his people, let us pray that he grant us this grace: that in all distresses and difficulties we may flee to his most holy and most secure providence as to a sacred anchor, waiting patiently for the outcome, as Psalm 27 beautifully advises; so that at last, with the same Prophet, we may truly break out in this praise: "I waited patiently for the LORD, and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry" (Ps. 40.1).

units.la: Accipite igitur hac in re Sacerdotum consilium, à Deo tamen in contrarium conuersum: nempe quum Lege statutum esset vt eorum qui in ligno pependerant cadauera, deponerentur eodem die, Deut. 21. 23. deinde sequens hanc executionem dies dupliciter festus esset, tum propter ordinarium Sabbathū, tum quod Paschain sequentem diem reiectum esset, vt suprà monuimus: & praeterea vererentur ne si tamdiu exspectarent dum naturali morte crucifixi morerentur reliqua dici pars quae occasu Solis finiebatur, non sufficeret illis de Cruce deponendis, idcirco Pilatum rogarunt vt fractis cruribus mors ipsorū maturaretur. At quaenam haec religio? Nimirum eadem qua Pilati
units.tr: Hear, then, in this matter the counsel of the priests, yet turned by God to the contrary. For although the Law had ordained that the bodies of those hanged on a tree should be taken down the same day (Deut. 21.23), and the following day was doubly festive, both because of the ordinary Sabbath and because the Passover was to follow, as we noted above, and moreover they feared that if they waited until the crucified died a natural death, the remaining part of the day, which ended at sunset, would not suffice for taking them down from the cross, therefore they asked Pilate that their death be hastened by breaking their legs. But what kind of religion is this? Namely, the same as Pilate's.

units.la: Iudaeorum denotio ex parte firmo nixa fundamento, sed magis in vtum vocata. tectum subire ne polluerentur refugerant, Ioh. 18.28. non tamen veriti se tot tamque infandis flagitiis polluere, iudicemque ad innocentis hominis condemnationem ad Crucem impellere, quod olim ipsis Dominus exprobrarat, excolare nimirum ipsos culicem, camelum autem deglutire, Matth. 23. 24.
