Sin obiiciatur contrà, quod à quatuor Euangelistis memoriæ prodi-tum est de Maria sorore Lazari, quæ caput eius vnguento pretiosissimo perfuderat, quod factum Christus non modò comprobarat, sed eos etiam quibus displicuerat increparat: aio Christi responsum satis conspicuum facere non respexisse illum Mariæ intentionem, nec proprie vnctionem illam quam approbaret vel incusaret. Factum enim illud dixit ipsius Dei Patris prouidentia, quo ipsos admoneret pro gaudio & triumpho quem sibi polliceri viderentur ex tam celebri ipsius in Ierusalem introitu, quasi omnia peruenisset ad eum finem quem Messiam sperabant allaturum, contrà hanc vnctionem, quam sponte receperat, sepulturam eius ac proinde mortem propinquam ipsis portendere. Aliam verò historiam quòd attinet, à superiore prorsus diuersam, vt ex temporis, loci & personarum circunstantiis apparet, à Luca descriptam, cap.7. in qua dicitur etiam Iesus Christus tali quadam vnctione pedes suos inungi passus, Dominus euidenter ostendit id quo maximè superbi & delicati homines non crebrò solerent vti, à se non admitti lotionis vllius aut vnctionis pedum respectu: sed vt Pharisaicæ superbiæ tam eximiū poenitentiæ & fidei miseræ illius peccatricis exemplum ob oculos poneretur.
units.tr: Moreover, the expense and outlay of this burial may perhaps seem new and strange to someone, in the case of a man who, while he lived, had sufficiently testified how far he was from such things. Otherwise, these things were customary at that time and adiaphora, and suited to the dignity of the persons, for the reasons we heard above. First, then, besides the two reasons we brought forward above, it must be noted that they had received no command of the Lord in this matter. They acted from the simple love of those two men and their outstanding will towards Christ, and likewise of the women, about whom the following history will say something. Next, it should be noted that the Lord so governed all things by his providence that he did not allow this preparation of theirs to take effect. The anointing was deferred until the next day, and he rose before the women came to the sepulchre. Indeed, on the contrary, the Lord, rebuking them through his Angels for seeking the living among the dead, understood this not only of a visit to the sepulchre but of a preparation suited to the dead rather than to the living. But if it is objected, on the contrary, what the four Evangelists have recorded about Mary, the sister of Lazarus, who poured very precious ointment on his head, and which deed Christ not only approved but also rebuked those who were displeased by it: I answer that Christ's reply makes it plain enough that he did not regard Mary's intention, nor properly that anointing, whether to approve or to condemn it. For he said that the deed came by the providence of God the Father himself, to admonish them about the joy and triumph which they seemed to promise themselves from his so celebrated entry into Jerusalem, as if everything had reached the end which they hoped the Messiah would bring. Whereas this anointing, which he had willingly accepted, foretold to them his burial and therefore his approaching death. As for the other history, altogether different from the previous one, as the circumstances of time, place and persons show, described by Luke in chapter 7, in which it is also said that Jesus Christ allowed his feet to be anointed in a similar way: the Lord clearly showed that he did not accept such washing or anointing of the feet from himself, a thing which proud and fastidious men do not often use. Rather, it was so that the outstanding example of repentance and faith of that wretched sinful woman might be set before the eyes of Pharisaic pride.

units.la: Quanta est igitur bonorum illorum scilicet Ecclesiasticorum impudentia qui Scripturas ipsas prophanare non erubescunt, talibus exemplis velantes luxum suum & ambitiosas delicias ac helluationes, vt Regum & magnorum Principum pompam & munificentiam superent? Qua in re si perfrictam frontem detegunt, quænam eorum etiam est conscientia, quum ne obolum quidem nisi pauperum sumptibus impendant, ac proinde tot habeant manifestissima intolerandorum sacrilegiorum testimonia? Sed quid agas? Tantum est ac tam inueteratum istud malum, vt vnus Deus medicam manum admouere possit, quod se facturum est pollicitus, Apoc.17. & 18. in illius scorti & procorū inducias è cælo pluens, quod per Prophetam olim ipsis promissum est, Psal.11.6.
units.tr: How great, then, is the impudence of those good ecclesiastics, who are not ashamed to profane the Scriptures themselves, using such examples to veil their luxury, their ambitious delights and their gluttony, so that they may surpass the pomp and munificence of kings and great princes? If in this matter they show a brazen forehead, what conscience do they have, when they spend not even a penny except from the funds of the poor? So they have many most manifest testimonies of intolerable sacrileges. But what can one do? This evil is so great and so deeply rooted that only God can apply a healing hand, as he has promised to do, Rev. 17 and 18, sending down from heaven a truce for that harlot and her suitors, as was once promised them through the Prophet, Psalm 11:6.

units.la: Gratias autem immortales agamus Deo Optimo Maximo, Patri Domini nostri Iesu Christi pro immensa ipsius erga nos miseri-cordia, cordia,& tam benigna patientia, vt quum nos vndique tam rabidi & truculenti hostes tam propè circunstent, tamen hanc nobis gratiam concesserit, vt hactenus totum tractatum au-diuerimus vltimæ illius tantæ aduersus capita-lissimos hostes nostros luctæ, in qua superior euasit mortem ipsam intra ipsius penetralia persequens. At quoniam tantus hic thesaurus iis qui abutuntur condemnationi cedit, aut etiam iis qui per simulationem acceptum abiiciunt, supplices eum precemur vt nobis hac gratiam largiatur, quò vera & viua fide ipsum amplectamur, & viuificum in nobis efficiat ad honorem & gloriam ipsius per Sancti Spiritus in nobis habitantis vim & efficaciam:quò magis ac magis fructum huius mortis & sepulturæ percipiamus, verè in nobis vetere homine moriente, nouóque contra vires nouas accipiente per virtutem resurrectionis ipsius, cuius etiam deinceps,Deo nobis annuente,sumus historiam ad perfectam nostram consolationem omnino necessariam audituMRI. AMEN.
units.tr: Let us give immortal thanks to God, Best and Greatest, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, for his immense mercy towards us and for his so kind patience. Although such raging and savage enemies surround us so closely on every side, he has nevertheless granted us this grace: that so far we have heard the whole account of that last great struggle against our most deadly enemies, in which the Superior one prevailed, pursuing death itself into its innermost chambers. But since this so great treasure yields to those who abuse it to their condemnation, or who by pretence cast it away after receiving it, let us pray humbly that he would grant us this grace, that we may embrace it with true and living faith, and that he would make it life-giving in us, to his honour and glory, through the power and efficacy of the Holy Spirit dwelling in us. So that more and more we may receive the fruit of this death and burial, truly the old man dying in us and a new man receiving new strength through the power of his resurrection. Of this history, God granting it to us, we shall hereafter hear, which is wholly necessary for our perfect consolation. AMEN.
